[וְזֶה דְּאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (בְּרָכוֹת נּוּן חֵית עַמּוּד אָלֶף) [
And this explains what is stated in the Gemara (Berakhot 58a):
הָרוֹאֶה חַכְמֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אוֹמֵר בָּרוּךְ שֶׁחָלַק מֵחָכְמָתוֹ לִירֵיאָיו,
One who sees the sages of Israel recites, "Blessed is He Who has imparted (chalak—shared a portion) of His wisdom to those who fear Him,"
חַכְמֵי עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת אוֹמֵר בָּרוּךְ שֶׁנָּתַן מֵחָכְמָתוֹ לְבָשָׂר וָדָם
while one who sees the sages of the nations recites, "Blessed is He Who has given (natan) of His wisdom to flesh and blood,"
וְכֵן הוּא הַחִילּוּק בֵּין מַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְמַלְכֵי עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
and the same distinction applies between the kings of Israel and the kings of the nations;
וְהַיְינוּ מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל הֵם חֵלֶק מִמֶּנּוּ יִתְבָּרַךְ
and this is because Israel are an actual portion (chelek) of Him, blessed be He,
וְחָכְמַת עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת הוּא חָכְמַת הַטֶּבַע וְאֵין לָהּ שַׁיָּיכוּת לְהַקְּדוּשָּׁה
whereas the wisdom of the nations is merely the wisdom of nature, which has no intrinsic connection to holiness,
כִּי חָכְמַת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהִתְנַהֲגוּתָם הוּא עַל פִּי תּוֹרַת הַשֵּׁם. תַּשְׁלוּם.]
for the wisdom of Israel and their entire conduct is governed according to the Torah of Hashem. End of addendum.
h:
Yishmael, Hagar, and the Spiritual Roots of Generations
It is written (Psalms 111:6): "He has declared to His people the power of His works, in giving them the heritage of the nations

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Toldot 1
p: וְאֵלֶּה תּוֹלְדֹת יִצְחָק בֶּן אַבְרָהָם אַבְרָהָם הוֹלִיד אֶת יִצְחָק.
And these are the generations of Isaac, son of Abraham; Abraham begot Isaac.
כְּתִיב (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים אָלֶף כָּף חֵית, טֵית) "אִם תִּדְרְשֶׁנּוּ יִמָּצֵא לָךְ",
It is written (I Chronicles 28:9): "If you seek Him, He will be found by you"—
הַדְּרִישָׁה הוּא אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וְהַמְּצִיאָה הוּא יִצְחָק,
the "seeking" is our father Abraham, peace be upon him, and the "finding" is Isaac;
כִּי עִנְיַן אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ הָיָה שֶׁהָיָה מִשְׁתּוֹקֵק תָּמִיד לְדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה מְאֹד מְאֹד
for the essence of our father Abraham was that he constantly yearned for words of Torah exceedingly,
וְשֶׁיִּתְפַּרְסֵם בָּעוֹלָם כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֶלֶךְ עֲלֵיהֶם, וְזֹאת הוּא מִדּוֹת הָאַהֲבָה.
and desired that it be publicized throughout the world that Hashem, blessed be He, reigns over them, and this is the attribute of Love (Chesed).
וּמִדּוֹת יִצְחָק הוּא מִדּוֹת גְּבוּרָה,
And the attribute of Isaac is the attribute of Might (Gevurah),
הַיְינוּ אַחַר שֶׁנִּתְבָּרֵר זֹאת וְיָרַד הִתְגַּלּוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
namely, what unfolds after this seeking has been clarified and the revelation of Hashem, blessed be He, has descended into this world;
וְזֹאת יִקָּרֵא גְּבוּרָה כְּמוֹ דְּאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (מְגִילָּה לָמֶד אָלֶף עַמּוּד בֵּית) כָּךְ שָׁמַע מֹשֶׁה מִפִּי הַגְּבוּרָה.
and this divine revelation is called Gevurah, as is stated in the Gemara (Megillah 31b): "Thus Moses heard from the mouth of the Gevurah (the Almighty)."
וְיִצְחָק הָיָה גַּם כֵּן נִקְרָא גְּבוּרַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּעוֹלָם.
And Isaac was likewise called the Gevurah of Hashem, blessed be He, in the world.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר הַכָּתוּב "וְאֵלֶּה תּוֹלְדוֹת יִצְחָק בֶּן אַבְרָהָם" וְכוּלֵי
And this is what Scripture states: "And these are the generations of Isaac, son of Abraham," etc.—
הַיְינוּ תּוֹלְדוֹת יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ הוּא פִּרְסוּם הִתְגַּלּוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
meaning that the spiritual offshoot of our father Isaac is the manifestation of the revelation of Hashem, blessed be He, in this world;
"אַבְרָהָם הוֹלִיד אֶת יִצְחָק" הַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּקַת אַבְרָהָם הָיְתָה זֹאת,
and "Abraham begot Isaac" means that this revelation came about directly through the yearning of Abraham,
כִּי הַתְּשׁוּקָה הוּא מִדּוֹת אַבְרָהָם,
for yearning is the attribute of Abraham,
וְכֵן כָּל דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה אֲמִיתִּיִּים אֵין לָהֶם הוֹלָדָה רַק אַחַר גּוֹדֶל תְּשׁוּקָה שֶׁיִּשְׁתּוֹקֵק הָאָדָם לָהֶם.
and similarly, all authentic words of Torah are born only after the immense yearning with which a person longs for them.
וְזֶה גַּם כֵּן עִנְיַן הַגְּמָרָא (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא מֵם דָּלֶת עַמּוּד אָלֶף)
And this is also the inner meaning of the Gemara (Bava Metzia 44a):
מַתְנֵי לֵיהּ רַבִּי לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרֵיהּ בְּיַלְדוּתֵיהּ, הַכֶּסֶף קוֹנֶה אֶת הַזָּהָב,
Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi taught his son Rabbi Shimon in his youth: "Silver acquires gold,"
וּבְזִקְנוּתֵיהּ הַזָּהָב קוֹנֶה אֶת הַכֶּסֶף.
and in his old age he taught him: "Gold acquires silver."
הַיְינוּ כִּי בַּיַּלְדוּת שֶׁל הָאָדָם יֵשׁ גּוֹדֶל תְּשׁוּקָה וְחֶמְדָּה לְדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה
That is, in a person's youth there is a natural intensity of yearning and desire for words of Torah,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה קוֹנֶה אֶת הַזָּהָב הַיְינוּ דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה לַאֲמִיתָּם יִקָּרְאוּ בְּשֵׁם זָהָב,
and through this he acquires "the gold"—for words of Torah in their ultimate truth and clarity are called gold (which corresponds to Gevurah/Isaac),
וְכֶסֶף הַיְינוּ תְּשׁוּקָה וּכְסִיפָה.
while "silver" (kesef) denotes yearning and longing (kesifah, corresponding to Chesed/Abraham).
אֲבָל בַּזִּקְנָה צָרִיךְ הָאָדָם לְבַקֵּשׁ שֶׁלֹּא יוּסַר מִמֶּנּוּ הַחֵשֶׁק לְדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה,
However, in old age a person must pray that the desire for words of Torah not be taken away from him,
כִּי לְעֵת הַזִּקְנָה כָּל כֹּחוֹת הַתְּשׁוּקָה שֶׁל הָאָדָם מִתְחַלְּשִׁין,
because in old age all of a person's natural faculties of passion and longing weaken;
עַל כֵּן שִׁינָּה לוֹ הַזָּהָב קוֹנֶה אֶת הַכֶּסֶף,
therefore he revised his teaching in his old age to "Gold acquires silver,"
וְהוּא תְּפִלָּה שֶׁהִתְפַּלֵּל לַהַשֵּׁם שֶׁעַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה יָבֹא בְּלִבּוֹ חֵשֶׁק לְהוֹסָפַת עוֹד דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה,

which was a prayer that he prayed to Hashem: that through the words of Torah he had already acquired ("gold"), there would be awakened in his heart a fresh desire ("silver") to add even more words of Torah;
וְהוּא לְמָשָׁל לְאָדָם שֶׁשָּׂבֵעַ מֵאֲכִילָה וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן אִם בָּא לְפָנָיו מַאֲכָל טוֹב
and this is analogous to a person who is already full from eating, yet even so, if a delectable dish is placed before him,
הַמַּאֲכָל הַזֶּה מַמְשִׁיךְ לוֹ תַּאֲוָה וְחֵשֶׁק לֶאֱכוֹל יוֹתֵר,
that delicious food itself draws forth in him a new appetite and desire to eat more,
וְכֵן הוּא הָעִנְיָן בְּדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה.
and so it is with words of Torah.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָנוּ מִתְפַּלְּלִין בְּכָל יוֹם, וְהַעֲרֵב נָא הַשֵּׁם אֱלֹקֵינוּ אֶת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָתְךָ בְּפִינוּ,
And this is what we pray every day: "Please make sweet, O Hashem our God, the words of Your Torah in our mouth,"
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּמְתְּקוּ לָנוּ הַדִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לָנוּ בְּכָל פַּעַם תְּשׁוּקָה יוֹתֵר אֲלֵיהֶם.
meaning that the words of Torah themselves should be so sweet to us that they continually generate within us an ever-greater yearning for them.
וְזֶה פֵּירוּשׁ הַפָּסוּק (יוֹאֵל בֵּית, כָּף וָאו) "וַאֲכַלְתֶּם אָכוֹל וְשָׂבוֹעַ"
And this is the meaning of the verse (Joel 2:26): "And you shall eat, eating and being satisfied,"
וּכְפִילַת הַלָּשׁוֹן מוֹרֶה עַל זֶה, דְּעַל יְדֵי הָאֲכִילָה יָבֹא לְךָ חֶמְדָּה יוֹתֵר
where the doubling of the verb ("eat, eating") indicates this—that through the act of eating itself, a greater desire will come to you,
וְהוּא לְמָשָׁל לְדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר.
serving as a metaphor for words of Torah, as has been explained.
h:
The Generations of Yitzchak and the Search for Hashem
It is written (I Chronicles 28:9): "If you seek Him, He will be found by you"—

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Toldot 2
p: וַיֶּאֱהַב יִצְחָק אֶת עֵשָׂו כִּי צַיִד בְּפִיו.
And Isaac loved Esau, because game (tzayid) was in his mouth.
וְנִתְפָּרֵשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סָמֶךְ גִּימֶל, יוֹד) שֶׁהָיָה צָד אֶת אָבִיו הַאֵיךְ מְעַשְּׂרִין אֶת הַמֶּלַח וְאֶת הַתֶּבֶן.
And this was explained in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 63:10) that he used to trap (tzad) his father with pious questions on his lips, asking how one tithes salt and straw.
וְהִנֵּה אֵין לַחֲשֹׁב אֶת הַדָּבָר כִּפְשׁוּטוֹ כִּי בֶּטַח לֹא טָעָה יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ בּוֹ, בְּאִם הָיָה רַמַּאי מְפֹרָשׁ.
Now, one must not think of this matter according to its superficial meaning, for our father Isaac certainly would not have been deceived by him had he been a blatant deceiver.
אַךְ שֶׁמִּתְּחִלָּה הָיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם שָׁוִים אֲנָשִׁים גְּדוֹלִים,
Rather, initially both of them (Jacob and Esau) appeared equally as great men,
וְרַק שֶׁדַּעַת עֵשָׂו הָיָה לְיַפּוֹת אֶת עַצְמוֹ לִפְנֵי אָבִיו כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּשָּׂא חֵן בְּעֵינָיו
except that Esau's approach was to embellish himself before his father so as to find favor in his eyes,
לְמַעַן יִתְפַּלֵּל עֲבוּרוֹ לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּתֵּן חָכְמָה בְּלִבּוֹ,
in order that Isaac would pray on his behalf to Hashem, blessed be He, to place wisdom in his heart;
וְיַעֲקֹב הָלַךְ בְּתֻמּוֹ וְאָמַר לָמָּה לִי זֹאת,
whereas Jacob walked in his simple wholesomeness and said, "Why do I need such artifices?
אִם אֲנִי הָגוּן בְּעֵינֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יִתֵּן בְּלֵב אָבִי יִצְחָק שֶׁיִּתְפַּלֵּל עֲבוּרִי אֵלָיו,
If I am worthy in the eyes of Hashem, blessed be He, He Himself will place it in the heart of my father Isaac to pray for me!"
וְלֹא הָיָה יָשַׁר בְּעֵינָיו דַּרְכּוֹ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו כִּי דֶּרֶךְ זֶה צָרִיךְ בָּרֵר
And Esau's way was not upright in Jacob's eyes, because such a path requires clarification (beirur),
כִּי מִי יֹאמַר שֶׁכַּוָּנָתוֹ רְצוּיָה פֶּן הוּא רַק לְרַמָּאוּת.
for who can say that his motive is genuinely desirable, lest it be merely for deception?
וּבְיַעַן כִּי יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ הִפְרִישׁ אֶת עַצְמוֹ מִכָּל סָפֵק וְרַק בַּהַשֵּׁם לְבַדּוֹ בָּטַח לִבּוֹ,
And whereas our father Jacob separated himself from any doubtful conduct and trusted his heart to Hashem alone—
וּבֶאֱמֶת בְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁהָאָדָם מַכְנִיס אֶת עַצְמוֹ בִּסְפֵיקוֹת בַּעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וּבִדְבָרִים הַצְּרִיכִים בֵּרוּר,
yet in truth, wherever a person enters into doubtful areas in the service of Hashem, blessed be He, and into matters requiring clarification,
אִם יִתְבָּרֵר לְטוֹב אָז הוּא גָּדוֹל מִמִּי שֶׁסִּלֵּק עַצְמוֹ מִסְּפֵיקוֹת,
if it is ultimately clarified for the good, then he reaches a level even greater than one who withdrew himself from doubts;
רַק זֹאת הִיא בְּזֶרַע יַעֲקֹב לְפִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם מִבְטַח עֹז בְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיְּבָרֵר הַכֹּל לְטוֹב
however, this applies only to the seed of Jacob: because they possess a mighty trust in Hashem, blessed be He, that He will clarify everything for the good,
זֶה מֻתָּר לוֹ לְהַכְנִיס עַצְמוֹ בְּסָפֵק.
such a person is permitted to enter into a situation of doubt.
אֲבָל מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מִבְטַח עֹז אָסוּר לְהַכְנִיס עַצְמוֹ בְּסָפֵק,
But one who lacks this mighty, unshakable trust is forbidden to place himself into moral doubt,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁעֵשָׂו הִכְנִיס עַצְמוֹ בִּדְבָרִים שֶׁנִּתְבָּרְרוּ אַחַר כָּךְ שֶׁהָיוּ רָעִים,
just as Esau entered into behaviors that were subsequently clarified to be thoroughly evil,
כִּי לֹא מְבָרֵר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְטוֹב רַק אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
for the Holy One, blessed be He, clarifies doubtful matters for the good only for Israel,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר בַּפָּסוּק "וּצְדָקָה תִּהְיֶה לָנוּ" [פָּרָשַׁת וָאֶתְחַנַּן]
as was explained on the verse "And it shall be righteousness (tzedakah) for us" (Parashat Va'etchanan),
וְכָל מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִזֶּרַע יַעֲקֹב טוֹב לְפָנָיו לְצַמְצֵם אֶת עַצְמוֹ בְּכָל מִינֵי צִמְצוּמִים
whereas anyone who is not of the seed of Jacob would do better to restrict himself with all manner of restraints,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר בְּעִנְיַן גֵּרִים שֶׁאֲסוּרִים לְהַכְנִיס עַצְמָם בִּסְפֵיקוֹת,
as was explained regarding converts, who are forbidden to place themselves into doubtful situations;
וּלְפִיכָךְ יִצְחָק כַּאֲשֶׁר רָאָה שֶׁעֵשָׂו מַכְנִיס עַצְמוֹ בִּדְבָרִים כָּאֵלּוּ
and therefore Isaac, when he saw that Esau was entering into such ambiguous behaviors,
אָמַר אִם יִתְבָּרֵר זֶה יִהְיֶה גָּדוֹל מִיַּעֲקֹב,
said to himself: "If this is clarified for the good, he will be even greater than Jacob!"
אַךְ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הֵעִיד עָלָיו אַחַר כָּךְ שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה כַּוָּנָתוֹ לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם.
Yet Hashem, blessed be He, subsequently testified against Esau that his intention was not for the sake of Heaven.
וְכֵן גַּם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל נִמְצְאוּ נְפָשׁוֹת שֶׁמֻּתָּרִים לְהַכְנִיס עַצְמָם יוֹתֵר בִּסְפֵיקוֹת מִנְּפָשׁוֹת אֲחֵרוֹת אַף שֶׁאֵלּוּ וְאֵלּוּ מִזֶּרַע יַעֲקֹב,
And similarly within Israel itself, there are certain souls who are permitted to enter into doubtful situations more than other souls, even though both are from the seed of Jacob,
כְּמוֹ הָעִנְיָן שֶׁל שִׁמְעוֹן וְדִינָה,
such as the incident of Simeon and Dinah:
כִּי לֵוִי לֹא חָפַץ לְקַחְתָּהּ כִּי יָרֵא לְנַפְשׁוֹ פֶּן אֵין כַּוָּנָתוֹ בְּעֹמֶק לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם,
for Levi did not wish to marry her after she had been defiled by Shechem, because he feared for his soul lest his deepest intention not be purely for the sake of Heaven,
כִּי כָל שֵׁבֶט לֵוִי הֵם בְּיִרְאָה וְהִסְתַּלְּקוּת מִסָּפֵק אֶצְלָם
for the entire tribe of Levi conducts itself with awe and withdrawal from doubt,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב אֶצְלָם (מַלְאָכִי בֵּית, הֵא) "וָאֶתְּנֵם לוֹ מוֹרָא" וְכוּלֵי
as it is written of them (Malachi 2:5): "And I gave them to him for fear, and he feared Me," etc.,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יָצְאוּ מֵאִתָּם כֹּהֲנִים שֶׁנִּכְנָסִים לִפְנַי וְלִפְנִים,
and through this caution emerged from them the Kohanim (priests) who enter into the innermost Sanctum,
וְעַל כֵּן נִתְבָּרֵר הַחַיִּים שֶׁלָּהֶם מִיָּד כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּתְבָּאֵר בְּפָרָשַׁת קֹרַח בְּהַמַּטּוֹת [דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל וַיֹּאמֶר הַשֵּׁם].
and therefore their spiritual vitality was clarified immediately (when Aaron's staff blossomed), as will be explained in Parashat Korach regarding the staffs (s.v. VaYomer Hashem).
אֲבָל שִׁמְעוֹן הִכְנִיס עַצְמוֹ בְּסָפֵק וְאָמַר חַס וְשָׁלוֹם שֶׁאֲנִי מַחְזִיק עַצְמִי לְנוֹאֵף,
Simeon, however, entered into the doubtful situation and said, "Heaven forbid that I should suspect myself of being an adulterer!"
וְנָשָׂא אֶת דִּינָה וְהִכְנִיס אֶת עַצְמוֹ בְּדָבָר הַצָּרִיךְ בָּרֵר,
And he married Dinah, placing himself into a matter requiring deep clarification,
כִּי אָמַר שֶׁהוּא בָּטוּחַ בַּהַשֵּׁם שֶׁיְּבָרְרוֹ לְטוֹב
for he said that he was confident in Hashem that He would clarify it for the good—
שֶׁכַּוָּנָתוֹ לֹא הָיְתָה רַק לְהוֹצִיאָהּ מִשְּׁכֶם וְכָל כַּוָּנָתוֹ הָיְתָה רַק לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם,
proving that his motive was solely to rescue her from the house of Shechem and that his entire intention was purely for the sake of Heaven;
וְעַל כֵּן הָיָה צָרִיךְ כָּל שֵׁבֶט שִׁמְעוֹן לְבֵרוּרִין בִּדְבָרִים כָּאֵלֶּה,
and consequently the entire tribe of Simeon had to undergo arduous clarifications in matters of this sort,
כְּגוֹן זִמְרִי שֶׁהָיָה אוֹמֵר גַּם כֵּן שֶׁכַּוָּנָתוֹ טוֹב כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּתְבָּאֵר בִּמְקוֹמוֹ [פָּרָשַׁת בָּלָק דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל וְהִנֵּה]
such as Zimri, prince of Simeon, who also claimed that his intention with Cozbi was for a good purpose, as will be explained in its place (Parashat Balak, s.v. VeHineh),
וְלֶעָתִיד כְּשֶׁיִּתְבָּרֵר שֵׁבֶט שִׁמְעוֹן יִהְיֶה מַעֲלָתוֹ גָּדוֹל מִשֶּׁל לֵוִי.
and in the ultimate future, when the tribe of Simeon is fully clarified, its spiritual stature will be even greater than that of Levi.

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Toldot 3
p: וַיִּשְׁאֲלוּ אַנְשֵׁי הַמָּקוֹם לְאִשְׁתּוֹ וַיֹּאמֶר אֲחֹתִי הִיא.
And the men of the place asked concerning his wife, and he said, "She is my sister."
אִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא פֶּרֶק הַזָּהָב (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא נּוּן טֵית עַמּוּד אָלֶף) אוֹקִירוֹ לִנְשַׁיְכוּ כִּי הֵיכִי דִּתְתַעְתְּרוּ,
It is stated in the Gemara, chapter HaZahav (Bava Metzia 59a): "Honor your wives so that you may become wealthy,"
וְזֶה נִרְמַז גַּבֵּי אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "וַיִּקְרָא הָאָדָם שֵׁם אִשְׁתּוֹ חַוָּה" וְכוּלֵי
and this is alluded to regarding Adam the First, of whom it is stated, "And the man called his wife's name Eve (Chavah), because she was the mother of all living," etc.,
וּמִיָּד נֶאֱמַר "וַיַּעַשׂ הַשֵּׁם לְאָדָם וּלְאִשְׁתּוֹ כָּתְנוֹת עוֹר וַיַּלְבִּשֵׁם",
and immediately afterward it is stated, "And Hashem made for Adam and for his wife garments of skin, and clothed them"—
הַיְנוּ אַחַר שֶׁנִּתְמַעֵט הַשְׁפָּעָתוֹ עַל יְדֵי הַנָּחָשׁ,
meaning that after his spiritual and material bounty had been diminished through the sin of the serpent,
וְעַל יְדֵי כָּתְנוֹת עוֹר חָזְרָה אֵלָיו הַהַשְׁפָּעָה מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוֹקִיר לְחַוָּה וּקְרָאָהּ עַל שֵׁם אֵם כָּל חַי.
the bounty returned to him through the garments of skin because he honored Eve and named her "the mother of all living."
וְכֵן מָצִינוּ גַּם בְּאַבְרָהָם שֶׁאָמַר עַל שָׂרָה אֲחוֹתִי הִיא כְּשֶׁהָלַךְ לְמִצְרַיִם וְיָצָא מִשָּׁם בִּרְכוּשׁ רַב,

And so we find also with Abraham, who said of Sarah "She is my sister" (an expression of endearment and honor, as in "My sister, my bride") when he went down to Egypt, and he emerged from there with great wealth;
וְכֵן יִצְחָק שֶׁאָמַר עַל רִבְקָה אֲחוֹתִי הִיא נֶאֱמַר תֵּכֶף "וַיִּזְרַע יִצְחָק בָּאָרֶץ הַהִיא וַיִּמְצָא מֵאָה שְׁעָרִים".
and likewise with Isaac, who said of Rebecca "She is my sister," it is immediately stated afterward: "And Isaac sowed in that land, and reaped in the same year a hundredfold, and Hashem blessed him."

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Toldot 4
p: וַיָּשָׁב יִצְחָק וַיַּחְפֹּר אֶת בְּאֵרֹת וְכוּלֵי.
And Isaac dug again the wells of water, etc.
כְּתִיב (תְּהִלִּים קוּף מֵם זַיִן, יוֹד זַיִן) "מַשְׁלִיךְ קַרְחוֹ כְפִתִּים וְכוּלֵי יַשֵּׁב רוּחוֹ יִזְּלוּ מָיִם".

It is written (Psalms 147:17–18): "He casts forth His ice like morsels; who can stand before His cold? He sends out His word and melts them; He causes His wind to blow (yashev rucho), and the waters flow."
"מַשְׁלִיךְ קַרְחוֹ כְפִתִּים" הַיְינוּ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נָתַן כֹּחַ בָּאֻמּוֹת לִמְשֹׁל עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
"He casts forth His ice like morsels" means that Hashem, blessed be He, gave power to the nations to rule over Israel.
"יַשֵּׁב רוּחוֹ" שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יִתְרַצֶּה אַחַר כָּךְ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
"He causes His wind to blow (yashev rucho)" means that the Holy One, blessed be He, is subsequentlyconciliated toward Israel—
כִּי יַשֵּׁב הוּא לְשׁוֹן מְשִׁיבַת נֶפֶשׁ,
for yashev is an expression of restoring and refreshing the soul (meshivat nefesh)—
אָז "יִזְּלוּ מָיִם" מְתוּקִים.
and then sweet "waters flow" (the waters of Torah).
"מַגִּיד דְּבָרָיו לְיַעֲקֹב" הַיְינוּ שֶׁמַּגִּיד לָהֶם הַחֵטְא וְהַחֶסְרוֹן הַנִּמְצָא בָם
The next verse continues: "He declares His words unto Jacob" (Psalms 147:19), meaning that He reveals to them the specific flaw and deficiency found within them
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה יֵשׁ כֹּחַ בָּאֻמּוֹת לִמְשֹׁל עֲלֵיהֶם, וְיַחְזְרוּ מִיָּד בִּתְשׁוּבָה.
through which the nations gained the power to rule over them, so that Israel may immediately return in repentance.
"לֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי" כִּי לָהֶם אֵינוֹ מוֹדִיעַ כַּוָּנָתוֹ כְּלָל.
"He has not dealt so with any nation, and as for His judgments, they have not known them" (Psalms 147:20)—for to the nations He does not make known His inner intention at all.
וְזֶה הָיָה הָעִנְיָן גַּם כֵּן כָּאן,
And this was the very matter here as well:
כַּאֲשֶׁר רָאָה יִצְחָק שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ אֲבִימֶלֶךְ לֵךְ מֵעִמָּנוּ לְפִי שֶׁחָשַׁב אֲשֶׁר יִצְחָק מִתְגָּאֶה עֲלֵיהֶם,
when Isaac saw that Abimelech said to him, "Go away from us, for you have become much mightier than we," because Abimelech thought that Isaac was lording his wealth over them,
וּבֶאֱמֶת אֵצֶל יִצְחָק לֹא הָיָה נֶחְשַׁב זֹאת לְשׁוּם חִסָּרוֹן מָה שֶׁהוּא מִתְגָּאֶה עַל אֲבִימֶלֶךְ,
whereas in truth, in Isaac's eyes it was not considered any flaw at all to hold himself above Abimelech,
כִּי הָיָה אֶצְלוֹ כְּמוֹ אָדָם הַמִּתְגָּאֶה עַל הַבְּהֵמָה, אֲשֶׁר כֵּן הָיְתָה הַבְּרִיאָה שֶׁהָאָדָם גָּדוֹל מֵהַבְּהֵמָה,
for to him it was simply like a human being standing superior over an animal, which is the natural order of Creation wherein man is greater than beast;
עַל כֵּן הֵרַע מְאֹד בְּעֵינָיו, אַחֲרֵי כִּי הָיָה בֶּן אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ שֶׁהָיָה מֶלֶךְ בָּעוֹלָם
therefore his expulsion troubled Isaac greatly—since he was the son of our father Abraham, who was revered as a king in the world,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרֵאשִׁית כָּף גִּימֶל, וָאו) "נְשִׂיא אֱלֹקִים" וְכוּלֵי וְהָיָה חָשׁוּב בְּכָל הָעוֹלָם וְטִבְעוֹ יָצָא
as it is written (Genesis 23:6), "You are a prince of God among us," etc., and he was esteemed throughout the entire world where his fame (coin) had spread—
וּמַדּוּעַ יָעִיקוּ לוֹ עַד שֶׁהֻצְרַךְ לְהִגָּלוֹת מִגְּרָר.
so why should they harass him to the point that he was forced to go into exile from Gerar?
וְהִתְיַשֵּׁב בְּדַעְתּוֹ אֲשֶׁר בְּוַדַּאי פָּגַם וְחִסֵּר בְּעִסְקֵי עֲבוֹדַת אָבִיו
So Isaac reflected in his mind that he had surely fallen short and lacked in the spiritual service of his father Abraham,
הַיְינוּ מִדּוֹת אַהֲבָה שֶׁהוּא חֶמְדָּה וּתְשׁוּקָה לְדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה,
namely the attribute of Love, which is intense desire and yearning for words of Torah,
וַאֲבִימֶלֶךְ לֹא הָיָה רַק שָׁלִיחַ שֶׁעַל יָדוֹ יִוָּדַע לְיִצְחָק שֶׁיִּתֵּן זֹאת עַל לִבּוֹ,
and Abimelech was merely an unwitting messenger through whom this would become known to Isaac so that he would take it to heart,
וַאֲבִימֶלֶךְ בְּעַצְמוֹ לֹא הֵבִין כְּלוּם מָה שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַנְהִיג עַל יָדוֹ כִּי "מִשְׁפָּטִים בַּל יְדָעוּם".
while Abimelech himself understood nothing at all of what Hashem, blessed be He, was orchestrating through him, for "as for His judgments, they have not known them."
וְכַאֲשֶׁר הֵבִין יִצְחָק אֶת זֹאת נֶאֱמַר מִיָּד "וַיָּשָׁב וַיַּחְפֹּר אֶת בְּאֵרֹת הַמַּיִם אֲשֶׁר חָפְרוּ עַבְדֵי אָבִיו",
And as soon as Isaac understood this, it is immediately stated: "And Isaac dug again the wells of water which they had dug in the days of Abraham his father,"
הַיְינוּ שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה בָּא לְמִדּוֹת אַהֲבָה מֵחֲמַת שֶׁרָאָה בְּעַצְמוֹ הַחֶסְרוֹן
meaning that through this realization he returned to the attribute of Love, because he recognized the deficiency within himself,
וּמִמֵּילָא בָּא לוֹ חֵשֶׁק חָדָשׁ לְדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה.
and consequently a renewed desire for words of Torah ("wells of water") awakened within him.
וְזֶה הָיָה עִנְיָן בִּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כְּמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (סַנְהֶדְרִין כָּף אָלֶף עַמּוּד בֵּית)
And this was also the matter regarding King Solomon, peace be upon him, as is stated in the Gemara (Sanhedrin 21b):
"אֵין כֶּסֶף נֶחְשָׁב בִּימֵי שְׁלֹמֹה לִמְאוּמָה" וּכְתִיב "וַיִּתֵּן שְׁלֹמֹה אֶת הַכֶּסֶף כָּאֲבָנִים"

One verse states, "Silver was not accounted for anything in the days of Solomon" (I Kings 10:21), while another verse states, "And the king made silver in Jerusalem as stones" (I Kings 10:27, implying it had some value)—
וּמְשַׁנֵּי כָּאן קֹדֶם שֶׁנָּשָׂא אֶת בַּת פַּרְעֹה כָּאן לְאַחַר שֶׁנָּשָׂא אֶת בַּת פַּרְעֹה.
and the Gemara answers: Here it was before he married Pharaoh's daughter; there it was after he married Pharaoh's daughter.
כִּי תְּחִלָּה מֵחֲמַת שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ הַשְׁפָּעָה הַרְבֵּה בְּדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה
For initially, because Solomon possessed such an overwhelming abundance of wisdom and words of Torah,
עַל כֵּן לֹא הָיָה אֶצְלוֹ כָּל כָּךְ חֵשֶׁק לְדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה הַנִּקְרָא כֶּסֶף, כִּי כֶּסֶף הַיְינוּ חֵשֶׁק
he did not experience as much unfulfilled yearning for words of Torah, which is called "silver" (kesef), for kesef denotes longing;
וּלְאַחַר שֶׁנָּשָׂא אֶת בַּת פַּרְעֹה אֲשֶׁר זֹאת הָיָה נֶחְשָׁב אֶצְלוֹ לְחֶסְרוֹן
but after he married Pharaoh's daughter, which he recognized as a spiritual deficiency within himself,
וּמִמֵּילָא נִתְהַוָּה לוֹ חֵשֶׁק חָדָשׁ
a renewed yearning ("silver") naturally came into being within him,
עַל כֵּן לֹא נֶאֱמַר כָּאן לִמְאוּמָה כִּי אַחַר כָּךְ נִתְהַוָּה לוֹ חֵשֶׁק.
and therefore in the second verse it does not say that silver was accounted as "nothing," because afterward a fresh longing had been awakened in him.

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Toldot 5
p: וַיִּכְרוּ שָׁם עַבְדֵי יִצְחָק בְּאֵר.
And Isaac's servants dug a well there.
עִנְיַן הַבְּאֵרוֹת שֶׁל יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ,
The inner meaning of the wells dug by our father Isaac
כִּי יִצְחָק הִשְׁתַּדֵּל לִבְחֹר בְּמִדָּה שֶׁעַל יָדָהּ יִהְיֶה הֶפְרֵשׁ וְהֶבְדֵּל בֵּינוֹ וּבֵין אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם,
is that Isaac strove to choose a spiritual attribute through which there would be an absolute distinction and separation between himself (Israel) and the nations of the world,
וְעַל זֶה מְרַמֵּז חֲפִירוֹת הַבְּאֵרוֹת.
and the digging of the successive wells alludes to this quest.
הַבְּאֵר הָרִאשׁוֹן הָיָה דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבָּחַר בְּדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה וְהַכָּרָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹרֵא וְלָאֵלּוּ אֵין שַׁיָּכוּת לָאֻמּוֹת,
The first well ("Esek") represented words of Torah, for he chose words of Torah and the recognition that there is a Creator, assuming the nations had no connection to these;
"וַיָּרִיבוּ רוֹעֵי גְרָר לֵאמֹר לָנוּ הַמָּיִם",
"And the herdsmen of Gerar strove with Isaac's herdsmen, saying, 'The water is ours'"—
הַיְנוּ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שֶׁגַּם לָהֶם יֵשׁ שַׁיָּכוּת בְּאֵלּוּ כִּי גַּם לָהֶם יֵשׁ הַכָּרָה בַּהַשֵּׁם וְגַם שֶׁבַע מִצְווֹת שֶׁנִּצְטַוּוּ.
meaning they claimed that they too had a share in these waters, since they also possess recognition of Hashem as well as the Seven Noahide Commandments that they were commanded.
וְהַבְּאֵר הַשֵּׁנִי הַיְנוּ שֶׁבָּחַר בָּעֲבוֹדָה הַיְנוּ קָרְבָּנוֹת
And the second well ("Sitnah") represents his choosing the pillar of Divine Service (Avodah), namely sacrificial offerings,
וְאָמְרוּ שֶׁגַּם לָהֶם יֵשׁ שַׁיָּכוּת בָּזֶה כִּי נְדָרִים וּנְדָבוֹת מְקַבְּלִין מֵהֶם.
yet they contended that they also have a share in this, because vowed and freewill burnt-offerings are accepted from gentiles in the Temple.
וְאַחַר זֶה נֶאֱמַר "וַיַּעְתֵּק מִשָּׁם וַיַּחְפֹּר",
And after this it is stated, "And he removed from there, and dug another well" ("Rechovot"),
וְעִנְיַן הַבְּאֵר הַזֶּה הַיְנוּ שֶׁבָּחַר בְּסַבְלָנוּת וְיִסּוּרִין, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר לִסְבֹּל עֲבוּר עֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
and the essence of this third well was that he chose patience and suffering—that is to say, lovingly bearing afflictions for the sake of serving Hashem, blessed be He,
כִּדְאִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סָמֶךְ טֵית, חֵית) יִצְחָק חִדֵּשׁ יִסּוּרִין,
as is stated in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 64:4 / 65:9) that Isaac innovated the request for suffering—
"וְלֹא רָבוּ עָלֶיהָ" כִּי מִיָּד שֶׁחָפַר הַבְּאֵר הַזֹּאת בָּרְחוּ הַכֹּל כִּי הֵם בָּעֲטוּ בָּזֶה,
"and for that they strove not," because the moment he dug this well of suffering, all the nations fled, for they spurn and rebel against suffering;
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר בָּזֶה הַבְּאֵר "כִּי עַתָּה הִרְחִיב הַשֵּׁם לָנוּ",
and this is why he said over this well, "For now Hashem has made room for us,"
הַיְנוּ שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ שֶׁלֹּא יָבוֹא חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לְיִסּוּרִין גְּדוֹלִים רַק תַּכְלִית יִסּוּרִין
meaning he prayed that Israel not come, Heaven forbid, to overwhelming afflictions that disrupt Torah study, but only to the minimal boundary of suffering,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּבֹאָר בַּגְּמָרָא (עֲרָכִין טֵית זַיִן עַמּוּד בֵּית) בִּקֵּשׁ לַעֲלוֹת דִּינַר זָהָב וְעָלָה בְיָדוֹ דִּינַר כֶּסֶף.

as is explained in the Gemara (Arachin 16b): even if one merely reached into his pocket to take out a gold dinar and a silver dinar came up in his hand instead, that minor inconvenience already counts as the tribulation of suffering.
"וּפָרִינוּ בָּאָרֶץ" הַיְנוּ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יַחְזִיר לָנוּ אֶת כָּל מַה שֶּׁסָּבַלְנוּ טוֹבָה מְרֻבָּה עַל זֶה,
"And we shall be fruitful in the land" means that Hashem, blessed be He, will repay us with abundant goodness for all that we have endured,
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁקָּרָא שֵׁם הַבְּאֵר הָרְבִיעִי שִׁבְעָה כִּי שִׁבְעָה רוֹמֵז עַל עָתִיד כַּיָּדוּעַ,
and this is why he called the name of the fourth well "Shiv'ah" (Seven), for seven alludes to the World to Come, as is known,
הַיְנוּ כִּי לֶעָתִיד יַחְזִיר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְכָל מִי שֶׁסָּבַל יִסּוּרִין בַּעֲבוּר קְדֻשַּׁת שְׁמוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
meaning that in the ultimate future the Holy One, blessed be He, will richly compensate everyone who endured suffering for the sanctification of His Name, blessed be He.
וְזֶה פֵּרוּשׁ הַמִּדְרָשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סָמֶךְ דָּלֶת, יוֹד) "וַיָּבוֹאוּ עַבְדֵי יִצְחָק" אֵין אָנוּ יוֹדְעִים אִם מָצְאוּ מַיִם אִם לֹא מָצְאוּ,

And this is the meaning of the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 64:10):Regarding the fourth well ("And Isaac's servants came and told him concerning the well which they had dug, and said to him, 'We have found water'"), we do not know with certainty whether they found water or did not find water;
כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר "וַיִּמְצְאוּ שָׁם בְּאֵר מַיִם חַיִּים" הֱוֵי שֶׁמָּצְאוּ מַיִם חַיִּים,
when Scripture earlier states, "And they found there a well of living water" (Genesis 26:19), it proves that here too they found living water—
פֵּרוּשׁ שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָדוּעַ אִם מָצְאוּ מַיִם חַיִּים,
the explanation being that in the fourth well it was not explicitly stated whether they found "living water" (eternal life),
כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר בַּבְּאֵר הָרִאשׁוֹן "וַיִּמְצְאוּ בְּאֵר מַיִם חַיִּים" כָּל שֶׁכֵּן בַּבְּאֵר הָרְבִיעִי שֶׁרוֹמֵז עַל טוּב הַצָּפוּן לֶעָתִיד,

yet since it states regarding the first well "and they found a well of living water," all the more so did they find living water in the fourth well, which alludes to the hidden goodness reserved for the World to Come;
וְעַל זֶה גַּם בַּבְּאֵר הַשְּׁלִישִׁי אָמַר "כִּי עַתָּה הִרְחִיב הַשֵּׁם לָנוּ וּפָרִינוּ בָּאָרֶץ".
and anticipating this, already at the third well he declared, "For now Hashem has made room for us, and we shall be fruitful in the land."
h:
The Wells as Paths to Spiritual Discernment
The inner meaning of the wells dug by our father Isaac

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Toldot 6
p: וַיֵּרָא אֵלָיו הַשֵּׁם וְכוּלֵי וַיִּבֶן שָׁם מִזְבֵּחַ וְכוּלֵי וַיִּכְרוּ שָׁם עַבְדֵי יִצְחָק בְּאֵר.
And Hashem appeared to him that night, etc., and he built an altar there, etc., and Isaac's servants dug a well there.
וְלֹא כְתִיב כָּאן קְרִיאַת שְׁמָהּ,
And before the arrival of Phichol and Abimelech, the naming of this well is not yet written here;
וְהִיא עַל דֶּרֶךְ מָשָׁל לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה
and this may be understood by way of a parable: to what is the matter comparable?
אִם מוֹדִיעִין לְאָדָם שֶׁיָּבוֹא אֵלָיו הַמֶּלֶךְ בְּיוֹם פְּלוֹנִי וְהוּא מֵכִין בְּכָל מִינֵי הֲכָנוֹת
If a person is informed that the king will visit him on a certain day, and he busies himself with all manner of preparations,
וּבְתוֹךְ כָּךְ בָּא אֵלָיו הַמֶּלֶךְ הוּא מַשְׁלִיךְ הַכֹּל וּמְקַבֵּל פְּנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ,
and in the midst of his preparations the king suddenly arrives—he immediately drops everything to welcome the king;
כֵּן כָּאן כַּאֲשֶׁר הֶרְאָה אֵלָיו הַשֵּׁם לֹא הָיָה פּוֹנֶה לְשׁוּם דָּבָר.
so too here, once Hashem appeared directly to Isaac, he did not turn his attention to any other matter.
h:
The Altar and the Wells: Two Forms of Avodah
And this may be understood by way of a parable: to what is the matter comparable?

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Toldot 7
p: וַיְהִי עֵשָׂו בֶּן אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה וַיִּקַּח אֶת יְהוּדִית וְכוּלֵי וְאֶת בָּשְׂמַת וְכוּלֵי וַתִּהְיֶיןָ מֹרַת רוּחַ.
And Esau was forty years old when he took to wife Judith (Yehudit), etc., and Basemat, etc., and they were a bitterness of spirit unto Isaac and to Rebecca.
הִנֵּה עֵשָׂו הָיָה פּוֹשֵׁט טְלָפָיו וְהֶרְאָה שֶׁלָּקַח אֶת יְהוּדִית
Behold, Esau used to hypocritically display his split hooves (like a pig pretending to be kosher), and he made a show of marrying "Yehudit,"
אֲשֶׁר שְׁמָהּ מוֹרֶה עַל הַמְשָׁכָה כְּמוֹ אוֹת יוּ"ד שֶׁהוּא מוּכָן לַעֲשׂוֹת מִמֶּנּוּ כָּל הָאוֹתִיּוֹת,
whose name indicates submissive drawing after holiness, like the small letter Yud which is ready and malleable to form all the other letters of the alphabet,
כִּי הָיָה לָהּ גָּוֶן שֶׁהָיָה לָהּ רַךְ לֵבָב לִהְיוֹתָהּ נִמְשֶׁכֶת אַחַר יִצְחָק וְרִבְקָה.
for she put on an outward appearance of having a soft, receptive heart that would be drawn after the ways of Isaac and Rebecca.
וְשֵׁם בָּשְׂמַת מוֹרֶה עַל יִשּׁוּב הַדַּעַת כִּי הוּא לְשׁוֹן מְבֻשָּׂם
And the name "Basemat" indicates settledness of mind and pleasantness, for it is an expression of sweet fragrance (mevusam),
וְאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (יוֹמָא עַיִן וָאו עַמּוּד בֵּית) חַמְרָא וְרֵיחָנֵי פָּקְחִין,
as is stated in the Gemara (Yoma 76b): "Wine and pleasant aromas make a person's mind clear and receptive";
עַל כֵּן נֶאֱמַר תֵּיכֶף שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת לֹא הָיָה כֵן, רַק מֹרַת רוּחַ מִלְּשׁוֹן זָקֵן מַמְרֵא, הַיְנוּ בְּרֵיחַ רַע.

therefore Scripture immediately states that in truth it was not so at all, rather "they were a bitterness of spirit (morat ruach)"—from the expression of a rebellious elder (zaken mamre) and a foul odor (ruach).
וְזֶה שֶׁתִּרְגֵּם אוּנְקְלוּס מְסָרְבָן וּמַרְגְּזָן,
And this is why Onkelos translated morat ruach with two words: "rebellious and provoking" (mesarvan u'margizan)—
מְסָרְבָן הוּא נֶגֶד שֵׁם יְהוּדִית הַיְנוּ שֶׁאֵין לָהּ שׁוּם הַמְשָׁכוֹת
"rebellious" (stubbornly refusing) counters the name Yehudit, showing that she had no genuine submissiveness or drawing toward holiness,
וּמַרְגְּזָן נֶגֶד שֵׁם בָּשְׂמַת שֶׁמּוֹרֶה עַל נְיָיחָא וְיִשּׁוּב הַדַּעַת.
and "provoking" (agitating with anger) counters the name Basemat, which ostensibly indicated tranquility and settledness of mind.
h:
Esav’s Marriages and the Bitterness of Spirit
Behold, Esau used to hypocritically display his split hooves (like a pig pretending to be kosher), and he made a show of marrying "Yehudit

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Toldot 8
p: וַיְהִי כִּי זָקֵן יִצְחָק וַתִּכְהֶיןָ עֵינָיו מֵרְאֹת.
And it came to pass, that when Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim, so that he could not see.
עִנְיַן יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ הָיָה הֵיפֶךְ מִמֹּשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
The spiritual aspect of our father Isaac was the exact converse of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him:
כִּי יִצְחָק לֹא הוּרְשָׁה לָצֵאת מֵהָאָרֶץ אַךְ כֹּחַ הָרְאוּת נִטַּל מִמֶּנּוּ,
for Isaac was never permitted to leave the Land of Israel, yet the power of physical sight was taken from him;
וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לֹא הוּרְשָׁה לִהְיוֹת בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲבָל נֶאֱמַר לוֹ "וּרְאֵה בְעֵינֶיךָ".

whereas Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, was not permitted to enter and dwell in the Land of Israel, yet it was said to him, "And behold it with your eyes" (Deuteronomy 3:27), and "his eye was not dim" (Deuteronomy 34:7).
h:
Yitzchak’s Dimming Eyes and Inner Vision
The spiritual aspect of our father Isaac was the exact converse of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Toldot 9
p: רְאֵה רֵיחַ בְּנִי כְּרֵיחַ שָׂדֶה וְכוּלֵי.
See, the smell of my son is as the smell of a field which Hashem has blessed, etc.
שָׂדֶה רוֹמֵז עַל הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת בִּתְשׁוּקוֹת,
A "field" (an open, unbounded expanse) alludes to expansion in desires;
עַל כֵּן עֵשָׂו נִקְרָא אִישׁ שָׂדֶה לְפִי שֶׁהִתְפַּשֵּׁט בְּכָל מִינֵי חֶמְדוֹת וְתַאֲווֹת רָעוֹת,
therefore Esau is called "a man of the field," because he expanded without restraint into all manner of base cravings and evil lusts;
אַךְ יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ הָיָה לוֹ הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת בִּקְדֻשָּׁה,
whereas our father Jacob possessed boundless expansion within holiness,
וְזֶה "כְּרֵיחַ שָׂדֶה אֲשֶׁר בֵּרְכוֹ הַשֵּׁם" הַיְנוּ חֲקַל תַּפּוּחִין קַדִּישִׁין.
and this is the meaning of "as the smell of a field which Hashem has blessed"—namely, the mystical Field of Holy Apples (Chakal Tapuchin Kadishin).
h:
Yaakov’s Fragrance as a Blessed Field
A "field" (an open, unbounded expanse) alludes to expansion in desires

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Toldot 10
p: אֲחִי רִבְקָה אֵם יַעֲקֹב וְעֵשָׂו.
The brother of Rebecca, the mother of Jacob and Esau.
הַיְינוּ כִּי הוֹדִיעַ יִצְחָק לְיַעֲקֹב כִּי כְּבָר נִשְׁלַם עַל יָדוֹ כָּל הַבֵּרוּרִים שֶׁבֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם,

That is, through this phrasing ("the mother of Jacob and Esau"), Isaac informed Jacob that all the separations and clarifications between Israel and the nations of the world had already been completed through him,
וּלְכָךְ לֹא יִהְיֶה מֵעַתָּה שׁוּם עֵסֶק בָּזֶה כִּי בָּנֶיךָ יִהְיוּ כֻּלָּם נִקְרָאִים בְּשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל,
and therefore from now on Jacob would have no further occupation with separating out unfit children, for all of his sons would be called by the name of Israel;
אַךְ עֲלֵיהֶם יֵשׁ בֵּרוּרִים הַיּוֹתֵר גְּדוֹלִים מֵאֵלּוּ בֵּין נַפְשׁוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל עַצְמָם לֵידַע אֵיזֶה מֵהֶם נִבְחָר
however, upon them would remain clarifications even greater than these—namely, discerning among the holy souls of Israel themselves to know which of them is chosen for leadership,
כִּי יֵשׁ הַרְבֵּה מַדְרֵגוֹת בָּהֶם,
because there are many distinct spiritual gradations among them;
וַאֲפִילּוּ לֶעָתִיד שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (יְשַׁעְיָה יוֹד אָלֶף, טֵית) "וּמָלְאָה הָאָרֶץ דֵּעָה",
and even in the ultimate future, concerning which it is stated (Isaiah 11:9), "For the earth shall be full of the knowledge of Hashem,"
אַף עַל פִּי כֵן נֶאֱמַר (יִרְמְיָהוּ לָמֶד אָלֶף, כָּף וָאו) "וְזָרַעְתִּי וְגוֹמֵר זֶרַע אָדָם וְזֶרַע בְּהֵמָה", שֶׁהֵם מַדְרֵגוֹת חֲלוּקוֹת,

nevertheless it is stated (Jeremiah 31:26), "And I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of man and with the seed of beast," indicating that there will still be distinct spiritual levels;
אַךְ מוֹרָא רַבּוֹ לֹא יִהְיֶה אָז, כִּי לֹא יְלַמֵּד אִישׁ אֶת רֵעֵהוּ,
only that the awe of one's human teacher will no longer exist then, for "they shall teach no more every man his neighbor" (Jeremiah 31:33),
אַךְ כָּל מַה שֶּׁיְּחַדֵּשׁ כָּל אֶחָד בְּדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה יוֹדִיעַ לַחֲבֵירוֹ בְּפָנִים שׂוֹחֲקוֹת,
rather, whatever novel insight each person innovates in words of Torah, he will share with his fellow with a radiant, smiling countenance,
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד יַעֲמוֹד מְבוֹרָר עַל חֶלְקוֹ בְּדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה הַשַּׁיָּיךְ לוֹ,
because each individual will stand clearly established in his own unique portion of Torah that belongs to the root of his soul;
וְהַרְבֵּה סָבַל יַעֲקֹב מֵאֵלּוּ הַבֵּרוּרִין וְזֶה הָיָה הָעִנְיָן בְּיוֹסֵף שֶׁהָיָה סָבוּר שֶׁהוּא הַנִּבְחָר.
and Jacob suffered greatly from these internal clarifications among his sons, and this was the core of the conflict regarding Joseph, who believed that he alone was the chosen one.

p: אֲחִי רִבְקָה וְכוּלֵי.
The brother of Rebecca, etc.
שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ יִצְחָק שֶׁיִּרְאֶה וְיָבִין כְּמוֹ שֶׁרָאָה בְּאִמּוֹ שֶׁבְּהוֹלָדָה אַחַת הוֹלִידָה טוֹב וָרַע,
Another explanation is that Isaac told Jacob to observe and understand: just as he saw regarding his mother Rebecca, that in a single birth she bore both good and evil (Jacob and Esau),
כְּמוֹ כֵן הֱוֵי זָהִיר בְּלָבָן שֶׁנִּמְצָא בּוֹ גַּם כֵּן מְעוֹרָב טוֹב וָרַע וְתִרְאֶה לְקַבֵּל רַק הַטּוֹב.
so too be vigilant with her brother Laban, within whom good and evil are likewise intermingled, and see to it that you extract and receive only the good.

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Toldot 12
p: וַיֵּלֶךְ עֵשָׂו אֶל יִשְׁמָעֵאל וַיִּקַּח אֶת מָחֲלַת וְכוּלֵי.
And Esau went unto Ishmael, and took Machalat to wife, etc.
וְאִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סָמֶךְ זַיִן, יוֹד גִּימֶל) מָחֲלַת מִכָּאן שֶׁמָּחַל לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עַל כָּל עֲוֹנוֹתָיו,
And it is stated in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 67:13): Why was she called "Machalat"? From here we learn that the Holy One, blessed be He, pardoned (machal) him for all his iniquities.
הָעִנְיָן בָּזֶה כִּי עֵשָׂו הָיָה אָפְיוֹ רְצִיחָה וְאָפְיוֹ שֶׁל יִשְׁמָעֵאל הוּא נִיאוּף,

The inner meaning of this is that Esau's innate disposition was bloodshed and murder (stemming from corrupted Gevurah), whereas Ishmael's disposition was sexual immorality and lust (stemming from corrupted Chesed);
וְהִנֵּה כָּל הַחֶסְרוֹנוֹת הַנִּמְצָאוֹת בָּעוֹלָם יֵשׁ בָּהֶם צַד טוֹב,
now behold, all negative traits found in the world possess a potential positive side:
כְּגוֹן שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַכַּעַס אַף שֶׁהוּא רַע מִכָּל מָקוֹם נִמְצָא בּוֹ צַד טוֹב כִּי יִכְעוֹס גַּם עַל עוֹבְרֵי רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.

for instance, the root of anger—even though it is bad, there is nevertheless a positive side to it, for a person with that trait can direct his anger against those who transgress the will of Hashem, blessed be He.
וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנִּיאוּף אַף שֶׁהוּא רַע מִכָּל מָקוֹם נִמְצָא בּוֹ צַד טוֹב,
And similarly the root of lust (corrupted love)—even though it is bad, there is nevertheless a positive side to it,
כִּי חֶסְרוֹן הַנִּיאוּף הוּא שֶׁמֵּיטִיב בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁאֵין רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְנִמְצָא בּוֹ צַד טוֹב כִּי לַטּוֹבִים מוּתָּר לְהֵיטִיב.

because the flaw of illicit desire is that one bestows love and goodness in a place contrary to the will of Hashem, blessed be He, yet it contains a positive aspect in that toward the righteous it is indeed proper to bestow love and goodness.
וְכַאֲשֶׁר הָלַךְ עֵשָׂו וְלָקַח אֶת בַּת יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֵּירֵר אֶת עַצְמוֹ שֶׁלֹּא נִמְצָא בּוֹ שׁוּם צַד טוֹב,
However, when Esau went and married the daughter of Ishmael, he clarified and exposed himself as having no positive side whatsoever,
כִּי הוּא כּוֹעֵס עַל צַדִּיקִים וּמְרַחֵם עַל רְשָׁעִים כִּי צֵירֵף שְׁנֵי הַחֶסְרוֹנוֹת יַחְדָּו,
for he raged with murderous anger against the righteous (Jacob) while showing love and affinity toward the wicked (Ishmael), thereby combining the worst of both flaws together!
וְזֶה פֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁמָּחֲלוּ לוֹ כָּל עֲוֹנוֹתָיו
And this is the true meaning of the statement that "all his iniquities were pardoned":
שֶׁלֹּא יוּצְרַךְ לְהַשְׁגִּיחַ עַל פְּרָטֵי חֲטָאָיו, מֵאַחַר שֶׁבֵּירֵר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ שׁוּם צַד טוֹב וְאֵין לוֹ חַיִּים כְּלָל,
namely, that Heaven no longer needed to keep an accounting of his individual sins, since he had demonstrated that he possessed no redeeming spark of goodness and had no share in eternal life at all—
דֶּרֶךְ מָשָׁל מִי שֶׁרוֹצֶה לִנְקוֹם מֵחֲבֵירוֹ זוֹכֵר כָּל מַה שֶּׁעָשָׂה לוֹ
by way of analogy, one who wishes to settle scores with his fellow carefully remembers every slight he committed against him,
אֲבָל כְּשֶׁרוֹאֶה שֶׁחֲבֵירוֹ מָרַד בַּמַּלְכוּת אָז הוּא מוֹחֵל לוֹ כֹּל, מֵאַחַר שֶׁאֵין לוֹ חַיִּים כְּלָל,
but when he sees that his fellow has committed high treason against the king and is condemned to death, he drops all petty claims and "forgives" him everything, since the man has no life left at all;
וְכֵן הָיָה הָעִנְיָן כָּאן שֶׁמָּחֲלוּ לוֹ עַל כָּל עֲוֹנוֹתָיו.
and such was the meaning here that they "pardoned" him for all his iniquities.

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Toldot 13
p: וַיֵּרָא אֵלָיו הַשֵּׁם וַיֹּאמֶר וְכוּלֵי גּוּר בָּאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת.
And Hashem appeared unto him, and said: Go not down into Egypt... sojourn in this land.
הָעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱסַר לְיִצְחָק לִנְסוֹעַ לְמִצְרַיִם וּלְאַבְרָהָם לֹא נֶאֱסַר,
The reason why Isaac was forbidden to travel down to Egypt during the famine whereas Abraham was not forbidden
כִּי יִצְחָק הָיָה צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת תָּמִיד בְּיִרְאָה וְלִהְיוֹת בְּצִמְצוּם,
is because Isaac's spiritual service required him to remain constantly in a state of awe (Yirah) and holy contraction (tzimtzum),
כִּי הִרְגִּישׁ שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִשְׁמוֹר עַצְמוֹ בָּזֶה כַּיָּדוּעַ,
for he sensed that he needed to guard himself in this regard, as is known,
וְלָכֵן נֶאֱסַר לוֹ לָצֵאת כִּי מִי שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְצִמְצוּם אָסוּר לוֹ לֵילֵךְ לְבַקֵּשׁ סִיבָּה לְפַרְנָסָה עַד שֶׁיַּזְמִין לוֹ הַשֵּׁם בְּבֵיתוֹ.

and therefore he was forbidden to depart from the Holy Land; because one whose soul requires contraction and restraint is forbidden to go out pursuing external avenues for livelihood until Hashem provides for him right in his own home.
[וְלִהְיוֹת בְּצִמְצוּם בַּאֲכִילָה, [
Specifically, Isaac needed to exercise contraction regarding physical eating,
לָכֵן אָמַר לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֵׁב בְּבֵיתְךָ וּתְצַפֶּה עַד אֶמְצָא לְךָ סִיבָּה לְפַרְנָסָה,
and therefore Hashem, blessed be He, told him: "Remain in your home and wait in trust until I provide an avenue of livelihood for you";
וּבִבְרִית הַמָּעוֹר הָיָה מוּגְדָּר מְאֹד לָכֵן לֹא הָיָה צָרִיךְ לְשׁוּם גֶּדֶר בָּזֶה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב "וְהִנֵּה יִצְחָק מְצַחֵק",

whereas regarding the covenant of sexual purity, Isaac was already completely fenced in andsanctified, so he required no extra external safeguard in that area, as it is written (Genesis 26:8), "And behold, Isaac was sporting with Rebecca his wife" (openly in Gerar);
אֲבָל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ הָיָה מוּגְדָּר בַּאֲכִילָה לָכֵן הוּתַּר לוֹ לַחְזוֹר אַחַר סִיבָּה לְפַרְנָסָה,

our father Abraham, however, was completely sanctified and detached regarding physical eating, and therefore he was permitted to travel to Egypt to pursue natural avenues of livelihood (while taking extra precautions regarding Sarah);
וְכֵן בְּכָל נֶפֶשׁ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל מִי שֶׁמַּכִּיר תְּכוּנַת נַפְשׁוֹ שֶׁהוּא מוּגְדָּר מוּתָּר לוֹ לִיסַּע מִמְּקוֹמוֹ וְלַחְזוֹר אַחַר סִיבָּתוֹ,

and the same applies to every soul in Israel: one who recognizes the disposition of his soul and knows that he is firmly guarded is permitted to travel from his place and pursue avenues of livelihood,
אָכֵן מִי שֶׁמַּכִּיר נִגְעֵי לְבָבוֹ שֶׁיּוּכַל לָבוֹא חָלִילָה לְהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת,
whereas one who recognizes the vulnerabilities of his own heart, knowing that traveling abroad might lead him, Heaven forbid, into unholy expansion,
זֶה צָרִיךְ לְהַמְתִּין עַל יְשׁוּעַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיַּזְמִין לוֹ בִּמְקוֹמוֹ וּבְבֵיתוֹ אֵיזֶה סִיבָּה. תַּשְׁלוּם.]
such a person must wait patiently for the salvation of Hashem, blessed be He, to prepare an avenue of sustenance for him right in his own place and home. End of addendum.
