Why Yitzchak Could Not Descend to Egypt
The reason why Isaac was forbidden to travel down to Egypt during the famine whereas Abraham was not forbidden

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayetzei 1
p: וַיֵּצֵא יַעֲקֹב מִבְּאֵר שָׁבַע וַיֵּלֶךְ חָרָנָה.
And Jacob departed from Beersheba and went toward Haran.
בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סָמֶךְ חֵית, אָלֶף)
In the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 68:1):
"שִׁיר לַמַּעֲלוֹת אֶשָּׂא עֵינַי אֶל הֶהָרִים מֵאַיִן יָבֹא עֶזְרִי",
"A Song for Ascents: I will lift up my eyes to the mountains; from where will my help come?" (Psalms 121:1)—
אֶשָּׂא עֵינַי אֶל הַהוֹרִים לְמַלְּפָנַי וְלִמְעַבְּדָנַי וְכוּלֵי
I will lift up my eyes to my parents (horim), to my teachers and those who formed me, etc.;
חָזַר וְאָמַר מַה אֲנָא מוֹבֵיד סִבְרִי מִן בָּרְיִי
then he reconsidered and said: Why should I lose my hope in my Creator?
לֵית אֲנָא מוֹבֵיד סִבְרִי מִן בָּרְיִי חַס וְשָׁלוֹם אֶלָּא "עֶזְרִי מֵעִם הַשֵּׁם".
I shall not lose my hope in my Creator, Heaven forbid, rather "my help is from Hashem, Maker of heaven and earth!"
הָעִנְיָן בָּזֶה כְּשֶׁיָּצָא יַעֲקֹב מִבְּאֵר שֶׁבַע וְלֹא הָיָה לוֹ לֶחֶם לֶאֱכוֹל וְלֹא שׁוּם דָּבָר
The inner meaning of this is that when Jacob departed from Beersheba penniless, having neither bread to eat nor anything else,
וְהוּצְרַךְ לֵילֵךְ אֶל לָבָן וְלַעֲסוֹק בַּצֹּאן לְמַעַן פַּרְנָסָתוֹ,
and was forced to go to Laban and tend sheep for his livelihood,
נָפַל דַּעְתּוֹ מְאֹד, לַאֲשֶׁר הִבִּיט וְרָאָה עַצְמוֹ קָטָן מְאֹד נֶגֶד אֲבוֹתָיו,
his spirits fell greatly, because he looked and saw himself as exceedingly small compared to his fathers (Abraham and Isaac);
כִּי הֵם לֹא הָיוּ צְרִיכִים כְּלָל לְהַבִּיט לְעִנְיְינֵי הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
for they had no need at all to concern themselves with the mundane affairs of this world,
וְהָיוּ עוֹסְקִים תָּמִיד בַּעֲבוֹדָה וּבְמַעֲשֵׂה מֶרְכָּבָה,
and were constantly immersed in divine service and the esoteric Account of the Chariot,
וְהוּא יִצְטָרֵךְ לַעֲסוֹק בִּדְבָרִים קְטַנִּים כָּאֵלּוּ,
whereas he would have to occupy himself with such petty, worldly matters;
חָזַר וְאָמַר לֵית אֲנָא מוֹבֵיד סִבְרִי מִן בָּרְיִי,
so he reconsidered and declared: "I shall not lose my hope in my Creator!"
הַיְינוּ אַף שֶׁהֵם הָיוּ בִּדְבָרִים גְּדוֹלִים וַאֲנִי רוֹאֶה אֶת עַצְמִי בִּדְבָרִים קְטַנִּים,
Meaning: even though they stood in lofty spiritual matters while I find myself immersed in small, mundane matters,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם גַּם בָּזֶה יֵשׁ עַבְדוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כִּי יוֹצֵר הַכֹּל הוּא.
nevertheless, within this too there is service of Hashem, blessed be He, for He is the Maker of all ("Maker of heaven and earth").
h:
Yaakov’s Journey from Beersheva to Charan
A Song for Ascents: I will lift up my eyes to the mountains; from where will my help come?" (Psalms 121:1)—

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayetzei 2
p: וַיֵּצֵא יַעֲקֹב.
And Jacob departed.
הָעִנְיָן שֶׁלֹּא הִתְפַּלֵּל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ תְּפִלַּת הַדֶּרֶךְ מִיָּד כְּשֶׁיָּצָא מִבְּאֵר שֶׁבַע
The reason why our father Jacob did not recite the Traveler's Prayer (Tefillat HaDerekh) immediately upon departing from Beersheba,
וְלָמָּה הִמְתִּין עַד כֹּה בִּתְפִלָּתוֹ, "אִם יִהְיֶה הַשֵּׁם עִמָּדִי וּשְׁמָרַנִי",
and why he waited until arriving at Bethel to offer his prayer, "If God will be with me and guard me on this way,"
כִּי זֶה הָיְתָה תְּפִלַּת הַדֶּרֶךְ שֶׁהִתְפַּלֵּל.
for that vow was indeed the Traveler's Prayer that he prayed—
אַךְ הָעִנְיָן בָּזֶה עַל פִּי מַה דְּאִיתָא בְּמַסֶּכֶת בְּכוֹרוֹת [נּוּן וָאו עַמּוּד אָלֶף]
the explanation of this is based on what is stated in Tractate Bekhorot (56a):
אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לָקַח עֲשָׂרָה עוּבָּרִין בִּמְעֵי אִמָּן כֻּלָּן נִכְנָסִין לַדִּיר לְהִתְעַשֵּׂר
Rabbi Assi said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: If one purchased ten animal fetuses while still in their mothers' wombs, they all enter the corral to be tithed;
וּפָרִיךְ הַגְּמָרָא וְהָא אֲנַן תְּנַן הַלָּקוּחַ וְשֶׁנִּיתַּן לוֹ בְּמַתָּנָה פָּטוּר מִמַּעֲשֵׂר
and the Gemara challenges this: But have we not learned in a Mishnah that a purchased animal or one given to a person as a gift is exempt from the animal tithe?
וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן חֲזַאי בְּחֶלְמָא מִילְּתָא מְעַלְּיָתָא אֲמֵינָא,
And Rabbi Elazar resolved this, saying: "I saw Rabbi Yochanan in a dream, which is a sign that I am about to state an excellent legal teaching:
"תַּעֲשֶׂה" כְּתִיב בִּשְׁעַת עֲשִׂיָּה,

Scripture writes 'you shall do (ta'aseh)' (Deuteronomy 14:22, regarding tithing), implying that the exemption of a purchased animal applies only when purchased after 'it is made' (i.e., after birth),"
הַיְינוּ שֶׁאִם מַעֲשֵׂה הַלְּקִיחָה הוּא בִּזְמַן חִיּוּב בְּמַעֲשֵׂר אָז פָּטוּר מִמַּעֲשֵׂר לְאַפּוּקֵי לָקַח בִּמְעֵי אִמָּן.

meaning that if the act of purchasing takes place at a time when the animal is already subject to tithing (after birth), then it is exempt as "purchased," to the exclusion of where one purchased them while still fetuses in their mothers' wombs.
וְזֶה הָעִנְיָן הָיָה גַּם כָּאן אֵצֶל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ,
And this very principle applied here as well regarding our father Jacob:
כִּי עַל זֹאת הַסְּבָרָא לֹא בָּא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר רַק כְּשֶׁרָאָה רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בַּחֲלוֹם,
for Rabbi Elazar (Eliezer) did not arrive at this subtle legal distinction until he beheld Rabbi Yochanan in a dream,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁאֵין לְהָבִין זֹאת רַק לְמִי שֶׁמַּרְאֶה לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִדּוֹת חֲנִינָה
meaning that this concept can only be grasped by one to whom the Holy One, blessed be He, reveals the attribute of grace (Chaninah),
כִּי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מוֹרֶה עַל חֲנִינָה, כִּדְאִיתָא בִּבְרָכוֹת [נּוּן זַיִן עַמּוּד אָלֶף] הָרוֹאֶה יוֹחָנָן וְכוּלֵי,
for the name "Yochanan" indicates divine grace, as is stated in Berakhot (57a): "One who sees Yochanan in a dream, miracles of grace will be wrought for him," etc.;
וְלָכֵן לֹא הָיָה יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ יָכוֹל לְהִתְפַּלֵּל תְּחִלָּה,
and therefore our father Jacob was unable to pray this prayer initially upon leaving Beersheba,
כִּי רָאָה בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ כָּל מַה שֶּׁיִּקְרֶה אוֹתוֹ בַּדֶּרֶךְ
because he foresaw through the Holy Spirit everything that would befall him on his journey,
וְהָיָה יוֹדֵעַ גַּם כֵּן שֶׁתְּפִלָּתוֹ יְסַיֵּם "וְכֹל אֲשֶׁר תִּתֶּן לִי עַשֵּׂר אֲעַשְּׂרֶנּוּ",
and he also knew that his prayer would conclude with the vow, "and of all that You give me, I will surely tithe a tenth to You";
וְהָיָה קָשֶׁה לוֹ קֻשְׁיָא הַנִּזְכֶּרֶת לְעֵיל כִּי הַלָּקוּחַ פָּטוּר מִמַּעֲשֵׂר
yet the aforementioned halakhic difficulty troubled him—namely, that purchased livestock is exempt from the animal tithe,
וְלָכֵן לֹא הָיָה יָכוֹל לְהִתְפַּלֵּל תְּפִלָּה הַלֵּזוּ,
and therefore he could not utter that prayer,
וְאֶצְלוֹ נֶאֱמַר (בְּרֵאשִׁית לָמֶד אָלֶף, מֵם אָלֶף) "עֲבַדְתִּיךָ שֵׁשׁ שָׁנִים בְּצֹאנֶךָ" וְאִם כֵּן הֲוֵי לָקוּחַ.

since regarding his flocks it is stated (Genesis 31:41), "I served you six years for your flock" (as wages, which is legally equivalent to a purchase), and if so, his sheep would be "purchased" and exempt from tithing!
רַק אַחַר שֶׁנִּרְאָה אֵלָיו הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּחֲלוֹמוֹ
Only after Hashem, blessed be He, appeared to him in his dream at Bethel—
וְאֵצֶל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ הָיָה נִקְרָא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אָז בְּתֹאַר חַנּוּן
where to our father Jacob, Hashem, blessed be He, was revealed specifically under the attribute of Gracious (Chanun),
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרֵאשִׁית לָמֶד גִּימֶל, הֵא) "הַיְלָדִים אֲשֶׁר חָנַן" וְכוּלֵי
as it is written (Genesis 33:5), "The children whom God has graciously given (chanan) your servant," etc.,
וְהַיְינוּ דְּאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן חֲזַאי בְּחֶלְמָא,
which corresponds to the Gemara's statement, "I saw Rabbi Yochanan (Grace) in a dream"—
עַל כֵּן יָדַע יַעֲקֹב מִילְּתָא חֲדַתָּא "תַּעֲשֶׂה" כְּתִיב בִּשְׁעַת עֲשִׂיָּה
therefore Jacob now grasped the novel legal insight that "you shall do (ta'aseh)" refers only to animals purchased after birth,
וְיַעֲקֹב קָנָה מִלָּבָן בִּמְעֵי אִמָּן קֹדֶם עֲשִׂיָּה כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּבֹאָר,
whereas Jacob acquired his flocks from Laban while they were still fetuses in their mothers' wombs prior to birth, as is explained in Scripture,
כִּי הִתְנָה עִמּוֹ עַל הַנּוֹלָדִים מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא שֶׁבָּא לוֹ בְּרָכָה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּמְעֵי אִמָּן וְחַיָּב בְּמַעֲשֵׂר,

for he stipulated with Laban regarding the speckled and spotted lambs that would be conceived and born from then on, receiving the blessing of Hashem, blessed be He, while still in their mothers' wombs, rendering them obligated in tithing;
וְכַאֲשֶׁר בָּא עַל זֶה הַטַּעַם אָז הָיָה יָכוֹל שַׁפִּיר לְהִתְפַּלֵּל "אִם יִהְיֶה אֱלֹקִים וְכוּלֵי וְכֹל אֲשֶׁר תִּתֶּן לִי" וְכוּלֵי.
and once he arrived at this legal reasoning through his dream, he was then well able to pray, "If God will be with me... and of all that You give me, I will surely tithe it to You."
h:
The Traveler’s Prayer and Divine Guidance
The reason why our father Jacob did not recite the Traveler's Prayer (Tefillat HaDerekh) immediately upon departing from Beersheba

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayetzei 3
p: וְהִנֵּה הַשֵּׁם נִצָּב עָלָיו.
And behold, Hashem was standing (nitzav) over him.
הִנֵּה זֹאת יָדוּעַ כִּי עִיקַּר הִתְגַּלּוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּעוֹלָם הוּא עַל יְדֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה הַיְינוּ עוֹלָם, שָׁנָה, נֶפֶשׁ.
Behold, it is known (from Sefer Yetzirah) that the primary revelation of Hashem, blessed be He, in the universe occurs through three dimensions: Space (Olam), Time (Shanah), and Soul (Nefesh).
עוֹלָם הוּא מְקוֹם הַמִּקְדָּשׁ אֲשֶׁר שָׁם הוּא הִתְגַּלּוּת אֱלֹקוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
"Space" (Olam) is the site of the Holy Temple, where the revelation of His Godliness, blessed be He, abides;
וְשָׁנָה הִיא בְּהַמֻּבְחָר שֶׁבַּזְּמַנִּים הוּא שַׁבָּת שֶׁבּוֹ נִמְצָא הִתְגַּלּוּת אֱלֹקוּתוֹ,
and "Time" (Shanah) is the choicest of times, namely Shabbat, wherein the revelation of His Godliness is found;
וְנֶפֶשׁ הוּא עַל נְפָשׁוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל יִתְגַּלֶּה שְׁכִינָתוֹ.
and "Soul" (Nefesh) refers to the souls of Israel, upon whom His Divine Presence (Shechinah) is revealed.
וְהִנֵּה כָּאן הָיוּ אֵלֶּה הַשְּׁלֹשָׁה בִּשְׁלֵימוּת,
And behold, here at Bethel all three of these converged in utter perfection:
מְקוֹם הַמִּקְדָּשׁ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "אֵין זֶה כִּי אִם בֵּית אֱלֹקִים",
the site of the Holy Temple, as it is stated, "This is none other than the House of God";
וְהַזְּמַן הַמֻּבְחָר כִּי בֶּטַח הָיָה הִתְגַּלּוּת הַזֹּאת בְּשַׁבָּת קֹדֶשׁ,
and the choicest of times, for this revelation certainly took place on the holy Shabbat;
וְנֶפֶשׁ הוּא יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ הַמֻּבְחָר שֶׁבַּנְּפָשׁוֹת שֶׁבּוֹ נִכְלְלוּ כָּל נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל
and the choicest of souls, namely our father Jacob, within whom all the souls of Israel were encompassed,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (יְשַׁעְיָה כָּף טֵית, כָּף גִּימֶל) "וְהִקְדִּישׁוּ אֶת קְדוֹשׁ יַעֲקֹב".
as it is written (Isaiah 29:23): "And they shall sanctify the Holy One of Jacob."
h:
Hashem Standing Over Yaakov
Behold, it is known (from Sefer Yetzirah) that the primary revelation of Hashem, blessed be He, in the universe occurs through three dimensions: Space (Olam…

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayetzei 4
p: וְהִנֵּה הַשֵּׁם נִצָּב עָלָיו.
And behold, Hashem was standing firmly (nitzav) over him.
זֶה הַפָּסוּק בְּעַצְמוֹ הוּא בְּרָכָה,
This clause in itself constitutes a divine blessing,
וּבֵיאֵר זֶה כְּמוֹ שֶׁקְּדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת הִיא קָבוּעַ וְקַיְימָא בְּלִי שׁוּם הַקְדָּשָׁה וְאִתְעֲרוּתָא מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
and he explained this: just as the holiness of Shabbat is permanently fixed and enduring without requiring any sanctification or awakening from below by Israel,
רַק מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּעַצְמוֹ הוּא קָדוֹשׁ,
being holy solely from the side of Hashem, blessed be He, Himself—
לֹא כְּיָמִים טוֹבִים שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל מְקַדְּשִׁין אוֹתָם,
unlike the Festivals, which depend upon Israel sanctifying them through the calendar—
כָּךְ הוּא קְדוּשַּׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ כִּקְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת,
so too is the holiness of our father Jacob like the holiness of Shabbat,
שֶׁקָּדוֹשׁ מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְשׁוּם אִתְעֲרוּתָא,
in that he is intrinsically holy from the side of Hashem, blessed be He, and requires no prior awakening from below;
וְעַל כֵּן לֹא נֶאֱמַר "עוֹמֵד עָלָיו" רַק "נִצָּב"
and therefore it does not state "standing (omed) over him" but rather "firmly stationed (nitzav) over him,"
כִּי "עוֹמֵד" מַשְׁמַע שֶׁעַתָּה עוֹמֵד עָלָיו וְלֹא מִקֹּדֶם וְהַיְינוּ מִכֹּחַ אִתְעֲרוּתָא דִּילֵיהּ,
because omed would imply that He is standing over him only now and not previously—namely, drawn down by virtue of Jacob's own awakening—
אֲבָל "נִצָּב" הַיְינוּ שֶׁתָּמִיד מְקֻשָּׁר עִמּוֹ.
whereas nitzav signifies that He is perpetually and immutably bound with him.
h:
The Blessing of Divine Presence
This clause in itself constitutes a divine blessing

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayetzei 5
p: וַיֹּאמֶר אֲנִי הַשֵּׁם אֱלֹקֵי אַבְרָהָם אָבִיךָ וְכוּלֵי.
And He said: "I am Hashem, the God of Abraham your father, and the God of Isaac."
אִיתָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית קוּף נּוּן עַמּוּד אָלֶף) אִיהוּ בְּאֶמְצָעוּתָא.
It is stated in the holy Zohar (Bereishit 150a): He (Jacob) stands in the center (harmonizing the two columns).
וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר "אָבִיךָ" גַּבֵּי אַבְרָהָם וְלֹא גַּבֵּי יִצְחָק,
And this explains why Scripture says "your father" regarding Abraham, and does not repeat "your father" regarding Isaac:
דְּהִנֵּה מִדּוֹת אַבְרָהָם הוּא מִדּוֹת אַהֲבָה וּמִדּוֹת יִצְחָק הוּא מִדּוֹת יִרְאָה
for behold, the attribute of Abraham is the attribute of Love (Chesed), and the attribute of Isaac is the attribute of Awe (Gevurah/Yirah);
וְהִנֵּה בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁהָאַהֲבָה בְּהַשְׁפָּעָה מְרֻבָּה מִצְטַמְצֵם מִדּוֹת הַיִּרְאָה
now, wherever Love flows in great abundance, the attribute of Awe is naturally contracted,
וְכֵן כְּשֶׁנִּמְצָא מִדַּת הַיִּרְאָה בִּשְׁלֵימוּת מִצְטַמְצֵם מִדּוֹת הָאַהֲבָה,
and similarly where the attribute of Awe is present in its fullness, the attribute of Love is contracted;
אֲבָל לְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם בְּמִשְׁקָל
however, within our father Jacob, peace be upon him, both of them existed in perfect equilibrium,
וְזֹאת נִקְרָא מִדּוֹת תִּפְאֶרֶת
and this synthesis is called the attribute of Tiferet (Beauty/Harmony),
וְהוּא מִדּוֹת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ כָּלוּל מִשְּׁנֵיהֶם וְאֵינָם סוֹתְרִים זֶה אֶת זֶה.
which is the attribute of our father Jacob, encompassing both of them together as one unified fatherhood so that they do not contradict one another at all.
h:
The God of Avraham and the God of Yitzchak
He (Jacob) stands in the center (harmonizing the two columns)

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayetzei 6
p: הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה שֹׁכֵב עָלֶיהָ לְךָ אֶתְּנֶנָּה.
The land upon which you lie, to you I will give it.
עִנְיַן הַבְּרָכָה הַזֹּאת הִיא שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ בִּשְׁעַת הַשְּׁכִיבָה וְהַשֵּׁינָה יִהְיוּ רַעְיוֹנוֹתֶיךָ בְּרוּרִים וּנְקִיִּים.
The inner meaning of this blessing is that even at the time of lying down and sleeping ("upon which you lie"), your thoughts and dreams shall remain clarified and pure.
"וְנִבְרְכוּ בְךָ כָּל מִשְׁפְּחוֹת" וְכוּלֵי,
"And all the families of the earth shall be blessed through you," etc.,
הַיְינוּ בְּדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁלְּךָ יְפָאֲרוּךָ כָּל הָאֻמּוֹת
meaning that through your words of Torah all the nations will glorify you,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (דְּבָרִים דָּלֶת, וָאו) "כִּי הִיא חָכְמַתְכֶם וּבִינַתְכֶם".
as it is written (Deuteronomy 4:6): "For it is your wisdom and your understanding in the eyes of the peoples."
"וְהִנֵּה אָנֹכִי עִמָּךְ",
"And behold, I (Anokhi) am with you"—
וְלֹא נֶאֱמַר "אֲנִי" כִּי אוֹת הַכָּ"ף מוֹרָה עַל מְקוֹר הַחַיִּים בְּלִי דַּי כִּדְאִיתָא בְּסֵפֶר יְצִירָה [פֶּרֶק דָּלֶת מִשְׁנָה אָלֶף לְגִירְסַת הָאֲרִיזַ"ל],

and it does not state "Ani," because the added letter Kaf in Anokhi indicates the boundless source of life, as is stated in Sefer Yetzirah (4:1, according to the version of the Arizal: the letter Kaf creates life);
וְהֶרְאָה לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אָז הַבֵּירוּרִין שֶׁיִּצְטָרֵךְ עוֹד לְהִתְבָּרֵר וְלִסְבּוֹל,
and the Holy One, blessed be He, showed him then the arduous clarifications and trials that he would still have to undergo and endure,
וְעַל זֶה הִבְטִיחַ לוֹ "וּשְׁמַרְתִּיךָ בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר תֵּלֵךְ וַהֲשִׁיבוֹתִיךָ אֶל הָאֲדָמָה הַזֹּאת",
and regarding this He promised him: "And I will guard you wherever you go, and I will bring you back (va'hashivotikha) to this land";
וַהֲשִׁיבוֹתִיךָ הוּא לְשׁוֹן הֲשָׁבַת אֲבֵידָה,
and the word va'hashivotikha is an expression of restoring a lost object (hashavat aveidah),
כִּי אֵין אָדָם עוֹמֵד עַל דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִכְשַׁל בָּהֶם (גִּיטִּין מֵם גִּימֶל עַמּוּד אָלֶף),
for "a person does not firmly grasp words of Torah unless he has first stumbled in them" (Gittin 43a),
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי עַל יְדֵי הַמִּכְשׁוֹל שֶׁבָּא לָאָדָם יִכָּנְסוּ הַדִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה בְּלֵב הָאָדָם בְּחֵשֶׁק גָּדוֹל יוֹתֵר מִמִּקֹּדֶם,
meaning that through the temporary stumbling or sense of loss that befalls a person, the words of Torah subsequently enter his heart with a far greater yearning than before,
וְזֶהוּ "וַהֲשִׁיבוֹתִיךָ" הַיְינוּ לְשׁוֹן תְּשׁוּבָה.
and this is the deeper meaning of "and I will bring you back" (va'hashivotikha)—namely, an expression of Teshuvah (repentance and spiritual return).
h:
The Land on Which Yaakov Lay
The inner meaning of this blessing is that even at the time of lying down and sleeping ("upon which you lie"), your thoughts and dreams shall remain clarifi…

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayetzei 7
p: שֵׁם הַגְּדֹלָה לֵאָה וְשֵׁם הַקְּטַנָּה רָחֵל.
The name of the elder was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.
אִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (קֹהֶלֶת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה זַיִן, גִּימֶל) שְׁלֹשָׁה שֵׁמוֹת יֵשׁ לָאָדָם,
It is stated in the Midrash (Kohelet Rabbah 7:3): A person has three names:
אֶחָד מַה שֶּׁקָּרְאוּ לוֹ אָבִיו וְאִמּוֹ,
one is that which his father and mother call him,
וְאֶחָד מַה שֶּׁקּוֹרְאִין לוֹ בְּנֵי אָדָם,
one is that which other people call him,
וְאֶחָד מַה שֶּׁקָּנָה לְעַצְמוֹ.
and one is that which he acquires for himself.
בֵּאוּר הָעִנְיָן, מַה שֶּׁקּוֹרְאִין לוֹ אָבִיו וְאִמּוֹ הַיְינוּ מַה שֶּׁנִּכָּר בְּצוּרַת הַוָּלָד מִיָּד כְּשֶׁהוּא נוֹלָד
The explanation of the matter is that what his father and mother call him reflects what is discernible in the form of the infant immediately upon birth—
מַה יִּהְיֶה חָכָם אוֹ טִפֵּשׁ עָצֵל אוֹ זָרִיז וְכַדּוֹמֶה,
whether his innate temperament will be wise or foolish, lazy or diligent, and the like;
כִּי בַּדּוֹרוֹת הָרִאשׁוֹנִים הָיְתָה זֹאת הַחָכְמָה מְפֹרֶשֶׁת בְּעֵינֵי כֹל,
for in the early generations this wisdom of physiognomy was clear before the eyes of all,
שֶׁהָיוּ מַכִּירִין בְּפַרְצוּף הַוָּלָד מַה שֶּׁיִּהְיוּ מִדּוֹת טִבְעוֹ,
such that they could recognize in the countenance of the newborn what his natural character traits would be,
וְזֶה גַּם כֵּן שֶׁהָיָה לָבָן קוֹרֵא לִבְנוֹתָיו שֵׁמוֹת כְּפִי שֶׁהָיָה מַכִּיר בְּטִבְעָם שֶׁל כָּל אַחַת.
and this is also how Laban named his daughters according to what he discerned in the innate nature of each one.
שֵׁם רָחֵל מוֹרֶה שֶׁאוֹחֶזֶת קִנְאָה וְנִצָּחוֹן בְּלִבָּהּ, וְאֵינָהּ מוֹצִיאָה בִּשְׂפָתֶיהָ
The name "Rachel" (ewe) indicates that even when she holds zeal and competitive drive in her heart, she does not utter a word with her lips,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (יְשַׁעְיָה נּוּן גִּימֶל, זַיִן) "וּכְרָחֵל לִפְנֵי גּוֹזְזֶיהָ נֶאֱלָמָה",
as it is written (Isaiah 53:7): "and like a ewe (rachel) before her shearers is dumb,"
וְהָיְתָה קִנְאָתָהּ לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב "וַתְּקַנֵּא רָחֵל בַּאֲחוֹתָהּ",
and her envy was purely for the sake of Heaven (envy of her sister's righteous deeds), as it is written, "And Rachel envied her sister";
וְשֵׁם לֵאָה הִיא לְשׁוֹן נִלְאָה שֶׁהָיְתָה תָּמִיד נִלְאָה וּצְמֵאָה לִישׁוּעוֹת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and the name "Leah" is an expression of weariness (nil'ah), for she was constantly weary with longing and thirsty for the salvations of Hashem, blessed be He.
עִנְיַן הַשֵּׁם שֶׁקּוֹרְאִין לוֹ בְּנֵי אָדָם הַיְינוּ מַה שֶּׁרוֹאִין עֲסָקָיו וְטִבְעוֹ בַּמֶּה הוּא מִשְׁתַּדֵּל.
The second name—that which other people call him—reflects what people observe of his habitual pursuits and nature, in what he exerts himself.
וְשֵׁם שֶׁקּוֹנֶה לְעַצְמוֹ הַיְינוּ מַה שֶּׁמְּתַקֵּן וּמְרַפֵּא הַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁלּוֹ אֲפִילּוּ הַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁנִּטְבַּע בּוֹ מִיּוֹם הִוָּלְדוֹ,
And the third name—that which he acquires for himself—is what he rectifies and heals of his own deficiencies, even the innate flaw stamped into his nature from the day he was born;
וְזֶה פֵּירוּשׁ הַפָּסוּק (מִשְׁלֵי גִּימֶל, חֵית) "רִפְאוּת תְּהִי לְשָׁרֶּךָ"
and this is the meaning of the verse (Proverbs 3:8): "It shall be healing to your navel (sharekha),"'
הַיְינוּ לְהַחִסָּרוֹן הַנִּמְצָא בּוֹ מִשְּׁעַת הִוָּלְדוֹ,
meaning healing for the congenital flaw found within him from the moment of his birth,
כִּי אִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (סוֹטָה מֵם הֵא עַמּוּד בֵּית) שֶׁתְּחִילַּת יְצִירָתוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם הוּא מִטַּבּוּרוֹ.
for it is stated in the Gemara (Sotah 45b) that the embryonic formation of a human being begins from his navel.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר יְשַׁעְיָה הַנָּבִיא [מֵם חֵית, חֵית] "וּפֹשֵׁעַ מִבֶּטֶן קֹרָא לָךְ",
And this is what Isaiah the prophet meant (Isaiah 48:8): "and you were called a transgressor from the womb"—
עַל כֵּן גָּדוֹל מַה שֶּׁקּוֹנֶה הוּא לְעַצְמוֹ,
therefore, greatest of all is the name that a person acquires for himself by overcoming his inborn nature,
כִּי מִלַּת שֵׁם בְּכָל מָקוֹם מוֹרֶה עַל שֹׁרֶשׁ הַחַיִּים, שֶׁכָּל הַנֶּפֶשׁ הוּא מְדוּגָּל בּוֹ.
for the word shem (name) everywhere indicates the root of vitality under whose banner the entire soul is arrayed.
h:
Leah and Rachel: Two Spiritual Paths
One is that which his father and mother call him

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayetzei 8
p: וַתֹּאמֶר הַפַּעַם אוֹדֶה אֶת הַשֵּׁם.
And she said, "This time I will praise Hashem."
אִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (מְגִילָּה וָאו עַמּוּד בֵּית) אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק
It is stated in the Gemara (Megillah 6b): Rabbi Yitzchak said:
אִם יֹאמַר לְךָ אָדָם יָגַעְתִּי וְלֹא מָצָאתִי אַל תַּאֲמִין
If a person says to you, "I have toiled and not found," do not believe him;
לֹא יָגַעְתִּי וּמָצָאתִי אַל תַּאֲמִין
if he says, "I have not toiled, yet I have found," do not believe him;
יָגַעְתִּי וּמָצָאתִי תַּאֲמִין.
"I have toiled and I have found"—believe him!
וְהִנֵּה בַּגְּמָרָא וַדַּאי לֹא בְּשׁוֹפְטָנֵי עָסְקִינַן
Now behold, the Gemara is certainly not dealing with obvious fools or liars;
שֶׁזֶּה הָאוֹמֵר יָגַעְתִּי וְלֹא מָצָאתִי אַיְירֵי שֶׁאָנוּ רוֹאִין שֶׁיָּגַע הַרְבֵּה וְלֹא מָצָא,
rather, when one says "I have toiled and not found," it speaks of a case where we ourselves see that he toiled greatly and yet did not find,
וְכֵן הָאוֹמֵר לֹא יָגַעְתִּי וּמָצָאתִי אַיְירֵי שֶׁאָנוּ רוֹאִין שֶׁלֹּא יָגַע וּמָצָא
and likewise when one says "I have not toiled and yet I found," it speaks of a case where we see with our own eyes that he did not toil then and yet found—
וְאִם כֵּן אֵיךְ שַׁיָּיךְ לֵאמֹר אַל תַּאֲמִין.
and if so, how is it possible to say "do not believe him"?
אַךְ עוֹמֶק הָעִנְיָן הוּא מְבוֹאָר בְּרָחֵל וּבְלֵאָה,
However, the depth of the matter is explained through Rachel and Leah:
כִּי בֶּטַח אִמֵּנוּ רָחֵל כַּמָּה תְּפִלּוֹת וְכַמָּה בַּקָּשׁוֹת בִּקְשָׁה שֶׁיּוֹשִׁיעַ לָהּ הַשֵּׁם,
for surely our mother Rachel offered countless prayers and supplications that Hashem grant her salvation with children,
אַךְ מִפְּנֵי זֶה לֹא הוֹעִיל לָהּ לְפִי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "וַתְּקַנֵּא רָחֵל בַּאֲחוֹתָהּ"
yet the reason her toil did not avail her at first is because it is stated, "And Rachel envied her sister,"
וְהוּצְרְכָה הַקִּנְאָה לְהִתְבָּרֵר אִם הִיא קִנְאַת סוֹפְרִים שֶׁהִיא לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם
and that trait of envy had to be clarified in action to prove whether it was the "envy of scholars," which is purely for the sake of Heaven,
אוֹ קִנְאָה בְּעָלְמָא כְּפִי דֶּרֶךְ הַטֶּבַע חַס וְשָׁלוֹם.
or mere worldly jealousy according to the way of nature, Heaven forbid.
וְהִנֵּה הִתְנַהֲגוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עִם הָאָדָם אֲשֶׁר בְּאוֹתָהּ הַטּוֹבָה שֶׁנָּתַן בְּהַמִּדָּה, בְּהַמִּדָּה הַזֹּאת עַצְמָהּ בָּרָא בּוֹ חֶסְרוֹן,

Now behold, the way of Hashem, blessed be He, in conducting a person is that within the very same character trait in which He placed a person's special goodness, He also created a corresponding vulnerability and deficiency,
עַל כֵּן לֹא יוּכַל הַטּוֹבָה לָצֵאת לַפֹּעַל קוֹדֶם שֶׁיִּתְרַפֵּא חֶסְרוֹנוֹ,
and therefore the goodness cannot emerge into actuality before its accompanying deficiency is healed;
וְקוֹדֶם שֶׁיִּתְרַפֵּא הַחֶסְרוֹן לֹא יוֹעִיל כַּמָּה תְּפִלּוֹת וְסִיגּוּפִים לְהָאָדָם עַד שֶׁיִּתְרַפֵּא חֶסְרוֹנוֹ וְאָז יִוָּשַׁע.
and prior to the healing of that specific flaw, no amount of prayers or fasts will avail the person, until he rectifies his deficiency—and then he is saved.
עַל כֵּן לְפִי שֶׁרָחֵל הוּצְרְכָה לְהִתְבָּרֵר בְּמִדּוֹת קִנְאָה
Therefore, because Rachel needed to be clarified in the attribute of envy,
וְקוֹדֶם שֶׁנִּתְבָּרְרָה בְּזֹאת לֹא הוֹעִיל לָהּ שׁוּם תְּפִלָּה וְכָל יְגִיעָתָהּ,
before she underwent clarification in this point, none of her prayers and all her spiritual toil availed her;
וְעַל כֵּן כַּאֲשֶׁר בִּקְשָׁה מִיַּעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ שֶׁיִּתְפַּלֵּל בַּעֲדָהּ חָרָה אַפּוֹ עָלֶיהָ.
and consequently, when she demanded of our father Jacob that he pray on her behalf ("Give me children, or else I die"), his anger burned against her.
וּלְהָבִין זֹאת כִּי הֲלֹא כַדִּין עָשְׂתָה,
Now to understand this—after all, did she not act properly according to the law,
כִּי מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ צָרָה בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ יֵלֵךְ אֵצֶל חָכָם (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קוּף טֵית זַיִן עַמּוּד אָלֶף) וְכֵן הִקְשָׁה הָרַמְבַּ"ן זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה.
which states that anyone who has distress in his house should go to a sage to pray for him (Bava Batra 116a), as the Ramban, of blessed memory, indeed asked?
אַךְ מֵחֲמַת שֶׁכָּתוּב קוֹדֶם "וַתְּקַנֵּא רָחֵל", עַל כֵּן וַיִּחַר לְיַעֲקֹב מֵחֲמַת שֶׁמִּקּוֹדֶם הָיְתָה צְרִיכָה לְהִתְבָּרֵר קִנְאָתָהּ,

However, because it is written immediately beforehand, "And Rachel envied her sister," Jacob was angered because her envy first needed to be clarified and rectified in action before prayer could help;
אַךְ כְּשֶׁאָמְרָה לְיַעֲקֹב "הִנֵּה אֲמָתִי לְפָנֶיךָ וְכוּלֵי וְאִבָּנֶה גַם אָנֹכִי מִמֶּנָּה",
yet once she said to Jacob, "Behold my maid Bilhah, go in unto her... that I also may be built up through her,"
מִזֶּה נִרְאָה שֶׁכַּוָּונָתָהּ הָיְתָה לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם שֶׁהֲרֵי הִכְנִיסָה צָרָתָהּ לְתוֹךְ בֵּיתָהּ.
from this selflessness it became clear that her envy was purely for the sake of Heaven, since she willingly brought her own rival into her house!
וְזֶה פֵּירוּשׁ יָגַעְתִּי וְלֹא מָצָאתִי אַל תַּאֲמִין אַף שֶׁאָנוּ רוֹאִין שֶׁיָּגַע אֶת עַצְמוֹ,
And this is the meaning of "I have toiled and not found—do not believe him": even though we see that he exerted himself greatly,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם לֹא הָיָה בְּמָקוֹם הָרָאוּי לְפָנָיו לְהִתְיַגֵּעַ
nevertheless, he was not toiling at the specific point where he needed to toil—
כְּאָדָם הָרוֹצֶה לִכָּנֵס לְבַיִת וְדוֹפֵק שֶׁלֹּא בִּמְקוֹם הַפֶּתַח אֲפִילּוּ יִדְפֹּק כָּל הַיּוֹם לֹא יוֹעִיל לוֹ,
like a person who wants to enter a house and knocks on the wall rather than at the door; even if he knocks all day long it will not avail him,
אֲבָל כְּשֶׁיָּבוֹא לִמְקוֹם הַפֶּתַח וְיִדְפֹּק אָז מִיָּד יִפָּתַח לוֹ.
whereas as soon as he comes to the place of the door and knocks, it is immediately opened for him.
וְלֹא יָגַעְתִּי וּמָצָאתִי, מוּבָן בְּלֵאָה,
And the second clause—"I have not toiled, yet I have found, do not believe him"—is understood through Leah:
כִּי כְּשֶׁיָּלְדָה אֶת יְהוּדָה אָמְרָה "הַפַּעַם אוֹדֶה אֶת הַשֵּׁם", לְפִי שֶׁלֹּא בִּקְשָׁה עַל זֶה,
for when she bore Judah, her fourth son, she said, "This time I will praise Hashem," because she had not prayed specifically for this fourth child,
כִּי כְּבָר נָטְלָה חֶלְקָהּ מִקּוֹדֶם כְּפִי הַחֶשְׁבּוֹן עַל אַרְבַּע אִמָּהוֹת וְנִרְאֶה כְּלֹא יָגַעְתִּי וּמָצָאתִי,
since she had already received her full share of three sons according to the division of twelve tribes among the four mothers, so Judah's birth appeared to be a case of "I did not toil, yet I found";
וְאֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא הַכֹּל בְּמִשְׁפָּט כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הֵעִיד עָלֶיהָ כִּי יָגְעָה אֶת עַצְמָהּ מְאֹד בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה בָּנִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים,

yet with Hashem, blessed be He, everything is done with exact justice, for Hashem, blessed be He, testified concerning her that she had toiled and suffered immensely prior to bearing her first three sons,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב "כִּי רָאָה הַשֵּׁם בְּעָנְיִי", "כִּי שָׁמַע הַשֵּׁם כִּי שְׂנוּאָה אָנֹכִי",
as it is written, "Because Hashem has seen my affliction," and "Because Hashem has heard that I am hated";
וְנָתַן לָהּ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֶת יְהוּדָה כְּאָדָם שֶׁנּוֹתֵן הֶכְרֵעַ לַחֲבֵירוֹ אִם לוֹקֵחַ מִמֶּנּוּ הַרְבֵּה,
and therefore Hashem, blessed be He, gave her Judah as an added measure, like a merchant who tips the scale with a generous bonus (hekhre'a) when a customer purchases a large quantity from him,
וְתוֹסַפְתּוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא הוּא מְרוּבָּה עַל הָעִיקָּר,
and the added bonus of the Holy One, blessed be He, is greater than the principal itself!
וְזֶהוּ יִקְרַת נֶפֶשׁ יְהוּדָה אֲשֶׁר גָּבַר בְּאֶחָיו כִּי כָּל הַגְּדוּלּוֹת יָצְאוּ מִמֶּנּוּ,
And this accounts for the surpassing preciousness of the soul of Judah, who prevailed among his brothers so that royalty and all greatness emerged from him,
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרָה "הַפַּעַם אוֹדֶה אֶת הַשֵּׁם",
and regarding this she declared, "This time I will praise Hashem,"
כִּי נֶפֶשׁ כָּזֶה לֹא יִוָּלֵד בְּכֹחַ וּבִשְׂכַר צִדְקוּת וְיוֹשֶׁר הָאָדָם רַק מִבִּרְכַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
because such a transcendent soul cannot be born merely by the power and earned reward of human righteousness and uprightness, but solely from the boundless blessing of Hashem, blessed be He;
כִּי כְּשֶׁיָּבוֹא מִכֹּחַ הָאָדָם אֵינוֹ בָּא רַק כְּפִי מַעֲשָׂיו,
for what comes by virtue of human effort comes only in proportion to one's finite deeds,
אֲבָל מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נוֹתֵן הֶכְרֵעַ מִצִּדּוֹ אָז הוּא בְּלִי שׁוּם גְּבוּל עַל כֵּן תּוֹסַפְתּוֹ מְרוּבָּה עַל הָעִיקָּר.
whereas what Hashem, blessed be He, bestows from His own side as a generous tipping of the scale is completely without limit, which is why His addition surpasses the principal.
וְעַל כֵּן נִכְתַּב עַל "וַתַּהַר עוֹד" שֶׁל שִׁמְעוֹן וְלֵוִי מוּנַּח זַרְקָא, עַל כִּי הֵם בָּאוּ לָהּ בִּיגִיעָתָהּ,

And for this reason, the cantillation notes written on the words "And she conceived again" (Vatahar od) regarding Simeon and Levi are Munach Zarka, indicating that they came to her through her own grounded toil,
אֲבָל עַל "וַתַּהַר עוֹד" עַל שֶׁל יְהוּדָא נָקוּד קַדְמָא וְאַזְלָא הַיְינוּ בְּלֹא יְגִיעָתָהּ וְהָבֵן.

whereas on "And she conceived again" regarding Judah, the cantillation is Kadma VeAzla (literally "preceding and flowing onward"), signifying that he came as a supernal flow beyond her immediate toil; understand this.
h:
Leah’s Gratitude and the Power of Praise
If a person says to you, "I have toiled and not found," do not believe him

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayetzei 9
p: וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָנוּ מִתְפַּלְּלִין בִּתְפִילַּת שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה "וְקוֹנֵה הַכֹּל וְזוֹכֵר חַסְדֵי אָבוֹת וּמֵבִיא גוֹאֵל לִבְנֵי בְנֵיהֶם לְמַעַן שְׁמוֹ".

And this is what we pray in the Shemoneh Esrei prayer: "Who acquires all, and remembers the pious deeds of the Patriarchs, and brings a redeemer to their children's children for the sake of His Name in love."
"וְקוֹנֵה הַכֹּל" הַיְינוּ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יֵשׁ לוֹ עֵסֶק עִם כָּל בְּרִיּוֹתָיו כִּי לֹא בָּרָא דָּבָר אֶחָד לְבַטָּלָה,
"Who acquires all" means that Hashem, blessed be He, is intimately involved with all His creations, for He did not create a single thing in vain;
"וְזוֹכֵר חַסְדֵי אָבוֹת" הַיְינוּ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ זוֹכֵר הַטּוֹב שֶׁהָיוּ הָאָבוֹת עוֹשִׂים בְּכָל כֹּחָם וּבְכָל נַפְשָׁם
"and remembers the pious deeds of the Patriarchs" means that Hashem, blessed be He, remembers the good that the Patriarchs performed with all their might and with all their soul,
וְהָיוּ מְקָרְבִים כָּל הָעוֹלָם לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְלֹא הָיוּ עוֹמְדִים רֶגַע בְּלֹא אַהֲבָה וְיִרְאָה,
drawing the entire world close to Hashem, blessed be He, and never standing for a single moment without love and awe of Him;
וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן "וּמֵבִיא גּוֹאֵל לִבְנֵי בְנֵיהֶם לְמַעַן שְׁמוֹ",
and nevertheless, He "brings a redeemer to their children's children for the sake of His Name"—
כִּי בִּזְכוּתָם אֵינוֹ כְּדַאי לְגַלּוֹת אוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מֶלֶךְ הַמָּשִׁיחַ רַק לְמַעַן שְׁמוֹ,
because finite human merit, even theirs, is not sufficient in itself to reveal the infinite light of the King Messiah, which comes rather "for the sake of His Name" as a boundless divine addition;
וְהַיְינוּ מַה דְּאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (סַנְהֶדְרִין קוּף עַמּוּד אָלֶף)
and this corresponds to what is stated in the Gemara (Sanhedrin 100a):
"הַנּוֹתֵן לֶעָנִי מְלֹא עוּמְסוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נוֹתֵן לוֹ מְלֹא עוּמְסוֹ לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא",
"Whoever gives to a poor man according to his full capacity in this world, the Holy One, blessed be He, gives to him according to His full capacity in the World to Come"—
וְהַיְינוּ מֵחֲמַת שֶׁהֵם מְיַגְּעִים אֶת עַצְמָם בְּכָל כֹּחָם, שֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה כְּבוֹד שָׁמַיִם עַל יָדָם,
meaning that because the Patriarchs exerted themselves to the absolute limit of their finite strength so that the glory of Heaven would be revealed through them,
עַל כֵּן מִדַּת הַדִּין נוֹתֶנֶת שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יְשַׁלֵּם לָהֶם כְּפִי כֹּחוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
the attribute of justice itself dictates that the Holy One, blessed be He, repay them according to His own infinite power, blessed be He.
h:
Remembering the Avos in the Amidah
Who acquires all" means that Hashem, blessed be He, is intimately involved with all His creations, for He did not create a single thing in vain

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayishlach 1
p: וַיָּבֹא יַעֲקֹב שָׁלֵם עִיר שְׁכֶם וַיִּחַן אֶת פְּנֵי הָעִיר.
And Jacob came whole to the city of Shechem... and he encamped before (vayichan et penei) the city.
פְּנֵי הָעִיר הַיְינוּ הַנִּכְבָּדִים שֶׁבָּעִיר וּמִי הָיוּ אָז פְּנֵי הָעִיר שְׁכֶם וַחֲמוֹר,
"The face (penei) of the city" refers to the prominent dignitaries of the city, and who were the dignitaries of the city then? Shechem and Hamor.
וּלְשׁוֹן וַיִּחַן הַיְינוּ שֶׁנָּשְׂאוּ חֵן בְּעֵינָיו
And the expression vayichan denotes that they found grace (chen) in his eyes;
וְהַיְינוּ דְּאִיתָא בְּכִתְבֵי הָאֲרִיזַ"ל [סֵפֶר הַגִּילְגּוּלִים פֶּרֶק נּוּן] כִּי שְׁכֶם נִתְגַּלְגֵּל אַחַר כָּךְ בְּזִמְרִי בֶּן סָלוּא בֶּן דִּינָה,

and this aligns with what is stated in the writings of the Arizal (Sefer HaGilgulim, ch. 50), that the soul-spark of Shechem subsequently reincarnated into Zimri son of Salu, a descendant of Dinah (through Simeon),
וְלָכֵן חָשְׁקָה נַפְשׁוֹ גַּם עַתָּה,
and therefore his soul longed for Dinah even now,
וְלָכֵן נֶאֱמַר "שְׁכֶם בְּנִי חָשְׁקָה" וְכוּלֵי הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא רָצָה לִישָּׂא אֶת בְּנוֹת הָאָרֶץ, רַק אֶת דִּינָה,
which is why it is stated, "My son Shechem longs for your daughter," etc., meaning that he had never wished to marry any of the daughters of the land, but desired only Dinah,
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁנָּשָׂא חֵן בְּעֵינֵי יַעֲקֹב כִּי הָיָה לוֹ מְעַט שַׁיָּיכוּת לְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ.
and this is why he initially found grace in Jacob's eyes, because he possessed a faint spiritual connection to our father Jacob.
h:
Yaakov Arrives Whole at Shechem
The face (penei) of the city" refers to the prominent dignitaries of the city, and who were the dignitaries of the city then? Shechem and Hamor

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayishlach 2
p: וַיַּעַל מֵעָלָיו אֱלֹקִים בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר אִתּוֹ.
And God went up from upon him in the place where He had spoken with him.

כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הֶרְאָה לוֹ שֶׁצָּרִיךְ עוֹד לְבֵירוּרִים [הַיְינוּ הַבֵּרוּרִים מִמְּכִירַת יוֹסֵף. תַּשְׁלוּם], [This phrasing indicates that Hashem, blessed be He, showed him that he still needed to undergo further clarifications
namely, the clarifications stemming from the sale of Joseph. End of addendum
,] וְזֶהוּ "וַיַּעַל מֵעָלָיו" כְּאִילּוּ עֲדַיִין צָרִיךְ לֶאֱחֹז בּוֹ.
and this is the meaning of "And God went up from upon him," implying that he still needed to strive to hold fast to Him.
"בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר אִתּוֹ", הַיְינוּ בְּאוֹתוֹ עִנְיָן עַצְמוֹ שֶׁהַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר בּוֹ בְּעֵסֶק מָמוֹן בָּזֶה צָרִיךְ עוֹד לְבֵירוּרִין, כִּי עוֹד לֹא נִשְׁלַם,

"In the place where He had spoken with him" means in that very same matter of which Scripture was speaking—namely, his dealings with money and property (and the vow of tithing at Bethel)—in this area he still required clarifications, as it was not yet complete;
וְעַל זֹאת הַכַּוָּונָה גַּם כֵּן נֶאֱמַר בְּאַבְרָהָם (בְּרֵאשִׁית יוֹד זַיִן, כָּף בֵּית) "וַיַּעַל אֱלֹקִים מֵעַל אַבְרָהָם",
and with this same intention it is likewise stated regarding Abraham (Genesis 17:22), "And God went up from upon Abraham" after the passage of circumcision,
אַחַר פָּרָשַׁת מִילָה שֶׁגַּם עַכְשָׁיו הָיָה צָרִיךְ לְבֵירוּרִין בְּנִסְיוֹן הָעֲקֵדָה
indicating that even then he still needed to undergo the ultimate clarification of the test of the Akeidah,
אַךְ שָׁם לֹא נֶאֱמַר "בַּמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר אִתּוֹ" כִּי לֹא הָיָה בְּעִנְיָן אֶחָד.
except that there it does not add "in the place where He had spoken with him," because Abraham's next test was not in the same subject matter.
h:
The Divine Ascent and the Clarification of Yosef’s Sale
Namely, the clarifications stemming from the sale of Joseph. End of addendum

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayishlach 3
p: וַיִּסַּע יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיֵּט אָהֳלֹה מֵהָלְאָה לְמִגְדַּל עֵדֶר.
And Israel journeyed, and pitched his tent beyond Migdal Eder (the Tower of the Flock).
הַיְינוּ כִּדְאִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ [רוּת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה בֵּית, זַיִן] אֲשֶׁר אַחַר כָּל הַרְפַּתְקָאוֹת שֶׁעָלוּ עַל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, מִיתַת רָחֵל הָיְתָה קָשָׁה עָלָיו מִכֻּלָּם,
That is, as is stated in the Midrash (Ruth Rabbah 2:7), that after all the tribulations that befell our father Jacob, peace be upon him, the death of Rachel weighed harder upon him than all of them;
וְהִנֵּה מִדַּרְכֵי הַצַּדִּיקִים וּבִפְרָט יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ לְהַחֲזִיק לִבּוֹ מְאֹד וְלֹא לְהַרְהֵר אַחַר מִדּוֹתָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁבְּוַדַּאי הַכֹּל הוּא לְטוֹבָה,

now behold, it is the way of the righteous, and especially our father Jacob, to strengthen his heart greatly and not question the attributes of the Holy One, blessed be He, trusting that everything is certainly for the good;
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר כָּאן אַחַר מִיתַת רָחֵל "וַיֵּט אָהֳלֹה מֵהָלְאָה לְמִגְדַּל עֵדֶר" הַיְינוּ שֶׁחִזֵּק אֶת לִבּוֹ שֶׁלֹּא לְהַרְהֵר אַחַר מִדּוֹתָיו,
and this is what is meant here immediately after the death of Rachel: "and he pitched his tent beyond Migdal Eder," meaning that he fortified his heart not to harbor any doubts after His attributes,
כִּי מִגְדַּל עֵדֶר שְׁנֵיהֶם לְשׁוֹן תַּקּוּפוּת הֵם,
for both words, Migdal (tower) and Eder (power/majesty, as in adir), are expressions of strength and fortitude,
וּבֶאֱמֶת הָיָה לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עוֹמֶק גָּדוֹל בְּמִיתַת רָחֵל כִּדְאִיתָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית קוּף עַיִן הֵא עַמּוּד אָלֶף).
and in truth Hashem, blessed be He, had a profound hidden purpose in the sudden death of Rachel on the road, as is stated in the holy Zohar (Bereishit 175a).
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "וַיְהִי בִּשְׁכֹּן יִשְׂרָאֵל", שְׁכֹן הַיְינוּ לְשׁוֹן נַיְיחָא שֶׁהָיָה בְּנַיְיחָא וְלֹא הִרְהֵר אַחַר מִדּוֹתָיו כְּלוּם,

And this is the meaning of the next verse, "And it came to pass, while Israel dwelt (bishkon) in that land"—shkon is an expression of tranquility and calm acceptance, indicating that he remained at peace and did not question His ways at all,
כִּי בָּטַח בַּהַשֵּׁם שֶׁיֵּשׁ עוֹמֶק בָּזֶה לְמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגָתוֹ,
because he trusted in Hashem that there was a depth in this far above his own comprehension;
וְאַחַר כָּךְ הֶרְאָה לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כִּי רָאוּי לוֹ לְבַקֵּשׁ מֵאִתּוֹ שֶׁיְּגַלֶּה לוֹ אֶת הָעוֹמֶק
yet afterward Hashem, blessed be He, showed him that it was fitting for him to pray and ask of Him to reveal that hidden depth to him—
כִּי זֹאת צָרִיךְ הָאָדָם לְבַקֵּשׁ, אַף שֶׁאָסוּר לְהַרְהֵר אַחַר מִדּוֹתָיו,
for this a person must indeed seek: even though it is forbidden to question His attributes,
[מִכָּל מָקוֹם צָרִיךְ לְבַקֵּשׁ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיַּרְאֶה לוֹ הָעוֹמֶק מַה שֶּׁחָפֵץ בָּזֶה,]
nevertheless one must beseech Hashem, blessed be He, to show him the inner depth of what He desires through this event,
כִּי דַּרְכֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁלֹּא לְהַעֲלִים שׁוּם דָּבָר מֵהַמְיַחֲלִים לְחַסְדּוֹ,
for it is the way of Hashem, blessed be He, not to conceal anything from those who hope for His lovingkindness;
וְזֶה הֶרְאָה לוֹ בְּמַעֲשֵׂה דִרְאוּבֵן,
and He signaled this to him through the incident of Reuben rearranging the beds,
וְאַחַר זֶה "וַיִּהְיוּ בְנֵי יַעֲקֹב שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר",
and immediately following that it is written, "Now the sons of Jacob were twelve"—
הַיְינוּ כִּי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא פָּתַח לוֹ סֵדֶר מִנְיַן הַשְּׁבָטִים אֵיךְ הוּא
meaning that the Holy One, blessed be He, unlocked for him the mystical order of the counting of the twelve tribes and how it now stood completed through Benjamin's birth and Rachel's passing;
כִּי נִמְצָא בְּכָל פַּעַם סֵדֶר אַחֵר לְמִנְיַן הַשְּׁבָטִים פַּעַם בְּכֹה וּפַעַם בְּכֹה,
for throughout Scripture we find a different sequence each time the tribes are enumerated—sometimes in this order and sometimes in that order—
וּבְכָל סֵדֶר יֵשׁ לִמּוּד בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ לְמִי שֶׁפּוֹנֶה עַצְמוֹ לְדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה
and within each specific arrangement lies an independent Torah teaching for one who turns his heart to words of Torah,
וְלָכֵן עַתָּה אַחַר מִיתַת רָחֵל בָּאוּ עַל הַסֵּדֶר הַלָּז.
and therefore now, following the death of Rachel, they were enumerated according to this particular sequence.
h:
Migdal Eder and the Hidden Destiny of Israel
That is, as is stated in the Midrash (Ruth Rabbah 2:7), that after all the tribulations that befell our father Jacob, peace be upon him, the death of Rachel…

Thus they are enumerated sixteen times in varying orders across their places in the Torah, and from each variation a distinct spiritual teaching is derived;
וּכְנֶגֶד זֶה סִדְּרוּ אַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה שִׁשָּׁה עָשָׂר שְׁבָחִים בֶּאֱמֶת וְיַצִּיב, וְהַמַּשְׂכִּיל יָבִין.

and corresponding to these sixteen arrangements, the Men of the Great Assembly instituted the sixteen expressions of affirmation and praise in the blessing of Emet VeYatziv ("True and firm, established and enduring..."), and the insightful person will understand.
h:
