The sixteen orders correspond to the praises of Emet VeYatziv

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayishlach 38
p: וְאֵלֶּה הַמְּלָכִים אֲשֶׁר מָלְכוּ בְּאֶרֶץ אֱדוֹם לִפְנֵי מְלָךְ מֶלֶךְ לִבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.
And these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom, before there reigned any king over the children of Israel.
בְּזוֹ הַפָּרָשָׁה הִתְחִיל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהַרְאוֹת הַבֵּרוּרִין הַדַּקִּין מְאוֹד שֶׁבֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לְאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם.
In this section the Holy One, blessed be He, began to reveal the exceedingly subtle clarifications and distinctions between Israel and the nations of the world.
כִּי קְלִיפַּת אֱדוֹם הִיא הַגְּדוֹלָה שֶׁבְּכוּלָּן, כִּי אֵין רַק הֶבְדֵּל דַּק מְאֹד בֵּינָהּ לְבֵין יִשְׂרָאֵל,
For the husk (kelippah) of Edom/Esau is the most formidable of them all, because there is only a hair's-breadth of outward distinction between it and Israel,
כִּי מִיָּד אַחַר חַיִּים שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל מַתְחִיל חַיִּים שֶׁל עֵשָׂו,
for immediately adjacent to the spiritual life-boundary of Israel begins the realm of Esau;
כִּי בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לְכָל אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם נִיכָּר הֶבְדֵּל וְהֶפְרֵשׁ גָּדוֹל
since between Israel and all the other nations of the world a vast difference and separation is readily apparent,
וַאֲפִילּוּ נֶגֶד יִשְׁמְעֵאלִים, אַף שֶׁהֵם זֶרַע אַבְרָהָם יֵשׁ הֶפְרֵשׁ גָּדוֹל כִּי מִצַּד אִמָּם אֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל.
and even compared to the Ishmaelites—although they are the seed of Abraham, there is a clear distinction because from their mother's side (Hagar) they have no shared lineage with Israel.
אֲבָל נֶגֶד עֵשָׂו לֹא נִיכָּר שׁוּם הֶבְדֵּל וְהֶפְרֵשׁ לָעַיִן, כִּי נִרְאִים כִּנְקִיִּים אַגַּב אִמָּן,
Against Esau, however, no external difference in lineage is visible to the eye, for both twins were born of the same holy womb and appear pure by virtue of their mother Rebecca,
וְרַק רְצוֹן הַבּוֹרֵא יִתְבָּרַךְ הָיָה שֶׁיַּעֲקֹב הוּא הַנִּבְחָר,
and it was solely the primordial will of the Creator, blessed be He, that Jacob is the chosen one;
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (מַלְאָכִי אָלֶף, בֵּית) "הֲלֹא אָח עֵשָׂו לְיַעֲקֹב" וְכוּלֵי,
and this is what is stated (Malachi 1:2): "Was not Esau Jacob's brother? says Hashem; yet I loved Jacob, and Esau I hated"—
אָח מַשְׁמַע שֶׁהָיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם שָׁוִים, וְהַיְינוּ בִּשְׁעַת זְרִיעָה שֶׁעֲדַיִין לֹא נִיכָּר שׁוּם מַעֲלָה בְּאֶחָד עַל חֲבֵירוֹ
the word "brother" implies that initially both were equal, namely at the moment of conception when no behavioral superiority was yet discernible in one over the other,
כִּי אָז לֹא נִמְצָא מִצְוֹת וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים גַּם לֹא חֵטְא וְעָוֹן, וּשְׁנֵיהֶם מִיִּצְחָק וְרִבְקָה,
for at that point there were neither mitzvot and good deeds nor sin and iniquity, and both stemmed equally from Isaac and Rebecca,
וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן "וָאֹהַב אֶת יַעֲקֹב וְאֶת עֵשָׂו שָׂנֵאתִי" וְהַיְינוּ רַק מֵרְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and nevertheless, "I loved Jacob, and Esau I hated," solely by virtue of His inscrutable divine choice, blessed be He,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (יְחֶזְקֵאל כָּף גִּימֶל, כָּף) "אֲשֶׁר בְּשַׂר חֲמוֹרִים בְּשָׂרָם וְזִרְמַת סוּסִים" וְכוּלֵי.
as it is written (Ezekiel 23:20): "whose flesh is the flesh of donkeys, and whose issue is the issue of horses," etc.
וְהוּא כִּי מִשְּׁעַת זְרִיעָה מְבָרֵר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁזֶּה טִיפָּה כְּשֵׁרָה שֶׁל קְדוּשָּׁה וְזֹאת הוּא זִרְמַת סוּסִים.

That is, from the very moment of seminal emission Hashem, blessed be He, separates and clarifies that this drop is a pure drop of holiness (Jacob), whereas that drop is spiritually coarse like the "issue of horses" (Esau).
וְהִנֵּה אַף כִּי עַל עֵשָׂו לֹא הָיָה נִיכָּר שׁוּם דָּבָר רַע, מִכָּל מָקוֹם נִמְשַׁל לַחֲזִיר (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יוֹד גִּימֶל, הֵא),
Now behold, even when nothing overtly wicked was yet recognizable on the surface of Esau, he was nevertheless compared to a swine (Vayikra Rabbah 13:5),
וְהַיְינוּ דְּאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (בְּכוֹרוֹת חֵית עַמּוּד אָלֶף) תַּפּוּחַ מְגַדֵּל לְשִׁשִּׁים יוֹם וּכְנֶגְדּוֹ חֲזִיר מוֹלִיד לְשִׁשִּׁים יוֹם

and this corresponds to what is stated in the Gemara (Bekhorot 8a): an apple ripens in sixty days from its blossoming, and corresponding to it in the animal kingdom, a swine gestates and gives birth in sixty days;
כִּי אוֹת סָמֶ"ךְ הוּא כְּעֵין קֶשֶׁת וְקֶשֶׁת הוּא מִבְטַח עוֹז,
for the number sixty (Samekh) is shaped like a closed circle or bow (keshet), and a bow represents mighty trust and reliance (mivtach oz),
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מִבְטַח עוֹז בְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵאַחַר שֶׁנּוֹלַד מִיִּצְחָק וּמֵרִבְקָה כְּמוֹ אָנוּ, כִּי יִשְׂרָאֵל נִמְשְׁלוּ לַתַּפּוּחַ,

meaning that Esau (the swine) boasts that he too possesses mighty trust and pedigree in Hashem, blessed be He, since he was born of Isaac and Rebecca in sixty just like us—for Israel is compared to the apple tree ("As an apple tree among the trees of the forest," Song of Songs 2:3)—
אַךְ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא הַמְּבָרֵר שֶׁזֶּה הוּא רַק גִּוּוּן, וְזֶה בֶּאֱמֶת דִּבּוּק בַּהַשֵּׁם.
yet Hashem, blessed be He, is the One Who clarifies that Esau's resemblance is merely an external veneer and pretension (gavvan), whereas Jacob is in truth cleaving to Hashem.
וּמִי שֶׁמַּשְׂכִּיל בִּשְׁמוֹת הַמְּלָכִים יוּכַל לִרְאוֹת זֹאת מְפוֹרָשׁ.
And whoever contemplates with insight the names of the kings of Edom listed here will be able to see this distinction clearly.
h:
The Kings of Edom Before Israel’s Kingship
In this section the Holy One, blessed be He, began to reveal the exceedingly subtle clarifications and distinctions between Israel and the nations of the wo…

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayeshev 1
p: וַיֵּשֶׁב יַעֲקֹב.
And Jacob dwelt.
זֶה שֶׁאָמַר הַכָּתוּב (יִרְמְיָה לָמֶד, יוֹד) "וְשָׁב יַעֲקֹב וְשָׁקַט וְשַׁאֲנַן וְאֵין מַחֲרִיד".
This is what Scripture states (Jeremiah 30:10): "And Jacob shall return, and shall be quiet and at ease, and none shall make him afraid."
"וְהָיָה אַחֲרֵי כֵן אֶשְׁפּוֹךְ אֶת רוּחִי וְכוּלֵי זִקְנֵיכֶם חֲלוֹמוֹת יַחֲלוֹמוּ בַּחוּרֵיכֶם חֶזְיוֹנוֹת יִרְאוּ" (יוֹאֵל גִּימֶל, אָלֶף).
"And it shall come to pass afterward, that I will pour out My spirit upon all flesh... your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions" (Joel 3:1).
הַיְינוּ כָּל הַמַּעֲשִׂים הַנַּעֲשִׂים בָּעוֹלָם נִרְאִים לְמַעֲשֵׂה בָּשָׂר וָדָם,
That is, all the actions performed in the world appear on the surface to be the doings of flesh and blood,
אַךְ מֵהַהִרְהוּר וְהַמַּחֲשָׁבָה נִרְאִים שֶׁהֵם מַעֲשֵׂה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
whereas inner reflections, dreams, and thoughts appear to come from the hand of Hashem, blessed be He.
וּבְאֵלּוּ הַפָּרָשִׁיּוֹת מְלַמֵּד אוֹתָנוּ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֲשֶׁר הַמַּעֲשִׂים הֵם מִיַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְהַמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת הֵם מִצַּד הָאָדָם

Yet in these Torah portions Hashem, blessed be He, teaches us the exact converse: that practical actions and events actually stem from the hand of Hashem, blessed be He, whereas thoughts and dreams stem from the side of man;
וְכָל הַמַּעֲשִׂים שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה הָאָדָם דְּבַר רְשׁוּת עַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר (בְּרָכוֹת לָמֶד גִּימֶל עַמּוּד בֵּית) כִּי הַכֹּל בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם.
and regarding all optional, mundane actions that a person performs, concerning this it is stated (Berakhot 33b) that "everything is in the hands of Heaven."
וּמַעֲשֵׂה הַמִּצְוֹת אוֹ הֵיפֶךְ הֵם בְּיַד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְרַק לִפְעָמִים יִתְלֶה אוֹתָם בָּאָדָם,
And even the performance of mitzvot or the opposite is ultimately orchestrated in the hand of Hashem, blessed be He, and only sometimes does He attribute them to man,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ (סוֹטָה יוֹד עַמּוּד בֵּית) עַל מַעֲשֵׂה יְהוּדָא הֵעִיד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ "צָדְקָה מִמֶּנִּי",
as we find (Sotah 10b) regarding the deed of Judah with Tamar, where Hashem, blessed be He, testified, "She is righteous; from Me (mimeni) this came forth,"
וְעַל הַחֲלוֹמוֹת שֶׁל יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק נֶאֱמַר שֶׁהֵם מֵהִרְהוּרָא דְּיוֹמָא,
whereas regarding the dreams of Joseph the Righteous it is stated that they stemmed from his daytime thoughts (hirhura d'yoma);
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת כֵּן הֵשִׁיבוּ אוֹתוֹ הַשְּׁבָטִים כַּאֲשֶׁר סִיפֵּר לָהֶם הַחֲלוֹם,
for in truth, this is precisely what the tribes (his brothers) answered him when he recounted the dream to them:
כִּי יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כַּאֲשֶׁר חָלַם לוֹ הַחֲלוֹם בַּהֲלִיכָתוֹ לְלָבָן הִתְחִיל לְעַיֵּין בּוֹ וְלָמַד אֶת עוֹמֶק הַנִּמְצָא בּוֹ לְכָל הַשְּׁבָטִים,

for when our father Jacob, peace be upon him, dreamed his prophetic dream of the ladder on his journey to Laban, he began to delve into it and taught the profound depths contained within it to all the tribes,
וְהֵם לָמְדוּ אוֹתוֹ וְנִתְחַדֵּשׁ לָהֶם בּוֹ בְּכָל פַּעַם דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה חֲדָשִׁים,
and they studied it, continually innovating new words of Torah within it at every turn,
כִּי כַּמָּה עַמְקוּת דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה נִמְצָא בְּהַחֲלוֹם הַזֶּה.
for immense depths of Torah are found within that dream.
וְכַאֲשֶׁר אָמַר לָהֶם יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק כִּי גַּם לוֹ חָלְמוּ חֲלוֹמוֹת כָּאֵלֶּה יְקָרִים, הֵשִׁיבוּ לוֹ, "הֲמָלוֹךְ תִּמְלוֹךְ עָלֵינוּ",
So when Joseph the Righteous told them that he too had dreamed such precious, prophetic dreams, they retorted to him, "Shall you indeed reign over us?"
כִּי אֵיךְ תִּדְמֶה לְאָבִינוּ הֲלֹא אָבִינוּ הוּא כָּל הַיּוֹם בְּיִרְאָה וְדָבוּק בְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
Meaning: "How can you compare yourself to our father? Behold, our father spends the entire day in awe and cleaving to Hashem, blessed be He,
וּלְכָךְ מַרְאֶה לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חֲלוֹמוֹת אַף בְּשֵׁינָה כִּי גַּם אָז הוּא דָּבוּק בְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and therefore Hashem, blessed be He, shows him true visions even in sleep, because even then he remains cleaving to Hashem, blessed be He!
אֲבָל אַתָּה אֵינְךָ בַּמַּדְרֵיגָה הַזֹּאת וְכָל חֲלוֹמוֹתֶיךָ הֵמָּה מֵהִרְהוּרָא דְּיוֹמָא
You, however, are not on that spiritual level, and all your dreams are merely the product of your own daytime thoughts—
שֶׁאַתָּה רוֹצֶה בִּגְדוּלָּה וּבְהִתְנַשְּׂאוּת וּלְכָךְ יַחֲלִים לְךָ חֲלוֹמוֹת כָּאֵלֶּה,
because you crave greatness and self-exaltation over us, and therefore your imagination conjures up such dreams for you!"
כִּי אֵין לְךָ גְּדוּלָּה מִמִּדּוֹת יִרְאָה וַעֲנָוָה, וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ הָיָה תָּמִיד עֲבוֹדָתוֹ בָּזֶה,
For there is no true greatness other than the attributes of awe (Yirah) and humility (Anavah), and our father Jacob's constant divine service was rooted in these two:
יִרְאָה הַיְינוּ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַשְׁגִּיחַ עַל הַכֹּל כְּדִכְתִיב (תְּהִלִּים לָמֶד גִּימֶל, יוֹד דָּלֶת) "מִמְּכוֹן שִׁבְתּוֹ הִשְׁגִּיחַ", וְ"לֹא יָנוּם" [שָׁם קוּף כָּף אָלֶף, דָּלֶת].

Awe is the constant awareness that Hashem, blessed be He, supervises everything, as it is written (Psalms 33:14), "From the place of His habitation He looks intently upon all the inhabitants of the earth," and "He neither slumbers nor sleeps" (Psalms 121:4).
וַעֲנָוָה הַיְינוּ שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִתְגָּאֶה עַל שׁוּם בְּרִיָּה כִּי מוֹתַר הָאָדָם מִן הַבְּהֵמָה אָיִן,
And humility means that he does not exalt himself over any creature, recognizing that "the preeminence of man over beast is naught (ayin)" (Ecclesiastes 3:19)—
לְשׁוֹן אַיִן הַיְינוּ אַף שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יֵשׁ חִילּוּק אַךְ מִצַּד הָאָדָם אֵין לְבָרֵר.
the word ayin signifying that although in truth from the side of Hashem, blessed be He, there is an immense distinction, from the side of mortal man's own perception it is impossible to verify.
וְזֶה "וַיֵּשֶׁב יַעֲקֹב בְּאֶרֶץ מְגוּרֵי אָבִיו" הַיְינוּ יִרְאָה (זוֹהַר בְּרֵאשִׁית קוּף פֵּא עַמּוּד אָלֶף) וְ"בְּאֶרֶץ כְּנָעַן" הוּא עֲנָוָה,

And this is the meaning of "And Jacob dwelt in the land of the sojournings (megurei) of his father"—megurei denoting awe and fear (as in the Zohar, Bereishit 180a)—and "in the land of Canaan (Kena'an)," which denotes submissive humility (hakhna'ah);
וּבִקֵּשׁ לֵישֵׁב בְּשַׁלְוָה, זֹאת הַשַּׁלְוָה הַיְינוּ, כִּי כְּשֶׁאָדָם מַנְהִיג אֶת עַצְמוֹ לְהִסְתַּלֵּק מִכָּל סָפֵק וְלִשְׁמוֹר מִכָּל מַעֲשֵׂה רַע אָז הוּא בְּשַׁלְוָה,

and through these two attributes "Jacob sought to dwell in tranquility" (Rashi)—this tranquility meaning that when a person conducts himself by withdrawing from every doubtful situation and guarding himself from any questionable deed, he enjoys spiritual serenity;
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כִּי בְּעוֹד הָאָדָם בַּגּוּף אֵין בְּאֶפְשָׁר לְהִתְנַהֵג בְּכָל כָּךְ שְׁמִירָה וְיִרְאָה וַעֲנָוָה,

and regarding this Hashem, blessed be He, said to him that as long as a person is clothed in a physical body in this world, it is impossible to conduct oneself exclusivamente with such passive guardedness, awe, and withdrawal,
כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חָפֵץ בַּמַּעֲשִׂים שֶׁל הָאָדָם כִּי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה צָרִיךְ לְהִתְנַהֵג בְּאַהֲבָה, וּמַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁאֵינָהּ מְבוֹרֶרֶת כָּל כָּךְ,

because Hashem, blessed be He, desires the active deeds of man, for in this world one must also act through the attribute of Love and engage in practical actions whose outcome is not yet entirely clarified;
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר לֶעָתִיד "וְשָׁב יַעֲקֹב" לְשׁוֹן "נַפְשִׁי יְשׁוֹבֵב" בְּתַעֲנוּג מִמַּחְשְׁבוֹת דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה.

and only regarding the ultimate future is it stated, "And Jacob shall return (veshav)"—an expression of "He restores (yeshovev) my soul" (Psalms 23:3) with pure delight in the contemplation of words of Torah:
"וְשָׁקַט" הַיְינוּ מַדְרֵגַת שַׁבָּת "וְעָמְדוּ זָרִים וְרָעוּ צֹאנְכֶם".
"and shall be quiet"—attaining the level of eternal Shabbat, when "strangers shall stand and feed your flocks" (Isaiah 61:5);
"וְשַׁאֲנַן" הַיְינוּ בְּמַחְשָׁבָה מִבְּלִי לִירֹא מִמִּלְחָמוֹת וּמְאוֹרָעוֹת.
"and at ease"—in his mind, without having to fear wars and worldly upheavals;
"וְאֵין מַחֲרִיד" הַיְינוּ אַף בְּשֵׁינָה יִהְיֶה דָּבוּק בְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְלֹא יָרֵא פֶּן הוּא חַס וְשָׁלוֹם נָסוֹג מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
"and none shall make him afraid"—meaning that even in sleep he will remain completely cleaving to Hashem, blessed be He, without any fear lest he, Heaven forbid, slip away from Hashem, blessed be He.
וְזֶה הָיָה טַעֲנוֹת הַשְּׁבָטִים עַל יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק, כִּי גַּם הוּא הָיָה מִתְנַהֵג אֶת עַצְמוֹ בְּמִדּוֹת הַיִּרְאָה
And this was the critique of the tribes against Joseph the Righteous: for he too conducted himself strictly according to the attributes of awe and guardedness,
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה פֵּא דָּלֶת, חֵית) שֶׁהָיָה זִיו אִיקוֹנִין דּוֹמֶה לוֹ,
concerning which it is stated in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 84:8) that the radiance of Joseph's countenance resembled Jacob's,
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהֶעֱמִיק עַצְמוֹ לִשְׁתֵּי מִדּוֹת הַלָּלוּ יִרְאָה וַעֲנָוָה כְּדֵי שֶׁיֵּלֵךְ בֶּטַח,
meaning that he immersed himself deeply in these two attributes of awe and humility so that he might walk in complete spiritual security;
וְלָזֶה נֶאֱמַר עָלָיו "כִּי בֶן זְקוּנִים הוּא לוֹ",
and for this reason it is stated of him, "for he was the son of his old age (zekunim) to him,"
הַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁיַּעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ הִתְנַהֵג עַצְמוֹ בְּמִדַּת יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ הַיְינוּ יִרְאָה גַּם הוּא הִתְנַהֵג עַצְמוֹ בְּהַמִּדָּה הַזֹּאת, וּבַעֲנָוָה כְּמוֹ אָבִיו.
meaning that just as our father Jacob conducted himself in the attribute of his father Isaac, namely awe, so too did Joseph conduct himself in that attribute, as well as in humility like his father.
וְעַל זֶה דִּקְדֵּק עִמּוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ גַּם כֵּן עַד כְּחוּט הַשַּׂעֲרָה
And because Joseph relied on his own meticulous self-guarding, Hashem, blessed be He, was exacting with him to a hair's breadth:
כִּי אַף שֶׁהַמִּדּוֹת הַלָּלוּ טוֹבִים, מִכָּל מָקוֹם צָרִיךְ הָאָדָם לִבְטוֹחַ בַּהַשֵּׁם גַּם כֵּן, כִּי הַנַּעֲשֶׂה מִצַּד הָאָדָם אֵינוֹ בִּנְיַן עֲדֵי עַד.

for even though these attributes are good, a person must nevertheless cast his trust upon Hashem rather than relying on his own guardedness, because whatever is built from the finite side of man is not an eternal edifice!

כִּי אַף שֶׁיּוֹסֵף פָּעַל בִּשְׁמִירָתוֹ מְאֹד, אֲשֶׁר מִמֶּנּוּ יָצְאוּ כָּל מַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הַנִּקְרָאִים גְּדוֹלִים כִּדְאִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ [שָׁם אוֹת יוֹד טֵית] שַׂק נָהוּג בִּבְנֵי אָדָם גְּדוֹלִים שֶׁהֲרֵי יְהוֹרָם לָבַשׁ שַׂק,

For although Joseph accomplished tremendously through his personal sanctity and guardedness, to the extent that from him emerged all the kings of the ten tribes of Israel who are called "great men"—as is stated in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 84:19) that sackcloth is worn by great men, since King Jehoram wore sackcloth—
אַךְ נֶאֱמַר עֲלֵיהֶם (מְלָכִים אָלֶף יוֹד אָלֶף, לָמֶד טֵית) "אַךְ לֹא כָל הַיָּמִים".
nevertheless, regarding the kingship of Joseph's house versus David's house it is stated (I Kings 11:39), "yet not forever (not all the days)."
הַיְינוּ כִּי בִּנְיַן עֲדֵי עַד אֵינוֹ שַׁיָּיךְ לְחֶלְקָם רַק לְחֵלֶק יְהוּדָא,
That is, an eternal edifice does not belong to the portion of Joseph, but solely to the portion of Judah;
כִּי אַף שֶׁעַל כָּל הַשֵּׁשֶׁת אֲלָפִים שָׁנָה פָּעַל בְּצִדְקוֹ שֶׁיַּעֲמוֹד בָּעוֹלָם, אַךְ בִּנְיַן עֲדֵי עַד זֶה שַׁיָּיךְ לִיהוּדָא.
for even though Joseph accomplished through his righteousness that his merit endures throughout the six thousand years of this world, the eternal edifice beyond time belongs exclusively to Judah.
וְיוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק הָיָה תָּמִיד בְּתַרְעוֹמוֹת מַדּוּעַ כָּל מַעֲשֵׂה יְהוּדָא אָחִי אֲשֶׁר עוֹשֶׂה הַשֵּׁם מַצְלִיחַ בְּיָדוֹ, וְעִמִּי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְדַקְדֵּק עַד כְּחוּט הַשַּׂעֲרָה.

And Joseph the Righteous constantly wondered in his heart: "Why is it that in every deed my brother Judah does—even when it appears questionable—Hashem makes it prosper in his hand, whereas with me the Holy One, blessed be He, is exacting to a hair's breadth?"
וְהֶרְאָה לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ דּוּגְמָא בַּמַּעֲשֶׂה דְּשַׂר הַמַּשְׁקִים וְהָאוֹפִים,
So Hashem, blessed be He, showed him a living parable through the incident of the Chief Butler and the Chief Baker in prison:
הַיְינוּ לְכָל מֶלֶךְ יֵשׁ שְׁנֵי שָׂרִים שַׂר הַמַּשְׁקֶה וְשַׂר הָאוֹפֶה
namely, every king has two ministers, a Chief Butler and a Chief Baker;
וּבֶאֱמֶת לְשַׂר הַמַּשְׁקֶה, מֵהָרָאוּי לְבַל לְהַעֲנִישׁ אוֹתוֹ אִם יִמָּצֵא זְבוּב בְּכוֹסוֹ,
and in truth, regarding the Chief Butler, it is fitting not to punish him severely if a fly is found in the king's cup (Rashi, Genesis 40:1),
כִּי מֶה הָיָה יָכוֹל לַעֲשׂוֹת, כִּי הַזְּבוּב הוּא בַּעַל חַי וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהִשָּׁמֵר מִמֶּנָּה פֶּן בְּעֵת נָתְנוֹ הַכּוֹס עַל כַּף הַמֶּלֶךְ אָז פָּרְחָה לְתוֹךְ הַכּוֹס.

for what could he have done? Since a fly is a living, flying creature, it is impossible to guard against it completely, as it may have flown into the cup at the very instant he placed it into the king's palm.
אֲבָל שַׂר הָאוֹפִים, לַאֲשֶׁר בַּפַּת הַנִּמְצָא בָּהּ צְרוֹר הֲלֹא עָלָיו הָאָשָׁם, כִּי הַצְּרוֹר אֵינוֹ בַּעַל חַי וְיוּכַל לְהִשָּׁמֵר מִזֶּה,

Regarding the Chief Baker, however, when a pebble is found baked inside the royal bread, the blame rests squarely upon him, because a pebble is not a living creature that flies in on its own, and he could have sifted the flour and guarded against it!
לָזֹאת הֶרְאָה לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כִּי יוֹסֵף הוּא נֶגֶד שַׂר הָאוֹפִים
Through this Hashem, blessed be He, showed Joseph that he corresponds to the Chief Baker:
כִּי אוֹתוֹ הֶעֱמִיד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל מָקוֹם בָּהִיר וְנָקִי נֶגֶד עֵשָׂו בִּכְדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה לְעֵשָׂו שׁוּם מְקוֹם טַעֲנָה,
for Hashem, blessed be He, stationed Joseph in a place of crystal clarity and purity as the direct adversary of Esau, so that Esau would have no grounds for accusation whatsoever;
הֶעֱמִיד אֶת יוֹסֵף נֶגְדּוֹ מְנוּקֶּה מִכֹּל כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (עוֹבַדְיָה אָלֶף, יוֹד חֵית) "וּבֵית יוֹסֵף לֶהָבָה",
He stationed Joseph opposite him cleansed of all dross, as it is written (Obadiah 1:18), "and the house of Joseph shall be a flame,"
וְנָתַן בּוֹ כֹּחַ כְּדֵי שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהִתְגַּבֵּר עַל כָּל תַּאֲוָתוֹ,
endowing him with the innate strength to completely master all his desires;
וְלָכֵן אִם נִמְצָא בּוֹ אֵיזֶה דָּבָר מִחוּץ, לְפֶשַׁע יֵחָשֵׁב לוֹ,
and therefore, if even the slightest foreign pebble of a flaw is found in him, it is reckoned as a willful transgression on his part—
אַךְ מֵאַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְיוֹסֵף נָתַן אָדָם תַּחְתָּיו וְנֶהֱרַג שַׂר הָאוֹפִים כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (יְשַׁעְיָה מֵם גִּימֶל, דָּלֶת) "וְאֶתֵּן אָדָם תַּחְתֶּיךָ", וּמִזֶּה הֵבִין הַדָּבָר.

except that out of Hashem's love for Joseph, He gave another man in his stead as an atonement, and the Chief Baker was executed, fulfilling the verse (Isaiah 43:4), "and I will give men in your stead," and from this Joseph understood the matter.

וִיהוּדָא הוּא נֶגֶד שַׂר הַמַּשְׁקֶה כִּי דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם נִקְרָא בָּדְחָנָא דְּמַלְכָּא (זוֹהַר שְׁמוֹת קוּף זַיִן עַמּוּד אָלֶף) וְעַל נִיסּוּךְ הַיַּיִן נִשְׁמָעִין שִׁירֵי דָּוִד,

Judah, on the other hand, corresponds to the Chief Butler (who pours the wine), for his descendant King David, peace be upon him, is called "the Jester of the King" (Zohar Shemot 107a), and over the wine-libations on the Altar the songs of David were sung;

וּבֶאֱמֶת לִיהוּדָא בְּמַעֲשֵׂה דְּתָמָר וְכֵן בְּכָל הַמַּעֲשִׂים מִשֵּׁבֶט יְהוּדָא הַדּוֹמִין לָזֶה נָתַן בָּהֶם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כֹּחַ הַתַּאֲוָה כָּל כָּךְ עַד שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בְּאֶפְשָׁרוּתָם לְהִתְגַּבֵּר

and in truth, regarding Judah in the incident of Tamar—as well as in all similar episodes involving the tribe of Judah (such as David and Bathsheba)—Hashem, blessed be He, implanted such an overwhelming force of desire in that moment that it was humanly impossible for them to overcome it,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמְּבוֹאָר (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה פֵּא הֵא, טֵית) שֶׁמַּלְאָךְ הַמְמוּנֶּה עַל הַתַּאֲוָה הִכְרִיחוֹ,
as is explained in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 85:8) that the angel appointed over desire compelled Judah against his will,
וְלָכֵן לֹא עָלָיו הָאָשָׁם בְּמַה שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה יָכוֹל לְהִתְגַּבֵּר עַל יִצְרוֹ,
and therefore the blame did not rest upon him for being unable to conquer his inclination (just like the fly flying into the butler's cup);
וְזֶה פֵּירוּשׁ בָּדְחָנָא דְּמַלְכָּא הַיְינוּ שֶׁמַּנִּיחַ אֶת עַצְמוֹ לְהִנָּצֵחַ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
and this is the deep meaning of "the Jester of the King": namely, one who humbles himself and allows himself to be "defeated" by Hashem, blessed be He, so that God's hidden design may prevail,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם (תְּהִלִּים נּוּן אָלֶף, וָאו) "לְמַעַן תִּצְדַּק בְּדָבְרֶיךָ" לְמִי נָאֶה שֶׁיּוּצְדַּק אֲנִי אוֹ אַתָּה.

as King David, peace be upon him, declared (Psalms 51:6), "Against You, You only, have I sinned... so that You may be justified in Your words"—as if to say: "For whom is it fitting to be vindicated as righteous, me or You? Surely You!"
h:
Yaakov’s Tranquility and Yosef’s Dreams
This is what Scripture states (Jeremiah 30:10): "And Jacob shall return, and shall be quiet and at ease, and none shall make him afraid

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayeshev 2
p: וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (יְשַׁעְיָה יוֹד אָלֶף, יוֹד גִּימֶל) "אֶפְרַיִם לֹא יְקַנֵּא אֶת יְהוּדָא וִיהוּדָא לֹא יָצוֹר אֶת אֶפְרָיִם",
And this is the meaning of what is stated regarding the future redemption (Isaiah 11:13): "Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not harass Ephraim";
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת אֵלּוּ הַשְּׁנֵי שְׁבָטִים הֵם תָּמִיד מִתְנַגְּדִים זֶה לָזֶה,
for in truth, throughout history these two tribes stand in constant opposition to one another:
כִּי עִנְיַן הַחַיִּים שֶׁנָּתַן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּשֵׁבֶט אֶפְרַיִם הוּא לְהַבִּיט תָּמִיד בְּכָל דְּבַר מַעֲשֶׂה עַל הַדִּין וְהַהֲלָכָה מִבְּלִי לָזוּז מִמֶּנּוּ,

for the spiritual mode of life that the Holy One, blessed be He, implanted within the tribe of Ephraim (Joseph) is to look constantly in every practical matter at the strict letter of the law and formal Halakhah, without budging an inch from it;
וְלָכֵן כְּשֶׁהַכָּתוּב מַזְהִיר אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְבִלְתִּי יֶחֶטְאוּ, מַטְּרַת הַתּוֹרָה אָז יֹאמַר (עָמוֹס הֵא, וָאו) "פֶּן יִצְלַח כָּאֵשׁ בֵּית יוֹסֵף",
and therefore, when Scripture warns Israel not to sin against the boundary of the Torah, it states (Amos 5:6), "lest the house of Joseph break out like fire,"
הַיְינוּ שֶׁתִּרְאוּ כִּי לֹא יִהְיֶה מִתְנַגֵּד לְמַעֲשֵׂיכֶם,
meaning: see to it that the strict halakhic standard of Joseph's house will have no cause to oppose your deeds!
וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַחַיִּים שֶׁל יְהוּדָא הוּא לְהַבִּיט תָּמִיד לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּכָל דְּבַר מַעֲשֶׂה
Whereas the root of the spiritual life of Judah is to look constantly toward Hashem, blessed be He, Himself in every single action;
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁרוֹאֶה הַאֵיךְ הַדִּין נוֹטֶה עִם כָּל זֶה מַבִּיט לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיַּרְאֶה לוֹ עוֹמֶק הָאֱמֶת בְּהַדָּבָר,
so that even though he sees which way the formal law inclines, he nevertheless looks yearningly to Hashem, blessed be He, to show him the inner depth of truth in the matter;

כִּי יוּכַל לִהְיוֹת אַף שֶׁהַדִּין אֱמֶת הוּא לְפִי טַעֲנוֹת בַּעֲלֵי דִּינִים, אַךְ אֵינוֹ לַאֲמִיתּוֹ כִּי פֶּן יִטְעוֹן אֶחָד טַעֲנָה שִׁקְרִית כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ (נְדָרִים כָּף הֵא עַמּוּד אָלֶף) בְּקַנְיָא דְּרָבָא,

for it can happen that although a legal ruling is technically correct based on the claims presented by the litigants, it is not true to the ultimate reality because one party is empleying a deceptive trick, as we find (Nedarim 25a) in the case of the hollow reed filled with coins before Rava,
וּכְמוֹ כֵן נִמְצָא בְּכָל עִנְיָנִים,
and the same dynamic exists across all spiritual matters;
וְזֹאת הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַחַיִּים שֶׁל יְהוּדָא לְהַבִּיט לַהַשֵּׁם בְּכָל דָּבָר וְלֹא לְהִתְנַהֵג עַל פִּי מִצְוַת אֲנָשִׁים מְלוּמָּדָה
and this is the root of Judah's vitality: to look directly to Hashem in every situation and not act by rote habit ("a commandment of men learned by rote"),
אַף שֶׁעָשָׂה אֶתְמוֹל מַעֲשֶׂה כָּזוֹ מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַיּוֹם אֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה לִסְמוֹךְ עַל עַצְמוֹ, רַק שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יָאִיר לוֹ מֵחָדָשׁ רְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
so that even if he performed a certain deed yesterday, today he refuses to rely on his own past precedent, praying instead that Hashem, blessed be He, illuminate His will anew for him right now—
וְעִנְיָן הַזֶּה יְחַיֵּיב לִפְעָמִים לַעֲשׂוֹת מַעֲשֶׂה נֶגֶד הַהֲלָכָה כִּי עֵת לַעֲשׂוֹת לַהַשֵּׁם וְכוּלֵי.

and this responsiveness sometimes compels one to perform an action that appears to step outside the formal Halakhah, under the principle, "It is a time to act for Hashem, they have voided Your Torah" (Psalms 119:126).
וְלָזֶה אֵלּוּ הַשְּׁנֵי שְׁבָטִים מִתְנַגְּדִים זֶה לָזֶה,
And because of this, these two tribes clash with one another in this world;
וְלֶעָתִיד נֶאֱמַר "אֶפְרַיִם לֹא יְקַנֵּא וְכוּלֵי וִיהוּדָא לֹא יָצוֹר" וְכוּלֵי,
yet regarding the future era it is stated, "Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not harass Ephraim,"
הַיְינוּ שֶׁלְּאֶפְרַיִם לֹא יִהְיֶה טַעֲנָה עַל יְהוּדָא בַּמֶּה שֶׁיּוֹצֵא חוּץ לַהֲלָכָה וְלֹא יֵצַר לוֹ מִזֶּה
meaning that Ephraim will no longer harbor any grievance against Judah when Judah steps beyond the strict boundary of the law, nor will it distress him,
כִּי יַרְאֶה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְאֶפְרַיִם אֶת כַּוָּונַת יְהוּדָא שֶׁהוּא מְכַוֵּון לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם וְלֹא לַהֲנָאַת עַצְמוֹ וּמִמֵּילָא יִהְיֶה שָׁלוֹם בֵּינֵיהֶם.

because Hashem, blessed be He, will openly reveal to Ephraim the pure heart of Judah—that his intention is solely for the sake of Heaven and never for his own self-gratification—and consequently there will be complete peace between them.
h:
Ephraim and Yehudah in the Future Redemption
For in truth, throughout history these two tribes stand in constant opposition to one another

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayeshev 3
p: וַיֵּשֶׁב יַעֲקֹב בְּאֶרֶץ מְגוּרֵי אָבִיו בְּאֶרֶץ כְּנָעַן.
And Jacob dwelt in the land of the sojournings of his father, in the land of Canaan.
הִנֵּה בְּזֹאת הַסִּדְרָה הִתְחִיל לְבָרֵר הַבֵּרוּרִין שֶׁבֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל,
Behold, in this Torah portion begins the process of clarifying the internal distinctions among the souls of Israel themselves:

דְּהִנֵּה אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה שׁוֹרְשׁוֹ מִדּוֹת אַהֲבָה הַיְינוּ שֶׁהָיָה מְבָרֵר כָּל אֲהָבוֹת שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם שֶׁלֹּא יֶאֱהַב שׁוּם דְּבַר עוֹלָם הַזֶּה זוּלַת רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,

for behold, our father Abraham, peace be upon him, had his root in the attribute of Love, meaning that he refined and clarified all forms of love in the world so as not to love any worldly thing except the will of Hashem, blessed be He;
וְיִצְחָק הָיָה מְבוֹרָר בְּזֹאת הַמִּדָּה כִּי הוּא נוֹלַד מֵאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ אַחַר כָּל הַבֵּרוּרִים שֶׁבֵּרֵר אֶת עַצְמוֹ.
and Isaac was already born fully clarified in that attribute of Love, since he was born from our father Abraham after all the clarifications through which Abraham had refined himself.
וּמִדָּתוֹ הָיְתָה רַק לְבָרֵר מִדּוֹת הַיִּרְאָה הַיְינוּ לְבָרֵר כָּל הַיִּרְאוֹת שֶׁלֹּא יִרָא מִשּׁוּם גָּוֶון רַק מֵהַשֵּׁם לְבַדּוֹ,
Thus Isaac's task was solely to clarify the attribute of Awe—namely, to refine all forms of fear so as not to fear anything in any manner except Hashem alone;
וְאֵצֶל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ הָיוּ אֵלּוּ הַשְּׁנַיִם מְבוֹרָרִים הֵיטֵב,
and within our father Jacob, both of these attributes were already thoroughly clarified,
אַךְ כָּל עֲסָקָיו הָיָה מִדּוֹת תִּפְאֶרֶת, הַיְינוּ בְּרִיחַ הַתִּכוֹן לְסַדֵּר הַיִּרְאָה לִמְקוֹמָהּ וּבְעוֹנָתָהּ וְכֵן הָאַהֲבָה.

so that his entire occupation was the attribute of Tiferet (Harmony), which is the "middle bar" (Exodus 26:28) that harmonizes and orders Awe in its proper place and time, and likewise Love in its proper place and time.

וְהִנֵּה בִּימֵי אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לֹא יָצָא מְפוֹרָשׁ עוֹמֶק יִקְרַת אוּמָּה יִשְׂרְאֵלִית וְכֵן בִּימֵי יִצְחָק וְלָכֵן הָיוּ צְרִיכִין לְהִתְבָּרֵר מִמִּדּוֹת הָאוּמּוֹת וּלְהַפְרִישׁ עַצְמָם מִכֹּחָם,

Now in the days of our father Abraham, peace be upon him, the full depth of the preciousness of the nation of Israel had not yet emerged into actuality, and similarly in the days of Isaac, and therefore their children still needed to be sifted out from the traits of the nations (Ishmael and Esau) and separated from their forces;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר שִׁבְטֵי יְשׁוּרֻן שֶׁכֻּלָּם מַתְאִימוֹת וְאֵין בָּהֶם שׁוּם נְטִיָּה מֵרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
whereas our father Jacob, peace be upon him, merited the twelve tribes of Yeshurun, all of whom were whole and harmonious without any deviation from the will of Hashem, blessed be He,
רַק עֲסָקָיו הָיָה בָּהֶם עַצְמָם לְבָרֵר אֵיזֶה מֵהֶם מוּקְדָּם וְאֵיזֶה מֵהֶם מְאוּחָר,
so that his occupation was solely among the holy tribes themselves, to clarify which of them takes precedence in kingship and leadership and which follows;
וְהִנֵּה גַּם מִזֶּה סָבַל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ, כִּי הָיָה סָבוּר שֶׁיּוֹסֵף הוּא הַמּוּבְחָר וְגַם יוֹסֵף סָבוּר כֵּן
and behold, our father Jacob suffered great anguish from this clarification as well, because he thought that Joseph was the chosen leader of the tribes, and Joseph likewise thought so,
וְאֵלּוּ הֵם בֵּרוּרִין דַּקִּין בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל עַצְמָם כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּתְבָּאֵר.
and these are the exceedingly subtle clarifications between the souls of Israel themselves, as will be explained.
h:
Yaakov Dwells in the Land of Canaan
Behold, in this Torah portion begins the process of clarifying the internal distinctions among the souls of Israel themselves

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayeshev 4
p: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוּדָא אֶל אֶחָיו מַה בֶּצַע וְכוּלֵי.
And Judah said to his brothers, "What profit (mah betza) is it if we slay our brother and conceal his blood?"
אִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (סַנְהֶדְרִין וָאו עַמּוּד בֵּית) כָּל הַמְּבָרֵךְ אֶת יְהוּדָא נִקְרָא בּוֹצֵעַ.

It is stated in the Gemara (Sanhedrin 6b): "Whoever praises Judah for saying 'mah betza' is a blasphemer, concerning whom it is said, 'And the covetous (botze'a) reviles and blasphemes Hashem' (Psalms 10:3)."
הָעִנְיָן בָּזֶה דְּהִנֵּה אִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (נְדָרִים לָמֶד בֵּית עַמּוּד בֵּית) בְּשַׁעְתָּא דְּיֵצֶר הָרַע לֵית מַאן דְּמַדְכַּר לְיֵצֶר טוֹב,
The inner meaning of this is based on what is stated in the Gemara (Nedarim 32b): "At the hour when the evil inclination dominates, there is no one who remembers the good inclination";
וְהוּא כְּשֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חָפֵץ לְנַסּוֹת אֶת הָאָדָם אָז מְשַׁכֵּחַ מִמֶּנּוּ כָּל חוֹמֶר הָאִיסּוּר מֵהַדָּבָר שֶׁרוֹצֶה לְנַסּוֹתוֹ בּוֹ,
meaning that when Hashem, blessed be He, wishes to test a person, He causes him to momentarily forget the entire severity of the prohibition of the matter in which He is testing him;
וְזֶה גַּם כֵּן הָיָה עִנְיַן הַשְּׁבָטִים כַּאֲשֶׁר רָצוּ לְהָרְגוֹ אָז נֶעְלַם מֵהֶם כָּל הָאִיסּוּר

and this was also what happened to the tribes when they wanted to execute Joseph: in that moment of spiritual trial, the prohibition of bloodshed was completely concealed from their awareness (as they judged him a pursuer),
וְרַק בְּעֵצוֹת זוּלַת דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה נִיצַּל מִיָּדָם וְגַם הֵם נִיצּוֹלוּ מֵעָוֹן,
and it was only through pragmatic counsel outside of formal words of Torah that Joseph was rescued from their hands and they themselves were saved from iniquity!
כִּי יְהוּדָא הָיָה חָכָם גָּדוֹל בְּחָכְמוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה עַל כֵּן זָמַם עֵצָה וְאָמַר "מַה בֶּצַע"
For Judah possessed great practical wisdom in the ways of this world, and therefore he devised a pragmatic argument and said, "What profit is there?"—
פֵּירוּשׁ אַף שֶׁהָיָה נִרְאֶה לוֹ שֶׁמִּצַּד הַדִּין מוּתָּר לְהָרְגוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁיִּתְבָּאֵר אַךְ מָה הֲנָאָה יַגִּיעַ לָנוּ מִזֶּה.
meaning: even though it appears to us that according to the strict law it is permissible to execute him, as will be explained, yet what practical benefit will accrue to us from killing him?
[וְכִי יִתֵּן לִי אָבִי הַכְּתוֹנֶת פַּסִּים, הֲלֹא עִנְיַן הַכְּתוֹנֶת פַּסִּים שַׁיָּיךְ רַק לְיוֹסֵף. תַּשְׁלוּם.] [
Will our father give me thefine woolen tunic (ketonet passim) if Joseph is dead? Surely the spiritual aspect of the ketonet passim belongs uniquely to Joseph! End of addendum.
] וְכִי בִּשְׁבִיל זֶה יֹאהֲבֶנּוּ אָבִינוּ בְּיוֹתֵר,
And will our father love us any more because of this?
וּמִיָּד כְּשֶׁהוּסְכַּם בֵּינֵיהֶם שֶׁלֹּא יַהַרְגוּ אוֹתוֹ רָאוּ חוֹמֶר הָאִיסּוּר שֶׁאָסוּר לְהָרְגוֹ מִצַּד הַדִּין גַּם כֵּן,

And the moment they agreed among themselves not to kill him on account of this practical argument, the veil lifted and they saw the severity of the prohibition—that it was forbidden to kill him according to the law as well!
וְזֹאת הָעֵצָה שֶׁעַל פִּי חָכְמַת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה אָסוּר לְאָדָם שֶׁיָּגֵן עִמָּהּ בַּעֲדוֹ בְּכָל עֵת רַק בְּעֵת הַנִּסָּיוֹן שֶׁאֵין עֵצָה אַחֶרֶת,

Now, regarding such a pragmatic stratagem based on worldly logic ("what profit is there in sinning?"), a person is forbidden to use it as his standard shield against sin at all times—it may be used only in a moment of blinding temptation when no other counsel avails;
אֲבָל לִפְרוֹשׁ מֵאִיסּוּר בָּעֵת שֶׁזּוֹכֵר שֶׁהַדָּבָר אָסוּר, אָסוּר לוֹ לִפְרוֹשׁ אֶת עַצְמוֹ עַל פִּי עֵצָה כָּזֹאת רַק מֵחֲמַת פְּקוּדָּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.

whereas when one is in his right mind and remembers that the deed is forbidden by God, it is forbidden to abstain from sin merely out of pragmatic calculation ("what profit is there?"), rather one must abstain solely out of reverence for His decree, blessed be He.
וְזֶה פֵּירוּשׁ הַגְּמָרָא כָּל הַמְבָרֵךְ אֶת יְהוּדָא הַיְינוּ שֶׁיָּשָׁר הַדָּבָר בְּעֵינָיו לַעֲשׂוֹת תָּמִיד כֵּן נִקְרָא בּוֹצֵעַ

And this is the meaning of the Gemara: "Whoever praises Judah"—meaning whoever considers it proper to always refrain from sin by asking "what profit (betza) is in it?"—is called a botze'a (a self-serving calculator),
כִּי יְהוּדָא גַּם כֵּן לֹא לָקַח לוֹ עֵצָה הַזֹּאת בִּלְתִּי בִּשְׁעַת הַנִּסָּיוֹן.
for Judah himself only employed this tactic in that acute hour of blinding trial.
h:
Yehudah Asks: What Profit in Yosef’s Death?
Whoever praises Judah for saying 'mah betza' is a blasphemer, concerning whom it is said, 'And the covetous (botze'a) reviles and blasphemes Hashem' (Psalms…

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayeshev 5
p: לְכוּ וְנִמְכְּרֶנּוּ לַיִּשְׁמְעֵאלִים.
Come, and let us sell him to the Ishmaelites.
לֶהֱיוֹת כִּי הַשְּׁבָטִים דָּנוּ אוֹתוֹ תְּחִילָּה לְמִיתָה מֵחֲמַת שֶׁהֵבִיא אֶת דִּבָּתָם רָעָה אֶל אֲבִיהֶם
Since the tribes initially judged Joseph liable to death because "he brought their evil report unto their father,"
וְהַחֵטְא הַזֶּה הָיָה נֶחְשָׁב בְּעֵינֵיהֶם לְחֵטְא בְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ חַיָּיו חָלִילָה, כִּי הָיָה מַפְרִיד בֵּינָם לְבֵין אֲבִיהֶם
this sin was considered in their eyes a fatal blemish in the very root of his soul, Heaven forbid, because he was driving a wedge between them and their father,
וְהָיָה נִרְאֶה בְּעֵינָם כְּמַפְרִיד הַיִּחוּד שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עִם כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
which appeared in their eyes as severing the sacred union of the Holy One, blessed be He, with the Congregation of Israel;
כִּי יַעֲקֹב הָיָה אָז הַצַּדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם שֶׁהָעוֹלָם נִשְׁעָן עָלָיו, וְהָיָה בִּמְקוֹם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְהֵם הָיוּ כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל,

for Jacob was then the "Righteous One, Foundation of the World," upon whom the universe rested, standing in the place of Hashem, blessed be He, in this world, while the tribes constituted the entirety of the Congregation of Israel—
כִּי בְּתֵיבַת אֶחָד שֶׁבִּשְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל הָיוּ כּוּלָּם נִכְלָלִים, כִּי אָלֶ"ף הוּא נֶגֶד יַעֲקֹב, וְהַחֵי"ת נֶגֶד שְׁמוֹנָה בְּנֵי הַגְּבִירוֹת, וְדָלֶ"ת נֶגֶד אַרְבָּעָה בְּנֵי הַשְּׁפָחוֹת,

for within the word Echad (אֶחָד — "One") of Shema Yisrael they were all encompassed: the letter Alef (1) corresponds to Jacob, the letter Chet (8) corresponds to the eight sons of the matriarchs Rachel and Leah, and the letter Dalet (4) corresponds to the four sons of the handmaids Bilhah and Zilpah—
וּכְפִי דַּעְתָּם הָיָה רְצוֹנוֹ לְהַפְרִיד הַיִּחוּד הַלָּזֶה,
and according to their assessment, Joseph was seeking to disrupt this sacred unity!
רַק יְהוּדָא אָמַר בְּחָכְמָתוֹ שֶׁאֵין הַמִּשְׁפָּט מְבוֹרָר כָּךְ כִּי אוּלַי הוּא טוֹב וְרַק אָנוּ טוֹעִין בּוֹ,
Judah alone said in his wisdom that the judgment was not so clear-cut, for "perhaps he is truly righteous in his root and it is we who are mistaken regarding him!"
עַל כֵּן יָעַץ אוֹתָם שֶׁיִּמְכְּרוּ אוֹתוֹ, הַיְינוּ שֶׁאָנוּ לֹא נַעֲשֶׂה לוֹ בְּיָדֵינוּ שׁוּם דָּבָר רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יְבָרֵר אוֹתוֹ
Therefore he advised them to sell him to the Ishmaelites—meaning: "Let us not do anything to him with our own hands; rather, let Hashem, blessed be He, clarify his true nature!
וְאִם הוּא טוֹב בְּשׁוֹרְשׁוֹ אָז בְּוַודַּאי גַּם מִמִּצְרַיִם יַצִּילֶנּוּ הַשֵּׁם מִכָּל חֵטְא וְלֹא יִדַּח מִמֶּנּוּ נִדָּח,
And if he is genuinely pure in his root, then even down in the depravity of Egypt Hashem will surely save him from all sin, and 'no outcast will be cast out from Him' (II Samuel 14:14)."
וְעַל כֵּן בֵּרֵר אוֹתוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְצֵרַף אוֹתוֹ עַל יְדֵי מַעֲשֶׂה דְּאֵשֶׁת פּוֹטִיפַר.
And indeed, Hashem, blessed be He, clarified and smelted him through the fiery test of Potiphar's wife:
כִּי בְּרִית הַמָּעוֹר מְכֻוָּן כְּנֶגֶד בְּרִית הַלָּשׁוֹן [סֵפֶר יְצִירָה פֶּרֶק אָלֶף, מִשְׁנָה גִּימֶל]
for the covenant of sexual purity (brit hama'or) is directly aligned with the covenant of the tongue (brit halashon; Sefer Yetzirah 1:3),
וְכַאֲשֶׁר נִמְצָא מְבוֹרָר בָּזֶה, בֵּירֵר אֶת עַצְמוֹ עַל מַה שֶּׁחָשְׁדוּ אוֹתוֹ בְּעִנְיַן לָשׁוֹן הָרַע גַּם כֵּן שֶׁהוּא נָקִי.

so that when Joseph proved himself utterly pure in guarding the covenant of the flesh in Egypt, he retroactively clarified and vindicated himself regarding their suspicion of slander (lashon hara), proving that his tongue too had been completely pure in intention!
h:
The Brothers Sell Yosef
Since the tribes initially judged Joseph liable to death because "he brought their evil report unto their father

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayeshev 6
p: וַיֵּרֶד יְהוּדָא מֵאֵת אֶחָיו.
And Judah went down from his brothers.
טַעַם הָעִנְיָן לָמָּה הָלַךְ יְהוּדָא לִישָּׂא אִשָּׁה בְּזֶה הַזְּמַן,
The reason why Judah went to marry a wife at this specific time
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁרָאָה כִּי יַעֲקֹב מֵיאֵן לְהִתְנַחֵם וּבְיַעַן כִּי עָלָיו נָפַל הַגּוֹרָל לָשֵׂאת הַכֻּתּוֹנֶת לְאָבִיו וְנָפַל דַּעְתּוֹ מְאֹד מִזֶּה,

is because he saw that Jacob refused to be comforted over Joseph, and since the lot had fallen upon Judah to bring the bloodied tunic to his father (or because his brothers blamed him for advising the sale), his spirits fell greatly over this,
וְחָשַׁב כִּי חַס וְשָׁלוֹם אֶפֶס תִּקְוָה מִמֶּנּוּ
and he thought that, Heaven forbid, all hope was lost for him personally,
וְהָלַךְ לִישָּׂא אִשָּׁה שֶׁאָמַר אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לִי בָּנִים טוֹבִים אֲשֶׁר מֵהֶם יִצְמַח בִּנְיַן עֲדֵי עַד,
so he went to marry a wife, saying to himself: "Perhaps through marriage I will have worthy sons from whom the eternal edifice will sprout,"
[לָכֵן קָרָא שְׁמוֹ עֵר הַיְינוּ יָעִיר עָלֵינוּ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רוּחַ מִמָּרוֹם. תַּשְׁלוּם.] [
which is why he named his firstborn "Er" (עֵר)—praying that Hashem, blessed be He, would awaken (ya'ir) upon us a spirit from on high. End of addendum.
] וְאַחַר כָּךְ הֵבִין לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, אִם חַס וְשָׁלוֹם בֶּאֱמֶת אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה חוֹשֵׁב שֶׁאֵין לְךָ תִּקְוָה וְאֵין לְךָ חַיִּים בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ,

And afterward, through the death of his first two sons, the Holy One, blessed be He, made him understand: "If, Heaven forbid, it were true as you think in your despair—that you yourself have no hope and no spiritual life in your root—
אִם כֵּן אַף אִם תּוֹלִיד מֵאָה הֲלֹא לֹא יוּכְלוּ לִהְיוֹת בַּחַיִּים יוֹתֵר מִמְּךָ,
then even if you were to beget a hundred children, they could not possibly possess more life than you!
כִּי אֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַצִּינּוֹר שֶׁשּׁוֹלֵחַ עַל יָדָהּ הַחַיִּים גַּם הַצִּינּוֹר צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת שֶׁל הַחַיִּים,
For with Hashem, blessed be He, the conduit through which He channels life must itself be a living vessel,
וְאִם כֵּן כַּאֲשֶׁר בְּדַעְתְּךָ, לֹא יִהְיֶה רַק חַיֵּי שָׁעָה אַף כָּל תּוֹלְדוֹתֶיךָ.
and consequently, as long as you consider yourself spiritually dead in your own mind, all your offspring can only have fleeting, temporary life (like Er and Onan)!"
וְלָכֵן כַּאֲשֶׁר בָּא עַל בֵּירֵר הַדָּבָר נוֹלַד לוֹ שֵׁלָה, וְקָרָא שְׁמוֹ שֵׁלָה הַיְינוּ טָעוּת שֶׁטָּעָה בַּדָּבָר

And therefore, once Judah arrived at the clarity of this truth, his third son Shelah was born, and he named him "Shelah" (שֵׁלָה), which is an Aramaic expression for "error" (shalut)—acknowledging the error he had made in despairing of himself—
וְלָכֵן בָּנִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים לֹא הָיָה לָהֶם חַיִּים וְשֵׁלָה נִשְׁאַר בַּחַיִּים.
and that is why the first two sons born out of his despondency had no enduring life, whereas Shelah remained alive.
h:
Yehudah’s Descent and the Beginning of a New House
The reason why Judah went to marry a wife at this specific time

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayeshev 7
p: וַיְהִי עֵר בְּכוֹר יְהוּדָא רַע בְּעֵינֵי הַשֵּׁם.
And Er, Judah's firstborn, was wicked in the sight of Hashem.
פֵּירֵשׁ רַשִׁ"י שֶׁהָיָה מִתְיָרֵא שֶׁמָּא תִּתְעַבֵּר וְתַכְחִישׁ יָפְיָהּ.
Rashi explained (from Yevamot 34b) that he plowed on the roof (wasted his seed) because he was afraid lest Tamar conceive and mar her beauty.
עִנְיַן חֵטְא עֵר נִצְמַח כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר, בִּקֵּשׁ יַעֲקֹב לֵישֵׁב בְּשַׁלְוָה הַיְינוּ לְהִשָּׁמֵר מִכָּל מַעֲשֶׂה לְבַל יִכְנוֹס בְּשׁוּם סָפֵק,
The root of the sin of Er sprouted from what was explained earlier: Jacob sought to dwell in tranquility, meaning to guard himself from any ambiguous action lest he enter into any spiritual doubt;
וְהִנֵּה זֹאת אֵין רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לָכֵן הֶרְאָה לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and since such passive withdrawal is not the will of Hashem, blessed be He, in this world of action, Hashem, blessed be He, showed him its consequence:

רְאֵה מִי שֶׁיּוֹצֵא מִיּוֹצְאֵי חֲלָצֶיךָ שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן יִשְׁתַּמֵּר מִמַּעֲשֶׂה בְּכַוָּנָה שֶׁלֹּא יָבֹא לִידֵי הֶפְסֵד, רַק שֶׁהוּא בְּעִנְיָנִים גּוּפָנִים וּרְאֵה וְהָבֵן עֵרֶךְ דָּבָר בָּזֶה,

"See what has emerged from your own loins (your grandson Er)—one who likewise refrains from productive action (begetting children) with the intention of avoiding loss of beauty, except that in him it has devolved into coarse, bodily matters! Observe and understand the measure of this matter!"
כִּי אֵצֶל יַעֲקֹב הָיָה נִמְצָא גַּם כֵּן חֶסְרוֹן הַזֶּה, רַק חֶסְרוֹנוֹ הָיָה בְּעַבְדוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהָיָה מְשַׁמֵּר עַצְמוֹ מִבְּלִי לְהַכְחִישׁ יוֹפִי עֲבוֹדָתוֹ,

For within Jacob existed the subtle root of this very flaw, except that in Jacob it was entirely spiritual in the service of Hashem, blessed be He—guarding himself from worldly entanglement so as not to mar the pristine beauty of his meditative service—
וְכַאֲשֶׁר יִסְתַּעֵף זֶה עַד הַגּוּף אָז הוּא חֵטְא מְפוֹרָשׁ
yet when that same impulse branches down into the physical realm, it manifests as an explicit sin;

וְכֵן הוּא בְּכָל מַחְשְׁבוֹת הָאָבוֹת שֶׁאֶצְלָם הָיָה קָטָן מְאֹד וְאַחַר כָּךְ כַּאֲשֶׁר יְבָרֵר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְיִבְרָא מִמַּחֲשָׁבָה כָּזֹאת נֶפֶשׁ מְיוּחָד יִתְבָּרֵר מַה שֶּׁיִּתְבָּרֵר.

and so it is with all the subtle thoughts of the Patriarchs: within them a flaw is infinitesimal and spiritual, yet afterward, when the Holy One, blessed be He, externalizes that thought by creating a distinct soul from it, its latent flaw is starkly exposed and clarified.
וְהִנֵּה חֵטְא עֵר וְאוֹנָן הָיָה כְּפִי הַמְּבוֹאָר בַּמִּשְׁנָה (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק בֵּית, מִשְׁנָה אָלֶף)
Now, the respective sins of Er and Onan may be understood according to what is explained in the Mishnah (Pirkei Avot 2:1):
רַבִּי אוֹמֵר אֵיזֶה דֶּרֶךְ יְשָׁרָה שֶׁיָּבוֹר לוֹ הָאָדָם כָּל שֶׁהוּא תִּפְאֶרֶת לְעוֹשֶׂיהָ וְתִפְאֶרֶת לוֹ מִן הָאָדָם,

Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi says: Which is the right path that a person should choose for himself? Whatever is a harmony and beauty to the one who does it (tiferet l'oseha), and brings him beauty and esteem from mankind (tiferet lo min ha'adam).
תִּפְאֶרֶת לְעוֹשֶׂיהָ הַיְינוּ שֶׁהַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁהָאָדָם עוֹשֶׂה תִּשָּׂא חֵן בְּעֵינֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם,
Here, "tiferet l'oseha" means that the outward deed a person performs finds favor in the eyes of fellow human beings,
וְתִפְאֶרֶת לוֹ מִן הָאָדָם הַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה טוֹב בְּעוֹמֶק בְּמַעֲמַקֵּי חַיִּים שֶׁלּוֹ הַיְינוּ צוּרַת אָדָם.
while "tiferet lo min ha'adam" means that it is good and luminous in the innermost depths of his spiritual life—namely, the supernal image of Man (tzurat Adam).
[כִּי אָדָם הוּא בְּמַעֲלָה גְּדוֹלָה יוֹתֵר מֵאִישׁ כַּמְּבוֹאָר (בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ תַּזְרִיעַ מֵם חֵית עַמּוּד אָלֶף) תַּשְׁלוּם.] [
For the title "Adam" represents a higher spiritual stature than "Ish," as is explained in the holy Zohar, Tazria 48a. End of addendum.
] וְצָרִיךְ הָאָדָם לְהַבִּיט לְכָל מַעֲשָׂיו שֶׁיִּהְיוּ מְבוֹרָרִים עַל פִּי שְׁנֵי אוֹפַנִּים הַלָּלוּ,
And a person must see to it that all his deeds are clarified according to both of these dimensions;
וְאִם יֶאֱרַע לִפְנֵי אָדָם מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁלֹּא תִּשָּׂא אֶת שְׁנֵי הַבֵּרוּרִים הָאֵלֶּה, בָּזֶה הִיא מַחְלוֹקֶת בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל בְּמַסֶּכֶת כְּתוּבּוֹת [טֵית זַיִן עַמּוּד בֵּית]

and if a situation arises before a person that cannot simultaneously satisfy both of these standards, Which takes precedence is the subject of the dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel in Tractate Ketubot (16b–17a),
דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן כֵּיצַד מְרַקְּדִין לִפְנֵי הַכַּלָּה בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים כַּלָּה כְּמוֹת שֶׁהִיא,
where the Rabbis taught: How does one dance and sing before the bride? Beit Shammai say: "The bride as she is" (praising her only according to her actual physical features),
וְהוּא שֶׁלְּפִי סְבָרָתָם הָעִיקָּר הוּא תִּפְאֶרֶת לְעוֹשֶׂיהָ, שֶׁאִם יֹאמַר כַּלָּה נָאָה וַחֲסוּדָה לֹא יִהְיֶה הַתִּפְאֶרֶת לְעֵינֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם מִשּׁוּם "מִדְּבַר שֶׁקֶר תִּרְחָק",

because according to their reasoning, the primary requirement is that the act itself look irreproachable to observers ("tiferet l'oseha"), for if one calls an unattractive bride "beautiful and graceful," it will look like flatterers' falsehood in the eyes of onlookers, violating "Keep far from a false matter" (Exodus 23:7);
וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים כַּלָּה נָאָה וַחֲסוּדָה,
whereas Beit Hillel say: We always sing, "A beautiful and graceful bride!"
הַיְינוּ אַף שֶׁאֵין בָּזֶה תִּפְאֶרֶת לְעוֹשֶׂיהָ, מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵין צָרִיךְ לְהַשְׁגִּיחַ עַל זֶה מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא תִּפְאֶרֶת לוֹ מִן הָאָדָם הַיְינוּ, שֶׁכָּל הָאָדָם יַכְרִיחוּ לָזֶה

Meaning that even if the statement does not appear outwardly accurate, one need not be concerned with that, because it fulfills "tiferet lo min ha'adam"—inner harmony with the supernal image of Man and lovingkindness,
[כְּמוֹ שֶׁכְּתִיב (מִשְׁלֵי גִּימֶל, דָּלֶת) "וּמְצָא חֵן וְשֵׂכֶל טוֹב בְּעֵינֵי אֱלֹקִים" וְאַחַר כָּךְ בְּעֵינֵי אָדָם. תַּשְׁלוּם.] [
as it is written (Proverbs 3:4), "So shall you find grace and good understanding in the sight of God," and only afterward "and in the sight of man." End of addendum.
] וּכְמוֹ שֶׁבֵּיאֲרוּ שָׁמָּה, מִי שֶׁלָּקַח מִקָּח רַע מִן הַשּׁוּק יְשַׁבְּחֶנָּה בְּעֵינָיו אוֹ יְגַנֶּנָּה בְּעֵינָיו.
And as Beit Hillel explained there: If someone has made a poor purchase in the marketplace, should one praise it in his eyes or disparage it in his eyes? Surely one must praise it!
וְהִנֵּה עֵר הִשְׁגִּיחַ עִיקָּר עַל תִּפְאֶרֶת לוֹ מִן הָאָדָם
Now behold, Er focused exclusively on the inner spiritual dimension ("tiferet lo min ha'adam"),
כִּי זֹאת יָדוּעַ, כִּי כָּל הוֹלָדָה לֹא תָּבוֹא רַק עַל יְדֵי הַסְתָּרָה וְשִׁכְחָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁהַגַּרְעִין הַנִּזְרָע לֹא יַצְמִיחַ בִּלְתִּי אִם יִכְלֶה בְּעָפָר וְיִרְקַב,

for it is known that all procreation and new birth can come about only through a momentary concealment and self-forgetfulness—just as a planted seed cannot sprout unless it first disintegrates and rots in the soil,
וְכֵן הַטִּיפָּה חַיִּים שֶׁיּוֹרֵד מֵהַמּוֹחַ לֹא יוּכַל לָבוֹא לִידֵי הוֹלָדָה עַד שֶׁיִּתְעַבֶּה וְיִתְגַּשֵּׁם בְּזֶרַע אֲנָשִׁים,
and similarly the drop of vitality that descends from the father's brain cannot produce a child until it thickens and materializes into physical semen;

כִּי בָּזֶה הָרֶגַע נִפְסַק וְנִשְׁכַּח דַּעַת הָאָדָם וּבְאִם הָיָה הָאָדָם עוֹמֵד תָּמִיד בְּדַעְתּוֹ נֶגֶד בּוֹרְאוֹ לֹא הָיָה יָכוֹל לָבוֹא לִידֵי הֶסְתֵּר וְשִׁכְחָה הַזֹּאת שֶׁיָּבֹא מִמֶּנָּה הוֹלָדָה,

for at that moment of marital union, a person's abstract intellectual consciousness is momentarily suspended and forgotten, and if a person were to insist on standing uninterruptedly in pure intellectual contemplation before his Creator, he could never enter into that state of concealment and descent from which physical birth emerges;
וְלָכֵן עֵר בְּיַעַן שֶׁהִשְׁגִּיחַ רַק עַל תִּפְאֶרֶת לוֹ מִן הָאָדָם וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ שֵׂכֶל בָּהִיר תָּמִיד וְהָיָה עוֹמֵד נוֹכַח הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, עַל כֵּן לֹא רָצָה לְהַכְחִישׁ זֹאת,

and therefore Er, because he cared only for his own inner spiritual lucidity and refused to step down from his clear intellectual contemplation before Hashem, blessed be He, did not want to mar that spiritual beauty by descending into physical procreation—
וְזֶה פֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁלֹּא תַכְחִישׁ יָפְיָהּ הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא לְהַכְחִישׁ תִּפְאֶרֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
and this is the mystical meaning of "lest she conceive and mar her beauty": namely, he was afraid to mar the inner spiritual beauty of his soul!
וְאוֹנָן לָקַח לוֹ דֶּרֶךְ הַשֵּׁנִי כִּי מַעֲשָׂיו הָיוּ לְפִי שֶׁרָאָה כַּוָּונַת אָבִיו שֶׁרַק יִקָּרֵא הַזֶּרַע עַל שֵׁם אָחִיו

Onan, conversely, erred on the second path: for his sin in levirate marriage stemmed from seeing that his father's intention was solely to raise up offspring bearing the name of his deceased brother ("the seed will not be his," Genesis 38:9),
עַל כֵּן הֵרַע בְּעֵינָיו שֶׁלֹּא יְתַקֵּן אֶת עַצְמוֹ, רַק אֶת נֶפֶשׁ אָחִיו וְהָיָה לוֹ תַּרְעוֹמוֹת
and therefore it displeased him that through his act he would not be building and rectifying his own name in the eyes of the world, but only the soul of his brother, so he harbored resentment;
וְזֹאת הָעִנְיָן נִמְצָא גַּם בְּצַדִּיקִים גְּדוֹלִים וּמַעֲשֵׂה אוֹנָן נִקְרָא תִּפְאֶרֶת לְעוֹשֶׂיהָ,
and the subtle root of this concern—insisting that one's deed visibly belong to its doer—is found even among great tzaddikim, corresponding to "tiferet l'oseha" (beauty to the one who does it);
עַל כֵּן הָיָה תִּיקּוּן לְנִשְׁמָתָם שֶׁנּוֹלְדוּ אַחַר כָּךְ פֶּרֶץ וְזֶרַח,
therefore the rectification for both of their souls came when Peretz and Zerach were subsequently born to Judah from Tamar (as the reincarnations of Er and Onan):
פֶּרֶץ הָיָה נִשְׁמַת עֵר כִּי פֶּרֶץ הוּא לְשׁוֹן תַּקּוּפוּת הַיְינוּ תִּפְאֶרֶת לוֹ מִן הָאָדָם, הַיְינוּ אַף שֶׁהוּא הֵפֶךְ מִתִּפְאֶרֶת נֶגֶד בְּנֵי אָדָם לֹא יַשְׁגִּיחַ עַל זֶה,

Peretz was the rectified soul of Er, for "Peretz" (breach/breakthrough) is an expression of fierce fortitude, representing "tiferet lo min ha'adam"—breaking through for the inner truth of God's will even when the act looks scandalous or contrary to outward appearances before men;
וְזֶרַח הוּא נִשְׁמַת אוֹנָן כִּי שְׁמוֹ מוֹכִיחַ עָלָיו שֶׁהוּא תִּפְאֶרֶת נֶגֶד בְּנֵי אָדָם.
while Zerach ("shining") was the rectified soul of Onan, as his very name proves that he embodies "tiferet l'oseha"—shining visibly before the eyes of men.
וְעַל אֵלּוּ הַשְּׁנַיִם אָמַר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ צָדְקָה מִמֶּנִּי מִמֶּנִּי יָצְאוּ הַדְּבָרִים כְּבוּשִׁים,
And concerning the conception of these two twins Hashem, blessed be He, declared, "She is righteous; from Me (mimeni) these hidden matters came forth" (Sotah 10b)—
הַיְינוּ אַף שֶׁעֵר וְאוֹנָן לֹא הָיוּ רְאוּיִם בְּעֵינָיו, אֲבָל אֵלּוּ הַשְּׁנַיִם שֶׁהָיוּ נִשְׁמוֹתֵיהֶם יָשְׁרוּ לוֹ,
meaning that although Er and Onan in their first incarnation were displeasing in His eyes, these two rectified souls (Peretz and Zerach) were upright before Him;
כִּי אַף שֶׁנִּרְאֶה שֶׁפֶּרֶץ עוֹשֶׂה נֶגֶד הַהֲלָכָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בְּמַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד, עַל זֶה מֵעִיד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא מִפְּנֵי עֵת לַעֲשׂוֹת לַהַשֵּׁם,

for even when it appears on the surface that the line of Peretz acts contrary to the conventional law—as we find repeatedly in the lineage of the Royal House of David (Tamar, Ruth, Bathsheba)—Hashem, blessed be He, Himself testifies that it is done purely because "it is a time to act for Hashem";

וְאַף שֶׁעַל הַמַּעֲשֶׂה הָיָה נִרְאֶה שֶׁחֵטְא עֵר הָיָה גָּדוֹל מֵחֵטְא שֶׁל אוֹנָן מִכָּל מָקוֹם נִשְׁמָתוֹ הָיְתָה גְּדוֹלָה בְּעוֹמֶק מִנִּשְׁמַת אוֹנָן כִּי מִמֶּנּוּ נוֹלַד מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד,

and even though in their first lifetimes the sin of Er appeared worse than the sin of Onan (since Er had no legal excuse at all), nevertheless in its inner depth the soul of Er (Peretz) was greater than the soul of Onan (Zerach), for from Peretz was born the Royal House of David!
כִּי כָל הַבִּנְיָנִים שֶׁל מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד מַנְהִיג הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עַל יְדֵי בִּנְיָנִים כָּאֵלֶּה אַף שֶׁבִּשְׁעַת מַעֲשֶׂה הָיָה נִרְאֶה לוֹ שֶׁחָטָא,

For the Holy One, blessed be He, brings about all the foundational stages of the Royal House of David specifically through such paradoxical unions where, at the moment of the act, it appears as though a sin is being committed—
כִּי יְהוּדָא חֲשָׁבָהּ לְזוֹנָה כִּי כִסְּתָה פָּנֶיהָ, הַיְינוּ שֶׁהַדָּבָר הָיָה בְּסוֹד מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
as it is written, "Judah thought her to be a harlot, because she had covered her face," signifying that the true nature of the act was veiled in a divine mystery from Hashem, blessed be He,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמְּבוֹאָר (בַּמִּדְרָשׁ) (סוֹטָה יוֹד עַמּוּד בֵּית) מִמֶּנִּי יָצְאוּ הַדְּבָרִים כְּבוּשִׁים הַיְינוּ בְּסוֹד כָּבוּשׁ שֶׁנֶּעְלַם אַף מִנְּבִיאִים הַבִּנְיָן שֶׁל מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד.

and as is explained in the Gemara (Sotah 10b): "From Me came forth these hidden matters (kevushim)"—namely, in a concealed mystery (sod kavush), so that the genesis of the Royal House of David was hidden from the Accuser and even from the prophets.
h:
Er’s Sin and the Hidden Spiritual Work of Yehudah
Rashi explained (from Yevamot 34b) that he plowed on the roof (wasted his seed) because he was afraid lest Tamar conceive and mar her beauty

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Miketz 1
p: וַיְהִי מִקֵּץ שְׁנָתַיִם יָמִים.
And it came to pass at the end of two full years.
בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית קוּף צָדִי גִּימֶל עַמּוּד בֵּית) רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר פָּתַח "חַי הַשֵּׁם וּבָרוּךְ צוּרִי וְיָרוּם אֱלֹקֵי יִשְׁעִי".
In the holy Zohar (Bereishit 193b), Rabbi Elazar opened his discourse on this verse by quoting: "Hashem lives, and blessed is my Rock, and exalted be the God of my salvation" (Psalms 18:47).
"חַי הַשֵּׁם" הַיְינוּ מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ לֵב טָהוֹר וּמְנוּקֶּה מִכָּל חֶמְדּוֹת שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם רַק דָּבוּק בְּחַיִּים נִצְחִיִּים,
"Hashem lives" refers to one who possesses a pure heart cleansed of all worldly cravings, cleaving solely to eternal life;
"וּבָרוּךְ צוּרִי" הַיְינוּ מִי שֶׁמַּכִּיר שֶׁכָּל הַטּוֹבוֹת הֵם רַק מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְלָכֵן יֵשׁ לוֹ עַיִן טוֹבָה,
"and blessed is my Rock" refers to one who recognizes that all blessings and favors come exclusively from Hashem, blessed be He, and who therefore possesses a generous, benevolent eye;
אָז "וְיָרוּם אֱלֹקֵי יִשְׁעִי" הַיְינוּ שֶׁיַּשִּׂיג יְשׁוּעוֹת גְּבוֹהִים, יוֹתֵר מִכְּפִי שִׂכְלוֹ.
then "and exalted be the God of my salvation"—meaning he will attain lofty salvations far beyond the grasp of his own intellect!
כִּי טֶרֶם יִתְבָּרֵר הָאָדָם בְּאֵלּוּ דְּבָרִים הַנִּזְכָּרִים אֵין בְּאֶפְשָׁר לִתֵּן לוֹ יְשׁוּעוֹת כִּי עוֹד אֵינוֹ כְּלִי בָּהִיר לְקַבֵּל,
For before a person is clarified in these two aforementioned qualities, it is impossible to bestow true salvation upon him, since he is not yet a clear vessel fit to receive it;
וְלָזֹאת "וַיְהִי מִקֵּץ שְׁנָתַיִם יָמִים" הַיְינוּ אַחַר שֶׁנִּתְבָּרֵר בְּאֵלּוּ הַשְּׁנֵי דְּבָרִים, אָז חָלַם פַּרְעֹה וְהִשִּׂיג תֵּיכֶף יְשׁוּעָה,

and therefore "And it came to pass at the end of two years" means that after Joseph had been thoroughly clarified in these two matters during those two years, Pharaoh immediately dreamed his dream and Joseph attained instant salvation,
"עַד עֵת בֹּא דְבָרוֹ אִמְרַת הַשֵּׁם צְרָפָתְהוּ",
fulfilling the verse, "Until the time that his word came to pass, the word of Hashem refined him" (Psalms 105:19);
כִּי בַּלַּיְלָה הַהוּא גָּדְלָה צַעֲקַת יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק "שׁוּבָה הַשֵּׁם עַד מָתָי" וְתֵיכֶף הִשִּׂיג יְשׁוּעָה.
for on that very night of Rosh Hashanah, the outcry of Joseph the Righteous grew intense—"Return, O Hashem, how long?" (Psalms 90:13)—and immediately he attained salvation.
וְעַל זֶה כְּתִיב (תְּהִלִּים פֵּא חֵית, בֵּית) "הַשֵּׁם אֱלֹקֵי יְשׁוּעָתִי וְכוּלֵי צָעַקְתִּי בַלַּיְלָה נֶגְדֶּךָ",
And concerning this it is written (Psalms 88:2): "O Hashem, God of my salvation, by day I have cried out, and in the night before You";
כִּי כָּךְ הוּא מִדּוֹתָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא טֶרֶם אֲשֶׁר יִתֵּן הַיְשׁוּעָה מֵבִיא בְּלֵב הָאָדָם צְעָקָה בָּזֶה לְמַעַן אֲשֶׁר יִקָּרֵא "יְגִיעַ כַּפֶּיךָ".

for such is the attribute of the Holy One, blessed be He: right before He bestows a prepared salvation, He awakens an intense outcry in the person's heart to pray for it, so that the salvation may be credited to him as "the toil of your hands" (Psalms 128:2).

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Miketz 2
p: וַיְהִי מִקֵּץ שְׁנָתַיִם יָמִים וּפַרְעֹה חֹלֵם.
And it came to pass at the end of two full years (shnatayim yamim), that Pharaoh dreamed.
שְׁנָתַיִם יָמִים רוֹמֵז כִּי בִּשְׁנֵי יָמִים נִבְרְאוּ כָּל הַטּוֹבוֹת שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם
The phrase "shnatayim yamim" (literally "two years, days") alludes to thetwo days of Creation on which "that it was good" was said twice, wherein all the worldly goods were created:
הַיְינוּ בְּיוֹם גִּימֶל נִבְרָא טוֹבַת אֲכִילָה וּבְיוֹם וָאו נִבְרָא צוּרַת הָאָדָם הַיְינוּ שֹׁרֶשׁ חַיִּים וְכָבוֹד וְהִתְנַשְּׂאוּת, כִּי הָאָדָם מְנוּשָּׂא עַל כֹּל,

namely, on the third day (vegetation) was created the pleasure of eating, and on the sixth day was created the form of Man—which is the root of life, honor, and preeminence, since man is exalted over all creation;
וְכַאֲשֶׁר יִזְדַּכֵּךְ הָאָדָם בְּאֵלּוּ הַשְּׁנַיִם יָבֹא לִישׁוּעָה,
and when a person purifies himself in these two areas (bodily appetite and the desire for honor/preeminence), he arrives at salvation;
וְזֶה פֵּירוּשׁ "וַיְהִי מִקֵּץ שְׁנָתַיִם יָמִים" הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַסּוֹף וָקֵץ בְּהָרַע שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּאֵלּוּ הַשְּׁנֵי יָמִים אָז מִיָּד תָּבֹא הַיְשׁוּעָה,
and this is the meaning of "And it came to pass at the end (miketz) of two days": when an end is put to the evil inclination lurking within the gifts of those two days, salvation immediately arrives;
וְעַל זֶה רוֹמֵז הַתְחָלַת הַמִּדְרָשׁ בַּפָּרָשָׁה הַזֹּאת הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁיָּבֹא קֵץ לַחֹשֶׁךְ הַיְינוּ לְהָרַע הַנִּמְצָא בְּאֵלּוּ הַדְּבָרִים אָז יָבֹא תֵּיכֶף הַיְשׁוּעָה.

and the opening of the Midrash on this Torah portion (Bereishit Rabbah 89:1, quoting Job 28:3, "He sets an end to darkness") alludes to this: when an end comes to the darkness—namely, to the evil mixed into these two faculties—salvation comes at once.
