paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayechi 9
p: וַיֶּאֱסוֹף רַגְלָיו אֶל הַמִּטָּה.
And he gathered up his feet into the bed, and expired, and was gathered unto his people.
אִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (תַּעֲנִית הֵא עַמּוּד בֵּית) "יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ לֹא מֵת",
It is stated in the Gemara (Ta'anit 5b): "Our father Jacob did not die" (for "was died" is not written of him).

הָעִנְיָן בָּזֶה כִּי עִנְיַן מִיתָה הוּא הִשְׁתַּנּוּת הָאָדָם מֵעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְעוֹלָם הַבָּא, וְיַעֲקֹב כָּל אוֹתָן שָׁנִים שֶׁהָיָה בְּמִצְרַיִם הִטְעִימוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ טִיפָּה חַיִּים מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא,

The inner meaning of this is that the concept of "death" denotes a radical transition of a person from the mode of this world to the mode of the World to Come; whereas throughout those seventeen years that Jacob lived in Egypt ("And Jacob lived"), Hashem, blessed be He, granted him a direct taste of the drop of eternal life of the World to Come while still in his body,
עַל כֵּן נֶאֱמַר עָלָיו לֹא מֵת כִּי לֹא נִשְׁתַּנָּה בְּמוֹתוֹ כְּלוּם,
and therefore it is stated of him that "he did not die," because nothing in his essential consciousness changed at his passing at all!
וְעַל זֶה מַסְמִיךְ תֵּיכֶף הַגְּמָרָא "כָּל הָאוֹמֵר רָחָב רָחָב מִיָּד נִקְרֵי" וּמַסִּיק שָׁם הַגְּמָרָא בְּיוֹדְעָהּ וּמַכִּירָהּ,

And immediately following this statement in Ta'anit (5b), Rav Nachman and Rabbi Yitzchak discuss another statement: "Whoever merely says 'Rahab, Rahab' immediately experiences a seminal emission," and the Gemara concludes there that this happens only to one who already knew her and was intimately familiar with her image;

וְלָזֶה הִיא סְמִיכוּת הַגְּמָרָא לְהַרְאוֹת כִּי כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּמְצָא בְּעִנְיְינֵי הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה חֶמְדָּה שֶׁנִּשְׁאָר קָבוּעַ בְּלֵב הָאָדָם, כֵּן הָיָה הַטִּיפָּה חַיִּים שֶׁנִּקְבַּע בְּלֵב יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ בְּעֵת אֲשֶׁר נָטַף בּוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִשְׁאַר בּוֹ קָבוּעַ גַּם אַחַר כָּךְ,

and the reason the Gemara juxtaposed these two seemingly unrelated teachings is to show that just as in the realm of physical desire, once someone has intimately known a powerful attraction its impression remains permanently fixed in his heart, so too in the realm of supreme holiness, once that drop of eternal life was instilled by Hashem, blessed be He, into the heart of our father Jacob during his lifetime, it remained permanently fixed within him ever after—
עַל כֵּן לֹא יִתָּכֵן לְהֵאָמֵר בּוֹ לְשׁוֹן מִיתָה רַק כְּאָדָם שֶׁפּוֹשֵׁט מַלְבּוּשָׁיו וְלוֹבֵשׁ בְּגָדִים אֲחֵרִים,
and therefore the term "death" could not apply to him, for his passing was merely like a person taking off his weekday garments and donning other garments;
וְזֶה עִנְיַן הַפָּסוּק (יְשַׁעְיָה נּוּן חֵית, חֵית) "אָז יִבָּקַע כַּשַּׁחַר אוֹרֶךָ", יִבָּקַע הֵם אוֹתִיּוֹת יַעֲקֹב וְגַם אוֹתִיּוֹת קָבוּעַ, וְהָבֵן.

and this is the mystical allusion of the verse (Isaiah 58:8), "Then shall your light break forth (yibaka) as the morning": the word yibaka (יִבָּקַע) consists of the exact same letters as Yaakov (יַעֲקֹב) and also the exact same letters as kavu'a (קָבוּעַ — permanently fixed); understand this.
h:
Yaakov’s Passing and the Secret of Life
Our father Jacob did not die" (for "was died" is not written of him)

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayechi 10
p: וְאַתֶּם חֲשַׁבְתֶּם עָלַי רָעָה אֱלֹקִים חֲשָׁבָהּ לְטוֹבָה.
And as for you, you meant evil against me; but God meant it for good.

בָּזֶה הָעִנְיָן הֶרְאָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵיךְ הָיָה בְּאֶפְשָׁר לְהָבִיא הַשְּׁבָטִים בְּגָלוּת מִצְרַיִם וְעִיקָּר הָיָה הַפֵּירוּד שֶׁהִתְחִילוּ לְהִפָּרֵד, כִּי בְּעֵת שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל בְּאַחְדוּת לֹא יוּכַל לִשְׁלוֹט עֲלֵיהֶם שׁוּם דָּבָר.

In this final episode of Genesis, Hashem, blessed be He, revealed how it became spiritually possible for the bondage of the Egyptian exile to take hold over the holy tribes: the primary cause was the subtle division and estrangement that began to set in between Joseph and his brothers after Jacob's passing, for as long as Israel stands in complete unity, no foreign power can ever rule over them.
וְהָעִנְיָן בָּזֶה הָיָה שֶׁפֵּירַשׁ יוֹסֵף מִן הַשְּׁבָטִים,
And how did this estrangement happen? After returning from Jacob's burial, Joseph stopped dining together with the tribes (Tanchuma, Vayechi 17);

כִּי בְּעוֹד שֶׁיַּעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ הָיָה קַיָּים לֹא הָיָה נִיכָּר מִמֶּנּוּ מִי הוּא הַגָּדוֹל שֶׁבַּשְּׁבָטִים כִּי לִפְעָמִים הָיָה מְקָרֵב אֶת זֶה יוֹתֵר וְלִפְעָמִים זֶה יוֹתֵר, אֵיזֶה שֶׁהָיָה יָשָׁר בְּעֵינָיו בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה,

for as long as our father Jacob was alive, he sat at the head of the table, and it was not publicly fixed who was the preeminent leader among the tribes, as sometimes Jacob drew one son closer and sometimes another, according to what was fitting in that hour;
אַךְ קוֹדֶם לִפְטִירָתוֹ בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁבֵּרְכָם וְאָמַר לִיהוּדָא "יִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לְךָ בְּנֵי אָבִיךָ" אָז הִכִּירוּ כֻּלָּם כִּי יְהוּדָא גָּבַר בְּאֶחָיו,

however, just prior to his passing, when Jacob blessed them and declared to Judah, "Your father's sons shall bow down to you," everyone recognized clearly that Judah had prevailed among his brothers as the true spiritual king;
וּלְכָךְ לֹא הָיָה יוֹסֵף יוֹדֵעַ אֵיךְ לְהִתְנַהֵג, בְּאִם לְהוֹשִׁיב אֶת יְהוּדָא בָּרֹאשׁ הֲלֹא הוּא מֶלֶךְ וְאָסוּר לְזַלְזֵל בַּמֶּלֶךְ,

and consequently, after Jacob's death, Joseph wascaught in a dilemma as to how to conduct himself at the table: if he were to seat Judah at the head above himself, Joseph was the reigning viceroy/king in Egypt, and by law a king is forbidden to waive his royal honor (Sanhedrin 19b);
וּבְאִם שֶׁיֵּשֵׁב הוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ בָּרֹאשׁ הֲלֹא יוֹדֵעַ בְּעַצְמוֹ כִּי יְהוּדָא הוּא הָרֹאשׁ עַל כֵּן יָשַׁב בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ וְלֹא עִם הַשְּׁבָטִים,

yet if he himself were to sit at the head above Judah, he knew inwardly from his father's blessing that Judah was the true head! Therefore, to avoid either impropriety, Joseph chose to dine separately by himself rather than sit at the table with the tribes;
וְהַשְּׁבָטִים דָּנוּ אוֹתוֹ שֶׁעָשָׂה זֹאת מֵחֲמַת שִׂנְאָה וּלְכָךְ נֶעֶנְשׁוּ לִהְיוֹת בְּגָלוּת כִּי הָיָה לָהֶם לְדוּנוֹ לְכַף זְכוּת,

and the tribes misjudged his withdrawal, assuming he was distancing himself from them out of lingering hatred ("Perhaps Joseph will hate us"), and because of this failure to judge him favorably they were punished with the bondage of exile;

וְגַם לְיוֹסֵף נֶחְשַׁב לְחֵטְא עַל אֲשֶׁר הִנִּיחַ לָהֶם מָקוֹם לִטְעוֹת בּוֹ, כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הָיָה לוֹ לְהִתְנַהֵג שֶׁהוּא יֵשֵׁב בָּרֹאשׁ מֵאַחַר שֶׁלְּעֵת עַתָּה הוּא מֶלֶךְ, אַךְ בְּלִבּוֹ הָיָה צָרִיךְ לֵידַע כִּי יְהוּדָא גָּדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ.

and for Joseph too, at his exalted level, it was reckoned as a slight flaw that he left room for his brothers to misunderstand his actions—for in truth he should have continued dining with them and seated himself at the head of the table, since for the present hour he held the royal office, while privately holding in his heart the awareness that Judah was greater than he.
וּבֶאֱמֶת מֵאַחַר שֶׁהַשְּׁבָטִים טָעוּ בּוֹ הָיָה נִמְצָא בַּדָּבָר שֵׁמֶץ מֶנְהוּ לְעֵינֵי אָדָם,

And indeed, the very fact that the holy tribes misconstrued his behavior shows that externally his action lacked complete perfection in the eyes of man ("you shall be clear before Hashem and before Israel," Numbers 32:22);
וְעַל זֶה צָרִיךְ הָאָדָם לְהִתְפַּלֵּל תָּמִיד לִפְנֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁלֹּא יָבוֹא בְּדַעְתּוֹ לָדוּן אֶת חֲבֵרוֹ לְחוֹב, וְגַם שֶׁחֲבֵרוֹ לֹא יְדוּנוֹ לְחוֹב

and regarding this a person must constantly pray before Hashem, blessed be He, both that it never enter his mind to judge his fellow unfavorably, and likewise that his fellow never come to judge him unfavorably—
וְעַל זֶה נֶעֶנְשׁוּ הַשְּׁבָטִים שֶׁעָבְרוּ עַל שֶׁהָיוּ צְרִיכִים לְדוּנוֹ לְכַף זְכוּת.
for it was on account of this subtle breach in judging favorably that the tribes became vulnerable to the decree of exile.
h:
The Brothers’ Intentions and Hashem’s Goodness
In this final episode of Genesis, Hashem, blessed be He, revealed how it became spiritually possible for the bondage of the Egyptian exile to take hold over…

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Shemot 1
p: וְאֵלֶּה שְׁמוֹת וְכוּלֵי וַיְהִי כִּי יָרְאוּ הַמְיַלְּדוֹת וְכוּלֵי וַיַּעַשׂ לָהֶם בָּתִּים.
Now these are the names, etc. And it came to pass, because the midwives feared God, that He made them houses.
דְּהִנֵּה יִרְאַת בָּשָׂר וָדָם כְּשֶׁאָדָם מִתְיָירֵא מִפְּנֵי אָדָם אֵין בּוֹ יִישּׁוּב הַדַּעַת, כִּי יִרְאָה הוּא הֵיפֶךְ מִזֶּה, אַךְ יִרְאַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יֵשׁ בָּהּ נַיְיחָא.

For behold, regarding the fear of flesh and blood, when a person is afraid of a mortal man, he has no settledness of mind (yishuv hada'at), because fear is the antithesis of composure; however, within the fear of Hashem, blessed be He, there is tranquility and calm.
וְעַל זֶה מוֹרֶה "וַיַּעַשׂ לָהֶם בָּתִּים" כִּי בַּיִת מוֹרֶה עַל יִישּׁוּב הַדַּעַת,
And this is indicated by "that He made them houses," for a "house" signifies settledness of mind,
וּמִמֵּילָא כַּאֲשֶׁר הָיָה לָהֶם יִישּׁוּב הַדַּעַת מֵחֲמַת יִרְאַת אֱלֹקִים לֹא הָיָה לָהֶם שׁוּם פַּחַד מִגְּזֵירַת פַּרְעֹה, וְזֶהוּ "וַיַּעַשׂ לָהֶם בָּתִּים",
and consequently, once they possessed settledness of mind by virtue of their fear of God, they had no fear whatsoever of Pharaoh's decree—and this is the meaning of "and He made them houses";
וְזֶה פֵּירוּשׁ הַפָּסוּק (בְּרֵאשִׁית מֵם טֵית, יוֹד גִּימֶל) "זְבוּלֻן לְחוֹף יַמִּים יִשְׁכֹּן וְהוּא לְחוֹף אֳנִיּוֹת",
and this is also the meaning of the verse (Genesis 49:13): "Zebulun shall dwell at the shore of the seas, and he shall be a haven for ships":

יָם מוֹרֶה עַל יִרְאָה וָאֳנִיָּה מוֹרֶה עַל יִישּׁוּב הַדַּעַת, וְהוּא שֶׁבְּיִרְאָתוֹ נִמְצָא יִישּׁוּב הַדַּעַת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא טֵית עַמּוּד בֵּית) "סְפִינָה מֵינָח נָיְיחָא".

the "sea" indicates awe and fear, while a "ship" indicates settledness of mind, teaching that within one's fear of Heaven resides calm composure, just as they stated in the Gemara (Bava Metzia 9b): "A ship rests calmly (upon the water)."
h:
The Midwives’ Fear and the Gift of Settled Mind
For behold, regarding the fear of flesh and blood, when a person is afraid of a mortal man, he has no settledness of mind (yishuv hada'at), because fear is…

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Shemot 2
p: וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה מִי אָנֹכִי כִּי אֵלֵךְ וְכוּלֵי וְכִי אוֹצִיא וְכוּלֵי.
And Moses said unto God, "Who am I, that I should go unto Pharaoh, and that I should bring forth the children of Israel out of Egypt?"
הַיְינוּ שֶׁהָיָה שׁוֹאֵל שְׁנֵי דְּבָרִים, "מִי אָנֹכִי" הַיְינוּ שֶׁהָיָה מְבַקֵּשׁ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיָּאִיר לוֹ מִפְּנֵי מָה הוּא הַנִּבְחָר לִגְאוֹל יוֹתֵר מִכָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל.

That is, he was asking two distinct questions: first, "Who am I?"—meaning that he was beseeching Hashem, blessed be He, to illuminate for him why he was chosen to redeem them above anyone else in Israel.

"וְכִי אוֹצִיא" הַיְינוּ אֱמֶת כִּי יַעַבְדוּ אוֹתָם בְּפָרֶךְ וְהָרָאוּי שֶׁיִּגָּאֲלוּ, רַק אַף עַל פִּי כֵן מַה יִּהְיֶה כְּשֶׁאוֹצִיאֵם הֲלֹא זֹאת בֶּטַח אֵין כַּוָּנַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיּוּטַב לָהֶם רַק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,

Second, "and that I should bring forth"—meaning: it is true that the Egyptians are enslaving them with rigor and it is fitting that they be relieved, yet nevertheless, what will be the ultimate purpose once I bring them out? Surely it is not the intention of Hashem, blessed be He, merely to bestow material relief upon them in this world!

וְעַל זֶה הֱשִׁיבוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, עַל הַשְּׁאֵלָה "מִי אָנֹכִי" הֵשִׁיב לוֹ "כִּי אֶהְיֶה עִמָּךְ", הַיְינוּ מֵחֲמַת שֶׁיְּדַעְתִּיךָ כִּי אֵינְךָ נוֹטֶה לְשׁוּם דָּבָר מִצִּדְּךָ, רַק לְמַה שֶּׁאֲנִי שׁוֹלֵחַ לְךָ,

And to this Hashem, blessed be He, answered him: to the question "Who am I?" He replied, "Because I will be with you"—meaning: because I know you, that you do not incline toward anything of your own accord, but solely toward that for which I send you;
כִּי שֵׁם מֹשֶׁה מוֹרֶה עַל זֶה כִּי מִן הַמַּיִם מְשִׁיתִיהוּ הַיְינוּ שֶׁנִּפְשַׁט מִכָּל חֶמְדָּה וַהֲנָאוֹת עַצְמוֹ וְלֹא נִמְצָא בּוֹ שׁוּם גַּאֲוָה מִמַּה שֶּׁהַשְּׁכִינָה מְדַבֶּרֶת עִמּוֹ.

for the very name "Moshe" indicates this—"Because I drew him out of the water"—meaning that he was stripped and drawn out of all personal craving and self-gratification, so that no trace of pride arose in him from the fact that the Shechinah spoke with him.
וְעַל שְׁאֵלַת "וְכִי אוֹצִיא" שֶׁשָּׁאַל, הֲלֹא אֵין כַּוָּנַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לַהֲנָאַת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, הֵשִׁיב לוֹ "בְּהוֹצִיאֲךָ וְכוּלֵי תַּעַבְדוּן אֶת הָאֱלֹקִים" וְכוּלֵי,

And to the second question, "and that I should bring forth"—wherein he asked that surely the intention of Hashem, blessed be He, is not merely for the physical benefit of this world—He replied to him: "When you have brought forth the people out of Egypt, you shall serve God upon this mountain";
הַיְינוּ שֶׁאַכְנִיס אֶתְכֶם תַּחַת עוּלִּי עוֹל תּוֹרָה וְיִהְיֶה לִי עֵסֶק עִמָּכֶם בִּדְבָרִים הַחַיִּים וְקַיָּמִים לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד,
meaning: I will bring you under My yoke, the yoke of the Torah, and My engagement with you will be in spiritual matters that live and endure for all eternity;
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ "וְזֶה לְּךָ הָאוֹת כִּי אָנֹכִי שְׁלַחְתִּיךָ" וְלֹא אָמַר לוֹ כִּי אֲנִי, כִּי אוֹת כָּ"ף מוֹרָה עַל דָּבָר הַקַּיָּם לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד, כַּיָּדוּעַ.

and this is why He said to him, "And this shall be the sign unto you that I (Anokhi) have sent you," rather than saying "that I (Ani)," because the added letter Kaf in Anokhi indicates eternal life that endures forever, as is known.
h:
Moshe’s Humility Before His Mission
That is, he was asking two distinct questions: first, "Who am I?"—meaning that he was beseeching Hashem, blessed be He, to illuminate for him why he was cho…

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Shemot 3
p: לֵךְ וְאָסַפְתָּ וְכוּלֵי וַיַּעַן מֹשֶׁה וַיֹּאמֶר וְהֵן לֹא יַאֲמִינוּ לִי.
"Go, and gather the elders of Israel together," etc. And Moses answered and said, "But behold, they will not believe me."

אַף שֶׁבָּטַח מֹשֶׁה כִּי יַאֲמִינוּ, מֵאַחַר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁלָחוֹ וּבְוַודַּאי יַצְלִיחַ, אַךְ אָמַר כִּי לֹא יֵאוֹת לַשָּׁלִיחַ הַנִּשְׁלָח מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה בְּיָדוֹ כֹּחַ לְהַכְרִיחָם לִשְׁמוֹעַ אֵלָיו וְלֹא שֶׁיָּבֹא אֲלֵיהֶם בְּבַקָּשָׁה.

Even though Moses trusted that they would ultimately believe him—since Hashem, blessed be He, had sent him and his mission would surely succeed—he nevertheless said that it is not befitting a messenger sent by Hashem, blessed be He, to lack the power to compel them to heed him, having instead to come before them with mere entreaties.
"וַיֹּאמֶר מַזֶּה בְּיָדֶךָ וַיֹּאמֶר מַטֶּה וַיֹּאמֶר הַשְׁלִיכֵהוּ אַרְצָה וַיְהִי לְנָחָשׁ".
And Hashem said unto him, "What is that in your hand?" And he said, "A staff." And He said, "Cast it on the ground." And he cast it on the ground, and it became a serpent.
כִּי מַטֶּה רוֹמֵז עַל שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַחַיִּים כִּדְאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (פְּסָחִים סָמֶךְ חֵית עַמּוּד אָלֶף) עֲתִידִים צַדִּיקִים שֶׁיְּחַיּוּ מֵתִים, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "וְאִישׁ מִשְׁעַנְתּוֹ בְּיָדוֹ".

For a "staff" alludes to the root of life, as is stated in the Gemara (Pesachim 68a): In the future the righteous will resurrect the dead, as it is stated (Zechariah 8:4), "and every man with his staff in his hand."

"הַשְׁלִיכֵהוּ אַרְצָה וַיְהִי לְנָחָשׁ", הַיְינוּ שֶׁהֶרְאָה לוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יָצְאוּ הַדְּבָרִים הַלָּלוּ מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הַחַיִּים רַק הוּא גָּוֶון הַנִּרְאֶה לַחַיִּים וּבַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ אֵין בּוֹ מַמָּשׁ, כִּי עַל זֶה רוֹמֵז נָחָשׁ,

"Cast it on the ground, and it became a serpent"—meaning that Hashem showed him that these words of his did not emerge from the true root of life, but were merely an outward semblance of truth that in its root had no substance, which is symbolized by the serpent;
כִּי הָיָה לְךָ לְהָבִין הֲלֹא בִּידֵי לִבּוֹת בְּנֵי אָדָם לְהַטּוֹתָם כְּפִי רְצוֹנִי, אִם שָׁלַחְתִּי אוֹתְךָ הָיָה לְךָ לְהַאֲמִין כִּי אֶשְׁלַח בְּלִבָּם שֶׁיּוּכְרְחוּ לִשְׁמוֹעַ לְךָ.

as if to say: "You should have understood that the hearts of men are in My hand to incline them according to My will; once I sent you, you should have believed that I Myself would place it into their hearts to be compelled to heed you!"
"וַיָּנָס מֹשֶׁה מִפָּנָיו", הַיְינוּ שֶׁהֵבִין טָעוּתוֹ.
"And Moses fled from before it"—meaning that he immediately recognized his error and recoiled from it.

"וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ שְׁלַח יָדְךָ וֶאֱחוֹז בִּזְנָבוֹ", הַיְינוּ שֶׁתְּעַיֵּין בְּזֶה הַדָּבָר עַצְמוֹ אֵיךְ בָּא בְּלִבְּךָ זֶה הָרַעְיוֹן לַחְשׁוֹב כִּי לֹא יַאֲמִינוּ לְךָ, הֲלֹא זֶה עַצְמוֹ גַּם כֵּן אֵינוֹ רַק בִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,

"And Hashem said unto Moses, 'Put forth your hand, and take it by the tail'"—meaning: examine the tail-end of this very matter, how such a thought could have entered your heart to think that they would not believe you, for surely even that thought itself could not have arisen without the will of Hashem, blessed be He!
וְכָאן הֶרְאָה לוֹ שֶׁנִּמְצָא מָקוֹם לִדְבָרָיו כִּי כֵן עָלָה בְּמַחְשָׁבָה שֶׁאֵיזֶה פְּעָמִים יִכָּשְׁלוּ שֶׁלֹּא יַאֲמִינוּ לוֹ הַיְינוּ בְּמַחְלוֹקֶת קֹרַח.

And through this He showed him that there was indeed a future basis for his words, because it had arisen in the Divine Thought that at certain times in the wilderness they would stumble in failing to believe him, such as in the rebellion of Korach.
וְהַשְּׁלֹשָׁה מוֹפְתִים רוֹמְזִים עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה מִכְשׁוֹלִים שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
Indeed, the three signs given here to Moses allude to three future stumblings that Israel would experience in the wilderness:

מוֹפֵת הַמַּטֶּה הָיָה נֶגֶד שֶׁהֵלִינוּ בְּפָרָשַׁת חֻקַּת (בְּמִדְבַּר כָּף אָלֶף, הֵא) "וַיְדַבֵּר הָעָם בֵּאלֹקִים וּבְמֹשֶׁה וְכוּלֵי. וְנַפְשֵׁנוּ קָצָה וְכוּלֵי. וַיְשַׁלַּח הַשֵּׁם בָּעָם אֵת הַנְּחָשִׁים" וְכוּלֵי.

the sign of the staff turning into a serpent corresponded to their complaining in Parashat Chukat (Numbers 21:5–6): "And the people spoke against God, and against Moses... 'and our soul loathes this light bread.' And Hashem sent fiery serpents among the people," etc.
וְעַל זֶה הָיָה תִּיקֻּן "וְהָיָה כָּל הַנָּשׁוּךְ וְהִבִּיט אֶל נְחַשׁ הַנְּחוֹשֶׁת וָחָי", וּלְפִיכָךְ גַּם כָּאן חָזַר הַנָּחָשׁ לְמַטֶּה.

And for that sin there was an immediate rectification—"that everyone who is bitten, when he looks upon the brass serpent, shall live" (Numbers 21:8)—and therefore here too the serpent turned back into a staff of life in his hand.
וְנֶגֶד הַמּוֹפֵת הַשֵּׁנִי "הָבֵא נָא יָדְךָ" וְכוּלֵי, הָיָה נֶגֶד שֶׁדִּבְּרוּ מִרְיָם וְאַהֲרֹן בְּמֹשֶׁה, וְגַם עַל זֶה הָיָה תִּיקֻּן וּלְפִיכָךְ גַּם זֶה חָזַר.

And the second sign—"Put now your hand into your bosom... and behold, his hand was leprous as snow"—corresponded to when Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses and Miriam was stricken with leprosy (Numbers 12:1–10); and since for that too there was a complete healing and rectification, here too his hand was restored as his other flesh.

וְהַמּוֹפֵת הַשְּׁלִישִׁי "וְלָקַחְתָּ מִמֵּימֵי הַיְאוֹר וְהָיָה לְדָם" וְכוּלֵי, זֶה הָיָה נֶגֶד מֵי מְרִיבָה שֶׁנִּרְאֶה לָעַיִן כִּי לֹא נִתְקַן, וְעַל זֶה גַּם כָּאן לֹא מָצִינוּ שֶׁיַּחְזוֹר הַדָּם לְמַיִם.

And the third sign—"that you shall take of the water of the river, and pour it upon the dry land; and the water... shall become blood"—corresponded to the incident of the Waters of Meribah (where the rock zuerst dripped blood, Rashi on Numbers 20:11), which to outward appearances was not rectified in Moses' lifetime (as the decree against entering the Land remained), and therefore here too we do not find that the blood turned back into water.

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Shemot 4
p: וַיֵּלֶךְ וַיִּפְגְּשֵׁהוּ בְּהַר הָאֱלֹקִים וַיִּשַּׁק לוֹ.
And he (Aaron) went, and met him in the mountain of God, and kissed him.
בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה חֵית, הֵא) "חֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת נִפְגָּשׁוּ צֶדֶק וְשָׁלוֹם נָשָׁקוּ", חֶסֶד זֶה אַהֲרֹן וֶאֱמֶת זֶה מֹשֶׁה, צֶדֶק זֶה מֹשֶׁה וְשָׁלוֹם זֶה אַהֲרֹן.

In the Midrash (Shemot Rabbah 5:10; cf. Bereishit Rabbah 8:5) this is expounded on the verse (Psalms 85:11): "Lovingkindness (Chesed) and Truth (Emet) have met together; Righteousness (Tzedek) and Peace (Shalom) have kissed each other"—"Lovingkindness" is Aaron and "Truth" is Moses; "Righteousness" is Moses and "Peace" is Aaron.

וְהִנֵּה אִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (תַּנְחוּמָא שְׁמוֹת כָּף חֵית, אָלֶף) בִּבְרִיאַת הָעוֹלָם שָׁאַל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְחֶסֶד וְאָמַר יִבָּרֵא שֶׁהָעוֹלָם מָלֵא חֲסָדִים, אֱמֶת אוֹמֵר לֹא יִבָּרֵא שֶׁהָעוֹלָם מָלֵא שְׁקָרִים, צֶדֶק אוֹמֵר יִבָּרֵא שֶׁהָעוֹלָם מָלֵא צְדָקוֹת, שָׁלוֹם אוֹמֵר אַל יִבָּרֵא שֶׁהָעוֹלָם מָלֵא קְטָטוֹת. מֶה עָשָׂה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא הִשְׁלִיךְ אֱמֶת אַרְצָה וּבָרָא אֶת הָעוֹלָם וְכוּלֵי.

Now behold, it is stated in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 8:5; cf. Tanchuma Shemot 28) regarding the Creation of the world: When the Holy One, blessed be He, came to create man, He consulted the ministering angels: Lovingkindness (Chesed) said, "Let him be created, because he performs acts of kindness"; Truth (Emet) said, "Let him not be created, because he is full of falsehoods"; Righteousness (Tzedek) said, "Let him be created, because he performs charitable deeds"; Peace (Shalom) said, "Let him not be created, because he is full of strife." What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He took Truth and cast it to the ground, and created the world, etc.

וְהַקֻּשְׁיָא מְפֻרְסֶמֶת מֶה עָשָׂה עִם שָׁלוֹם, הֲלֹא לֹא מָצִינוּ שֶׁהִשְׁלִיךְ גַּם אֶת שָׁלוֹם אַרְצָה, וְגַם כִּי מֹשֶׁה הָיָה אֱמֶת וְצֶדֶק אֵיךְ מִצַּד אֶחָד אוֹמֵר יִבָּרֵא וּמִצַּד הַשֵּׁנִי אָמַר אַל יִבָּרֵא.

And the famous question is asked: What did He do with Peace, which also opposed creation? After all, we do not find that He cast Peace to the ground as well! Furthermore, since Moses embodied both Truth and Righteousness, how could he say from one side (Truth) "let him not be created," and from the other side (Righteousness) "let him be created"?
וְהָעִנְיָן בָּזֶה, אֱמֶת אוֹמֵר אַל יִבָּרֵא וְגַם מֹשֶׁה שֶׁהָיָה מִדָּתוֹ אֱמֶת מְאֹד הִרְעִים בְּנַפְשׁוֹ מַדּוּעַ דֶּרֶךְ רְשָׁעִים צָלֵחָה,

The inner meaning of this is as follows: strict "Truth" says "let it not be created," and Moses too, whose innate attribute was uncompromising Truth, was deeply agitated in his soul as to why the way of the wicked prospers in this world—
וְאֵיךְ יוּכַל פַּרְעֹה לַעֲבֹד עִם יִשְׂרָאֵל וְיִשְׂרָאֵל יִהְיוּ נִכְנָעִים מִפָּנָיו הֲלֹא הוּא בְּשֶׁקֶר כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת פַּרְעֹה הוּא רָשָׁע גָּמוּר, וְזֹאת הִרְעִים בְּלֵב מֹשֶׁה.

how could Pharaoh be allowed to enslave Israel while Israel stood subjugated before him? Surely that is a blatant falsehood, since in truth Pharaoh is utterly wicked! And this indignation thundered in Moses' heart.
וְאַהֲרֹן אָחִיו הָיָה מִדָּתוֹ מִדַּת חֶסֶד וְהוּא לִמֵּד תָּמִיד דַּעַת לִסְבֹּל הַכֹּל וּלְקַבֵּל בְּאַהֲבָה בְּלִי שׁוּם טַעֲנָה נֶגֶד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.

His brother Aaron, by contrast, embodied the attribute of Lovingkindness (Chesed), and he constantly taught the mindset of bearing everything patiently and accepting God's decree with love, without harboring any complaint against Hashem, blessed be He.
וְזֶה בֵּאֵר (תַּנְחוּמָא שְׁמוֹת יוֹד, יוֹד אָלֶף) "מִי שָׂם פֶּה לָאָדָם" אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִי נָתַן עֵצָה לִבְרֹחַ מִפְּנֵי פַּרְעֹה,

And this explains what is stated in the Midrash (Tanchuma, Shemot 10) on the verse "Who has made man's mouth?"—Rabbi Yochanan said: Who gave you the counsel and ability to flee from before Pharaoh when he sought to kill you?

הַיְנוּ שֶׁאָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה מִי שָׁלַח בְּלִבְּךָ לִבְרֹחַ, הֲלֹא זֹאת הִיא מִדּוֹת אַהֲרֹן וְהִיא נֶגֶד מִדָּתְךָ, כִּי מִדָּתְךָ הִיא אֱמֶת וּלְפִי מִדָּתְךָ לֹא צָרַכְתָּ לִבְרֹחַ מִפְּנֵי פַּרְעֹה הָרָשָׁע, רַק אֲנִי לִמַּדְתִּי אוֹתְךָ אָז מִדַּת סַבְלָנוּת,

That is, the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses: "Who placed it into your heart to flee rather than stand and fight? Surely yielding and fleeing belongs to the attribute of Aaron and is contrary to your own innate nature! For your attribute is uncompromising Truth, and according to your nature you would never have fled before the wicked Pharaoh; rather, it was I Who taught you then the attribute of patient endurance (savlanut)!"

וְהִנֵּה מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אַחֲרֵי שֶׁבָּרַח מִפְּנֵי פַּרְעֹה לָמַד דַּעַת לִהְיוֹת סַבְלָן, וְזֶה הָעִנְיָן שֶׁנִּרְאָה אֵלָיו הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בַּסְּנֶה לְלַמְּדוֹ זֹאת הַמִּדָּה וְהֶרְאָה לוֹ שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹכֵן בַּסְּנֶה הַיְנוּ סַבְלָן גָּדוֹל כִּי "עִמּוֹ אָנֹכִי בְצָרָה" וְהוּא סַבְלָן נֶגֶד פַּרְעֹה.

And behold, after Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, fled from Pharaoh, he learned the wisdom of being patient and long-suffering; and this is why the Holy One, blessed be He, appeared to him specifically in a lowly thornbush (seneh): to teach him this attribute, showing him that He Himself dwells amidst the thorns—meaning that He is the Supreme Patient One, for "I am with him in distress" (Psalms 91:15), patiently bearing the provocation of Pharaoh until the appointed time.

וְזֶה הָעִנְיָן שֶׁבֵּרַךְ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אֶת יוֹסֵף (דְּבָרִים לָמֶד גִּימֶל, טֵית זַיִן) "וּרְצוֹן שֹׁכְנִי סְנֶה", כִּי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה רוֹצֶה לְהַכְנִיס מִדּוֹת סַבְלָנוּת לְתוֹךְ מִדָּתוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק,

And this is why Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, later blessed the tribe of Joseph with the words (Deuteronomy 33:16), "and the goodwill of Him Who dwelt in the thornbush": because Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, wanted to infuse this attribute of patient forbearance into the strict halakhic attribute of Joseph the Righteous,

כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מָלֵא רָצוֹן עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה לוֹ שׁוּם תַּרְעוֹמוֹת עַל נֶפֶשׁ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, כִּי מִשֵּׁבֶט הַזֶּה מִתְעוֹרֵר דִּין עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּעֵת שֶׁנּוֹטִים מֵרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.

so that Joseph would be filled with favorable goodwill toward Israel and harbor no prosecutorial grievance against any soul of Israel; for as explained earlier, from this tribe of Joseph strict judgment is aroused against Israel when they deviate from the will of Hashem, blessed be He,

כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ שֶׁהַנָּבִיא הִזְהִיר אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל אָמַר לָהֶם (עָמוֹס הֵא, וָאו) "פֶּן יִצְלַח כָּאֵשׁ בֵּית יוֹסֵף" וְהַיְנוּ שֶׁמִּדָּתוֹ לֹא תִכְעֹס וְיִהְיֶה בְּרָצוֹן עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל, עַל כֵּן אָמַר "וּרְצוֹן שֹׁכְנִי סְנֶה", הַיְנוּ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יְלַמֵּד אוֹתְךָ מִדּוֹת סַבְלָנוּת כְּמוֹ שֶׁלִּמֵּד אוֹתִי בַּסְּנֶה.

as we find the prophet warning Israel (Amos 5:6), "lest the house of Joseph break out like fire"—therefore, so that Joseph's attribute would not flare up in anger but remain in goodwill toward Israel, Moses blessed him with "the goodwill of Him Who dwelt in the thornbush," praying: "May Hashem, blessed be He, teach you the attribute of patient forbearance just as He taught me at the thornbush!"
וְכַאֲשֶׁר נִשְׁתַּוָּה בְּלֵב מֹשֶׁה זֹאת הַמִּדָּה, נַעֲשָׂה שָׁלוֹם לִגְאֹל אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
And once this attribute of patient forbearance became integrated within Moses' heart, complete harmony was achieved between him and Aaron to redeem Israel;
וְזֶה פֵּרוּשׁ "חֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת נִפְגָּשׁוּ", פְּגִישָׁה הַיְנוּ שֶׁהָיוּ מִתְנַגְּדִים זֶה לָזֶה, כִּי אַהֲרֹן הָיָה מִדּוֹת חֶסֶד וְאָמַר יִבָּרֵא וּמֹשֶׁה הָיָה מִדּוֹת אֱמֶת וְאָמַר אַל יִבָּרֵא,

and this resolves the Midrash on "Lovingkindness and Truth have met together": initially "meeting" (pegishah) denotes clashing in opposition to one another, for Aaron was the attribute of Lovingkindness who said "let the world be created," while Moses was the attribute of strict Truth who said "let it not be created";

וְהִנֵּה כַּאֲשֶׁר הֻצְרַךְ מֹשֶׁה לָנוּס מִפַּרְעֹה אָז נִקְרָא (דָּנִיֵּאל חֵית, יוֹד בֵּית) "וְתַשְׁלֵךְ אֱמֶת אַרְצָה", וְאָז נִשְׁתַּוָּה מִדַּת הָאֱמֶת לְחֶסֶד וְנַעֲשָׂה מִמִּדּוֹת אֱמֶת צֶדֶק הַיְנוּ כְּאַהֲרֹן וְאָמַר גַּם כֵּן יִבָּרֵא,

yet when Moses had to flee from Pharaoh and learn patience, that corresponded to "He cast Truth to the ground" (Daniel 8:12), whereby the uncompromising attribute of Truth was softened and harmonized with Lovingkindness, transforming strict "Truth" (Emet) into charitable "Righteousness" (Tzedek)—aligning with Aaron to likewise say "let him be created"!

וְאָז כְּשֶׁנִּשְׁתַּווּ, אָז "צֶדֶק וְשָׁלוֹם נָשָׁקוּ", הַיְנוּ כִּי אָז גַּם שָׁלוֹם אָמַר יִבָּרֵא, כִּי מַה שֶּׁשָּׁלוֹם אָמַר תְּחִלָּה אַל יִבָּרֵא [שֶׁלֹּא] הָיָה רוֹצֶה לִהְיוֹת בְּמַחְלֹקֶת נֶגֶד מִדּוֹת הָאֱמֶת, כִּי מִדָּתוֹ הוּא שָׁלוֹם,

And once they were harmonized, then "Righteousness and Peace have kissed each other"—meaning that at that point Peace too automatically said "let him be created"! For the only reason Peace had initially said "let him not be created" was because it did not want to be in conflict against the attribute of Truth, since its very essence is peace;
אֲבָל עַתָּה שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה מֵאֱמֶת צֶדֶק וְאוֹמֵר יִבָּרֵא אָז לֹא הָיָה שָׁלוֹם אוֹמֵר אַל יִבָּרֵא, וְאָז "צֶדֶק וְשָׁלוֹם נָשָׁקוּ" אִתְדַּבְּקוּתָא רוּחָא בְּרוּחָא.

so now that strict Truth had been transformed into Righteousness (Tzedek) and agreed "let him be created," Peace no longer opposed creation either, and then "Righteousness and Peace kissed each other" in a complete cleaving of spirit to spirit!

p: וַיֹּאמֶר לָמָה הֲרֵעוֹתָ.
And Moses returned unto Hashem, and said, "Lord, why have You done evil to this people?"
הִנֵּה לְפִי הָרְאוּת, הוּא פֶּלֶא אֵיךְ יָצָא מִפִּי מֹשֶׁה דָּבָר כָּזֶה נֶגֶד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
Behold, at first glance it is a wonder how such a sharp question against Hashem, blessed be He, could issue from the mouth of Moses!

אַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה אוֹהֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכַאֲשֶׁר שָׁמַע מִפִּי הַגְּבוּרָה, כִּי יִצְטָרְכוּ לִהְיוֹת עוֹד בְּמִצְרַיִם עַד אַחַר הַמַּכּוֹת שֶׁיַּעַבְרוּ עַל מִצְרַיִם, אָז שָׁאַל הֲלֹא בְּיָדְךָ בְּרֶגַע אֶחָד לִפְדּוֹת אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל,

However, in truth Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, was a devoted lover of Israel, and when he heard from the mouth of the Almighty that Israel would have to remain in Egypt for an entire year until all the Ten Plagues had passed over Egypt, he asked: "Surely it is in Your hand to redeem Israel in a single instant!

וְלָמָּה יִהְיוּ בְּמִצְרַיִם שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חוֹדֶשׁ לִרְאוֹת הַמַּכּוֹת שֶׁיִּפְחֲדוּ מִפְּנֵיהֶם כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (דְּבָרִים כָּף חֵית, סָמֶךְ) "אֲשֶׁר יָגֹרְתָּ מִפְּנֵיהֶם", כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת יָרְאוּ גַּם יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵהַמַּכּוֹת, וְלָכֵן שָׁאַל זֹאת מֵהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,

Why must they remain in Egypt for twelve months witnessing these terrifying plagues of which they themselves will be afraid—as it is written (Deuteronomy 28:60), 'all the diseases of Egypt, which you were afraid of'—for in truth Israel too experienced dread at the sight of the plagues?" Therefore he asked this of the Holy One, blessed be He;

וְהֶרְאָה לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא כִּי גַּם בָּזֶה יֵשׁ צוֹרֶךְ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הָיָה לָהֶם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל אֵיזֶה שַׁיָּכוּת עִם מִצְרַיִם כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (דְּבָרִים דָּלֶת, לָמֶד דָּלֶת) "לָקַחַת לוֹ גוֹי מִקֶּרֶב גּוֹי".

and the Holy One, blessed be He, showed him that this too was necessary for Israel's own purification: for in truth Israel had become intertwined with Egypt, as it is written (Deuteronomy 4:34), "to take Him a nation from the midst of another nation"—

הַיְינוּ כְּעוּבָּר הַנִּשְׁמָט מִבֶּטֶן אִמּוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שַׁיָּכוּת עִם אִמּוֹ, וְלָכֵן הֻצְרְכוּ גַּם הֵם לְהִתְבָּרֵר וְלִפְחוֹד מֵהֶם וְזֶה הַפַּחַד הָיָה מְזַכֵּךְ אֶת לִבָּם כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (בְּרָכוֹת נּוּן טֵית עַמּוּד אָלֶף) "לֹא נִבְרְאוּ רְעָמִים אֶלָּא כְּדֵי לִפְשׁוֹט עַקְמִימוּת שֶׁבַּלֵּב".

like a fetus being extracted from its mother's womb, which still has an attachment to its mother—and therefore Israel too needed to be refined by experiencing awe and dread during the plagues, for that very fear purified their hearts, just as we find in the Gemara (Berakhot 59a): "Thunderclaps were created solely to straighten out the crookedness in the heart."

וְזֶה בֵּאוּר הַפָּסוּק בְּשִׁיר שֶׁל פְּגָעִים (תְּהִלִּים צָדִי אָלֶף, חֵית) "רַק בְּעֵינֶיךָ תַבִּיט וְשִׁלֻּמַת רְשָׁעִים תִּרְאֶה". הַיְינוּ שֶׁאַתָּה מוּצְרָךְ לִרְאוֹת שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה הַפַּחַד יִתְבָּרֵר עַקְמִימוּת לִבְּךָ לְטוֹב.

And this is the meaning of the verse in the Psalm of Afflictions (Psalms 91:8): "Only with your eyes shall you behold, and see the retribution of the wicked"—meaning that while no harm will touch you, you yourself need to behold it with your eyes, so that through that awe the crookedness of your heart will be clarified for the good.
h:
Moshe’s Complaint and the Mystery of Redemption
Behold, at first glance it is a wonder how such a sharp question against Hashem, blessed be He, could issue from the mouth of Moses!

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Vaera 1
p: וַיְדַבֵּר אֱלֹקִים אֶל מֹשֶׁה וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו אֲנִי הַשֵּׁם.
And God (Elokim) spoke (vayedaber) unto Moses, and said (vayomer) unto him, "I am Hashem."

אַחַר שֶׁדִּבֵּר מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם דְּבָרָיו נֶגֶד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, עַל כֵּן נָתַן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ גְּעָרָה עָלָיו וְזֶה לְשׁוֹן "וַיְדַבֵּר" שֶׁהוּא לָשׁוֹן קָשֶׁה, גַּם הַשֵּׁם "אֱלֹקִים" מוֹרֶה עַל זֶה,

After Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, spoke his sharp words ("Why have You done evil to this people?") before Hashem, blessed be He, Hashem, blessed be He, issued a stern rebuke to him—indicated by the expression "vayedaber" (spoke), which is a harsh expression, as well as the Name "Elokim" (the attribute of strict Judgment);
אַךְ תֵּיכֶף "וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו" זֶהוּ כְּאָדָם שֶׁכּוֹעֵס עַל חֲבֵירוֹ וְאוֹהֲבוֹ וְכַאֲשֶׁר רוֹאֵהוּ עוֹמֵד וּמִשְׁתּוֹמֵם וּמְפַחֵד, אָז מְרַמֵּז לוֹ כִּי כָל כַּעֲסוֹ אֵינוֹ רַק לְפָנִים.

yet immediately the verse shifts to "and He said (vayomer) unto him, 'I am Hashem'": this is like a person who displays anger toward his beloved friend in public, and when he sees his friend standing stunned and terrified, he quietly signals to him that all his anger is merely for outward appearances.

וְכֵן הוּא הָעִנְיָן שֶׁל "וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו אֲנִי הַשֵּׁם", כִּי אֲמִירָה לָשׁוֹן רַכָּה הַיְינוּ שֶׁלָּחַשׁ לוֹ שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּכַעַס חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, וְזֶה עִנְיָן "אֲנִי הַשֵּׁם" כִּי שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה בָּרוּךְ הוּא הוּא מָלֵא רַחֲמִים, וְהַגְּעָרָה שֶׁגָּעַרְתִּי בְּךָ לֹא הָיָה רַק לְפָנִים, וְלֹא תְפַחֵד כְּלָל.

And such is the meaning of "and He said unto him, 'I am Hashem'": for amirah ("saying") is a gentle expression, meaning that He whispered to him that He was not truly angry at him, Heaven forbid; and this is signified by "I am Hashem," for the Name Havayah, blessed be He, is filled with pure mercy—as if to say: "The rebuke with which I rebuked you was only on the surface (before the Heavenly Court), so do not be afraid at all!"
h:
Vayedaber and Vayomer: Divine Judgment and Compassion
After Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, spoke his sharp words ("Why have You done evil to this people?") before Hashem, blessed be He, Hashem, blessed b…

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Vaera 2
p: וַיְדַבֵּר אֱלֹקִים אֶל מֹשֶׁה וְכוּלֵי וָאֵרָא וְכוּלֵי.
And God spoke unto Moses... "And I appeared unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob," etc.

הַיְינוּ אַחַר שֶׁאָמַר מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא הֲלֹא בְּכֹחֲךָ לִגְאוֹל תֵּיכֶף אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְלָמָּה הֲרֵעוֹתָ לְסַדֵּר הַסֵּדֶר הַזֶּה, לָזֶה אָמַר לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיֵּלֵךְ אֶל יִשְׂרָאֵל וְלֹא שָׁמְעוּ אֵלָיו.

That is, after Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, said to the Holy One, blessed be He, "Surely it is in Your power to redeem Israel immediately, so why have You arranged this drawn-out process?"—Hashem, blessed be He, told him to go speak to Israel, "and they hearkened not unto Moses for anguish of spirit and for cruel bondage."
וְהֶרְאָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה רָאֹה כִּי עוֹדֶנּוּ לֹא נִשְׁלַם הַבֵּירוּר וְלֹא הִגִּיעַ הָעֵת לִגְמוֹר הַגְּאוּלָּה,
Through this the Holy One, blessed be He, showed Moses: "See for yourself that their spiritual clarification is not yet complete, and the time has not yet arrived to consummate the redemption!"
וְלָזֶה נֶאֱמַר אַחַר כָּךְ "אֵלֶּה רָאשֵׁי בֵית אֲבוֹתָם" וְיִחֲסָם וְנִמְצְאוּ אַרְבָּעִים וַחֲמִשָּׁה רָאשֵׁי אַלְפֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
And for this reason Scripture immediately records the genealogy, "These are the heads of their fathers' houses" (Exodus 6:14–25), enumerating forty-five ancestral heads of Israel up to Pinchas,

וְהֶרְאָה לוֹ שֶׁגַּם אֵלּוּ אַרְבָּעִים וַחֲמִשָּׁה רָאשִׁים צְרִיכִים עוֹד לְבֵרוּרִים עַד הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁהוּא פִּנְחָס אַף שֶׁנִּרְאֶה שֶׁנִּתְבָּרֵר בַּכֹּל, עַד שֶׁזָּכָה לִבְרִית שָׁלוֹם מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְאַחַר זְמַן נִתְגַּלָּה לוֹ שֶׁיִּצְטָרֵךְ עוֹד לְבֵירוּר, כִּי וָא"ו דְּשָׁלוֹם קְטִיעָה הִיא,

showing him that even these forty-five exalted leaders still required further clarifications down to the very last one listed, namely Pinchas—who, even after he appeared to be completely clarified and merited the "covenant of peace" from Hashem, blessed be He (Numbers 25:12), was later shown that he still required further clarification (in the concubine of Gibeah and Jephthah's daughter), which is why the letter Vav in the word shalom ("peace") is written with a broken stroke in the Torah scroll!

וְהַפָּרָשָׁה הַזֹּאת תְּחַיֵּיב יִרְאָה לְכָל גְּדוֹלֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְזֶהוּ (דְּבָרִים יוֹד, יוֹד בֵּית) "מָה הַשֵּׁם אֱלֹקֶיךָ שֹׁאֵל מֵעִמָּךְ כִּי אִם לְיִרְאָה" וְכוּלֵי רוֹמֵז לְאַרְבָּעִים וַחֲמִשָּׁה מִינֵי יִרְאוֹת.

And this genealogical passage instills awe and self-scrutiny into all the great leaders of Israel; and this is alluded to in the verse (Deuteronomy 10:12): "What (מָ"ה — numerically 45) does Hashem your God ask of you, but to fear," etc., corresponding to these forty-five levels of awe.

That is, after Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, said to the Holy One, blessed be He, "Surely it is in Your power to redeem Israel immediately, so why h…

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Vaera 3
p: בֹּא דַּבֵּר אֶל פַּרְעֹה מֶלֶךְ מִצְרָיִם וְכוּלֵי.
"Go in, speak unto Pharaoh king of Egypt," etc.
בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (תַּנְחוּמָא וָאֵרָא בֵּית) הַמָּשָׁל אוֹמֵר מִן שִׁטַּיָּא לֵית הֲנָיָא אֶלָּא מִן קוֹצַיָּא.
In the Midrash (Shemot Rabbah 6:5; cf. Tanchuma Va'era 2): The proverb says, "There is no appreciation for the acacia trees except alongside the thornbushes."
בֵּאֵר הַמִּדְרָשׁ דְּהִנֵּה פַּרְעֹה לֹא שָׁמַע אֶל מֹשֶׁה וְגַם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל כְּתִיב "וְלֹא שָׁמְעוּ" וְכוּלֵי,
The explanation of the Midrash is that behold, Pharaoh did not listen to Moses, and regarding Israel too it is written, "and they did not listen to Moses";

וְזֶהוּ מִן שִׁטַּיָּא לֵית הֲנָיָא הַיְינוּ אִילָן טוֹב הַנִּקְרָא שִׁטִּים וְאֵין יְכוֹלִין לַעֲשׂוֹת מִמֶּנּוּ כְּלוּם וְלֵית הֲנָיָא מִינֵיהּ, רַק מִן קוֹצַיָּא הַיְינוּ מִן אִילָן שֶׁהוּא מָלֵא קוֹצִים מִזֶּה נִכָּר הַיִּתְרוֹן שֶׁל אִילָן הַשִּׁטִּים,

and this is the meaning of the proverb: when one looks at a good, non-fruit-bearing tree like the acacia (shittim) by itself, since one cannot eat from it, its virtue is not appreciated—until one encounters a thorny bramble-bush (kotzaya), and from the contrast with the thornbush the superiority of the acacia tree is recognized!
כִּי הַקּוֹץ הוּא יַכְאִיב וְהַשִּׁטִּים אַף שֶׁאֵין יְכוֹלִין לַעֲשׂוֹת מִמֶּנּוּ כְּלוּם, מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵינוֹ מַכְאִיב וְאֵינוֹ מַזִּיק כְּלוּם,
For the thornbush pricks and inflicts pain, whereas the acacia tree, even when it yields no immediate fruit, neither pricks nor harms anyone;

כָּךְ הַחִילּוּק אַף שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל גַּם כֵּן לֹא שָׁמְעוּ אֵלָיו, לֹא הָיָה רַק מִקֹּצֶר רוּחַ אֲבָל אַחַר כָּךְ יִשְׁמְעוּ אֵלָיו, וּפַרְעֹה חֵרֵף וְגִדֵּף וּמִמֶּנּוּ יוּכַּר יִתְרוֹן בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.

so too is the difference here: even though Israel also failed to listen to Moses at that moment, it was only out of crushed spirit and exhaustion, and afterward they would heed him, whereas when Moses went to Pharaoh, Pharaoh blasphemed and reviled God ("Who is Hashem that I should heed His voice?")—so that from Pharaoh's thorny wickedness the preciousness of the children of Israel was recognized!
h:
Moshe Is Sent to Confront Pharaoh
5; cf. Tanchuma Va'era 2): The proverb says, "There is no appreciation for the acacia trees except alongside the thornbushes

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Vaera 4
p: עִנְיַן הַשֶּׁבַע מַכּוֹת שֶׁבַּסֵּדֶר הַזֶּה. הֵם נֶגֶד פָּסוּק (מִשְׁלֵי וָאו, טֵית זַיִן) "שֵׁשׁ הֵנָּה שָׂנֵא הַשֵּׁם וְשֶׁבַע תּוֹעֲבוֹת נַפְשׁוֹ".

The matter of the seven plagues recorded in this Torah portion (Va'era): they correspond to the seven evils enumerated in the verse (Proverbs 6:16–19): "There are six things which Hashem hates, yes, seven which are an abomination unto His soul: (1) haughty eyes, (2) a lying tongue, (3) and hands that shed innocent blood; (4) a heart that devises wicked thoughts, (5) feet that are swift in running to evil; (6) a false witness that breathes out lies, (7) and he that sows discord among brethren."

[וְזֹאת תֵּדַע שֶׁכָּל הָעֳנָשִׁין שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּעוֹלָם אֲפִילּוּ אֵצֶל הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת כְּגוֹן שֶׁלִּפְעָמִים מַשְׁפִּילִים שַׂר אֶחָד וְנוֹתְנִים מֶמְשָׁלָה לְאֶחָד הַכֹּל הוּא מֵהַמִּידּוֹת הָרָעוֹת הַנִּזְכָּרִים בַּפָּסוּק "שֵׁשׁ הֵנָּה שָׂנֵא הַשֵּׁם" וְגוֹמֵר. תַּשְׁלוּם.] [

And know this: that all the punishments that occur in the world, even among the nations of the world—such as when one minister or ruler is brought low and dominion is given to another—all stem from the seven corrupt traits enumerated in the verse "There are six things which Hashem hates," etc. End of addendum.

] רַק שְׁלֹמֹה חָשַׁב לְסַדֵּר הָעֲווֹנוֹת, לְפִיכָךְ סִדֵּר תְּחִילָּה עָוֹן קַל וְאַחַר כָּךְ הֶחָמוּר, וְכָאן כְּשֶׁנֶּעֶנְשׁוּ מִצְרַיִם עַל כָּל הָעֲווֹנוֹת הַלָּלוּ שֶׁהָיוּ מְשׁוּקָּעִים בְּלִבָּם נֶעֶנְשׁוּ תְּחִילָּה עַל הֶחָמוּר.

The only difference in order is that King Solomon was listing the sins from the lightest to the most severe, whereas here, when the Egyptians were punished for all seven of these iniquities that were deeply entrenched in their hearts, they were punished in reverse order, beginning with the most severe:

מַכַּת דָּם הוּא נֶגֶד "מְשַׁלֵּחַ מְדָנִים בֵּין אַחִים", כִּי עִיקַּר הַהַרְחָקָה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא מִדַּת הַכַּעַס, כִּי אַף שֶׁהַתַּאֲוָה גַּם כֵּן מְרוּחֶקֶת מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, אַךְ עוֹד יוּכַל לְהִמָּצֵא בָּהּ טוֹב אֲבָל מִדַּת כַּעַס הוּא בְּיוֹתֵר מְרוּחָק מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.

(1) The plague of Blood (Dam) corresponded to the seventh and worst abomination, "he that sows discord among brethren"—for the primary alienation from Hashem, blessed be He, is the attribute of anger and strife (which heats the blood); because even though lust is also far from Hashem, blessed be He, a spark of goodness (love) can still be salvaged from it, whereas the attribute of anger and division is furthest removed from Hashem, blessed be He.

וְנֶגֶד "יָפִיחַ כְּזָבִים עֵד שָׁקֶר" הָיָה מַכַּת צְפַרְדֵּעַ, כִּי הַמִּצְרִים הָיוּ מְפִיחִים כְּזָבִים עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁלְּשׁוֹן יָפִיחַ הוּא, שֶׁכָּל דָּבָר קָטָן הָיוּ מְפִיחִים וּמַגְדִּילִים אוֹתוֹ,

(2) And corresponding to the sixth sin, "a false witness that breathes out (yafi'ach) lies," came the plague of Frogs (Tzfardea): for the Egyptians used to puff up and inflate false accusations against Israel—as the word yafi'ach denotes blowing up and exaggerating every minor fault;

כִּי בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הַדִּין הוּא אַף כְּשֶׁאֶחָד רוֹאֶה בַּחֲבֵירוֹ שֶׁחָטָא וְאֵין עֵדִים בַּדָּבָר רַק הוּא לְבַדּוֹ רָאָה, אָסוּר לוֹ לְהַגִּיד כִּי הַאי מַעֲשֶׂה דְּטוֹבִיָּה חָטָא (פְּסָחִים קוּף יוֹד גִּימֶל עַמּוּד בֵּית),

for among Israel the law is that even when a person sees his fellow commit an actual sin, if there are no two valid witnesses to the matter and he alone saw it, he is strictly forbidden to testify or publicize it, like the incident of "Toviyah sinned and Zigud alone testified and was lashed" (Pesachim 113b)—
וְהוּא מִפְּנֵי כְּשֶׁאֵין עֵדִים בַּדָּבָר אָז רְאָיָה כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לֹא יִרְצֶה בְּפִרְסוּם הַחֵטְא וְרוֹצֶה לְהַסְתִּיר אוֹתוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וּלְפִיכָךְ אָסוּר לְפַרְסְמוֹ,

and the inner reason for this is that when Providence arranges that there are no two witnesses to a sin, that itself is proof that Hashem, blessed be He, does not desire the publicizing of that sin and wishes to conceal it in this world, and therefore a single observer is forbidden to publicize it!
אֲבָל הֵם הָיוּ מְפַרְסְמִים מְאוֹד לָכֵן בָּא עֲלֵיהֶם מַכַּת צְפַרְדְּעִים שֶׁהֵם גַּם כֵּן מְקַרְקְרִים וְהוֹמִים וְלֹא הָיוּ הַמִּצְרִים יְכוֹלִין לְהַשְׁמִיעַ אֶת קוֹלָם.

The Egyptians, however, used to loudly publicize and inflate every accusation against Israel; therefore the plague of frogs came upon them, croaking and roaring incessantly so that the Egyptians could not even hear their own voices.

וְנֶגֶד "רַגְלַיִם מְמַהֲרוֹת לָרוּץ לָרָעָה" הָיָה מַכַּת כִּנִּים, כִּי אֵצֶל יִשְׂרָאֵל נֶאֱמַר (יְשַׁעְיָה אָלֶף, כָּף אָלֶף) "צֶדֶק יָלִין בָּהּ", הַיְינוּ שֶׁהָיוּ מַלִּינִים אֶת הַדִּין אַף בְּדָבָר שֶׁהָיוּ יוֹדְעִים שֶׁהַדִּין עִמָּהֶם, אַף עַל פִּי כֵן לֹא הָיוּ מְמַהֲרִים מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָיוּ רוֹצִים לְצַדֵּד וְלִמְצוֹא עוֹד זְכוּת,

(3) And corresponding to the fifth sin, "feet that are swift in running to evil," came the plague of Lice (Kinnim): for regarding Israel it is stated (Isaiah 1:21), "righteousness lodged overnight (yalin) in her," meaning that the judges of Israel used to hold a capital case overnight (Sanhedrin 32a) even when they already saw that the law inclined toward conviction, refusing to rush to judgment because they wanted to deliberate further and find some merit to acquit;

וְהַמִּצְרִים הָיוּ לְהֵיפֶךְ שֶׁהָיוּ מְמַהֲרִים לְצַעֵר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל אַךְ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּחֶמְלָתוֹ שְׁמָרָם וְלֹא פָּעֲלוּ כְּלוּם אַף בִּמְהִירָתָם, וְנֶגֶד זֶה הָיָה מַכַּת כִּנִּים כִּי בִּבְרִיאָה קְטַנָּה נִמְצָא גַּם כֵּן מְהִירוּת הַתְּנוּעָה, אַךְ מַה יִּפְעוֹל עִם כָּל מְהִירָתוֹ הֲלֹא קָטָן הוּא.

whereas the Egyptians were the exact opposite, rushing swiftly to afflict and destroy Israel—yet Hashem, blessed be He, in His compassion guarded Israel ("the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied"), so that the Egyptians accomplished nothing with all their frantic haste; and corresponding to this came the plague of tiny lice, for a tiny insect also darts about with rapid movement, yet what can it accomplish with all its scurrying when it is so puny and insignificant?

וְנֶגֶד "לֵב חוֹרֵשׁ מַחְשְׁבוֹת אָוֶן", הָיָה מַכַּת עָרוֹב, לְפִי שֶׁהָיוּ מְחַשְּׁבִים עֵצוֹת לְהָרַע לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, עַל כֵּן הָיָה מַכַּת עָרוֹב עִרְבּוּב שֶׁל חַיּוֹת רָעוֹת נֶגֶד עִרְבּוּב שֶׁל מַחֲשָׁבוֹת רָעוֹת שֶׁהָיָה בְּמַחְשַׁבְתָּם,

(4) And corresponding to the fourth sin, "a heart that devises wicked thoughts," came the plague of Arov (a wild mixture of beasts): because they were constantly scheming wicked plots ("Come, let us deal wisely with them") to harm Israel, the plague of Arov brought a chaotic mixture (irbuv) of ferocious beasts upon them, measure for measure against the chaotic mixture of malicious schemes in their minds;
וְלָזֶה נֶאֱמַר בְּמַכַּת עָרוֹב "וְהִפְלֵיתִי וְכוּלֵי לְבִלְתִּי הֱיוֹת שָׁם עָרֹב", הַיְינוּ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יְבָרֵר אֲשֶׁר לֹא נִמְצָא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל שׁוּם עִרְבּוּב בְּמַחְשַׁבְתָּם.

and for this reason it is specifically stated regarding the plague of Arov, "And I will set apart in that day the land of Goshen, in which My people dwell, that no mixture of wild beasts (arov) shall be there"—signifying that Hashem, blessed be He, testified and clarified that within the minds of Israel there is no chaotic mixture of impure thoughts.
וְנֶגֶד "יָדַיִם שׁוֹפְכוֹת דָּם נָקִי" הָיָה מַכַּת דֶּבֶר.
(5) And corresponding to the third sin, "hands that shed innocent blood," came the lethal plague of Pestilence (Dever).
וְנֶגֶד "לְשׁוֹן שָׁקֶר" הִיא מַכַּת שְׁחִין, לַאֲשֶׁר הֵעֵזוּ פְּנֵיהֶם בְּדִבְרֵי שֶׁקֶר, לָכֵן נִתְבַּיְּשׁוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב "וְלֹא יָכְלוּ הַחַרְטֻמִּים לַעֲמוֹד לִפְנֵי מֹשֶׁה".

(6) And corresponding to the second sin, "a lying tongue," came the plague of Boils (Shechin, which regularly comes as a punishment for lashon hara and falsehood, Arachin 15b): because they brazenly hardened their faces with words of falsehood, they were publicly shamed and covered with boils, as it is written, "And the magicians could not stand before Moses because of the boils."

וְנֶגֶד "עֵינַיִם רָמוֹת", הַיְינוּ שֶׁהָיוּ מִתְגָּאִים בְּעַצְמָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם הַשְׁפָּעוֹת כָּל טוּב הֶרְאָה לָהֶם מַכַּת בָּרָד, כִּי עִיקַּר הַהַשְׁפָּעָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא גֶּשֶׁם רְאוּ אֵיךְ הַגֶּשֶׁם שֶׁבָּא מִצִּדְּכֶם הוּא בָּרָד,

(7) And corresponding to the first sin, "haughty eyes"—namely that the Egyptians boasted arrogantly that they possessed the independent abundance of all bounty (through the Nile without needing Heaven)—He showed them the plague of Hail (Barad): for the primary heavenly bounty in this world is rain, as if to say, "See how the precipitation that falls on your account is destructive hail of ice and fire!"

וְלָזֶה הָיָה מַכָּה זוֹ עַל יְדֵי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב "נְטֵה אֶת יָדְךָ" כִּי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה מְבוֹרָר בַּמִּדָּה הַזֹּאת כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּמִדְבַּר יוֹד בֵּית, גִּימֶל) "וְהָאִישׁ מֹשֶׁה עָנָיו" וְכוּלֵי.

And for this reason the plague of Hail was brought about directly through the hand of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him—as it is written, "Stretch forth your hand toward heaven, that there may be hail"—because to counter their "haughty eyes," Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, was utterly perfected in the opposite attribute of humility, as it is written (Numbers 12:3): "Now the man Moses was exceedingly humble, more than any man upon the face of the earth."
h:
The Seven Plagues and the Seven Abominations
The only difference in order is that King Solomon was listing the sins from the lightest to the most severe, whereas here, when the Egyptians were punished…

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Bo 1
p: וַיָּבֹא מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן אֶל פַּרְעֹה וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֵלָיו כֹּה אָמַר הַשֵּׁם וְכוּלֵי כִּי אִם מָאֵן וְכוּלֵי הִנְנִי מֵבִיא מָחָר אַרְבֶּה וְכוּלֵי.
And Moses and Aaron came in unto Pharaoh, and said unto him, "Thus says Hashem... Or else, if you refuse to let My people go, behold, tomorrow I will bring locusts into your border," etc.
הָעִנְיָן שֶׁהֵבִין מֹשֶׁה לְהַתְרוֹת לְפַרְעֹה עַל מַכַּת אַרְבֶּה אַף כִּי לֹא נֶאֱמַר לוֹ שֶׁיַּתְרֶה בּוֹ עַל אַרְבֶּה,

The reason how Moses understood on his own to warn Pharaoh specifically regarding the plague of Locusts (Arbeh), even though it is not explicitly stated in the preceding verses that God told him to warn Pharaoh of locusts,
רַק הֵבִין מִמַּאֲמַר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ לֵאמוֹר לְפַרְעֹה "לְמַעַן שִׁתִי אֹתֹתַי אֵלֶּה בְּקִרְבּוֹ וּלְמַעַן תְּסַפֵּר" וְכוּלֵי.

is that he deduced it from the utterance of Hashem, blessed be He, Who told him at the opening of the portion regarding Pharaoh: "that I might show these My signs in his midst (bekirbo), and that you may tell in the ears of your son... what things I have wrought (hit'allalti) in Egypt."
מַה שֶּׁאָמַר לְשׁוֹן "בְּקִרְבּוֹ" הַיְינוּ מֵהֶם עַצְמָם כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב "וְסִכְסַכְתִּי מִצְרַיִם בְּמִצְרַיִם" (יְשַׁעְיָהוּ יוֹד טֵית, בֵּית),

What He meant by the expression "in his midst (bekirbo)" is that the strife would erupt from within the Egyptians themselves, as it is written (Isaiah 19:2), "And I will stir up Egyptians against Egyptians" (as Pharaoh's own servants turned against him in verse 10:7),
הַיְינוּ שֶׁהֵם עַצְמָם יִלָּחֲמוּ זֶה בָּזֶה, וְזֶה פֵּירוּשׁ "אֲשֶׁר הִתְעַלַּלְתִּי בְּמִצְרַיִם" וְזֹאת הִיא הַפְלֵא וָפֶלֶא שֶׁלֹּא כְּדֶרֶךְ הַטֶּבַע.

meaning that they themselves would fight and turn against one another; and this is the meaning of "what things I have wrought in mockery (hit'allalti) in Egypt," which is a wondrous marvel contrary to the natural solidarity of a nation.
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר לוֹ "לְמַעַן תְּסַפֵּר", לָכֵן הֵבִין מֹשֶׁה כִּי הוּא מַכַּת אַרְבֶּה
And since concerning this internal division it was said to him, "and that you may recount it," Moses immediately understood that the impending plague was the plague of Locusts:
כִּי בָּאַרְבֶּה נִמְצָא מִדָּה טוֹבָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מִשְׁלֵי לָמֶד, כָּף זַיִן) "מֶלֶךְ אֵין לָאַרְבֶּה וַיֵּצֵא חֹצֵץ כֻּלּוֹ",
for within the locust species is found a remarkable positive trait, as it is written (Proverbs 30:27): "The locusts have no king, yet they go forth all of them by bands"—

הַיְינוּ מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם אַחְדּוּת וְאַהֲבָה לָכֵן אֵין צְרִיכִין לְמֶלֶךְ, כִּי הִצְטָרְכוּת הַמֶּלֶךְ הוּא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין אַחְדּוּת בֵּין בְּנֵי אָדָם, וְהַמִּין הַזֶּה אֵין בָּהֶם שׁוּם שִׂנְאָה לָכֵן לֹא יִצְטָרְכוּ לְמֶלֶךְ.

meaning that because there is complete unity and harmony among them, they have no need for a king; for the necessity of a king arises only because there is no unity among human beings (who would otherwise swallow each other alive, Avot 3:2), whereas this species of locust harbors no hatred among itself and therefore requires no king.

וְכַאֲשֶׁר הֵבִין מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהֵם עַצְמָם יִלָּחֲמוּ וְיִשְׂנְאוּ זֶה אֶת זֶה, אָז הֵבִין כִּי יֵצֵא בְּפוֹעַל בָּעוֹלָם עַל מַכַּת אַרְבֶּה שֶׁזֶּה הַמִּין יָבֹא לִלְחוֹם בְּמִצְרַיִם, כִּי זֹאת הוּא כְּנֶגֶד זֶה הַמִּין,

Thus, when Moses understood from Hashem, blessed be He, that the Egyptians themselves would clash and hate one another ("in his midst"), he realized that this would manifest physically in the world through the plague of Locusts—that this unified species would come to wage war against divided Egypt, measure for measure,
וְהוּא אַף בְּמִי שֶׁבּוֹטְחִים בּוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׂנְאוּ אוֹתָם גַּם הֵם יִבְגְּדוּ בָּם.
showing that even those closest confidants in whom Pharaoh trusted never to oppose him would turn against him and betray him.

The Plague of Locusts and Pharaoh’s Resistance

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Bo 2
p: וַיְהִי חֹשֶׁךְ אֲפֵלָה וְכוּלֵי.
And there was a thick darkness in all the land of Egypt three days, etc.

בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יוֹד דָּלֶת, גִּימֶל) וְלָמָּה הֵבִיא עֲלֵיהֶם חֹשֶׁךְ, שֶׁהָיוּ רְשָׁעִים שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ הַדּוֹר שֶׁלֹּא רָצוּ לָצֵאת וּמֵתוּ בִּשְׁלֹשֶׁת יְמֵי אֲפֵלָה וְכוּלֵי.

In the Midrash (Shemot Rabbah 14:3): Why did He bring darkness upon them? Because there were wicked ones among Israel in that generation who did not want to leave Egypt, and they died during the three days of thick darkness so that the Egyptians would not see their downfall, etc.
הָעִנְיָן בָּזֶה דְּהִנֵּה הָאָבוֹת נִקְרָאִים אָבוֹת לְפִי שֶׁכָּל מַחֲשַׁבְתָּם לֹא הָיָה בְּמִקְרֶה רַק מִמְּקוֹר הַחַיִּים וְלֹא הָיוּ אֶצְלָם שׁוּם מַחֲשָׁבָה בְּטֵלָה.

The inner meaning of this is that behold, the Patriarchs are called "Fathers" (Avot—archetypes) because none of their thoughts ever occurred by mere chance; rather, every thought of theirs stemmed from the Source of Life, and there was never an idle or vain thought in their minds.
וּמִכָּל מַחְשְׁבוֹתָם יָצְאוּ נְפָשׁוֹת אַף לְאַחַר כַּמָּה דּוֹרוֹת,
And out of each of their thoughts, actual human souls emerged into reality even several generations later!

וְהִנֵּה בְּהַנִּסָּיוֹן שֶׁהָלַךְ לְהַצִּיל אֶת לוֹט וְלִרְדּוֹף לְהִלָּחֵם עִם הַמְּלָכִים הָיָה מְסֻפָּק אִם לִרְדּוֹף אִם לֹא, עַד שֶׁהֵאִיר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁיִּרְדּוֹף כִּי הָיָה צָרִיךְ לְהַצִּיל שְׁתֵּי פְּרֵידוֹת טוֹבוֹת (בָּבָא קַמָּא לָמֶד חֵית עַמּוּד בֵּית) כַּיָּדוּעַ,

Now behold, during the test when our father Abraham went to rescue Lot and pursue the four kings to wage war against them, he initially hesitated and was in doubt whether or not to pursue them, until the Holy One, blessed be He, illuminated for him that he must pursue them in order to rescue the two "good doves" (Ruth the Moabite and Naamah the Ammonite) destined to emerge from Lot (Bava Kamma 38b), as is known;

אָכֵן מֵאֵלּוּ הַמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ אֶצְלוֹ שֶׁלֹּא לִרְדּוֹף גַּם כֵּן נַעֲשׂוּ נְפָשׁוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ חֲפֵצִים גַּם עַתָּה בְּשֵׁב וְאַל תַּעֲשֶׂה וְשָׁרְשָׁם הָיָה גַּם כֵּן נוֹטֶה מִבְּלִי לְהִלָּחֵם בְּמִצְרַיִם,

however, out of those initial thoughts of hesitation in Abraham's mind not to go out and wage war, souls were also formed—souls who now in Egypt likewise desired passive inaction ("sit and do not act"), whose root inclined against disrupting their settled life and contending with Egypt to go out;
וְעַתָּה נִתְבָּרֵר מִדּוֹת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהַדֵּעוֹת הַלָּלוּ הָיוּ גַּם כֵּן מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְכָל אֵלּוּ מֵתוּ בִּשְׁלֹשֶׁת יְמֵי אֲפֵלָה.

and now, at the time of the Exodus, the attributes of our father Abraham, peace be upon him, were completely clarified—showing that while those cautious thoughts had also been orchestrated by Hashem, blessed be He, their temporary function was finished, and all those souls died during the three days of thick darkness.
h:
The Plague of Darkness and Israel’s Hidden Light

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Bo 3
p: הַשְּׁלֹשָׁה מַכּוֹת שֶׁבַּסִּדְרָה הַזֹּאת אַרְבֶּה חֹשֶׁךְ מַכַּת בְּכוֹרוֹת הֵם נֶגֶד (מִשְׁלֵי חֵית, יוֹד גִּימֶל) "גֵּאָה וְגָאוֹן וְדֶרֶךְ רָע".

The three final plagues recorded in this Torah portion—Locusts, Darkness, and the Smiting of the Firstborn—correspond in reverse order to the three evils mentioned in the verse (Proverbs 8:13): "The fear of Hashem is to hate evil: pride (ge'ah), and arrogancy (ga'on), and the evil way (derekh ra)."
כִּי דֶּרֶךְ רָע, הַיְינוּ צָרַת עַיִן וְתַאֲוָה וְעִקְּשׁוּת בַּאֲכִילָה, נֶגֶד זֶה נִיתַּן לָהֶם מַכַּת אַרְבֶּה.

For "the evil way" refers to a stingy eye, gluttonous craving, and perversity in physical eating—and corresponding to this, the plague of Locusts (which devoured all their crops and food) was visited upon them.
"גָּאוֹן" הַיְינוּ שֶׁמִּתְנַשֵּׂא נֶגֶד מִי שֶׁרָאוּי לְהִכָּנַע מִפָּנָיו, נֶגֶד זֶה הוּא מַכַּת חֹשֶׁךְ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מִשְׁלֵי כָּף, כָּף) "מְקַלֵּל אָבִיו וְאִמּוֹ יִדְעַךְ נֵרוֹ" וְכוּלֵי.

"Arrogancy (ga'on)" refers to exalting oneself rebelliously against someone before whom one ought to submit—and corresponding to this came the plague of Darkness, as it is written (Proverbs 20:20): "Whoever curses his father or his mother, his lamp shall be put out in obscure darkness."

כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת אַף כִּי הָאָדָם צָרִיךְ לִשְׁמוֹעַ רַק לַהַשֵּׁם לְבַדּוֹ וּלְאָב וָאֵם אֵין בָּאָדָם רַק חֵלֶק קָטָן, אַךְ כְּשֶׁהָאָב וָאֵם יִרְצוּ לְהַטּוֹת אֶת הַבֵּן לְדַרְכֵי הַשֵּׁם צָרִיךְ לִשְׁמוֹעַ אֲלֵיהֶם מְאֹד וּלְהִכָּנַע מִפְּנֵיהֶם, "וְגָאוֹן" הַיְינוּ שֶׁאֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה לְהִכָּנַע עַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר "יִדְעַךְ" וְכוּלֵי.

For in truth, even though a person must ultimately obey Hashem alone and one's father and mother only contribute the physical portion of a person, nevertheless when one's father and mother seek to guide their child toward the ways of Hashem (just as Israel and Moses sought to guide Egypt to recognize God), one must heed them earnestly and submit before them; and "arrogancy" (ga'on) is when one refuses to submit, concerning which it is stated, "his lamp shall be put out in obscure darkness."
וְ"גֵאָה" הַיְינוּ שֶׁמִּתְגָּאֶה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ בְּיוֹתֵר הִתְנַשְּׂאוּת מִמַּה שֶּׁנִּמְצָא בּוֹ, נֶגֶד זֶה הוּא מַכַּת בְּכוֹרוֹת כִּי בְּכוֹר הוּא לְשׁוֹן הִתְנַשְּׂאוּת בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ.

And "pride (ge'ah)" refers to an intrinsic self-conceit where a person puffs himself up within himself far beyond what he actually is—and corresponding to this came the Smiting of the Firstborn (Bekhorot), for the title "firstborn" (bekhor) is an expression of innate self-superiority and primacy.

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Bo 4
p: מִשְׁכוּ וּקְחוּ לָכֶם צֹאן.
Draw out (mishkhu) and take for yourselves lambs according to your families, and slaughter the Passover offering.
(שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה טֵית זַיִן, בֵּית) מִשְׁכוּ יְדֵיכֶם מֵעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וּקְחוּ לָכֶם צֹאן שֶׁל מִצְוָה.
In the Midrash (Shemot Rabbah 16:2; Mekhilta Bo 5): "Withdraw (mishkhu) your hands from idolatry, and take for yourselves a lamb of mitzvah."
כְּתִיב (מִשְׁלֵי טֵית וָאו, יוֹד טֵית) "דֶּרֶךְ עָצֵל כִּמְשֻׂכַת חָדֶק וְאֹרַח יְשָׁרִים סְלוּלָה".
It is written (Proverbs 15:19): "The way of the slothful man is like a hedge of thorns (kimshukhat chadek), but the path of the upright is a paved highway."

דֶּרֶךְ עָצֵל הַיְנוּ אַף שֶׁאָדָם מוֹנֵעַ אֶת עַצְמוֹ מִמַּעֲשִׂים רָעִים וּמִמַּחְשָׁבוֹת רָעוֹת וּרְצוֹנוֹת רָעוֹת, אַף שֶׁאֵינוֹ עוֹשֶׂה זֹאת מֵחֲמַת אַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רַק עוֹשֶׂה כְּעָצֵל, כְּגוֹן שֶׁמֵּבִין שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לֹא יִצְלְחוּ לוֹ דְּבָרִים כָּאֵלֶּה, אוֹ בְּאֹפֶן אַחֵר שֶׁאֵינוֹ מֵאַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, אָז דַּרְכּוֹ הוּא כִּמְשֻׂכַת חָדֶק,

"The way of the slothful man" means that even when a person restrains himself from evil deeds, evil thoughts, and evil desires, if he does not do so out of genuine love for Hashem, blessed be He, but merely acts like a sluggish pragmatist—for instance, because he calculates that such behaviors will not turn out well for him in this world, or for any other motive devoid of the love of Hashem, blessed be He—then his path is "like a hedge of thorns" (kimshukhat, sharing the root of mishkhu):

כִּי הַלֵּב לֹא יוּכַל לִהְיוֹת פָּנוּי מִמַּחְשָׁבוֹת וּרְצוֹנוֹת אַף רֶגַע אַחַת, וְכַאֲשֶׁר יָסוּר מַחְשְׁבוֹת תַּאֲוָה מִלִּבּוֹ יָבֹא לְלִבּוֹ מַחְשֶׁבֶת כַּעַס וְכַדּוֹמֶה, וְכָל דְּרָכֶיהָ הֵמָּה כִּמְשֻׂכַת חָדֶק, כִּי לְעוֹלָם יִצְטָרֵךְ לְסִגּוּף וַעֲבוֹדָה קֹדֶם שֶׁיָּסוּר דָּבָר אֶחָד מִלִּבּוֹ יָבֹא לְלִבּוֹ דָּבָר אַחֵר שֶׁאֵינוֹ הָגוּן.

for the human heart cannot remain a vacuum empty of thoughts and desires for even a single moment! Thus, if he merely withdraws from a thought of lust without filling his heart with love of God, a thought of anger or pride will immediately rush in to take its place, so that all his paths are like a tangled hedge of thorns—requiring endless mortification and struggle, because before he finishes uprooting one improper weed from his heart, another improper weed springs up in its stead!

אֲבָל "אֹרַח יְשָׁרִים" הַיְנוּ שֶׁפּוֹנֶה מִכָּל דָּבָר מֵחֲמַת אַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, זֶה הוּא דַּרְכּוֹ סָלוּל לְטוֹב, כִּי כַּאֲשֶׁר יָסוּר מִלִּבּוֹ אֵיזֶה דָּבָר רַע יִשָּׁאֵר בְּלִבּוֹ אַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וּמִמֵּילָא לֹא יָבֹא לְלִבּוֹ שׁוּם דָּבָר אַחֵר שֶׁלֹּא כַּהוֹגֶן.

Whereas "the path of the upright"—namely one who turns away from evil out of a burning love for Hashem, blessed be He ("withdraw your hands from idolatry and immediately take for yourselves a lamb of mitzvah")—his path is a smooth, paved highway for the good; because as soon as an evil thought departs from his heart, his heart remains filled to the brim with the love of Hashem, blessed be He, leaving no room for any other improper thought to enter.
וְגִימַטְרִיָּא שֶׁל מִשְׁכוּ שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת שִׁשִּׁים וָשֵׁשׁ, שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת שִׁשִּׁים וַחֲמִשָּׁה, נֶגֶד יְמוֹת הַחַמָּה, וְאֶחָד נֶגֶד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁרוֹכֵב עֲלֵיהֶם,

And the numerical value (gematria) of the word mishkhu (מִשְׁכוּ — 40+300+20+6) is 366: 365 corresponding to the 365 days of the solar year (and the 365 negative prohibitions), plus 1 corresponding to Hashem, blessed be He, the One Who rides upon and directs them all;
וְכֵן כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנִּמְצָא בַּפָּסוּק מִלַּת אָז מוֹרֶה שֶׁהָאַלּוּ"ף רוֹכֵב עַל זַיִ"ן הַיְנוּ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.

just as wherever the word Az (אָז — "Then," as in Az Yashir) appears in Scripture, it indicates the Alef (1 — the Master of the Universe, Alufo shel Olam) riding upon the Zayin (7 — the seven days of the week / natural time), signifying Hashem, blessed be He, governing nature.

Draw Out the Lamb: Leaving Idolatry Behind

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Bo 5
p: זֹאת חֻקַּת הַפָּסַח.
This is the statute (chukat) of the Passover offering.
בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יוֹד טֵית, בֵּית) נֶאֱמַר חֻקָּה בַּפֶּסַח וְנֶאֱמַר חֻקָּה בַּפָּרָה וְאִי אַתָּה יוֹדֵעַ אֵיזֶה מֵהֶן גְּדוֹלָה.

In the Midrash (Shemot Rabbah 19:2): "Statute (chukah)" is stated regarding the Passover offering ("This is the statute of the Passover") and "statute (chukah)" is stated regarding the Red Heifer ("This is the statute of the Torah," Numbers 19:2), and you do not know which of them is greater.
מָשָׁל לִשְׁתֵּי מַטְרוֹנוֹת דּוֹמוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ מְהַלְּכוֹת שְׁתֵּיהֶן כְּאַחַת נִרְאוֹת שָׁווֹת מִי גְּדוֹלָה מִזֶּה אוֹתָהּ שֶׁחֲבֶרְתָּהּ מְלַוָּה אוֹתָהּ וְכוּלֵי.
This may be compared to two noble matrons walking together who appear equal in rank; how do we know which of them is greater? The one whom her companion escorts to her home!

כָּךְ בַּפֶּסַח נֶאֱמַר חֻקָּה וּבַפָּרָה נֶאֱמַר חֻקָּה וּמִי גָּדוֹל הַפָּרָה שֶׁאוֹכְלֵי פֶּסַח צְרִיכִין לָהּ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (בְּמִדְבַּר יוֹד טֵית, יוֹד זַיִן) "וְלָקְחוּ לַטָּמֵא מֵעֲפַר שְׂרֵפַת" וְכוּלֵי.

So too, "statute" is stated regarding the Passover and "statute" is stated regarding the Red Heifer; and which appears greater? The Red Heifer, since those who eat the Passover offering need the ashes of the Red Heifer first to purify themselves, as it is stated (Numbers 19:17), "And for the unclean they shall take of the ashes of the burning of the purification-offering," etc.

הָעִנְיָן בָּזֶה כִּי חֻקַּת הַפֶּסַח הוּא נֶגֶד דִּבֵּר "אָנֹכִי הַשֵּׁם אֱלֹקֶיךָ" שֶׁהוּא כּוֹלֵל כָּל מִצְוֹת עֲשֵׂה, וְחֻקַּת הַפָּרָה הוּא נֶגֶד "לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ" שֶׁהוּא כּוֹלֵל כָּל מִצְוֹת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה,

The inner meaning of this is that the statute of the Passover offering corresponds to the First Commandment, "I am (Anokhi) Hashem your God Who brought you out of the land of Egypt," which encompasses all 248 positive commandments, whereas the purifying statute of the Red Heifer corresponds to the Second Commandment, "You shall have no other gods before Me," which encompasses all 365 negative commandments (cleansing from impurity);

וּבֶאֱמֶת מֵהָרָאוּי עַל פִּי שֵׂכֶל, שֶׁלֹּא יוּכַל הָאָדָם לְהַשִּׂיג יִקְרַת הַמַּאֲמָר "אָנֹכִי הַשֵּׁם אֱלֹקֶיךָ" קֹדֶם שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לִבּוֹ מְזֻכָּךְ מִ"לֹּא יִהְיֶה לְךָ", כִּי תְּחִלָּה צָרִיךְ הָאָדָם לָסוּר מֵרָע וְאַחַר כָּךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת טוֹב,

and in truth, according to strict logical order, a person should not be able to attain the precious light of "I am Hashem your God" before his heart is first completely purified of "You shall have no other gods" (just as one needs the Red Heifer before eating the Pesach), because logically a person must first "turn away from evil" and only afterward "do good" (Psalms 34:15)!

אַךְ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּרֹב רַחֲמָיו הִקְדִּים מַאֲמַר "אָנֹכִי" קֹדֶם "לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ", כִּי בְּאִם לָאו לֹא הָיָה אָדָם בָּעוֹלָם שֶׁיָּכוֹל לָבוֹא לְהַשִּׂיג דִּבּוּר "אָנֹכִי", כִּי מִי הוּא הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יֹאמַר זִכִּיתִי לִבִּי בְּכָל מִצְוֹת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה,

However, Hashem, blessed be He, in His abundant mercy, placed the utterance of "I am (Anokhi)" ahead of "You shall have no other gods" (just as the statute of Pesach was given in Egypt prior to the Red Heifer); for had He not done so, no person in the world would ever have been able to arrive at the perception of "Anokhi," since "who is the man who can say, 'I have completely cleansed my heart'" (Proverbs 20:9) of every trace of the negative commandments first?

וְעַל זֶה אָמַר דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם (תְּהִלִּים קוּף לָמֶד חֵית, בֵּית) "כִּי הִגְדַּלְתָּ עַל כָּל שִׁמְךָ אִמְרָתֶךָ", וַאֲמִירָה הַיְנוּ בִּלְחִישָׁה שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יְבָרֵר אַחַר כָּךְ כִּי לֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל מְנֻקֶּה.

And concerning this act of grace King David, peace be upon him, declared (Psalms 138:2): "I will praise Your Name for Your lovingkindness and for Your truth, for You have magnified Your soft utterance (imratekha) above all Your Name"—where amirah denotes a soft, intimate communication ("Anokhi"), trusting that through the light of Anokhi Hashem, blessed be He, will subsequently clarify and cleanse the heart of Israel.
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר "אוֹדֶה שִׁמְךָ" הַיְנוּ הַטּוֹבָה וְהַגְּדוֹלָה שֶׁעָשִׂיתָ עִמָּנוּ לָתֵת לָנוּ תְּחִלָּה דִּבֵּר "אָנֹכִי", כְּדֵי שֶׁאַחַר כָּךְ יְבָרֵר בְּלִבֵּנוּ הַדִּבּוּר "לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ",

And for this David said, "I will praise Your Name"—thanking God for the immense kindness He did with us in giving us first the utterance of "Anokhi," so that through its power the utterance of "You shall have no other gods" would afterward be clarified in our hearts;

וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה נֶגֶד "אָנֹכִי", וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בֶּן יוֹסֵף הָיָה נֶגֶד "לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ", כַּיָּדוּעַ שֶׁכָּל נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵמָּה בַּשֹּׁרֶשׁ דְּבוּקִים כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד בְּאוֹתִיּוֹת הַתּוֹרָה,

now Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, corresponded to "Anokhi," whereas Rabbi Akiva ben Yosef corresponded to "You shall have no other gods"—for as is known, all the souls of Israel are rooted in the letters of the Torah—
וְהִנֵּה נִשְׁמַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה נֶגֶד דִּבּוּר "אָנֹכִי" וְעִסְקוֹ הָיָה בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְבָרֵר בָּעוֹלָם אַחְדּוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ בָּעוֹלָם,

and the soul of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, was rooted in the utterance of "Anokhi," so his primary mission in this world was to reveal and illuminate the direct Oneness of His Name, blessed be He, in the world;
וְנִשְׁמַת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הָיָה נֶגֶד "לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ" וְהוּא לְבָרֵר וּלְנַקּוֹת כָּל רַע וְסִיג פְּסֹלֶת שֶׁבְּלֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהַרְחִיקָם מֵרָע שֶׁהוּא בִּכְלַל "לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ",

whereas the soul of Rabbi Akiva (to whom the mystery of the Red Heifer was revealed, Bamidbar Rabbah 19:6) was rooted in "You shall have no other gods," which is the work of sifting out and cleansing every trace of dross and impurity from the heart of Israel, distancing them from evil under the rubric of "You shall have no other gods";

וּמַה שֶּׁחִדֵּשׁ תָּמִיד גְּדָרִים וּסְיָגִים חֲדָשִׁים, הַיְנוּ שֶׁהוֹסִיף שֶׁגַּם זֶה הוּא בִּכְלַל "לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ" וְצָרִיךְ לִנָּקוֹת מִזֶּה גַּם כֵּן, וְכֵן כָּל הַהֲלָכוֹת אִסּוּר וְהֶיתֵּר פָּסוּל וְכָשֵׁר טָמֵא וְטָהוֹר, הֵם לְבָרֵר הָרַע מִן הַטּוֹב,

and the reason Rabbi Akiva constantly expounded new fences and halakhic safeguards was to show that even these subtle details fall under "You shall have no other gods" and must be cleansed as well—just as all the laws of forbidden and permitted, unfit and fit, impure and pure, serve to separate the evil from the good;

וְזֶה הָעִנְיָן הַמְבֹאָר בַּגְּמָרָא (מְנָחוֹת כָּף טֵית עַמּוּד בֵּית) בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁעָלָה מֹשֶׁה לַמָּרוֹם מְצָאוֹ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁהָיָה קוֹשֵׁר כְּתָרִים לָאוֹתִיּוֹת, אָמַר לְפָנָיו רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם מִי מְעַכֵּב עַל יָדְךָ, אָמַר לוֹ אָדָם אֶחָד יֵשׁ אַחַר כַּמָּה דּוֹרוֹת וַעֲקִיבָא בֶּן יוֹסֵף שְׁמוֹ שֶׁעָתִיד לִדְרֹשׁ עַל כָּל קוֹץ תִּלֵּי תִּלִּים שֶׁל הֲלָכוֹת, חָלְשָׁה דַּעְתּוֹ עַד שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לַהֲלָכָה אַחַת אָמַר לוֹ זוֹ מִנַּיִן אָמַר לוֹ הֲלָכָה לְמֹשֶׁה מִסִּינַי.

and this explains what is related in the Gemara (Menachot 29b): When Moses ascended on high, he found the Holy One, blessed be He, tying crowns onto the letters of the Torah. Moses asked Him, "Master of the Universe, who stays Your hand (why are the plain letters not enough)?" He answered him, "There is a man who will arise after several generations, and Akiva ben Yosef is his name, who is destined to expound upon every single thorn-crown mounds and mounds of halakhot!" When Moses saw Rabbi Akiva's academy, his spirit grew faint—until Rabbi Akiva reached one particular law where his disciples asked him, "Rabbi, from where do you know this?" and he replied to them, "It is a law given to Moses from Sinai!"—whereupon Moses' mind was set at ease.
לְפִי שֶׁרָאָה אֵיךְ הִתְפַּשֵּׁט רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אֶת הַדִּבּוּר "לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ" עַד שֶׁהוֹסִיף כַּמָּה גְּדָרִים וְחָלְשָׁה דַּעְתּוֹ,

Why did Moses' spirit grow faint at first? Because he saw how vastly Rabbi Akiva expanded the utterance of "You shall have no other gods," multiplying countless fences and restrictions, so Moses feared lest the negative restrictions overshadow the positive essence!

וְהִנֵּה זֹאת יָדוּעַ כִּי שֹׁרֶשׁ כֹּל, הוּא "אָנֹכִי הַשֵּׁם אֱלֹקֶיךָ", וְ"לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ" אֵינוֹ רַק שְׁמִירָה שֶׁלֹּא יִתְרַחֵק הָאָדָם מֵהַשֵּׁם אֱלֹקָיו לָכֵן חָלְשָׁה דַּעְתּוֹ, עַד שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לַהֲלָכָה אַחַת הַיְנוּ שֶׁרָאָה מֹשֶׁה לָמָּה צָרִיךְ כָּל כָּךְ גְּדָרִים אָמַר לוֹ הֲלָכָה לְמֹשֶׁה מִסִּינַי, הֲלָכָה אַחַת הַיְנוּ "אָנֹכִי" כִּי זֶה הוּא עִיקָּר בַּתּוֹרָה כִּדְאִיתָא (זוֹהַר דְּבָרִים רֵישׁ סָמֶךְ דָּלֶת עַמּוּד בֵּית) "שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל הַשֵּׁם אֱלֹקֵינוּ הַשֵּׁם אֶחָד" זֶה עִיקָּר גָּדוֹל בַּתּוֹרָה.

For it is known that the root of everything is "I am (Anokhi) Hashem your God," whereas "You shall have no other gods" is merely a protective guard to ensure that a person does not drift away from Hashem his God; therefore Moses was distressed until Rabbi Akiva reached "one law (halakhah achat)"—meaning that when the disciples asked what the ultimate purpose of all these myriad fences was, Rabbi Akiva answered: "It is all for the 'one law' (Halakhah Achat) of Moses from Sinai"—namely "Anokhi" (Hashem is One), which is the supreme foundation of the Torah, as is stated in the Zohar (Devarim 264b) on "Hear O Israel, Hashem our God, Hashem is One!"
וְ"לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ" הוּא רַק לִשְׁמֹר לְבֵית יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁלֹּא יִטּוּ מֵ"אָנֹכִי הַשֵּׁם אֱלֹקֶיךָ", אָז נִתְקָרְרָה דַּעְתּוֹ שֶׁהֵבִין כִּי לוֹ נִתַּן הָעִיקָּר.

And since all of Rabbi Akiva's fences in "You shall have no other gods" exist solely as a handmaid to escort and guard the House of Israel so that they never deviate from Moses' "I am Hashem your God," Moses' mind was immediately set at ease, seeing that the primary root had been given to him.

p: קַדֶּשׁ לִי כָל בְּכוֹר וְכוּלֵי בָּאָדָם וּבַבְּהֵמָה.
Sanctify unto Me all the firstborn, whatsoever opens the womb among the children of Israel, both of man and of beast: it is Mine.
עִנְיַן אָדָם מוֹרֶה עַל הַחָכְמָה וְהַמַּחְשָׁבָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ, כִּי זֶה הוּא עִיקַּר צוּרַת הָאָדָם, וּבְהֵמָה הַיְינוּ כֹּחַ הַמַּעֲשֶׂה,

Within a person, the aspect of "man (adam)" indicates the wisdom and thought in the brain—for that is the primary form of Man—whereas the aspect of "beast (behemah)" indicates the bodily faculty of physical action;

וְהִנֵּה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ צִוָּה לְקַדֵּשׁ וּלְצָרֵף שְׁתֵּיהֶן הַמַּעֲשֶׂה וְהַמַּחְשָׁבָה, וְאָז יִהְיֶה צוּרַת הָאָדָם בִּשְׁלֵימוּת מְבוֹרָר בִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר (תְּהִלִּים לָמֶד וָאו, זַיִן) "אָדָם וּבְהֵמָה תּוֹשִׁיעַ הַשֵּׁם".

and behold, Hashem, blessed be He, commanded us to sanctify and join together the firstfruits of both of them—thought and action—so that the entire form of man will be completely clarified in the will of Hashem, blessed be He; and concerning this it is stated (Psalms 36:7): "Man and beast You save, O Hashem."

כִּי אָדָם הוּא הַמַּחְשָׁבָה, וּבְהֵמָה רוֹמֵז עַל הַמַּעֲשֶׂה, וְהִנֵּה מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא הָיָה חָכְמוֹת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכָל כֹּחוֹ הָיָה בָּזֶה, הַיְינוּ הַמּוֹחַ וְהַמַּחְשָׁבָה לִהְיוֹת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נֶגְדּוֹ תָּמִיד.

Now since "man" is thought and "beast" alludes to physical action, behold, Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, embodied the supernal wisdom of all Israel and his primary strength lay in the mind and thought—having Hashem, blessed be He, constantly before him—
וְעַל כֵּן כָּל הַתּוֹרָה מְדַבֶּרֶת הָעִיקָּר בְּמַעֲשִׂים לְפוֹעַל הַיְינוּ שֶׁגַּם הַמַּעֲשֶׂה יִהְיֶה כָּךְ מְזוּכָּךְ כְּהַמַּחְשָׁבָה.
and therefore, to complete the synthesis, the Torah of Moses speaks primarily of practical, physical mitzvot in action, so that physical action too will become as purified as his thought!
וְלָזֶה עָשָׂה מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הַמִּשְׁכָּן, כִּי מְקוֹמוֹ הָיָה בְּצוּרַת אָדָם בְּעוֹמֶק הַלֵּב וְהַמִּשְׁכָּן הָיָה יָכוֹל לְהִתְפָּרֵק וּלְהִנָּשֵׂא לְמָקוֹם אַחֵר.

And for this reason Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, constructed the portable Tabernacle (Mishkan): because Moses' own root was in the spiritual form of Man within the depths of the heart and mind (which is not bound to a physical spot), his sanctuary was a portable Mishkan that could be dismantled and carried from place to place.

וְחָכְמַת שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה בְּמַעֲשִׂים עַל כֵּן בָּנָה בֵּית הַבְּחִירָה בְּמָקוֹם קָבוּעַ, וְסֵפֶר מִשְׁלֵי שֶׁעָשָׂה, מְדַבֵּר עִיקָּר בְּיִשְׁרַת הַלֵּב וְהַמַּחְשָׁבָה שֶׁיִּכּוֹנְנוּ כְּהַמַּעֲשֶׂה.

Whereas the wisdom of King Solomon, peace be upon him, was rooted in the realm of practical governance and action, which is why he built the Holy Temple fixed permanently in one physical spot; and conversely, to complete the synthesis, the Book of Proverbs (Mishlei) that he composed speaks primarily of rectifying the inner uprightness of the heart, character traits, and thought, so that one's inner thoughts become as ordered as one's deeds.

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Bo 7
p: קַדֶּשׁ לִי כָל בְּכוֹר וְכוּלֵי וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה זָכוֹר וְכוּלֵי, וְלֹא יֵאָכֵל חָמֵץ.
Sanctify unto Me all the firstborn, etc. And Moses said unto the people, "Remember this day, in which you came out from Egypt... there shall no leavened bread be eaten."
בֵּאוּר הָעִנְיָן לָמָּה אָמַר מֹשֶׁה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל תְּחִילָּה פָּרָשַׁת מַצּוֹת קוֹדֶם פָּרָשַׁת בְּכוֹר שֶׁצִּיוָּה לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לֵאמוֹר לָהֶם.

The explanation of the matter as to why Moses first communicated to Israel the passage of Matzah and unleavened bread (Exodus 13:3–10) before communicating the passage of the Firstborn (Exodus 13:11–16), even though the Holy One, blessed be He, had just commanded him regarding the firstborn first (in 13:1–2):

אַךְ הָעִנְיָן בָּזֶה כִּי פָּרָשַׁת בְּכוֹר מוֹרָה כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ צִוָּה לֵאמוֹר לָהֶם הַפָּרָשָׁה הַזֹּאת כְּדֵי לִהְיוֹת בָּרוּר וְנָקִי מִתַּאֲווֹת, כִּי בְּהַטִּיפָּה שֶׁל בְּכוֹר הִתְגַּבְּרוּת הַתַּאֲוָה שׁוֹלֶטֶת, וְזֶה עִנְיַן "קַדֶּשׁ לִי כָל בְּכוֹר",

the inner meaning of this is that the passage of the Firstborn was commanded by Hashem, blessed be He, in order that Israel be pure and sanctified in the covenant of procreation, cleansed of physical lust—for in the initial seminal drop of the firstborn ("the beginning of my vigor"), the surge of physical desire is strongest, and sanctifying that root is the essence of "Sanctify unto Me all the firstborn";
אַךְ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם יָדַע כִּי אֵין בָּאֶפְשָׁרוּת לְהִשָּׁמֵר מִתַּאֲוָה הַזֹּאת, רַק אִם יִהְיֶה הָאָדָם תְּחִילָּה בָּהִיר וְנָקִי מִתַּאֲוַות אֲכִילָה,

however, Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, knew that it is humanly impossible to guard oneself in the covenant of sexual purity unless a person first becomes clear and purified from the craving of gluttonous eating ("there shall no leavened bread be eaten")!

שֶׁאִם הָאָדָם נָקִי בְּקַבָּלוֹתָיו אָז גַּם הַשְׁפָּעוֹתָיו מְבוֹרָרִים, כִּי הַצַּוָּאר הַמְקַבֵּל מְכוּוָּן נֶגֶד בְּרִית הַמָּעוֹר, עַל זֹאת הַכַּוָּונָה אָמַר לָהֶם תְּחִילָּה פָּרָשַׁת מַצָּה קוֹדֶם פָּרָשַׁת בְּכוֹר.

For if a person is pure in what he takes into his body (his eating), then what he emanates outward from his body (his procreation) will likewise be pure and clarified—since the throat that receives food is directly aligned with the covenant of the flesh (brit hama'or)—and with this intention Moses taught them the passage of Matzah prior to the passage of the Firstborn.

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Beshalach 1
p: וַיְהִי בְּשַׁלַּח פַּרְעֹה וְכוּלֵי
And it came to pass, when Pharaoh had let the people go, etc.
וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה אֶת עַצְמוֹת יוֹסֵף.
and Moses took the bones of Joseph with him.
עִנְיַן סְמִיכוּת הַפְּסוּקִים,
The meaning of the juxtaposition of these verses is:
דְּהִנֵּה כַּאֲשֶׁר רָאָה מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
