The inner meaning is that the purpose of the shofar
הוּא לְעוֹרֵר הַפְּנִימִיּוּת מֵהַבְּרִיאָה;
is to awaken the innermost spiritual core of Creation;
כִּי הַפְּנִימִיּוּת מֵהַבְּרִיאָה הוּא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
for the inward core of Creation is words of Torah,
כִּדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (בְּהַרְבֵּה מְקוֹמוֹת):
as taught in the holy Zohar (in many places):
בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא בְּרָא קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא עָלְמָא;
through the Torah the Holy One, blessed be He, created the universe;
וּבְקוֹל שׁוֹפָר נִתְעוֹרֵר הַנְּקֻדָּה הַפְּנִימִיּוּת.
and through the shofar blast this innermost point is stirred.
כִּי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, מַעֲשֵׂי הַמִּצְווֹת הֵמָּה לְבוּשִׁים לַמִּצְווֹת דִּלְעֵילָּא,
For in this world, physical mitzvot are garments for the supernal mitzvot,
כִּדְאִיתָא בְּהָאֲרִ"י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה (עֵץ חַיִּים, הֵיכָל ו, שַׁעַר פְּנִימִיּוּת וְחִיצוֹנִיּוּת, דְּרוּשׁ ב);
as brought in the teachings of the holy Ari, of blessed memory (Etz Chayyim, Heikhal 6, Sha'ar Penimiyut Ve-Chitzoniyut, Derush 2);
וְזֶה שֶׁאָנוּ מְבָרְכִין עַל מִצְווֹת "אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ",
and this is why we bless over mitzvot ‘Who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us,’
הַיְינוּ שֶׁהִלְבִּישׁ הַמִּצְווֹת דִּלְעֵילָּא בְּמַעֲשֵׂי הַמִּצְווֹת שֶׁל עוֹלָם הַזֶּה;
meaning that He enclothed supernal commandments within the earthly actions of this world;
וּבְשׁוֹפָר שֶׁנִּתְעוֹרֵר הַפְּנִימִיּוּת מֵהַבְּרִיאָה,
and through the shofar which awakens the inward essence of Creation,
אָז נִתְחַבְּרוּ הַמִּצְוָה דִּלְעֵילָּא עִם הַפְּעֻלָּה מֵהַמִּצְוָה שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה;
the supernal mitzvah unites with the earthly performance in this world;
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהַפְּנִימִיּוּת מֵהַבְּרִיאָה, שֶׁהוּא הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בַּהַבְּרִיאָה,
meaning that the inner essence of Creation—the Torah embedded within Creation—
זֶה נִתְעוֹרֵר עַל יְדֵי שׁוֹפָר;
is awakened through the shofar;
וְלָכֵן קַבָּלַת הַתּוֹרָה הָיְתָה עַל יְדֵי קוֹל שׁוֹפָר,
and therefore the Giving of the Torah took place through the sound of the shofar,
שֶׁבָּזֶה נִתְעוֹרְרוּ הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁנִּתְלַבְּשׁוּ בַּהַבְּרִיאָה.
for through this the words of Torah enclothed in Creation were awakened.
וְעִנְיַן שַׁבָּת הוּא שֶׁהָאָדָם מְבַטֵּל כָּל פְּעוּלּוֹתָיו,
And the essence of Shabbat is that man desists from all his actions,
שֶׁרוֹאֶה מְפוֹרָשׁ שֶׁהַכֹּל הוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
perceiving clearly that all originates from Hashem,
לָכֵן פְּעוּלּוֹתָיו אָז בְּטֵלוֹת;
hence his personal actions cease;
וְלָכֵן בַּגְּבוּלִין אָסוּר תְּקִיעַת שׁוֹפָר בְּשַׁבָּת,
therefore in the provinces sounding the shofar is forbidden on Shabbat,
כִּי שַׁבָּת הוּא כּוֹלֵל כָּל הַמִּצְווֹת;
for Shabbat encompasses all commandments;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּל הַפְּעֻלּוֹת, אֲפִילּוּ שֶׁל מִצְוָה, אֲסוּרוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת
and just as all actions, even of a mitzvah, are forbidden on Shabbat
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁשַּׁבָּת גָּדוֹל יוֹתֵר מִכָּל הַמִּצְווֹת,
because Shabbat is greater than all the commandments,
וְאַף תְּקִיעַת שׁוֹפָר שֶׁמְּחַבֵּר מִצְוָה דִּלְעֵילָּא עִם מִצְוָה דִּלְתַתָּא,
and even the blowing of the shofar which binds the upper mitzvah with the lower,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם, כֵּיוָן שֶׁהוּא עַל יְדֵי פְּעֻלַּת אָדָם בַּהַמִּצְוָה,
nevertheless, since it operates through human action in the mitzvah,
לָכֵן נֶאֶסְרָה גַּם תְּקִיעַת שׁוֹפָר מִדְּרַבָּנָן.
therefore the blowing of the shofar was rabbinically prohibited.
אֲבָל בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ,
However in the Temple,
שָׁם קָרְבָּנוֹת דּוֹחִים שַׁבָּת,
sacrifices override Shabbat,
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁשָּׁם הָאָדָם רוֹאֶה שֶׁכָּל מַה שֶּׁהוּא פּוֹעֵל – הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא הַפּוֹעֵל;
because there man perceives that whatever he enacts, Hashem is the true Actor;
וְכִדְאִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (רַבָּה בְּרֵאשִׁית יא, ו):
as brought in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 11:6):
שֶׁשָּׁאַל טוּרְנוּסְרוּפּוּס אֶת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
Turnus Rufus asked Rabbi Akiva:
לָמָּה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מוֹרִיד גְּשָׁמִים וְעוֹשֶׂה מְלָאכָה בְּשַׁבָּת?
“Why does the Holy One bring down rain and perform work on Shabbat?”
וְהֵשִׁיב לוֹ: כֵּיוָן שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֵין רְשׁוּת אַחֶרֶת עִמּוֹ;
He replied to him: “Because the Holy One has no other domain beside Him;”
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כָּל הָעוֹלָם בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ,
meaning that for Hashem the entire universe is His singular domain,
וְלָכֵן אֵין שׁוּם דָּבָר אֶצְלוֹ מְלָאכָה,
hence nothing constitutes forbidden labor for Him,
שֶׁהֲרֵי הַכֹּל בְּיָדוֹ,
for all is in His hand,
וְאֵין שׁוּם חִילּוּק אֶצְלוֹ אַף שֶׁיִּשְׁתַּנֶּה מֵרְשׁוּת לִרְשׁוּת וּמִצּוּרָה לְצוּרָה,
and there is no division for Him even when shifting from domain to domain or form to form,
שֶׁהֲרֵי הַכֹּל בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ וּבְיָדוֹ;
for all is within His domain and in His hand;
וְכֵן בְּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ מִתְחַבֵּר מִצְוָה דִּלְתַתָּא עִם מִצְוָה דִּלְעֵילָּא,
and so in the Holy Temple the lower mitzvah unites with the supernal mitzvah,
כִּי שָׁם רוֹאֶה שֶׁכָּל פְּעוּלּוֹתָיו הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ פּוֹעֵל אוֹתָם,
for there he perceives that Hashem enacts all his deeds,
לָכֵן קָרְבָּנוֹת דּוֹחִים שַׁבָּת;
therefore sacrifices override Shabbat;
וְכֵן תְּקִיעַת שׁוֹפָר בְּשַׁבָּת בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ הָיוּ תוֹקְעִין,
and likewise they blew the shofar on Shabbat in the Temple,
כֵּיוָן שֶׁזֶּה עַצְמוֹ מוֹרֶה עִנְיַן שׁוֹפָר:
since this itself is the teaching of the shofar:
שֶׁנִּתְעוֹרֵר הַפְּנִימִיּוּת הָאָדָם
that the inner core of man is awakened
וְנִתְחַבֵּר עִם אוֹר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and united directly with the light of Hashem, blessed be He.
h: The Shofar Awakens the Inner Root of Creation

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Talmud, Megillah 10b:1
p: רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי פָּתַח לַהּ פִּתְחָא לְהַאי פָּרָשְׁתָא מֵהָכָא: (יְשַׁעְיָה נה, יג)
Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani opened his discourse on this biblical section from here (Isaiah 55:13):
"תַּחַת הַנַּעֲצוּץ יַעֲלֶה בְרוֹשׁ וְתַחַת הַסִּרְפַּד יַעֲלֶה הֲדַס",
“Instead of the thorn shall come up the cypress, and instead of the brier shall come up the myrtle”:
"תַּחַת הַנַּעֲצוּץ" – תַּחַת הָמָן הָרָשָׁע שֶׁעָשָׂה עַצְמוֹ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
“Instead of the thorn”—instead of Haman the wicked who made himself into an idol,
דִּכְתִיב (שָׁם ז, יט): "וּבְכָל הַנַּעֲצוּצִים וּבְכָל הַנַּהֲלוֹלִים";
as it is written (ibid. 7:19): “and upon all thorns, and upon all pastures”;
"יַעֲלֶה בְרוֹשׁ" – זֶה מָרְדֳּכַי וְכוּלֵי;
“shall come up the cypress”—this is Mordechai, etc.;
"תַּחַת הַסִּרְפַּד" – תַּחַת וַשְׁתִּי הָרְשָׁעָה,
“instead of the brier”—instead of Vashti the wicked,
בַּת בְּנוֹ שֶׁל נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר הָרָשָׁע שֶׁשָּׂרַף רְפִידַת בֵּית ה' וְכוּלֵי;
the granddaughter of Nebuchadnezzar the wicked who burned the floor-covering of the House of Hashem, etc.;
"יַעֲלֶה הֲדַס" – זוֹ אֶסְתֵּר.
“shall come up the myrtle”—this is Esther.
הִנֵּה מָרְדֳּכַי וְהָמָן הָיוּ זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה:
Behold, Mordechai and Haman stood in polar opposition, one directly facing the other:
מָרְדֳּכַי הָיָה אוֹהֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּתַכְלִית אַהֲבָה
Mordechai loved the people of Israel with the absolute perfection of love,
עַד שֶׁמָּסַר נַפְשׁוֹ עֲלֵיהֶם;
to the extent that he laid down his life on their behalf;
וְהָמָן הָיָה שׂוֹנֵא יִשְׂרָאֵל מְאֹד,
whereas Haman hated the Jewish people intensely,
כַּיָּדוּעַ שֶׁרָצָה לְבַזְבֵּז עֲשֶׂרֶת אֲלָפִים כִּכַּר כֶּסֶף
as is known, wishing to squander ten thousand talents of silver
מֵחֲמַת שִׂנְאָתוֹ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
out of his blinding hatred for Israel,
הֵיפֶךְ מִן מָרְדֳּכַי;
the diametric antithesis of Mordechai;
וְלָכֵן הָיָה הַמִּשְׁפָּט
and therefore divine justice dictated
שֶׁבְּמַפֶּלֶת הָמָן יַעֲלֶה מָרְדֳּכַי לִגְדֻלָּה.
that through the downfall of Haman, Mordechai should ascend to supreme greatness.
וְכֵן וַשְׁתִּי לְעֻמַּת אֶסְתֵּר:
And likewise Vashti facing Esther:
שֶׁאֶסְתֵּר הָיְתָה נְקִיָּה וּמְבוֹרֶרֶת מִזְּנוּת מְאֹד,
for Esther was completely pure and refined from any trace of licentiousness,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (סַנְהֶדְרִין עד:): "אֶסְתֵּר קַרְקַע עוֹלָם הָיְתָה",
as it is taught in the Gemara (Sanhedrin 74b): “Esther was merely passive like the earth of the world,”
הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לָהּ שׁוּם צַד נְגִיעָה וְרָצוֹן לְהִנָּשֵׂא לַאֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ;
meaning she possessed no personal bias or subjective desire to be married to Ahasuerus;
וְזֶהוּ מִדַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁשּׂוֹנֵא זִמָּה;
and this reflects the divine attribute of Hashem Who despises immorality;
אֲבָל וַשְׁתִּי הָיְתָה שְׁטוּפָה בְּזִמָּה,
whereas Vashti was thoroughly steeped in licentiousness,
כִּדְאִיתָא לְקַמָּן בַּגְּמָרָא (יב:);
as taught further on in the Gemara (12b);
וְגַם נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר אֲבִי אָבִיהָ הָיָה הֵיפֶךְ מִבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
and likewise Nebuchadnezzar her paternal grandfather stood as the antithesis of the Holy Temple
וְשָׂרַף אֶת רְפִידַת בֵּית ה';
and burned the foundational tapestry of Hashem’s Sanctuary;
כִּי מְקוֹם הַמִּקְדָּשׁ נָקִי בָּזֶה מְאֹד
for the site of the Sanctuary is exquisitely pure in this regard,
שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לִסְבּוֹל שׁוּם דְּבַר זִמָּה;
being utterly incapable of tolerating any trace of lewdness;
וְלָכֵן מֵעֲפַר הַמִּקְדָּשׁ הָיוּ בּוֹדְקִין הַסּוֹטָה,
and therefore with earth from the Sanctuary floor they would test the suspected adulteress (sotah),
שֶׁמְּבָרֵר תֵּיכֶף אִם הִיא נְקִיָּה מִזְּנוּת;
which clarified immediately whether she was clean from promiscuity;
וְלָכֵן נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר הָיָה שׂוֹנֵא אֶת מְקוֹם הַמִּקְדָּשׁ וְשׂוֹרְפוֹ,
and therefore Nebuchadnezzar hated the site of the Sanctuary and burned it,
וְלָכֵן בְּמַפֶּלֶת וַשְׁתִּי עָלְתָה אֶסְתֵּר לִגְדֻלָּה.
and consequently through the downfall of Vashti did Esther ascend to majesty.
h: Holy Opposites Rise Through the Fall of Evil

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Talmud, Megillah 12b:1
p: בִּסְעוּדָתוֹ שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע, הַלָּלוּ אוֹמְרִים מָדִיּוֹת נָאוֹת וְכוּלֵי, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁתְּהֵא עֲרֻמָּה.
“At the feast of that wicked man, some were saying: the Median women are beautiful, etc., provided only that she be naked.”
אִיתָא בְּשֵׁם הַבַּעַל שֵׁם טוֹב שֶׁזֶּה הָעִנְיָן "עֲרֻמָּה", וַעֲדַיִן לֹא בָּא.
It is brought in the name of the Baal Shem Tov that this theme is ‘naked,’ and yet it had not arrived.
בֵּיאוּר הָעִנְיָן בָּזֶה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (יְשַׁעְיָה סא, י):
The elucidation of this matter is as written (Isaiah 61:10):
"שׂוֹשׂ אָשִׂישׂ בַּה' תָּגֵל נַפְשִׁי בֵּאלֹהַי כִּי הִלְבִּישַׁנִי בִּגְדֵי יֶשַׁע מְעִיל צְדָקָה יְעָטָנִי".
“I will greatly rejoice in Hashem, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for He has clothed me with the garments of salvation, He has covered me with the robe of righteousness.”
הַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר בְּחֵלֶק רִאשׁוֹן (לִקּוּטֵי הַשַּׁ״ס מְגִילָּה יב: דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "וְהַקָּרוֹב")
This means, as explained in Part I (Likutim on the Shas, Megillah 12b, s.v. “Ve-hakarov”):
שֶׁכָּל הַמִּצְווֹת וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂים
that all commandments and virtuous deeds which Israel perform
הֵם לְבוּשִׁים לְאוֹר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ;
are conceptual garments for the transcendent light of Hashem, blessed be He;
שֶׁבְּעַצְמוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ לֵית מַחֲשָׁבָה תְּפִיסָה בֵּיהּ כְּלָל,
for within His essence no mortal thought can grasp Him at all,
רַק עַל יְדֵי הַמִּצְווֹת מַכִּירִים יִשְׂרָאֵל עַצְמוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and only through the mitzvot do Israel perceive His divine essence,
וְזֶה נִקְרָאִים "לְבוּשִׁים";
and these are titled ‘garments’;
כְּמוֹ לְבוּשִׁים שֶׁל הַכֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל שֶׁמּוֹרִים עַל עַצְמוּת הַכֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל,
like the vestments of the High Priest which signify the essence of the High Priest,
כִּי עַל הַצִּיץ הָיָה כָּתוּב "קֹדֶשׁ לַה'",
for upon the golden plate (tzitz) was inscribed ‘Holy unto Hashem,’
הַיְינוּ שֶׁכָּל מַחְשְׁבוֹת שֶׁל הַכֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל דָּבוּק בְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ;
meaning that all thoughts of the High Priest were cleaving to Hashem, blessed be He;
וְכֵן בַּחֹשֶׁן הָיָה מוּנָּח הַשֵּׁם הַמְפוֹרָשׁ
and likewise within the breastplate was deposited the Ineffable Name,
שֶׁמּוֹרֶה שֶׁלִּבּוֹ נָקִי מִכָּל סִיג וּפְסֹלֶת.
which demonstrates that his heart was cleansed from all dross and defect.
וְכֵן עַל יְדֵי שֶׁנָּתַן לָנוּ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ תּוֹרָה וּמִצְווֹת
And likewise through Hashem bestowing upon us Torah and commandments,
שֶׁהֵם לְבוּשִׁים לְאוֹר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
which serve as garments for Hashem’s light,
עַל יְדֵי כֵן אָנוּ דְּבוּקִים בְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
through this are we bound unto Hashem
וּמַכִּירִים שֶׁנִּמְצָא בּוֹרֵא עוֹלָם;
and recognize that there exists a Creator of the universe;
וְזֶהוּ מֵחֲמַת שֶׁלִּבּוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם הוּא מָלֵא נְגִיעָה,
and this requirement exists because the heart of mortal man is filled with personal bias,
לָכֵן עַל יְדֵי יְגִיעָה וַעֲבוֹדָה מְבָרֵר אֶת לִבּוֹ בְּהַלְּבוּשִׁים הָאֵלּוּ
therefore through toil and divine service he clarifies his heart within these garments
וְסוֹבֵל מִזֹּאת הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת וַעֲבוֹדָה;
and endures through this effort and spiritual service;
אָכֵן לֶעָתִיד, כַּאֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה לֵב הָאָדָם מְנוּקֶּה וּמְבוֹרָר בִּשְׁלֵימוּת,
however, in the World to Come, when the heart of man will be cleansed and refined in ultimate perfection,
אָז יִהְיֶה הִתְגַּלּוּת אֱלֹהוּת מְפוֹרָשׁ בְּלִי שׁוּם לְבוּשׁ.
divine revelation will then be manifest explicitly without any concealing garment.
וְהִנֵּה בַּזְּמַן הַהוּא הָיוּ אַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה
And behold, during that historical era lived the Men of the Great Assembly
שֶׁנִּצְּחוּ יִצְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, כִּדְאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (יוֹמָא סט:);
who conquered and nullified the evil inclination for idolatry, as taught in Yoma (69b);
וְיֵצֶר הָרָע דַּעֲרָיוֹת גַּם כֵּן הָיָה בְּיָדָם וְרָצוּ לְבַטְּלוֹ,
and the evil inclination for sexual immorality was likewise captured in their hands and they sought to eradicate it,
רַק מֵחֲמַת שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה אָז עֲדַיִן רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּזֶה,
only because it was not yet Hashem’s overarching will at that juncture,
כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רָצָה שֶׁיִּוָּולְדוּ עוֹד נְפָשׁוֹת יְקָרוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל,
since Hashem willed that further precious souls of Israel still be born,
לָכֵן הֶאֱרִיךְ עוֹד הַזְּמַן;
He therefore extended the timeline of history;
וְלָכֵן בָּזֶה הַזְּמַן הָיָה קָרוֹב הַדָּבָר שֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה אוֹר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְפוֹרָשׁ בְּלִי שׁוּם לְבוּשׁ,
and for that reason it was exceedingly close at that era for Hashem’s naked light to be revealed without garments,
וְכַמְבוֹאָר בְּחֵלֶק רִאשׁוֹן (שָׁם).
as explained in Part I (there).
וְהִנֵּה כְּתִיב (תְּהִלִּים סח, יב): "ה' יִתֶּן אֹמֶר הַמְבַשְּׂרוֹת צָבָא רָב",
And behold it is written (Psalms 68:12): “The Lord gave the word; great was the company of those that published it” –
הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְחַדֵּשׁ וּמְגַלֶּה אֵיזֶה אוֹר,
meaning that whenever Hashem renews and radiates a supernal illumination,
מִתְפַּשֵּׁט הָאוֹר לְהָאִיר בְּכָל הָעוֹלָמוֹת
that light expands to shine across all realms,
וְאַף הָאֻמּוֹת מַרְגִּישִׁים מִזֶּה מְעַט,
and even the gentile nations perceive a faint glimmer of it;
אַךְ הֵם מַרְגִּישִׁים בְּזוּהֲמָא וּבְגַשְׁמוּת,
yet they register it through defilement and coarse carnality,
אֲבָל יִשְׂרָאֵל יְקַבְּלוּ הָאוֹר כְּמוֹ שֶׁמַּשְׁפִּיעַ אוֹתוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ;
whereas Israel absorbs the light purely as Hashem emanates it;
וְלָכֵן אָז, שֶׁהָיָה קָרוֹב שֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה אוֹר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּלִי לְבוּשׁ, הִרְגִּישׁוּ הָאֻמּוֹת;
therefore then, when it was close for Hashem’s garmentless light to shine, the nations sensed it;
אַךְ הֵם הִרְגִּישׁוּ מְזוֹהָם וּמְגוּשָּׁם,
yet they registered it in a defiled, corporealized distortion,
לָכֵן רָצוּ גַּם הֵם בְּתַאֲוָתָם "עֲרֻמָּה", בְּלִי לְבוּשׁ;
hence in their base lust they demanded Vashti appear ‘naked,’ stripped of all garments;
וְזֶהוּ בֵּיאוּר דִּבְרֵי הַבַּעַל שֵׁם טוֹב זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
and this is the explanation of the Baal Shem Tov’s holy insight:
שֶׁזֶּה הָעִנְיָן הוּא "עֲרֻמָּה" וְלֹא בָּא,
that this matter was ‘naked’ and yet had not arrived,
שֶׁהָיָה קָרוֹב לְהִתְגַּלּוּת מְפוֹרָשׁ הָאוֹר בְּלִי לְבוּשׁ,
meaning it was on the verge of the explicit revelation of light without garments,
אַךְ עֲדַיִן לֹא בָּא עַד עֵת קֵץ.
yet it could not arrive until the final End of Days.
וְלָכֵן נִסְמַךְ לָזֶה מַאֲמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי
And therefore was juxtaposed to this the teaching of Rabbi Levi,
שֶׁהַפָּסוּק הַזֶּה עַל שֵׁם הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת נֶאֱמַר;
that this verse was stated concerning the sacrificial offerings;
הַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר בְּחֵלֶק רִאשׁוֹן (שָׁם)
meaning as explained in Part I (there):
שֶׁהָיוּ הַמַּלְאָכִים טוֹעֲנִים עַל זֶה:
that the ministering angels argued against this:
הֵיאַךְ יִהְיֶה לְעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת תְּפִיסָה לִבְלִי לְבוּשׁ אֲפִילּוּ בַּזּוּהֲמָא שֶׁלָּהֶם?
how could idolaters have any grasp of the garmentless light even in their crude defilement?
בִּשְׁלָמָא יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁיְּיַגְּעוּ אֶת עַצְמָם בִּלְבוּשִׁים,
Granted Israel, who toiled strenuously within holy garments,
לָכֵן אַחַר כָּךְ כְּשֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה הָאוֹר יִהְיֶה לָהֶם תְּפִיסָה בְּלִי לְבוּשׁ,
therefore afterward when the naked light shines they will possess true comprehension without garments,
וְכַמְבוֹאָר בְּחֵלֶק רִאשׁוֹן (שָׁם).
and as explained in Part I (there).
h: Holy Garments Prepare for Unconcealed Divine Light

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Talmud, Megillah 15a:1
p: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: בֹּא וּרְאֵה שֶׁלֹּא כְּמִדַּת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִדַּת בָּשָׂר וָדָם:
“And Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Chanina: Come and see that the way of the Holy One, blessed be He, is not like the way of flesh and blood;
מִדַּת בָּשָׂר וָדָם, אָדָם שׁוֹפֵת קְדֵרָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ נוֹתֵן לְתוֹכָהּ מַיִם,
the way of flesh and blood: a person sets the pot upon the fire and afterward pours water into it;
אֲבָל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נוֹתֵן מַיִם וְאַחַר כָּךְ שׁוֹפֵת הַקְּדֵרָה.
however the Holy One places the water first and afterward sets the pot.”
כָּל הַחֶמְדוֹת נִקְרָאוֹת בְּשֵׁם "מַיִם",
All longings and desires are termed ‘water,’
וּמִדַּת בָּשָׂר וָדָם הוּא "עַיִן רוֹאָה וְלֵב חוֹמֵד",
and the mortal way of flesh and blood is ‘the eye sees and the heart covets,’
וְזֶה נִקְרָא "שׁוֹפֵת הַקְּדֵרָה לְקַבֵּל הַמַּיִם",
and this is termed setting the pot to receive the water,
שֶׁהָעַיִן רוֹאָה מִקֹּדֶם וְאַחַר כָּךְ הַלֵּב חוֹמֵד;
in that the physical eye sees first and only afterward does the heart crave;
אֲבָל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא –
however with the Holy One, blessed be He –
הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁהָאָדָם דָּבוּק בְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְנִמְשָׁךְ אַחַר רְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
meaning when a person cleaves to Hashem and is drawn after His holy will,
בִּתְחִלָּה נוֹתֵן הַמַּיִם –
He first places the water –
הַיְינוּ שֶׁתְּחִלָּה יֵשׁ לוֹ חֵשֶׁק וְנִמְשָׁךְ אַחַר רְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
meaning that first a holy yearning arises in him and he is drawn after Hashem's will
אַף שֶׁאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ עֲדַיִן מַה הוּא רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
even before he knows consciously what Hashem’s specific will is,
וְאַחַר כֵּן מֵאִיר לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רְצוֹנוֹ,
and only afterward does Hashem illuminate His explicit will unto him,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר בְּחֵלֶק רִאשׁוֹן (פָּרָשַׁת בְּחֻקֹּתַי, דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "אִם בְּחֻקֹּתַי" ג').
as explained in Part I (Parashat Bechukotai, s.v. “Im Bechukotai” 3).
h: Holy Yearning Precedes the Revelation of Its Object

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Talmud, Megillah 18a:1
p: לָא הֲווֹ יָדְעֵי רַבָּנָן מַאי: "הַשְׁלֵךְ עַל ה' יְהָבְךָ";
“The Rabbis did not know what is meant by: ‘Cast your burden (yehavkha) upon Hashem’;
אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה: זִימְנָא חֲדָא הֲוָה אָזֵילְנָא בַּהֲדֵי הַהוּא טַיָּיעָא וְקָא דָּרֵינָא טוּנָא,
Rabbah bar Bar Chana said: One time I was walking with an Arab merchant and carrying a heavy burden,
אֲמַר לִי: שְׁקוֹל יְהָבָךְ וּשְׁדִי אַגַּמְלַאי.
he said to me: ‘Take your load (yehavakh) and throw it upon my camel’.”
הַיְינוּ כִּי הַחֲכָמִים לֹא יָדְעוּ עַד הֵיכָן מַגִּיעַ מִדַּת הַבִּטָּחוֹן לִבְטוֹחַ בְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיּוֹשִׁיעַ,
This means: the Sages did not know how far the attribute of trust extends to rely upon Hashem to save,
אֲפִילּוּ מַה שֶּׁלֹּא הָיְתָה דַּעַת הָאָדָם מְצַפָּה לָזֶה;
even in situations that human calculation would never anticipate;
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּרוֹב אַהֲבָתוֹ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
and that Hashem in His abundant love for Israel
יוֹשִׁיעַ לָהֶם לְכָל נֶפֶשׁ יְשׁוּעוֹת שֶׁהוּא בְּדַעְתּוֹ נִתְיָיאֵשׁ מֵהֶם.
will bestow upon every soul redemptions from which the person in his conscious mind had entirely despaired.
וְהֶרְאָה לָהֶם רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה לְהִתְבּוֹנֵן בְּהַהוּא טַיָּיעָא,
And Rabbah bar Bar Chana showed them to contemplate that Arab merchant,
שֶׁהוּא יִשְׁמָעֵאל, שֶׁהוּא מִקְּלִפַּת תַּאֲוָה,
who represents Ishmael stemming from the shell (kelipah) of lust,
וְכֵן גָּמָל רוֹמֵז עַל זֶה כַּמְבוֹאָר (בְּפָרָשַׁת שְׁמִינִי, דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "בַּגָּמָל") בְּחֵלֶק רִאשׁוֹן;
and likewise the camel signifies this as explained in Part I (Parashat Shemini, s.v. “Bagamal”);
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהֶרְאָה לָהֶם עַד הֵיכָן נוֹגֵעַ בְּרִית אָבוֹת:
meaning that he demonstrated how far the covenant of the Patriarchs reaches:
שֶׁאַף שֶׁיִּשְׁמָעֵאל הוּא זֶרַע פָּסוּל,
that even though Ishmael is discarded seed,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם מִפְּסוֹלֶת מִדָּתוֹ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ
nonetheless from the dross of Abraham’s attribute of Chesed
נִמְצָא גַּם בּוֹ אֵיזֶה גָּוֶון נְדִיבוּת;
there remains within him a superficial semblance of generous kindness;
וְאַף שֶׁאֶצְלוֹ עוֹשֶׂה בְּזֹאת הַמִּדָּה
and although with the Ishmaelite he utilizes this trait
וּמִתְפַּשְּׁטָה בִּפְסִיעָתוֹ לְבַר הֵיפֶךְ מֵרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
expanding in outward stepping contrary to Hashem's will,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם נִמְצָא בּוֹ גָּוֶון נְדִיבוּת
nevertheless a semblance of generosity exists within him
עַד שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ: "שְׁקוֹל יְהָבָךְ וּשְׁדִי אַגַּמְלַאי",
so that he said: ‘take your burden and throw it upon my camel,’
אַף שֶׁרַבָּה לֹא בִּקֵּשׁ זֹאת מִמֶּנּוּ;
even though Rabbah had never requested this of him;
וְכָל זֶה הוּא מֵחֲמַת שֶׁנִּמְצְאוּ בּוֹ נוֹבְלוֹת מֵחֶסֶד שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ.
and all this is because there reside in him the fallen traces of Abraham's lovingkindness.
וּמִכָּל שֶׁכֵּן (אֵיכָה ג, כב): "חַסְדֵי ה' כִּי לֹא תָמְנוּ, כִּי לֹא כָלוּ רַחֲמָיו",
And all the more so: “The lovingkindnesses of Hashem never cease, for His compassions fail not,”
שֶׁהֵם מְאִירִים יְשׁוּעוֹת מַה שֶּׁלֹּא עָלָה עַל דַּעַת שׁוּם אָדָם;
which illuminate redemptions that never entered any human mind;
וַאֲפִילּוּ אִם נֶפֶשׁ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל חָלִילָה מְשׁוּקָּע בְּמִדָּה אַחַת,
and even if a Jewish soul is Heaven forbid submerged in a corrupt trait,
אֲפִילּוּ בְּמִדַּת הַתַּאֲוָה שֶׁלֹּא עַל פִּי רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
even within illicit lust contrary to Hashem's will,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם כְּשֶׁעוֹשֶׂה תְּשׁוּבָה,
nevertheless when he performs teshuvah,
הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּרוֹב רַחֲמָיו וַחֲסָדָיו יְבָרֵר בְּרוֹב בֵּירוּרִים
Hashem in His abundant mercies and kindness will refine him with countless purifications
עַד שֶׁלֹּא יִדַּח מִמֶּנּוּ נִדָּח.
until the castaway not remain banished from Him.
h: Divine Kindness Brings Unanticipated Salvation

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Talmud, Megillah 25a:1
p: הַקּוֹרֵא אֶת שְׁמַע וּכְפָלָהּ – הֲרֵי זֶה מְגוּנֶּה.
“One who recites the Shema and repeats it—behold this is disgraceful.”
וְאַף שֶׁאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (בְּרָכוֹת י:):
And even though it is taught in the Gemara (Berakhot 10b):
הַקּוֹרֵא מִכָּאן וְאֵילָךְ לֹא הִפְסִיד, כְּאָדָם הַקּוֹרֵא בַּתּוֹרָה,
one who recites it after its proper time has not lost, being like one who reads Torah,
אִם כֵּן לָמָּה אוֹמֵר כָּאן שֶׁהוּא מְגוּנֶּה?
if so, why does the Mishnah state here that repeating it is disgraceful?
אַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת, צָרִיךְ הָאָדָם לְהַמְלִיךְ אֶת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּכָל רֶגַע
However in truth, man must crown Hashem at every single instant
עַל זֶה הַזְּמַן שֶׁעוֹמֵד בּוֹ וְכֵן עַל לְהַבָּא;
over the present moment wherein he stands and likewise over the future;
אֲבָל לְהַמְלִיךְ אֶת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל הַזְּמַן הֶעָבָר,
however, to crown Hashem over the past,
זֶה אֵינוֹ בִּיכוֹלֶת הָאָדָם,
this is beyond mortal human capacity;
כִּי זֶה עָבַר וְאֵינוֹ בְּיָדוֹ,
for the past has vanished and is no longer in his hand,
רַק בְּיַד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְהַחְזִיר אֶת הַקּוֹדֵם;
it being strictly in Hashem’s hand to rectify and transform the past;
אֲבָל בְּיַד הָאָדָם הוּא רַק הַהֹוֶה וְהֶעָתִיד;
for man has dominion only over the present and the future;
וְלָכֵן הַכּוֹפֵל אֶת שְׁמַע –
therefore one who doubles the Shema –
הַיְינוּ שֶׁמְּקַבֵּל עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם עַל הֶעָבָר,
meaning he presumes to accept the yoke of Heaven over the past,
שֶׁאוֹמֵר שֶׁגַּם הֶעָבָר בְּיָדוֹ –
as though the past were also within his autonomous control—
הֲרֵי זֶה מְגוּנֶּה.
behold this is disgraceful.
h: Accepting Heaven in the Present and Future

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Talmud, Megillah 27b:1
p: שָׁאֲלוּ תַּלְמִידָיו אֶת רַבִּי זַכַּאי: בַּמֶּה הֶאֱרַכְתָּ יָמִים?
“His disciples asked Rabbi Zakkai: In virtue of what have you lived long?
אָמַר לָהֶם: מִיָּמַי לֹא הִשְׁתַּנְתִּי מַיִם בְּתוֹךְ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שֶׁל תְּפִלָּה.
He said to them: In all my days I never urinated within four cubits of prayer.”
הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא נִכְנַסְתִּי לִתְפִלָּה עִם דִּמְיוֹן,
This means: I never entered into prayer with false illusion and vanity,
שֶׁזֶּה מוֹרֶה "הִשְׁתַּנְתִּי מַיִם",
which is what ‘urinating water’ signifies,
כִּדְאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (בְּכוֹרוֹת מד:):
as taught in the Gemara (Bekhorot 44b):
שְׁנֵי נְקָבִים יֵשׁ בָּאָדָם, אֶחָד מוֹצִיא שֶׁתֶן וְאֶחָד מוֹצִיא שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע;
man possesses two conduits: one discharges urine and one discharges seminal seed;
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאֶחָד מוֹצִיא זֶרַע לְהַחֲיוֹת זֶרַע,
meaning that the one issues seed to generate holy life,
וְהַשֵּׁנִי הוּא דִּמְיוֹן.
while the other is mere waste and illusion.
h: Entering Prayer Free From False Illusion

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Talmud, Megillah 28a:1
p: שָׁאֲלוּ תַּלְמִידָיו אֶת רַבִּי זֵירָא: בַּמֶּה הֶאֱרַכְתָּ יָמִים?
“His disciples asked Rabbi Zeira: In virtue of what have you lived long?
אָמַר לָהֶם וְכוּלֵי: וְלֹא הִרְהַרְתִּי בִּמְבוֹאוֹת הַמְטוּנָּפוֹת.
He said to them, etc.: And I never meditated in filthy alleys.”
שֶׁלֹּא הִרְהַרְתִּי בְּעִנְיָנִים הַמְלַכְלְכִים דַּעַת הָאָדָם.
Meaning: I never allowed myself to contemplate thoughts that soil the spiritual consciousness of man.
h: Guarding the Mind From Defiling Thoughts

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Talmud, Megillah 32b:1
p: קְלָלוֹת שֶׁבְּמִשְׁנֵה תּוֹרָה – מֹשֶׁה מִפִּי עַצְמוֹ אֲמָרָן.
“The curses in Deuteronomy—Moses uttered them from his own mouth.”
הַיְינוּ כִּי לְכָל גְּדוֹלֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מְנַסֶּה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּזֶה
This means: because all the great leaders of Israel Hashem tests
שֶׁמַּעֲלִים וּמַסְתִּיר מֵהֶם אוֹרוֹ,
by concealing and withdrawing His manifest light from them,
וְיִרְאוּ כָּל הָעוֹלָם הֵיאַךְ יִתְנַהֲגוּ אָז;
so that the whole world witnesses how they conduct themselves during obscurity;
וְלָכֵן גַּם בְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ הִסְתִּיר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ דַּרְכּוֹ,
and therefore with Moses our teacher Hashem likewise veiled His path,
וְאָז אָמַר הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה אֵלּוּ,
and right then did Moses utter these words of Torah,
שֶׁבָּהֶם נִכְלָלוּ הַרְבֵּה בְּרָכוֹת.
within which are enveloped countless profound blessings.
h: Hidden Blessings in Words Spoken During Concealment

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Talmud, Taanit 20a:1
p: תָּנוּ רַבָּנָן: לְעוֹלָם יְהֵא אָדָם רַךְ כְּקָנֶה וְאַל יְהֵא קָשֶׁה כְּאֶרֶז.
“Our Rabbis taught: A person should always be soft as a reed and not hard as a cedar.”
וּבֶאֱמֶת, הָא כְּתִיב (תְּהִלִּים צב, יג): "כְּאֶרֶז בַּלְּבָנוֹן יִשְׂגֶּה"?
Yet in truth, is it not written (Psalms 92:13): “he shall grow like a cedar in Lebanon”?
אָכֵן זֶה צָרִיךְ לְהִמָּצֵא בָּאָדָם עַצְמוֹ,
However, that cedar-like firmness must exist within the person himself,
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין עַצְמוֹ תַּקִּיפוּת וָעֹז בְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
that between himself and his own soul he maintains unwavering fortitude and strength in Hashem,
וְלֹא יִהְיֶה לוֹ הִתְרַשְּׁלוּת;
allowing no spiritual laxity or indolence;
אֲבָל נֶגֶד חֲבֵירוֹ צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת רַךְ כְּקָנֶה.
however, toward his fellow man he must be gentle and soft as a reed.
h: Inner Firmness and Gentleness Toward Others

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Talmud, Taanit 30b:1
p: אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: לֹא הָיוּ יָמִים טוֹבִים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל כַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּאָב וּכְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים.
“Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said: There were no days as festive for Israel as the Fifteenth of Av and Yom Kippur.”
וְאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (שָׁם):
And it is taught in the Gemara (there):
חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּאָב מַאי הִיא?
What is the significance of the Fifteenth of Av?
אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: יוֹם שֶׁהֻתְּרוּ שְׁבָטִים לָבוֹא זֶה בָּזֶה;
Rabbi Yehudah said in the name of Shmuel: The day on which the tribes were permitted to intermarry;
אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: יוֹם שֶׁהֻתַּר שֵׁבֶט בִּנְיָמִין לָבוֹא בַּקָּהָל;
Rav Yosef said in the name of Rav Nachman: The day on which the tribe of Benjamin was permitted to re-enter the congregation;
הַיְינוּ יוֹם שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה שָׁלוֹם וְנִתְקָרְבוּ הַמְרוּחָקִים,
meaning a day wherein peace was forged and the estranged were drawn close,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (יְשַׁעְיָה נז, יט): "בּוֹרֵא נִיב שְׂפָתָיִם שָׁלוֹם שָׁלוֹם לָרָחוֹק וְלַקָּרוֹב".
as it is written (Isaiah 57:19): “Creating the fruit of the lips: Peace, peace to him that is far off and to him that is near.”
רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שֶׁכָּלוּ בּוֹ מֵתֵי מִדְבָּר,
Rabbah bar Bar Chana said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: The day on which the dying of the generation of the wilderness ceased,
שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם זָכוּ לְחַיִּים שֶׁל אֱמֶת;
in that on that day they attained authentic eternal life;
עוּלָּא אָמַר: יוֹם שֶׁבִּטֵּל הוֹשֵׁעַ בֶּן אֵלָה פְּרוֹסְדָּיוֹת שֶׁהוֹשִׁיב יָרָבְעָם בֶּן נְבָט עַל הַדְּרָכִים.
Ulla said: The day on which Hoshea son of Elah removed the blockades that Jeroboam son of Nebat had stationed upon the roads to prevent pilgrimage to Jerusalem.
הַיְינוּ שֶׁבְּזֶה הַיּוֹם נִמְצָא כֹּחַ הַמּוֹעֲדִים,
Meaning that within this day resides the core power of the pilgrimage festivals,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁרָאִינוּ שֶׁנִּתְחַזֵּק בְּזֶה הַיּוֹם מִצְוַת עֲלִיַּת רְגָלִים,
just as we observed that the mitzvah of festival pilgrimage was reinvigorated on this day,
וּבֶטַח יֵשׁ בָּזֶה שַׁיָּיכוּת לְזֶה הַיּוֹם;
and surely there exists an essential connection to this specific day;
וּבְכָל שָׁנָה וְשָׁנָה נִמְצָא כֹּחַ הַזֶּה בְּזֶה הַיּוֹם,
and in every single year this spiritual force is renewed on this day,
כִּי בְּאִם לָאו לֹא נִתְחַזֵּק עֲלִיַּת רְגָלִים דַּוְקָא בְּזֶה הַיּוֹם, כִּי הָעוֹלָם אֵינוֹ בְּמִקְרֶה.
for otherwise the pilgrimage would not have been restored specifically on this date, since the universe does not run on coincidence.
רַב מַתְנָא אָמַר: יוֹם שֶׁנִּתְּנוּ הֲרוּגֵי בֵּיתָר לִקְבוּרָה,
Rav Matna said: The day on which the slain of Beitar were granted burial,
שֶׁנִּמְצָא בְּזֶה הַיּוֹם רָצוֹן,
for on this day divine favor and goodwill were uncovered,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (תְּהִלִּים סט, יד): "וַאֲנִי תְפִלָּתִי לְךָ ה' עֵת רָצוֹן",
as written (Psalms 69:14): “But as for me, let my prayer be unto You, Hashem, in an acceptable time,”
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (בְּרָכוֹת ח.):
and as taught in the Gemara (Berakhot 8a):
לִיבְעֵי אִינִישׁ רַחֲמֵי אֲפִילּוּ עַד זִיבּוּלָא בַּתְרָיְיתָא שְׁלָמָא.
a person should plead for mercy even unto the final shovelful of dirt in burial.
רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף דְּאָמְרֵי תַּרְוַויְיהוּ: יוֹם שֶׁפָּסְקוּ מִלִּכְרֹת עֵצִים לַמַּעֲרָכָה, שֶׁתָּשַׁשׁ כֹּחָהּ שֶׁל חַמָּה;
Rabbah and Rav Yosef both said: The day on which they ceased cutting wood for the altar arrangement, because the strength of the sun had weakened;
הַיְינוּ שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם יַתְחִיל הִתְגַּבְּרוּת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל עַל עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
meaning that on that day begins the spiritual ascendance of Israel over the pagan idolaters,
וְיֵצֵא כּוֹחָם שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאוֹרָם מְפוֹרָשׁ;
and the power and light of Israel will emerge explicitly;
כִּי עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת עוֹבְדִים וּמוֹנִים לַחַמָּה,
for idolaters worship and calculate according to the sun,
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁנִּרְאֶה שֶׁלִּפְעָמִים יוּתַּשׁ כֹּחַ הַחַמָּה,
and since it is visibly demonstrated that the power of the sun weakens,
בָּזֶה יְבוֹרַר שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ כֹּחַ עַצְמוֹ, רַק יֵשׁ מוֹשֵׁל גַּם עַל הַחַמָּה.
through this it is clarified that it has no autonomous power of its own, but rather a Sovereign Ruler governs the sun.
וּמְסַיֵּים שָׁם: אָמַר עוּלָּא בֵּירָאָה אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
And the Gemara concludes there: Ulla Bira’ah said in the name of Rabbi Elazar:
עָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לַעֲשׂוֹת מָחוֹל לַצַּדִּיקִים, וְהוּא יוֹשֵׁב בֵּינֵיהֶם בְּגַן עֵדֶן,
The Holy One is destined to make a circle dance for the righteous, with Him sitting among them in Gan Eden,
וְכָל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד מַרְאֶה בְּאֶצְבָּעוֹ;
and each one points with his finger;
הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֶּעָתִיד יְבָרֵר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
meaning that in the ultimate future the Holy One will demonstrate
שֶׁכָּל כַּוָּונַת יִשְׂרָאֵל הִיא רַק לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם,
that the entire intention of Israel was purely for the sake of Heaven,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (יְשַׁעְיָה כה, ט):
as it is written (Isaiah 25:9):
"וְאָמַר בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא: הִנֵּה אֱלֹהֵינוּ זֶה קִוִּינוּ לוֹ וְיוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ, זֶה ה' קִוִּינוּ לוֹ נָגִילָה וְנִשְׂמְחָה בִּישׁוּעָתוֹ".
“And it shall be said in that day: Behold, this is our God, we have waited for Him, and He will save us; this is Hashem, we have waited for Him, we will be glad and rejoice in His salvation.”
h: The Fifteenth of Av and the Revelation of Favor

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Talmud, Chagigah 5b:1
p: רַב אִידִי, אֲבוּהּ דְּרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי, הֲוָה רָגִיל דַּהֲוָה אָזֵיל תְּלָתָא יַרְחֵי בְּאוֹרְחָא וְחַד יוֹמָא בְּבֵי רַב;
“Rav Idi, father of Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi, was accustomed to travel three months on the road and spend one day in the study hall;
וַהֲווֹ קָרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן 'בַּר בֵּי רַב דְּחַד יוֹמָא'.
and the scholars mockingly called him ‘the one-day scholar.’
חָלַשׁ דַּעְתֵּיהּ, קָרֵי אַנַּפְשֵׁיהּ (אִיּוֹב יב, ד): 'שְׂחֹק לְרֵעֵהוּ אֶהְיֶה' וְכוּלֵי.
He became disheartened, and applied to himself (Job 12:4): ‘I am as one that is a mockery to his neighbor,’ etc.”
אַף שֶׁנִּרְאֶה שֶׁשָּׂחֲקוּ מִמֶּנּוּ,
Although it superficially appears that they were mocking him,
אָכֵן בֶּאֱמֶת הֵבִינוּ
yet in truth they comprehended
כִּי בָּא עַל יוֹם שֶׁהָיָה מוּכָן לוֹ
that he arrived precisely upon that single day destined for him
לְהַגִּיעַ לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה הַשַּׁיָּיכִים אֵלָיו בְּיִחוּד.
to attain those words of Torah uniquely tailored to his individual soul.
h: A Single Day Suited to a Particular Soul

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Talmud, Chagigah 9b:1
p: אֲמַר לֵיהּ בַּר הֵא הֵא לְהִלֵּל: מַאי דִּכְתִיב (מַלְאָכִי ג, יח):
“Bar Hei Hei said to Hillel: What is the meaning of that which is written (Malachi 3:18):
"וְשַׁבְתֶּם וּרְאִיתֶם בֵּין צַדִּיק לְרָשָׁע, בֵּין עֹבֵד אֱלֹהִים לַאֲשֶׁר לֹא עֲבָדוֹ"?
‘Then shall you return and discern between the righteous and the wicked, between him that serves God and him that serves Him not’?
הַיְינוּ "צַדִּיק" הַיְינוּ "עֹבֵד אֱלֹהִים" וְכוּלֵי?
Is not ‘righteous’ identical to ‘him that serves God’, etc.?
אֲמַר לֵיהּ: "עֲבָדוֹ" וְ"לֹא עֲבָדוֹ" – תַּרְוַויְיהוּ צַדִּיקֵי גְּמוּרֵי נִינְהוּ,
Hillel said to him: ‘Him that serves Him’ and ‘him that serves Him not’—both of them are wholly righteous;
וְאֵינוֹ דוֹמֶה שׁוֹנֶה פִּרְקוֹ מֵאָה פְּעָמִים לְשׁוֹנֶה פִּרְקוֹ מֵאָה וְאֶחָד.
and one who reviews his chapter a hundred times does not compare to one who reviews it a hundred and one times.”
שֶׁעִנְיַן הָ"אֶחָד" מוֹרֶה
For the theme of the ‘one’ additional review demonstrates
שֶׁאַף שֶׁשּׁוֹנֶה מֵאָה פְּעָמִים – עֲדַיִן הוּא עוֹמֵד בַּהַתְחָלָה;
that even after reviewing a hundred times—he still stands at the fresh inception;
וְזֶה הָעִנְיָן שֶׁל "וְאֶחָד" –
and this is the essence of ‘and one’ –
הַיְינוּ שֶׁעֲדַיִן עוֹמֵד אֶצְלוֹ "וְאֶחָד",
meaning that the ‘one’ still stands before him,
שֶׁהוּא אֶצְלוֹ כַּחֲדָשָׁה בְּחֵשֶׁק וּתְשׁוּקָה רַבָּה, וְלֹא כִּדְבָרִים יְשָׁנִים;
such that it remains for him brand new with fresh craving and great yearning, and not as stale routine;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (דְּבָרִים כו, טז): "הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ מְצַוְּךָ לַעֲשׂוֹת",
and as it is written (Deuteronomy 26:16): “This day Hashem your God commands you to do,”
וְדָרְשׁוּ חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: שֶׁיִּהְיוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה חֲדָשִׁים עָלֶיךָ.
and our Sages expounded: let words of Torah be brand new upon you each day.
h: The Hundred and First Review as a New Beginning

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Talmud, Yevamot 72a:1
p: הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לָן, דְּעֵת רָצוֹן מִילְּתָא הִיא.
“This comes to teach us that an ‘acceptable time’ (et ratzon) is a substantial reality.”
הַיְינוּ מַה שֶּׁפְּעָמִים הָאָדָם מַרְגִּישׁ חֵשֶׁק וְרָצוֹן
This means: that which at times a person feels a deep yearning and desire
לִדְרוֹשׁ אֶת ה' וְעֻזּוֹ וּלְבַקֵּשׁ פָּנָיו,
to seek Hashem and His strength and to search for His presence,
זֶהוּ "עֵת רָצוֹן";
this constitutes an ‘et ratzon’ (an hour of supernal favor);
וּ"מִילְּתָא" הִיא –
and ‘it is a substantial matter’ teaches:
שֶׁיְּאַמֵּץ אָז אֶת לִבּוֹ בִּתְפִלָּה,
that he should vigorously strengthen his heart in prayer at that very moment,
שֶׁיִּתְפַּלֵּל לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּקְבַּע זֹאת בְּלִבּוֹ כְּיָתֵד לֹא יִמּוֹט לְעוֹלָם,
praying to Hashem that He establish this in his heart like a tent-peg that will never move,
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה תָּמִיד זֶה הַחֵשֶׁק וְהָרָצוֹן בְּלִבּוֹ;
so that this longing and holy will remain forever within his heart;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ,
just as we found with King David,
כְּשֶׁהָיְתָה לוֹ נְדִיבוּת וְרָצוֹן בְּכָל לִבּוֹ הִתְפַּלֵּל לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
who when experiencing overflowing goodwill and desire with all his heart prayed to Hashem,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א כט, יח):
as it is stated (I Chronicles 29:18):
"ה' אֱלֹהֵי אַבְרָהָם יִצְחָק וְיִשְׂרָאֵל אֲבֹתֵינוּ שָׁמְרָה זֹּאת לְעוֹלָם לְיֵצֶר מַחְשְׁבוֹת לְבַב עַמֶּךָ",
“Hashem, God of Abraham, Isaac, and of Israel, our fathers, keep this forever in the imagination of the thoughts of the heart of Your people,”
הַיְינוּ שֶׁזֶּה הָרָצוֹן יִקָּבַע בְּלִבֵּנוּ לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד,
meaning that this holy desire be engraved in our hearts for all eternity,
וְזֶהוּ "עֵת רָצוֹן מִילְּתָא הִיא".
and this is ‘an acceptable time is a substantial reality.’
h: Praying for Holy Desire to Endure

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Talmud, Yevamot 75b:1
p: "וַיֹּאמֶר ה' אֶל שָׁאוּל וְאֶל בֵּית הַדָּמִים" (שְׁמוּאֵל ב כא, א) –
“And Hashem said: It is for Saul, and for his bloody house” (II Samuel 21:1) –
"אֶל שָׁאוּל" – שֶׁלֹּא נִסְפַּד כַּהֲלָכָה;
“for Saul”—because he was not eulogized according to halakhah;
"וְאֶל בֵּית הַדָּמִים" – עַל אֲשֶׁר הֵמִית הַגִּבְעוֹנִים וְכוּלֵי.
“and for his bloody house”—because he slew the Gibeonites, etc.
אָמַר דָּוִד: שָׁאוּל נְפַקוּ לְהוּ תְּרֵיסַר יַרְחֵי שַׁתָּא וְלָא דַּרְכֵּיהּ לְאַסְפְּדֵיהּ;
David said: For Saul, twelve months of the year have already passed and it is not customary to eulogize him now;
נְתִינִים – נִיקְרִינְהוּ וּנְפַיְּיסִינְהוּ.
as for the Gibeonites—let us summon them and appease them.
לְהָבִין, אִם כֵּן לָמָּה עָנַשׁ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל הַחֵטְא מַה שֶּׁלֹּא נִסְפַּד שָׁאוּל?
To understand: if so, why did Hashem punish for the failure to eulogize Saul,
הֲלֹא הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יָדַע שֶׁכְּבָר נָפְקוּ תְּרֵיסַר יַרְחֵי שַׁתָּא וְלֹא יוּכְלוּ לְתַקֵּן?
when Hashem knew that twelve months had already elapsed and they could no longer rectify it?
מִזֶּה הוּא לִימּוּד
From this emerges a vital lesson:
שֶׁאִם חָלִילָה יַעַבְרוּ מְאוֹרָעוֹת עַל הָאָדָם אוֹ עַל כְּלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
that if hardships, Heaven forbid, befall a person or the collective community of Israel,
וְלָא חָשׁוּד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא דְּעָבֵיד דִּינָא בְּלָא דִּינָא,
and the Holy One is never suspected of executing judgment without a righteous cause;
וְאַף שֶׁהָאָדָם יוֹדֵעַ בְּדַעְתּוֹ שֶׁכְּבָר לֹא יָכוֹל לְתַקֵּן חֶטְאוֹ
and even though a person knows in his mind that he can no longer rectify his past omission,
וְאַף שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יוֹדֵעַ זֹאת,
and even though Hashem likewise knows this full well,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם צָרִיךְ הָאָדָם מִצַּדּוֹ לְפַשְׁפֵּשׁ בְּמַעֲשָׂיו
nevertheless man must actively examine his deeds from his own side
וְלוֹמַר: מָה אֶעֱשֶׂה, הֲלֹא עוֹד אֵין בְּיָדִי לְתַקֵּן וְהַמְּנִיעָה הִיא בְּהֶכְרֵחַ!
and articulate: ‘What can I do, when it is no longer in my power to mend and the prevention was unavoidable!’
וּבָזֶה יְכֻפַּר עֲווֹנוֹ;
and through this heartfelt admission his iniquity is atoned;
וְלֹא יִסְמוֹךְ עַל מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יוֹדֵעַ זֹאת הַמְּנִיעָה,
and he must not rely passively on the fact that Hashem knows this constraint,
רַק הוּא מִצַּדּוֹ צָרִיךְ לְהִצְטַדֵּק בְּאָמְרוֹ כֵּן.
rather he must verbally vindicate himself through articulating this humble acknowledgment.
h: Acknowledging a Past Failure Beyond Present Repair

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Talmud, Ketubot 5a:1
p: דָּרַשׁ בַּר קַפָּרָא: גְּדוֹלִים מַעֲשֵׂה צַדִּיקִים יוֹתֵר מִמַּעֲשֵׂה שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ;
“Bar Kappara expounded: Greater are the works of the righteous than the creation of heaven and earth;
דְּאִילּוּ בְּמַעֲשֵׂה שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ כְּתִיב (יְשַׁעְיָה מח, יג): "אַף יָדִי יָסְדָה אֶרֶץ וִימִינִי טִפְּחָה שָׁמָיִם",
for regarding the creation of heaven and earth it is written (Isaiah 48:13): ‘My hand also has laid the foundation of the earth, and My right hand has spanned the heavens’ (each with one hand),
וְאִילּוּ בְּמַעֲשֵׂה יְדֵיהֶם שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים כְּתִיב (שְׁמוֹת טו, יז):
whereas regarding the work of the hands of the righteous it is written (Exodus 15:17):
"מָכוֹן לְשִׁבְתְּךָ פָּעַלְתָּ ה' מִקְּדָשׁ ה' כּוֹנְנוּ יָדֶיךָ".
‘The place, Hashem, which You have made for You to dwell in, the Sanctuary, O Lord, which Your hands have established’ (with two hands).”
הָעִנְיָן בָּזֶה, כִּי בְּרִיאַת שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ הָיְתָה כְּדֵי שֶׁיַּכִּיר הָאָדָם שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִמְצָא בָּעוֹלָם;
The inner meaning is that the creation of heaven and earth occurred in order that man recognize that Hashem is present in the world;
וְאִם הָיְתָה מְפוֹרֶשֶׁת זֹאת בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת,
and had this truth been overtly explicit,
אֵין שׁוּם מָקוֹם לִפְעֻלּוֹת אָדָם;
there would have remained no room for human action;
לָכֵן הִסְתִּיר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ זֹאת וְהִלְבִּישׁ זֹאת בִּלְבוּשִׁים;
therefore Hashem concealed it and enclothed it in worldly garments;
וְלָכֵן נִדְמֶה שֶׁעוֹלָם כְּמִנְהָגוֹ נוֹהֵג
and therefore it appears as though nature runs its course,
וְאֵינוֹ נִרְאֶה הַכָּרַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְפוֹרָשׁ;
and the recognition of Hashem is not overtly manifest;
רַק עַל יְדֵי מַעֲשֵׂה יְדֵיהֶם שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים,
rather through the deeds of the hands of the righteous,
הַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי מַעֲשֵׂה הַמִּצְווֹת,
namely through the active performance of mitzvot,
אָז נִתְרָאֶה הִתְגַּלּוּת אוֹר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּעוֹלָם.
then does the revelation of Hashem's light become manifest in the world.
וְכָל זֶה הוּא שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חָפֵץ לְהַצְדִּיק בְּרִיּוֹתָיו,
And all this is because Hashem desires to vindicate His creatures,
לָכֵן נָתַן מָקוֹם שֶׁעַל יְדֵי פְּעֻלּוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל נִתְגַּלָּה זֹאת;
therefore He provided conceptual room so that through the actions of Israel this is unveiled;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בְּעֵת שֶׁנִּגְמַר בִּנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
just as we found when the building of the Temple was completed,
הָיוּ כָּל הָאֻמּוֹת מַכִּירִים הִתְגַּלּוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּעוֹלָם,
all the nations recognized the revelation of Hashem in the world,
וְזֶה נִקְרָא "בִּשְׁתֵּי יָדַיִם",
and this is termed ‘with two hands,’
הַיְינוּ בִּשְׁלֵימוּת הַגָּמוּר.
meaning in absolute completion.
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם (קֹהֶלֶת א, ג):
And concerning this King Solomon, peace be upon him, declared (Ecclesiastes 1:3):
"מַה יִּתְרוֹן לָאָדָם בְּכָל עֲמָלוֹ שֶׁיַּעֲמֹל תַּחַת הַשָּׁמֶשׁ",
“What profit has a man of all his toil wherein he labors under the sun?”
כִּי "שֶׁמֶשׁ" נִקְרָא בְּהִירוּת, הַיְינוּ אוֹר מְפוֹרָשׁ;
for the ‘sun’ designates crystalline lucidity, namely explicit light;
וְ"תַחַת הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ" – הַיְינוּ שֶׁנִּסְתָּר אוֹר הַבָּהִיר
and ‘under the sun’ signifies where the clear light is concealed
כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מָקוֹם לִפְעֻלּוֹת אָדָם;
in order that there be room for human initiative;
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁעִיקַּר מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים לְהָאִיר וּלְהוֹסִיף עַל מַעֲשֵׂה שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ
and since the core purpose of the deeds of the righteous is to illuminate and add upon the creation of heaven and earth
וּלְהַרְאוֹת מְפוֹרָשׁ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִמְצָא בְּכָל הָעוֹלָמוֹת,
and to demonstrate explicitly that Hashem is present in all worlds,
אִם כֵּן, כֵּיוָן שֶׁמַּעֲשֵׂיהֶם אֵינָם מְבוֹרָרִים בִּשְׁלֵימוּת, מַה יִּתְרוֹן בְּכָל עֲמָלָם?
if so, when their deeds are not yet completely refined, what profit is there in all their toil?
כֵּיוָן שֶׁכָּל מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם הוּא לְהָאִיר אֶת הַהֶעְלֵם שֶׁנִּקְרָא "תַּחַת הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ",
Seeing that their whole striving is to illuminate the concealment called ‘under the sun,’
וְאִם אֵין מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם מְבוֹרָרִים בִּשְׁלֵימוּת – אִם כֵּן מַה יִּתְרוֹן בִּפְעֻלָּתָם?
and if their actions are not wholly refined—what profit is there in their labor?
וְנִתְבָּאֵר בְּחֵלֶק זֶה (קֹהֶלֶת) שֶׁזֶּה הַפָּסוּק מֵאִיר גַּם כֵּן תַּקִּיפוּת לָאָדָם,
And it was explained in this Part (Ecclesiastes) that this verse likewise radiates fortitude unto man:
כֵּיוָן שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חוֹתֵם עַל זֶה
since Hashem seals and confirms this:
שֶׁבִּפְעֻלָּתָם יְכַוְּונוּ אֶת עֹמֶק רְצוֹנוֹ,
that in their overall toil they align with the depth of His will,
אִם כֵּן בֶּטַח גַּם עַל סֵדֶר הַפְּעֻלּוֹת בִּפְרָטִים גַּם כֵּן יַסְכִּים הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ;
if so, surely Hashem will likewise give assent to the specific detailed order of their actions;
כִּמְשַׁל הַמְסַדֵּר עֲטָרָה לַמֶּלֶךְ,
like the parable of one setting a crown for the king,
וְהָיָה מְסוּפָּק אִם כִּיוֵּון בְּסִדּוּרוֹ לִרְצוֹן הַמֶּלֶךְ,
and doubted whether he aligned the stones to the king's pleasure,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ עָלָה בְּדַעְתּוֹ גַּם עַל עֶצֶם הָאֲבָנִים טוֹבוֹת אוּלַי אֵינָם אֲבָנִים טוֹבוֹת,
and afterward it occurred to him regarding the gems themselves that perhaps they were not precious stones,
וְאָז לֹא פָּחַד כְּלָל:
and right then his fear vanished entirely;
כֵּיוָן שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ יַסְכִּים עַל עֶצֶם הָאֲבָנִים טוֹבוֹת,
reasoning that since the king validates the very gems,
בֶּטַח יַסְכִּים עַל הַסֵּדֶר שֶׁסִּדְּרָם כְּעֹמֶק רְצוֹן הַמֶּלֶךְ;
he will surely validate the arrangement as matching the king’s desire;
וְלָכֵן הָעֵצָה לָזֶה
therefore the counsel for this is
שֶׁיִּקְבַּע אוֹתָם כְּפִי כֹּחוֹ וְחָכְמָתוֹ
that he set them according to his strength and wisdom,
וּבֶטַח הַמֶּלֶךְ, זֶה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, יַסְכִּים עַל הַכֹּל;
and surely the King, Who is Hashem, will consent to all;
כֵּיוָן שֶׁכָּל עִיקַּר הָרָצוֹן בִּפְעֻלַּת אָדָם גַּם כֵּן הוּא מֵחַסְדֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
since the fundamental divine will for human action is itself from Hashem's kindness,
שֶׁחָפֵץ שֶׁמַּעֲשֵׂה צַדִּיקִים יָאִירוּ הַכָּרַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּכָל הָעוֹלָמוֹת,
desiring that the deeds of the righteous illuminate the recognition of Hashem across all realms,
לָכֵן בֶּטַח יַסְכִּים הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל כָּל פְּעֻלָּתָם.
therefore Hashem will assuredly give His assent to all their endeavors.
h: Human Deeds Reveal the Purpose of Creation

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Talmud, Ketubot 5a:2
p: הֵשִׁיב בַּבְלִי אֶחָד וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא שְׁמוֹ: (תְּהִלִּים צה, ה) "וְיַבֶּשֶׁת יָדָיו יָצָרוּ".
“A certain Babylonian whose name was Rabbi Chiya challenged: (Psalms 95:5) ‘and His hands formed the dry land’ (two hands for physical earth).”
וְהָעִנְיָן שֶׁנִּקְרָא כָּאן רַבִּי חִיָּיא בְּשֵׁם "בַּבְלִי אֶחָד"
And the reason why Rabbi Chiya is titled here ‘a certain Babylonian,’
וְלֹא "רַבִּי חִיָּיא הַבַּבְלִי", כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּכָּר בְּכַמָּה מְקוֹמוֹת,
and not ‘Rabbi Chiya the Babylonian’ as found in several passages,
וּבְרוֹב מְקוֹמוֹת נִזְכָּר "רַבִּי חִיָּיא" סְתָם:
while in most places he is cited simply as ‘Rabbi Chiya’:
אָכֵן כִּי "בַּבְלִי" מוֹרֶה
Indeed, it is because ‘Babylonian’ denotes
שֶׁרוֹצֶה בְּכָל דָּבָר בְּכֹחַ עָצוּם וּבִמְהִירוּת זְמַן,
one who demands everything with mighty force and immediate haste,
וְכִדְאִיתָא (מְנָחוֹת צט:):
as taught in Menachot (99b):
וְהַבַּבְלִיִּים אוֹכְלִין אוֹתוֹ כְּשֶׁהוּא חַי,
the Babylonians eat it raw (hurriedly),
וּמְפָרֵשׁ בַּגְּמָרָא (שָׁם ק.):
and the Gemara clarifies (ibid. 100a):
לָא בַּבְלִיִּים הֵם וְכוּלֵי, קוֹרִין אוֹתָם עַל שֵׁם בַּבְלִיִּים;
they were not Babylonians, etc., they merely call them Babylonians;
וְכֵן הָיָה גָּדוֹל כֹּחוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי חִיָּיא,
and so mighty was the spiritual power of Rabbi Chiya,
כִּדְאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא פה:):
as taught in the Gemara (Bava Metzia 85b):
שֶׁיָּרַד לִפְנֵי הַתֵּיבָה לְעוֹרֵר אֶת הַגְּאוּלָּה קֹדֶם זְמַנָּהּ.
that he descended before the prayer ark seeking to arouse the final redemption before its time.
וְזֶה שֶׁהֵשִׁיב כָּאן: "וְיַבֶּשֶׁת יָדָיו יָצָרוּ" –
And this is why he challenged here: ‘and His hands formed the dry land’ –
אַף שֶׁכְּתִיב: "יָדִי יָסְדָה אֶרֶץ וִימִינִי טִפְּחָה שָׁמָיִם",
for although it is written: ‘My hand founded the earth and My right hand spanned the heavens,’
הַיְינוּ שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם נִכָּר אוֹר חֶסֶד שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת יָמִין,
meaning that in heaven the light of Chesed is manifest which is the right hand,
כִּי שָׁמַיִם רוֹמֵז לְגֹדֶל בְּהִירוּת,
for heaven signifies intense lucidity,
וְכֵן רוֹמֵז לַעֲבוֹדַת הָאָדָם כְּשֶׁהוּא בִּבְהִירוּת עֲצוּמָה אָז יַגִּיעַ לְמִדַּת יָמִין;
and likewise points to human service in that when it is in great clarity it reaches the right hand;
אֲבָל בָּאָרֶץ שֶׁשָּׁם נִסְתָּר אוֹר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ – נִבְרָא בִּשְׂמֹאל;
whereas on earth where Hashem’s light is concealed—it was created with the left hand;
אָכֵן רַבִּי חִיָּיא הֵשִׁיב: "וְיַבֶּשֶׁת יָדָיו יָצָרוּ" –
nevertheless Rabbi Chiya retorted: ‘and His hands formed the dry land’ –
הַיְינוּ שֶׁרַבִּי חִיָּיא מִצִּדּוֹ הִכִּיר
meaning that Rabbi Chiya from his elevated perspective recognized
שֶׁבְּכָל הֶסְתֵּר, אֲפִילּוּ הַיּוֹתֵר גָּדוֹל, גַּם כֵּן יֵשׁ "חֶסֶד אֵל כָּל הַיּוֹם";
that within every concealment, even the most opaque, ‘the kindness of God endures all day’;
וְכִדְאִיתָא בְּאִדְּרָא רַבָּא (נָשׂא קכט.):
and as taught in the Idra Rabba (Naso 129a):
שֶׁבְּאוֹר עַתִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא – לֵית שְׂמָאלָא בְּהַאי עַתִּיקָא סְתִימָאָה, כּוּלָּא יְמִינָא;
in the light of Atika Kadisha—there is no left side in this concealed Ancient One, all is right;
וּבֶאֱמֶת הַכֹּל מִשֹּׁרֶשׁ מָלֵא חֶסֶד וְרַחֲמִים;
and in truth everything from its primordial root is filled with lovingkindness and mercy;
וְאַף מַה שֶּׁנִּזְכַּר שָׁם בְּאִדְּרָא רַבָּא וְזוּטָא דִּבִּזְעֵיר אַנְפִּין אִית שְׂמָאלָא גַּם כֵּן,
and even what is noted there in the Idra Rabba and Zuta that in Ze'ir Anpin there exists a left side as well,
אָכֵן מִשֹּׁרֶשׁ הַכֹּל הוּא רַב חֶסֶד,
nonetheless at the source everything is abundant Chesed,
כִּדְאִיתָא (שָׁם קמא.): עַתִּיקָא דְּעַתִּיקִין וּזְעֵיר אַנְפִּין כּוּלָּא חַד וְכוּלֵי.
as taught (ibid. 141a): the Ancient of Ancients and Ze'ir Anpin are all one, etc.
h: Recognizing Kindness at the Root of Every Concealment

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Talmud, Ketubot 10b:1
p: מַאי "אַלְמָנָה"? אָמַר רַב חָנָא בַּגְדָּתָאָה: אַלְמָנָה עַל שֵׁם מָנָה.
“What is the etymology of ‘almanah’ (widow)? Rav Chana Bagdata’ah said: Almanah is named on account of the maneh (the statutory 100-zuz ketubah settlement).”
הָעִנְיָן בָּזֶה, כִּדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (מִשְׁפָּטִים קב.):
The inner meaning is as brought in the holy Zohar (Mishpatim 102a):
וּמַאן דְּנָסִיב אַרְמַלְתָּא – כְּמַאן דְּעָאל בְּיַמָּא בְּרוּחִין תַּקִּיפִין בְּלָא חֲבָלִין,
and whoever marries a widow is like one who embarks upon the sea in tempestuous winds without ropes,
וְלָא יָדַע אִי יַעֲבוֹר בִּשְׁלָם, אִי יִטְבַּע גּוֹ תְּהוֹמֵי;
not knowing whether he will cross in peace or drown within the abyss;
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ אִם שַׁיָּיכוּת לוֹ בְּשָׁרְשׁוֹ.
meaning he cannot know whether she truly belongs to his soul-root.
וְזֶה שֶׁנִּקְרֵאת "אַלְמָנָה" –
And this is why she is termed almanah:
אֶל מִי שַׁיָּיכוּת הַמָּנָה הַזֹּאת?
to whom does this portion (maneh) truly belong?
וַחֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה הִמְתִּיקוּ זֹאת בְּמֶתֶק לְשׁוֹנָם,
And our Sages of blessed memory sweetened this mystery through the sweetness of their language,
שֶׁקָּרְאוּ אוֹתָהּ עַל שֵׁם "מָנָה" –
naming her after the maneh—
הַיְינוּ שֶׁמְּבוֹרֶרֶת לְחֶלְקוֹ שֶׁהוּא מָנָה שֶׁלּוֹ.
meaning she is now clarified as his designated portion, being his true maneh.
h: Marriage and the Clarification of a Shared Soul Root

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Talmud, Ketubot 17a:1
p: רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק מְרַקֵּד אַתְּלָת;
“Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak would dance juggling three myrtle branches before the bride;
אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: קָא מַכְסֵיף לַן סָבָא!
Rabbi Zeira said: The elder is embarrassing us (by behaving undignified)!
כִּי נָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ, אִיפְּסִיק עַמּוּדָא דְּנוּרָא בֵּין דִּידֵיהּ לְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא וְכוּלֵי;
When he passed away, a pillar of fire intervened between him and the entire world, etc.;
אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: אַהַנְיָיא לֵיהּ שׁוּטִיתֵיהּ לְסָבָא,
Rabbi Zeira said: The elder’s myrtle branch (shutiteih) availed him!
וְאָמְרֵי לַהּ: שְׁטוּתֵיהּ לְסָבָא,
And some say: The elder’s ‘folly’ availed him!
וְאָמְרֵי לַהּ: שִׁיטָתֵיהּ לְסָבָא.
And some say: The elder’s consistent system (shitato) availed him!”
עַל זֶה כְּתִיב (אִיּוֹב יז, ט): "וְיֹאחֵז צַדִּיק דַּרְכּוֹ וּטֳהָר יָדַיִם יֹסִיף אֹמֶץ".
Concerning this it is written (Job 17:9): “The righteous shall hold on his way, and he that has clean hands shall wax stronger and stronger.”
"יֹאחֵז צַדִּיק דַּרְכּוֹ" –
“The righteous shall hold on his way” –
הַיְינוּ שֶׁהָאָדָם צָרִיךְ לְקַבֵּל עָלָיו מִדָּה טוֹבָה לַעֲשׂוֹת אוֹתָהּ
meaning that a person must adopt a virtuous practice
וּלְהִתְנַהֵג כֵּן תָּמִיד,
and conduct himself in it continually,
כַּאֲשֶׁר יָבִין שֶׁיִּצְטָרֵךְ לָהּ כְּפִי תְּכוּנַת נַפְשׁוֹ,
when he understands that he requires it according to the nature of his soul,
וְלֹא יַעַזְבֶנָּה כָּל יְמֵי חַיָּיו;
and never abandon it all the days of his life;
וְזֹאת תַּעֲזוֹר לוֹ בְּכָל עִנְיָנָיו;
and this practice will aid him in all his affairs;
וְאַף שֶׁיִּרְאֶה שֶׁבְּעֵינֵי אֲחֵרִים נִתְרָאֶה כִּשְׁטוּת, לֹא יָחוּשׁ כְּלוּם,
and even if he sees that in the eyes of others it appears as folly, he should pay no heed,
וְזֶה נִקְרָא "יֹאחֵז צַדִּיק דַּרְכּוֹ".
and this is titled “the righteous shall hold on his way.”
אַךְ אִם הָאָדָם יִתְנַהֵג בָּהּ תָּמִיד וְיִהְיֶה לוֹ רְגִילוּת,
However, if a person practices it constantly and it becomes mere routine,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יִתְרַשֵּׁל לַעֲשׂוֹתָהּ,
and on account of this he becomes lax in its execution,
עַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר "וּטֳהָר יָדַיִם יֹסִיף אֹמֶץ":
concerning this Scripture states: “and he that has clean hands shall wax stronger”:
כְּשֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה אוֹתָהּ בִּקְדֻשָּׁה וּבְטָהֳרָה לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם,
when he performs it with holiness and purity for Heaven’s sake,
יוֹסִיף לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֹמֶץ
Hashem will add strength unto him
שֶׁלֹּא יָבוֹא לוֹ שׁוּם הִתְרַשְּׁלוּת.
so that no laxity ever befalls him.
וְכֵן הָיָה הָעִנְיָן כָּאן בְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל,
And so was the case here with Rav Shmuel,
שֶׁתָּמִיד הִתְנַהֵג לְרַקֵּד אַתְּלָת,
who continually made it his practice to dance with three branches;
וְאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: "קָא מַכְסֵיף לַן סָבָא",
and Rabbi Zeira remarked: ‘the elder is embarrassing us,’
הַיְינוּ שֶׁהָיָה נִרְאֶה בְּעֵינֵי אֲחֵרִים כְּדָבָר קָטָן;
meaning that to others it appeared like a trivial, undignified act;
וְאַחַר כֵּן, כְּשֶׁנָּח נַפְשֵׁיהּ וְרָאוּ עַמּוּדָא דְּנוּרָא
and afterward, when he passed away and they beheld the separating pillar of fire
וְהֵבִינוּ שֶׁזֶּה הַמַּעֲשֶׂה עָזַר לוֹ,
and understood that this specific practice had aided him,
לָכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: "אַהַנְיָא לֵיהּ שׁוּטִיתֵיהּ" –
therefore Rabbi Zeira acknowledged: ‘his myrtle branch availed him’ –
הַיְינוּ מִזֶּה הַמַּעֲשֶׂה מִבַּדֵּי הַהֲדַס, מִזֶּה הָיְתָה לוֹ הַמַּדְרֵגָה הַזֹּאת;
meaning from this very deed with myrtle boughs he attained this exalted level;
"וְאָמְרֵי לַהּ: שְׁטוּתֵיהּ" –
“and some say: his folly” –
שֶׁהָיָה עוֹשֶׂה וְלֹא הִתְבַּיֵּישׁ
in that he performed it unabashedly
אַף שֶׁנִּרְאֶה בְּעֵינֵי אֲחֵרִים לִשְׁטוּת;
even though it appeared as folly in the eyes of others;
"וְאָמְרֵי לַהּ: שִׁיטָתֵיהּ" –
“and some say: his system” –
שֶׁהוֹסִיף אֹמֶץ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
in that he drew added fortitude from Hashem,
וְלֹא הָיָה אֶצְלוֹ כִּרְגִילוּת
and it never degenerated into mindless habit,
וְלֹא הִתְרַשֵּׁל בָּזֶה.
and he never became lax within it.
h: Holding to a Holy Practice Without Growing Weary

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Talmud, Ketubot 69a:1
p: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַב עָנָן לְרַב הוּנָא: "הוּנָא חַבְרִין, שְׁלָם וְכוּלֵי;
“Rav Anan sent a query to Rav Huna: ‘Huna our colleague, peace, etc.;
עָנָן עָנָן, מִמְּקַרְקְעֵי אוֹ מִמִּטַּלְטְלֵי?
Rav Huna replied: ‘Anan, Anan! Does the support of daughters collect from real estate or from movable property?
וּמַאן יָתֵיב בֵּי מַרְזֵיחָא בְּרֵישָׁא?"
And who sits at the head in the house of mourning?’”
הָעִנְיָן בָּזֶה, שֶׁזֹּאת הָיְתָה תְּשׁוּבָה עַל מַה שֶּׁלֹּא כִּבְּדוֹ
The inner meaning of this exchange is that this was Rav Huna's rejoinder to Rav Anan's failure to accord him proper honor
וְקָרָא לֵיהּ "חַבְרִין";
in addressing him merely as ‘our colleague’;
לָכֵן הֵשִׁיב לוֹ:
therefore he responded to him:
שֶׁאַף שֶׁעַל הַלְּבוּשׁ נִדְמֶה לְךָ שֶׁאַתָּה גָּדוֹל,
that although upon the external garment of this physical world it seems to you that you are prominent,
אַךְ תֵּדַע שֶׁהַאי עָלְמָא כְּבֵי הִלּוּלָא דָּמְיָא,
nevertheless know that this world is like a transient wedding feast,
וְיֵשׁ מִמֶּנּוּ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְבוּשִׁים הַמַּסְתִּירִים,
and within this world there exist deceptive garments that conceal absolute truth,
וְיוּכַל לְהִתְרָאוֹת שֶׁהַקָּטָן יִגְדַּל מֵהַגָּדוֹל;
such that it can appear as though the lesser person towers over the greater;
אֲבָל בֵּי מַרְזֵיחָא, שֶׁשָּׁם קָרוֹב לְעָלְמָא דִּקְשׁוֹט –
however in the house of mourning (bei marzeicha), which stands proximate to the World of Truth—
שָׁם יִתְרָאֶה הָאֱמֶת.
there the pristine truth becomes manifest.
וְכֵן מָצִינוּ כְּשֶׁבָּא אַבְרָהָם לִקְבּוֹר אֶת שָׂרָה,
And likewise we find when Abraham came to bury Sarah,
קָרְאוּ לוֹ בְּנֵי חֵת (בְּרֵאשִׁית כג, ו): "נְשִׂיא אֱלֹהִים אַתָּה בְּתוֹכֵנוּ",
the children of Heth proclaimed to him (Genesis 23:6): ‘You are a prince of God among us’,
כִּי שָׁם נִיכָּר הָאֱמֶת.
because there, at the threshold of burial, authentic truth is recognized.
וְלָכֵן בְּשִׁילְהֵי מַסֶּכֶת מוֹעֵד קָטָן (כח:)
And therefore at the conclusion of Tractate Moed Katan (28b)
אִיתָא בַּסְּפָרִים "אַנְשֵׁי דִּשְׁכֶנְצִיב":
mention is made in the commentaries of ‘the people of Shechentzib’:
כִּי שְׁכֶנְצִיב – שָׁם הָיוּ לֵיצָנִים,
for in Shechentzib the inhabitants were chronic cynics and scoffers,
כִּדְאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (פְּסָחִים קיב:):
as taught in the Gemara (Pesachim 112b):
"אַל תָּדוּר בִּשְׁכֶנְצִיב מִשּׁוּם דְּמַשְׁכֵי לָךְ בְּלֵיצָנוּתָא";
‘Do not reside in Shechentzib because they will draw you into cynicism’;
וְלָכֵן בְּעֵת הַהֶסְפֵּד,
and therefore, specifically at the solemn hour of the eulogy,
אֲפִילּוּ בִּשְׁכֶנְצִיב יִתְבַּטֵּל כָּל לֵיצָנוּתָם,
even in Shechentzib all their mocking cynicism evaporated,
וְיִתְרָאֶה נְקֻדַּת הָאֱמֶת,
and the inward point of truth shone forth,
וַאֲפִילּוּ הֵם בְּהֶכְרֵחַ יֹאמְרוּ דְּבָרִים טוֹבִים וַאֲמִתִּיִּים.
so that even they were irresistibly compelled to articulate words of goodness and truth.
h: Authentic Honor Revealed Near the World of Truth

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Talmud, Kiddushin 2a:1
p: "הָאִשָּׁה נִקְנֵית" –
“‘A woman is acquired’:”
מַאי שְׁנָא הָכָא דְּתָנֵי "הָאִשָּׁה נִקְנֵית",
what is the difference here that the Tanna teaches ‘A woman is acquired,’
וּמַאי שְׁנָא הָתָם דְּתָנֵי "הָאִישׁ מְקַדֵּשׁ" וְכוּלֵי?
and what is the difference there in the second chapter that he teaches ‘A man betroths (mekadesh), etc.’?
מֵעִיקָּרָא תָּנֵי לִישָּׁנָא דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא,
The Gemara resolves: Initially the Mishnah taught the phrasing of the Written Torah (kinyan),
וּלְבַסּוֹף תָּנֵי לִישָּׁנָא דְּרַבָּנַן;
and subsequently it taught the phrasing of the Rabbis (kiddushin);
וּמַאי לִישָּׁנָא דְּרַבָּנַן?
and what is the rabbinic meaning of kiddushin?
דְּאָסַר לַהּ אַכּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא כְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ
That he renders her forbidden unto the entire world like a consecrated object (hekdesh).
וּלְהָבִין לָמָּה נִקְרָא זֹאת "לִישָּׁנָא דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא" וּ"מְקַדֵּשׁ" "לִישָּׁנָא דְּרַבָּנַן",
And to understand why this term is called the language of the Torah while ‘mekadesh’ is titled the language of the Rabbis;
הֲלֹא לִישָּׁנָא דְּרַבָּנַן גַּם כֵּן הוּא לִישָּׁנָא דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא?
for is not the phrasing of the Rabbis inherently rooted in Torah?
וּבֶאֱמֶת, הָא לִישָּׁנָא דְּרַבָּנַן לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ אֶלָּא בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ הוֹסָפָה עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
Moreover in truth, rabbinic phrasing is strictly applicable where there exists an additional fence upon biblical law,
אֲבָל הָכָא אֵין זֶה הוֹסָפָה,
whereas here there is seemingly no addition,
דְּהָא גַּם מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא אָסַר לַהּ אַכּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא כְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ!
since biblically she is likewise rendered forbidden to all the world like hekdesh!
אָכֵן הָעִנְיָן בָּזֶה
However, the inner meaning is
כְּעִנְיָן שֶׁאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (חֻלִּין קט:):
in accordance with what is taught in the Gemara (Chullin 109b):
כָּל מִילְּתָא דְּאָסַר לָן רַחֲמָנָא – שָׁרֵי לָן כְּוָותֵיהּ;
for everything that the Merciful One prohibited unto us, He permitted to us something comparable;
וְכֵן שֶׁאִשָּׁה אֲסוּרָה לוֹ,
and so a woman is forbidden to him as an illicit relationship,
וְעַל יְדֵי קִדּוּשִׁין מוּתֶּרֶת;
and through sacred betrothal she becomes permitted;
וְלָכֵן לְשׁוֹן חֲכָמִים הוּא שֶׁ"הָאִישׁ מְקַדֵּשׁ",
therefore the phrasing of the Sages is that ‘a man consecrates (mekadesh),’
לִרְמוֹז שֶׁאַף בְּמַה שֶּׁמֻּתָּר לוֹ, גַּם כֵּן יְקַדֵּשׁ עַצְמוֹ
to allude that even within that which is permitted to him, he must likewise sanctify himself
שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה מְשׁוּקָּע בְּשׁוּם דָּבָר;
so that he does not become submerged within lustful desire;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמִּדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא מוּתֶּרֶת אִשָּׁה עַל יְדֵי קִדּוּשִׁין,
and just as biblically a woman is permitted through betrothal,
וְאִסּוּר פְּנוּיָה אֵינוֹ מְפוֹרָשׁ מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא,
while the prohibition against an unmarried woman is not explicitly spelled out in the Torah,
אַךְ בִּלְשׁוֹן חֲכָמִים שֶׁהָאִישׁ יְקַדֵּשׁ אִשָּׁה,
yet in rabbinic terminology a man must formally sanctify a woman,
וּבְלֹא קִדּוּשִׁין וּבְרָכָה אֲסוּרָה עָלָיו,
and without formal betrothal and nuptial blessings she remains forbidden to him,
וּמִמֵּילָא נִרְמָז בָּזֶה
and consequently it is alluded through this
שֶׁיְּקַדֵּשׁ עַצְמוֹ גַּם בַּמֻּתָּר לוֹ מִדְּרַבָּנָן.
that one must consecrate himself even within that which is permissible, fulfilling the rabbinic injunction to sanctify oneself in the permitted.
h: Sanctifying Oneself Within What Is Permitted

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Talmud, Bava Metzia 2a:1
p: מַאי "מְצָאתִיהָ"? "רְאִיתִיהָ".
“What is the meaning of ‘I found it’? It means: ‘I saw it’.
אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא אֲתַאי לִידֵיהּ, בִּרְאִיָּה בְּעָלְמָא קָנֵי?
The Gemara challenges: Even though it did not come into his hand, does one acquire ownership merely through visual sight?
The Tanna therefore taught: ‘It is all mine’,
דְּבִרְאִיָּה לָא קָנֵי.
proving that through mere sight he does not acquire ownership.”
כִּי בַּסַּלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ נוּכַל לוֹמַר
For on the initial premise (salka da'atakh) we might have reasoned
שֶׁבִּרְאִיָּה בְּעָלְמָא קָנֵי;
that through mere visual apprehension one acquires true spiritual possession;
וְכֵן הָיָה בִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם,
and so it occurred at the Exodus from Egypt,
שֶׁשָּׁם הִשִּׂיגוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּרְאִיָּה,
wherein Israel attained divine perception through direct vision,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא (מְכִילְתָּא פָּרָשָׁה ג): "רָאֲתָה שִׁפְחָה עַל הַיָּם",
as brought in the Mekhilta (Parashah 3): ‘a maidservant saw at the Sea what Ezekiel did not see’,
וְחָשְׁבוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבִּרְאִיָּה זוֹ קָנוּ אֶת הָאוֹר בְּקִנְיָן גָּמוּר;
and Israel assumed that through this visionary perception they had acquired the divine light as an absolute possession;
וְכֵן אַחַר כֵּן הָלְכוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים וְלֹא מָצְאוּ מַיִם,
and likewise subsequently they traveled three days in the desert and found no water,
הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה לָהֶם שׁוּם תְּשׁוּקָה וְחֵשֶׁק,
meaning they were completely depleted of inward yearning and spiritual desire,
וְכִדְאִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (תַּנְחוּמָא בְּשַׁלַּח יט): "בְּלֹא מַיִם – בְּלֹא תוֹרָה",
and as brought in the Midrash (Tanchuma, Beshalach 19): ‘without water means without Torah’,
וְאָז הִכִּירוּ שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם עֲדַיִן קִנְיָן גָּמוּר;
and then they recognized that they did not yet possess an enduring acquisition;
רַק בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה – אָז זָכוּ לְקִנְיָן בִּשְׁלֵימוּת;
only at the Giving of the Torah did they merit complete, permanent possession;
כִּי כָל מַה שֶּׁמַּשִּׂיג הָאָדָם בִּרְאִיָּה,
for whatever a person perceives through visionary sight,
יָכוֹל לִקְנוֹת אַחַר כֵּן בְּקִנְיָן גָּמוּר עַל יְדֵי הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת,
he can subsequently acquire as an enduring possession through laborious exertion,
רַק צָרִיךְ לָזֶה זְמַן;
only that this requires time;
וְאַחַר כֵּן מַה שֶּׁמִּשְׁתַּדֵּל וְקוֹנֶה עַל יְדֵי פְּעֻלּוֹתָיו –
and afterward, whatever he toils and acquires through his active deeds—
זֶה נִשְׁאָר לוֹ לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא גַּם כֵּן,
this remains his eternally for the World to Come as well,
כִּי זֶהוּ חֶלְקוֹ בְּשָׁרְשׁוֹ;
inasmuch as this constitutes his essential portion at his root;
אֲבָל מַה שֶּׁרוֹאֶה וְאֵין לוֹ בָּזֶה קִנְיָן גָּמוּר,
whereas that which he merely sees without holding full acquired possession,
זֶהוּ רַק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
this occurs only in this transient world,
שֶׁיָּכוֹל לִרְאוֹת אוֹר לְמַעְלָה מִמַּדְרֵגָתוֹ;
where one can momentarily glimpse light transcending his actual spiritual rung;
אֲבָל לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
however in the World to Come,
שָׁם יִשָּׁאֵר בְּיָדוֹ רַק מַה שֶּׁקָּנָה עַל יְדֵי הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ,
there shall remain in his hand solely what he acquired through his own labor,
שֶׁזֶּה שַׁיָּיךְ לוֹ בְּשָׁרְשׁוֹ.
which truly belongs to him in his primordial root.
h: Lasting Acquisition Comes Through Effort Beyond Vision

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Talmud, Bava Metzia 13a:1
p: כֵּיוָן דִּנְפַל – אִתְּרַע לֵיהּ, וְחָיְישִׁינַן דִּלְמָא אִקְּרִי וּכְתוּב.
“Once it fell—its legal presumption of validity was impaired, and we suspect that perhaps it was merely written as a draft.”
בְּעִנְיַן סְבָרַת "כֵּיוָן דִּנְפַל אִתְּרַע":
Regarding the legal rationale of ‘once it fell it was impaired’:
וְכִי בַּמֶּה אִתְּרַע חֶזְקָתוֹ?
wherein was its presumption impaired?
וַהֲלֹא כָּל דָּבָר שֶׁאָדָם אוֹבֵד, אִם יֵשׁ בּוֹ סִימָן הֲרֵי הוּא בְּחֶזְקָתוֹ הָרִאשׁוֹנָה?
For is it not so that regarding any object a person loses, if it possesses identifying marks it retains its initial presumption of validity?
אַךְ כֵּיוָן שֶׁהַשְּׁטָר אֵין גּוּפוֹ נִצְרָךְ לְהָאָדָם,
However, since the physical parchment of a legal contract is not an object of bodily consumption for man;
כִּי בִּשְׁאָר חֲפָצִים שֶׁאָדָם אוֹבֵד
for regarding other physical possessions that a person loses,
יֵשׁ לוֹמַר שֶׁהוּא בְּהַשְׁגָּחָה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיֹּאבַד הַחֵפֶץ מִמֶּנּוּ לִזְמַן מָה,
it can be said that it was directed by Hashem's providence that the item be withheld from him for a given time;
אֲבָל הַשְּׁטָר אֵינוֹ נִצְרָךְ לוֹ
but a legal document serves no bodily function,
וְלָמָּה אִבֵּד אוֹתוֹ?
why then did he lose it?
אָכֵן בָּזֶה הֶרְאָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּהַשְׁגָּחָתוֹ הַפְּרָטִית
Indeed, through this loss Hashem demonstrated through His individual providence
שֶׁאֵין הַשְּׁטָר הַזֶּה בָּרוּר,
that this contract is not legally upright and substantiated,
וְלָכֵן אִתְּרַע בְּנָפְלוֹ.
and therefore its validity was impaired through its very falling.
h: Providence and the Loss of a Legal Document

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Talmud, Bava Metzia (Yerushalmi) 1
p: (פֶּרֶק ג׳ הֲלָכָה ה׳) אִלֵּין עַכְבְּרַיָּיא רַשִּׁיעַיָּא נִינְהוּ, כַּד חָמְיָין פֵּירֵי סַגִּיאִין קָרְיָין לְחַבְרַיְיהוֹן וְאָכְלִין עִמְּהוֹן.
(Jerusalem Talmud Bava Metzia 3:5) “These mice are wicked: when they behold abundant fruit, they call their fellows and eat together with them.”
וְאַף שֶׁבַּגְּמָרָא (חֻלִּין בַּבְלִי סג.) אִיתָא:
And although in the Babylonian Gemara (Chullin 63a) it is taught:
לָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמָהּ "חֲסִידָה"? שֶׁעוֹשָׂה חֲסִידוּת עִם חַבְרוֹתֶיהָ,
why is the stork called chasidah? Because it acts with kindness toward its companions;
וְלָמָּה נִקְרְאוּ הָעַכְבָּרִים בְּמִדָּה זוֹ "רְשָׁעִים"?
why then are mice termed ‘wicked’ on account of this very same trait?
אֶלָּא שֶׁזֶּה הִכִּירוּ חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּשֹׁרֶשׁ מִדַּת כָּל הַבְּרוּאִים:
Rather, our Sages of blessed memory recognized the foundational root of each creature’s character:
שֶׁהַחֲסִידָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא בְּטִבְעָהּ רַחֲמָנִית, נוֹתֶנֶת גַּם לַחֲבֶרְתָּהּ;
that the stork, because it is inherently merciful in its nature, shares with its companion;
וְהָעַכְבָּר נוֹתֵן לַחֲבֵירוֹ מִפְּנֵי שֶׁרוֹצֶה לְהַפְסִיד,
whereas the mouse shares with its peer solely out of a malicious desire to destroy property;
וְאִם אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לֶאֱכֹל – קוֹרֵא לַחֲבֵירוֹ.
and when it cannot devour everything itself, it summons its fellow to maximize the damage.
וְכֵן רְאָיָה מִמַּה שֶּׁאִיתָא בְּהוֹרָיוֹת בַּבְלִי (יג.):
And likewise proof of this is found in the Babylonian Horayot (13a):
רָבָא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ גְּלִימֵי גָּיְיצֵי;
Rava said: They will even gnaw through woolen cloaks (from which they derive no nourishment);
הַיְינוּ שֶׁטִּבְעָהּ הוּא לְהַזִּיק וּלְקַלְקֵל אֲפִילּוּ בְּמַה שֶּׁאֵין לָהֶם הֲנָאָה.
meaning its innate nature is to ruin and damage even that from which it reaps no physical benefit.
וְזֶה דְּאִיתָא שָׁם: שֶׁסּוּרָן רַע עַל עַכְבָּרִים,
And this explains what is stated there: that mice have a malicious disposition;
וּכְפֵירוּשׁ רַשִׁ"י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה שָׁם, שֶׁיִּצְרָם רָע, הַיְינוּ שֶׁרְצוֹנָם לְקַלְקֵל.
and in the commentary of Rashi of blessed memory there: that their instinct is evil, meaning their overarching desire is to ruin.
h: Similar Deeds Can Arise From Opposite Motives

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Talmud, Bava Batra 8a:1
p: רַבִּי פָּתַח אוֹצָרוֹת בִּשְׁנֵי בַּצּוֹרֶת וְכוּלֵי;
“Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi opened his storehouses in years of drought, etc.;
אָמַר לֵיהּ: פַּרְנְסֵנִי כְּכֶלֶב וּכְעוֹרֵב!
a petitioner pleaded with him: ‘Sustain me like a dog and like a raven!’”
הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לוֹ לִתְלוֹת בְּשׁוּם זְכוּת,
Meaning that he did not seek to rely upon any personal merit,
רַק שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ שֶׁיִּשְׁוֶה לְקוֹנוֹ,
rather he implored him to equate himself with his Creator,
שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִשְׁתַּבַּח בְּרַחֲמָנוּתוֹ עַל שְׁנֵי הַבְּרוּאִים אֵלּוּ;
in that Hashem is praised for His compassion upon these two specific creatures;
וְכִדְאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (שַׁבָּת קנה:):
as taught in the Gemara (Shabbat 155b):
"יוֹדֵעַ צַדִּיק דִּין דַּלִּים" (מִשְׁלֵי כט, ז) –
‘The righteous knows the cause of the poor’ –
יוֹדֵעַ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בַּכֶּלֶב שֶׁמְּזוֹנוֹתָיו מוּעָטִין,
the Holy One knows regarding the dog that its food is scarce,
לְפִיכָךְ שׁוֹהֶה אֲכִילָתוֹ בְּמֵעָיו שְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים;
therefore He causes its food to linger in its stomach for three days;
וְלָמָּה מְזוֹנוֹתָיו מוּעָטִין?
and why is its food scarce?
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַכֶּלֶב אֵין לוֹ הַשְׁפָּעָה מִצַּד מִדַּת הַדִּין שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ מָזוֹן בְּשֶׁפַע,
because the dog has no entitlement from the strict attribute of justice to receive abundant nourishment,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (יְשַׁעְיָה נו, יא): "וְהַכְּלָבִים עַזֵּי נֶפֶשׁ".
and as it is written (Isaiah 56:11): ‘And the dogs are greedy of soul’.
וְכֵן הָעוֹרֵב הוּא אַכְזָרִי,
And likewise the raven is innately cruel to its young,
וּמִצַּד מִדַּת הַדִּין אָסוּר לְרַחֵם עַל אַכְזָרִי,
and from the perspective of justice it is forbidden to pity the cruel,
וְכִדְאִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (שְׁמוּאֵל פָּרָשָׁה יח, ו):
and as brought in Midrash Shemuel (18:6):
"כָּל הַמְרַחֵם עַל אַכְזָרִי סוֹפוֹ שֶׁיִּתְאַכְזֵר עַל רַחְמָנִי";
‘Whoever has mercy upon the cruel will ultimately become cruel upon the merciful’;
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּרוֹב חַסְדּוֹ וְרַחֲמָיו
nevertheless Hashem in His abundant lovingkindness and mercy
נוֹתֵן מָקוֹם גַּם לִבְרוּאִים אֵלּוּ.
provides sustenance even for these creatures.
וְרַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ הִתְעוֹרֵר לְבַקָּשָׁתוֹ,
And our holy Master (Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi) was moved by his plea,
שֶׁנִּתְעוֹרֵר בּוֹ רַחֲמָנוּת בְּשָׁרְשׁוֹ,
for compassion was stirred within him at his root,
לְפִי שֶׁהָיָה בֶּאֱמֶת תַּלְמִיד חָכָם;
inasmuch as the petitioner was in truth a profound Torah scholar;
וּלְאַחַר כֵּן הִתְחָרֵט,
yet subsequently Rabbi Yehudah regretted feeding him,
שֶׁחָשַׁב שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יָכוֹל לְרַחֵם אַף עַל בְּרוּאִים כָּאֵלּוּ,
reasoning that while Hashem can have mercy even upon such unworthy creatures,
שֶׁהוּא גְּדוֹל הָעֵצָה וְרַב הָעֲלִילִיָּה
being great in counsel and mighty in work
וְיָכוֹל לְרַחֵם אַף עַל אֵלּוּ,
and empowered to show mercy even to them,
וְיָכוֹל לְהַשְׁגִּיחַ שֶׁאַף שֶׁיַּשְׁפִּיעַ לְאֵלּוּ לֹא יַגִּיעַ מֵהֶם שׁוּם רָעָה לְאַחֵר;
and capable of overseeing that even if He provides for them, no harm will befall another through them;
אֲבָל אָדָם אֵין בִּיכָלְתּוֹ לְהַשְׁגִּיחַ וְלִבְטוֹחַ,
however mortal man has no power to safeguard and ensure this,
וְצָרִיךְ לִירֹא שֶׁמָּא כְּשֶׁיְּרַחֵם עַל אַכְזָרִי יַגִּיעַ רָעָה לְרַחְמָנִי;
and must tremble lest showing mercy to the cruel results in injury to the merciful;
וְאָמַר: אוֹי לִי שֶׁנָּתַתִּי פִּתִּי לְעַם הָאָרֶץ!
and he lamented: ‘Woe is me that I gave my bread to an unlearned boor!’
וְכַאֲשֶׁר בָּדַק וּמָצָא שֶׁיּוֹנָתָן בֶּן עַמְרָם תַּלְמִידוֹ הוּא,
And when he investigated and discovered that it was Yonatan ben Amram his disciple,
חָזַר מִדַּעְתּוֹ שֶׁהָיָה סָבַר שֶׁאָסוּר לִיתֵּן מִפִּתּוֹ לְעַם הָאָרֶץ;
he retracted his original opinion that it was forbidden to feed an unlearned person;
שֶׁהֲרֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא צִוָּה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל מִצְוַת צְדָקָה
for behold the Holy One commanded Israel the mitzvah of charity
וְצִוָּה לְרַחֵם עַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
and commanded compassion upon all Israel,
וּבַהֲדֵי כַּבְשֵׁי דְּרַחֲמָנָא לָמָּה לָךְ?
and why should you meddle in the hidden mysteries of the Merciful One?
וּמִזֶּה הִתְבּוֹנֵן רַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ
And from this our holy Master discerned
שֶׁלֹּא נָתַן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְאָדָם לְהַרְהֵר אַחַר מִצְווֹת ה';
that the Holy One did not grant permission for man to second-guess Hashem's commandments;
שֶׁהֲרֵי כְּפִי דַּעְתּוֹ שֶׁלֹּא לִיתֵּן מִפִּתּוֹ לְעַם הָאָרֶץ,
for according to his theory not to give his bread to an unlearned person,
יָכוֹל לִיפּוֹל בְּטָעוּת
one could easily fall into catastrophic error
וְלֹא לִיתֵּן גַּם לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁלֹּא יִרְצֶה לֵיהָנוֹת מִכְּבוֹד הַתּוֹרָה;
and withhold sustenance even from a sage who refuses to benefit from the honor of the Torah;
וְלָכֵן חָזַר מִדְּבָרָיו וְאָמַר: "יִכָּנְסוּ הַכֹּל";
therefore he retracted his words and proclaimed: ‘Let everyone enter!’
וְלֹא סָמַךְ עַצְמוֹ עַל מַה שֶּׁרָאָה שֶׁאֵירַע לוֹ נֵס
and did not rely upon the fact that a miracle had occurred for him
וְהִתְרַחֵם לְפִי שָׁעָה עַל תַּלְמִיד חָכָם אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא יָדַע אוֹתוֹ.
wherein he had momentarily shown compassion to a sage even without knowing him.
וְאִם הָיָה בּוֹ בְּרַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ שֶׁמֶץ תַּקִּיפוּת
And had there existed within our holy Master any trace of haughty self-assurance
לְהִתְגָּאוֹת וְלוֹמַר שֶׁהוּא מְכוּוָּן לִרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אַף שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעַת,
to boast that he intuitively aligns with Hashem's will even without conscious knowledge,
הָיָה נִשְׁאָר בְּדַעְתּוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה תְּחִלָּה
he would have remained in his original stance
שֶׁלֹּא לִיתֵּן מִפִּתּוֹ לְעַם הָאָרֶץ,
not to give of his bread to an unlearned person,
וְהָיָה סוֹמֵךְ שֶׁאַף אִם יֶאֱרַע תַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁאֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה לֵיהָנוֹת מִכְּבוֹד הַתּוֹרָה,
relying that should a modest sage appear who refuses to benefit from Torah prestige,
יְכַוֵּין שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעַת וְיִתֵּן לוֹ;
he would hit the mark unconsciously and provide for him;
אֶלָּא חָזַר וְשָׁב מִדַּעְתּוֹ וְאָמַר:
rather he fully retracted and acknowledged:
אַף שֶׁאֵירַע לוֹ פַּעַם אַחַת שֶׁכִּיוֵּון וְנָתַן לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם הַצְנֵעַ לֶכֶת,
even though it happened once that he aligned and fed a hidden, modest scholar,
אֲבָל לֹא בְּכָל שַׁעְתָּא וְשַׁעְתָּא מִתְרַחֵישׁ נִיסָּא;
nonetheless, not in every hour does a miracle occur;
שֶׁמָּא לֹא יִזְכֶּה בְּפַעַם אַחֶרֶת לְכַוֵּין בָּזֶה
lest on another occasion he fail to hit the mark
וְיִמְנַע פִּתּוֹ מִתַּלְמִיד חָכָם;
and withhold his bread from a righteous scholar;
וְלָכֵן אָמַר: "יִכָּנְסוּ הַכֹּל".
therefore he commanded: ‘Let all enter.’
וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן תּוֹדָה שֶׁנֶּאֱכֶלֶת רַק לְיוֹם אֶחָד,
And this corresponds to the thanksgiving offering (todah) which is eaten only for a single day,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר בְּחֵלֶק רִאשׁוֹן (אֱמוֹר, דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "בְּהֶסְדֵּרָא"),
as explained in Part I (Parashat Emor, s.v. “Be-hesdera”),
לְפִי שֶׁתּוֹדָה בָּאָה עַל הַנֵּס,
because the todah is brought over a miracle,
וּבְנֵס אָסוּר לִסְמוֹךְ עַל יוֹם מָחָר לוֹמַר שֶׁיֶּאֱרַע לוֹ מָחָר גַּם כֵּן,
and regarding a miracle it is forbidden to rely on tomorrow presuming that a miracle will occur tomorrow as well,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר שָׁם.
and as explained there.
h: Compassion Beyond Claims of Personal Merit

paras.r: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Talmud, Sanhedrin 99a:1
p: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כָּל הַנְּבִיאִים לֹא נִתְנַבְּאוּ אֶלָּא לְבַעֲלֵי תְּשׁוּבָה,
“And Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: All the prophets prophesied only concerning penitents;
אֲבָל צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים – 'עַיִן לֹא רָאָתָה אֱלֹהִים זוּלָתְךָ';
but concerning the wholly righteous: ‘No eye has seen, O God, beside You’;
וּפְלִיגָא דְּרַבִּי אַבָּהוּ, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּהוּ:
and this disputes the view of Rabbi Abbahu, for Rabbi Abbahu said:
מָקוֹם שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְּשׁוּבָה עוֹמְדִין, שָׁם צַדִּיקִים אֵינָן עוֹמְדִין,
‘In the place where penitents stand, righteous people cannot stand there,’
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (יְשַׁעְיָה נז, יט): 'שָׁלוֹם שָׁלוֹם לָרָחוֹק וְלַקָּרוֹב' –
as it is stated (Isaiah 57:19): ‘Peace, peace to him that is far off, and to him that is near’ –
בְּרֵישָׁא 'רָחוֹק' וַהֲדַר 'קָרוֹב';
first ‘far off’ and only then ‘near’;
מַאי 'רָחוֹק'? רָחוֹק דְּמֵעִיקָּרָא;
what is ‘far off’? One who was originally far off;
וּמַאי 'קָרוֹב'? קָרוֹב דְּמֵעִיקָּרָא וּדְהַשְׁתָּא;
and what is ‘near’? One who was near from the beginning and remains near now;
וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: לָרָחוֹק – שֶׁהוּא רָחוֹק מֵעֲבֵירָה;
while Rabbi Yochanan expounded: ‘to the far off’—who remained far from transgression;
קָרוֹב – שֶׁהוּא קָרוֹב מֵעֲבֵירָה וְנִתְרַחֵק מִמֶּנָּה.
‘to the near’—who was close to transgression and distanced himself from it.”
נִתְבָּאֵר בְּלִקּוּטֵי הַשַּׁ״ס (בְּרָכוֹת לד: חֵלֶק זֶה)
It was explained in Likutim on the Shas (Berakhot 34b in this Part)
שֶׁלֹּא פְּלִיגֵי, וְאֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים;
